## PR-116 — the `acc == thresh` boundary read at byte level: the engine
fires only STRICTLY past the threshold, the row handler writes the remainder
back at 0x52118, and no row of this corpus can skip the compare

- WHAT THIS PR DOES. No behaviour change, and no new fixture: it settles the
  reading PR-110 left open, measures how many rows the question covers, and
  prices changing the gate with four mutations. PR-110's item 2, quoted
  verbatim (NEXT_STEPS.md:8439-8446): "(2) The boundary at exact equality:
  13932 of the 14881 authored BY_TIME rows are exact multiples of 100 and
  the feed is exactly 100, so whether a row fires at `acc == thresh` (the
  port) or only above it (the literal flag direction of `39 d8` / `7d 27`
  read AT&T-style, which also makes the `sub ebx,eax` remainder negative) is
  a systematic +1-feed difference. PR-100's reading - threshold first,
  "return with the debt kept" - is the coherent one and is what the port
  implements; the two readings are not equivalent, and nothing in the repo
  or the clip separates them." The last clause is still true and still the
  reason the port keeps `>=`. What is NOT true is the parenthetical: the
  bytes do not read both ways. The DB was rebuilt first (`python3
  tools/re/leodb.py build`, over `build/leo/leo.img`, `meta.img_sha256`
  matching the image); every byte below is quoted from `leodb.py dis`, so
  nothing here depends on a syntax choice.
- THE DECISION POINT, byte for byte. The record step is 0x521f0: prologue
  `push ebx/ecx/esi/edi/ebp; sub esp,0x6c`, epilogue at 0x52354 (`83 c4 6c`
  `add esp,0x6c`, 5 pops, `ret`). It is vtable slot +0x0c in all 16 of the
  record classes' class tables, and the row handler 0x520c0 is slot +0x18 of
  the SAME 16 tables - all 16 sites where 0x520c0 is stored sit at base+0x18
  with base+0x0c = 0x521f0. Inside the step: 0x52317 `ff 92 a0 00 00 00`
  `call [edx+0xa0]` is the mode feed (PR-99's dispatcher, 0x543a2), and it
  runs BEFORE the compare; then 0x52320 `8b 43 10` loads the row node's
  threshold ([node+0x10]) into eax, 0x52323 `8b 9a a1 00 00 00` loads the
  object's accumulator ([obj+0xa1], from [ebp+0x0] at 0x5231d) into ebx,
  0x52329 `39 d8`, 0x5232b `7d 27 jge 0x52354`, then on the fall-through
  0x52331 `8b 75 44`, 0x52334 `29 c3 sub ebx,eax`, 0x52338 `ff 56 18`
  `call [esi+0x18]` - the handler, with ebx = acc - thresh.
- WHY THE "TWO READINGS" FRAME WAS WRONG. `39 d8` is `cmp eax,ebx`, and the
  AT&T spelling of those same two bytes is `cmp %eax, %ebx`: the operands,
  the order and the flag source (first minus second) are the same in both
  syntaxes, so "read AT&T-style" cannot flip the direction. The flags are
  thresh - acc; `jge` taken means thresh >= acc, i.e. the step returns
  through 0x52354 with the accumulator kept and runs NO row when acc ==
  thresh, and runs the row only when acc > thresh. Only swapping the
  operands flips it, and that reading is self-contradictory: with flags from
  acc - thresh the same `7d 27` would skip the row whenever acc >= thresh,
  so a row would run only while its threshold had never been reached. It is
  also where PR-110's "makes the `sub ebx,eax` remainder negative" comes
  from - a symptom of the swap, not of the bytes. Under the bytes, at exact
  equality nothing happens: the accumulator stays at thresh, the next feed
  makes it thresh + 100, and the row then runs with a remainder of exactly
  one feed. That is the systematic +1-feed difference, and the direction of
  it is the opposite of the one in the quoted text: it is the PORT that
  fires early, on the iteration that only reaches the threshold.
- CORRECTION TO PR-115'S RECORD (NEXT_STEPS.md:9166-9169), quoted: "And
  0x52334 `29 c3` (`sub ebx, eax`) computes the remainder in REGISTERS only:
  the only writes to `[obj+0xa1]` anywhere are the feeds at 0x543d1 /
  0x543e7 / 0x54412 / 0x5443b, so the accumulator is monotonic and there is
  no cap and no resync in that path." Two parts of that are wrong. (1) The
  remainder is not registers-only: the handler at 0x520c0 saves its entry
  ebx at 0x520cb (`89 5c 24 14`), reloads it at 0x52114 (`8b 54 24 14`) and
  stores it at 0x52118 (`89 90 a1 00 00 00`, `mov [eax+0xa1],edx`). The
  engine does commit the subtraction, through the handler. (2) 0x54412 and
  0x5443b are `add edi,eax` / `add ecx,eax` on a loaded copy, not stores:
  the mode-2 body is 0x54400 `8b bb a1 00 00 00` load / 0x5440c `81 c3 a1
  00 00 00` `add ebx,0xa1` / 0x54412 `01 c7` / 0x54414 `89 3b`
  `mov [ebx],edi`, and mode 4's is 0x54429 load / 0x54435 `add ebx,0xa1` /
  0x5443b `01 c1` / 0x5443d `89 0b` `mov [ebx],ecx`. Those stores carry no
  displacement at all, which is why a text search for `0xa1]` misses them.
  The complete set the DB finds - every instruction whose operands mention a
  +0xa1 displacement, listed in `/tmp/opencode/pr116_write_set.txt`; 9 in
  the 0x52000-0x54500 range and they are all this slot: WRITES 0x52118 (the
  remainder), 0x5236b / 0x533b0 / 0x5389e (`mov ptr,0x0` - the three zeroes
  PR-100 listed at NEXT_STEPS.md:5676-5685, in the same paragraph
  that says "The only non-zero assignment found is the one PR-99
  noted at 0x52118, which stores the result of an owner method"),
  0x543d1 / 0x543e7 (`add`,
  modes 0 and 1); stores that reach the slot through a pointer built by the
  `add reg,0xa1` above them: 0x54414 (mode 2, no gate) and 0x5443d (mode 4,
  gated on `[obj+0xbe] != 0` at 0x5441b); READS 0x52323 (this compare),
  0x54400, 0x54429. So the accumulator is not monotonic: every row that
  runs rewrites it, and three paths zero it. PR-100's record had 0x52118 and
  the zeroes right; PR-115's sentence contradicts it and this is the
  correction.
- THE OTHER BRANCH, AND HOW MANY ROWS COULD TAKE IT. At 0x52235-0x5224b the
  step tests the node's key string with 0x495b0 (the "is it empty" test).
  Empty -> the 0x522fc path quoted above: OR [node+0x0c] into the caller's
  key, feed, compare. Non-empty -> 0x52251: OR [obj+0x60] into the key,
  call 0x47e40, return if it finds nothing, else `31 db` (`xor ebx,ebx`) and
  `eb 3c` (`jmp 0x52338`) - the handler with the accumulator set to 0 and no
  threshold compare at any point. The only directive that builds such a node
  is `Wait`: the name is the string at 0x91989, compared at 0x46b52-0x46b59
  inside the level-text parser 0x45df0 (the same function that holds the
  row-split format ' , %[^,| ' at 0x91844, which tokenises on ',' '|' and
  space), and the handler at 0x46b62 writes the node's string through
  0x749a0 at 0x46b89 and gives it the vtable 0xa11c8. THE COMPARE IS NOT
  CASE-SENSITIVE: the helper at 0x76a69 lower-cases BOTH sides (`83 f9 41` /
  `7c 07`, `83 f9 5a` / `7f 02`, `04 20` / `80 c4 20`, then `38 e0`
  `cmp al,ah`), so the `WAIT` that the .MOV text really writes reaches that
  handler. Census, both counts: 0 tokens with the exact case the name table
  stores, 255 standalone `WAIT` tokens, 251 of them on lines this repo's row
  parser reads as rows - the `WAIT K_NEVER` (159), `WAIT K_GEN1` (25) and
  `WAIT AC_DUP`/`AC_TIME` tails PR-88's table names and the port counts
  without implementing them, plus the rest.
  Whether each of those builds a keyed ROW node or a separate event node is
  unread (item 3), so the tool prints the boundary population as a bracket:
  AT MOST 15317 of 18617 rows, AT LEAST 15066. Even at the bottom of that
  bracket the boundary is 81% of the corpus's row lines.
- WHAT THE CENSUS MEASURES (the same tool, `tools/re/mov_byx_gate.py`, new
  section 5; output `/tmp/opencode/pr116_census.txt`, whose sections 1-4 are
  byte-identical to the PR-115 output apart from the new blank separator).
  Of the 18617 row lines, counted on the thresholds the port's parser
  STORES (the M4-C clamp plus the block's `time_scale`, applied only at and
  after the line): 15317 are an exact positive multiple of 100, in 2012
  states. By mode: BY_TIME 15142 of 17011 (156 of them are what an authored
  0 became through the clamp), 1934 states whose MINIMUM stored threshold is
  on that boundary, in 754 files; BY_X 67 of 1349, 66 states, 59 files;
  BY_TY 108 of 108, 12 states, 7 files; BY_Y 0 of 149. Reconciled against
  the quoted PR-110 figures over the same files: its own reading
  (`pr110_thresholds()`, every row scaled, no clamp) gives 15164 multiples
  of 100 of 18617 rows, so the two readings differ by 203 rows out of
  15000+ and the same direction; its "13932 of the 14881" is that count
  taken over its own BY_TIME subset, which is a different mode attribution
  than the tool's (the tool counts 17011 BY_TIME rows). At any of these rows
  a feed of 100 lands the accumulator exactly on the threshold, so the
  engine's step returns and fires the row ONE FEED LATER, 100 iterations
  later, with a remainder of 100 where the port fires now with a remainder
  of 0. The quoted note called this "not hypothetical"; it is 82% of the
  corpus's rows. With the rows whose text carries a `WAIT` token kept out,
  as the keyed-branch candidates, the same count is 15066 at the bottom of
  the bracket and 15317 at the top.
- THE MUTATIONS, i.e. what the port's choice currently covers
  (`/tmp/opencode/mut/run116.sh`, output `/tmp/opencode/mut/run116.out`;
  each run prints the diff it applied and builds with 0 warnings; M0 is the
  control, the same pass with no patch at all, and finds nothing anywhere).
  G1 flips the player's gate `>=` -> `>` (ll_play.c:1286, one compare, so
  both feeds at once): 41 play-selftest failures from 14 distinct legs,
  including the `100u * t - closed` exact-carry loop at :2402 and :2420 and
  the `broke`/wrap legs at :2322-2323 and :2407 - the object chain is
  untouched (0). G2a flips only the object's time half (`: o->row_t <
  f->thresh` -> `<=`, ll_level.c:1231): 2 legs, "the first iteration did not
  close exactly one row (state 0 frame 0 t 100)" (ll_level.c:1761, PR-110's
  leg) and `obj_motion`'s "cross-state return: x 105 state 1 frame 0 (want
  105 back in A_RUN row 1: A_HIT's 100-unit row is exactly one iteration)"
  (:2407, PR-115's). G12 (both) is the union. G2b flips only the object's
  WALKING half (`o->facc <` -> `<=`) and NOTHING catches it: no leg of this
  repo puts a distance-fed accumulator exactly on a threshold. That is the
  one gap this PR found in its own fixtures, and it is item 2 below.
- NOT CHANGED, AND WHY. The port keeps `>=` on both sides. Nothing here is
  game data or a captured frame, and PR-110's closing clause still holds: no
  clip in the repo separates the two rules. The difference is now measured
  rather than guessed, and the decision has a number on it: moving to
  strict-greater would shift 15066-15317 authored rows by one whole feed
  of 100 iterations, and it is not a bug fix but an engine-alignment choice,
  so it is listed as item 1. No real-Windows probe was run (ADAM-HANDHELD is
  asleep and WOL does not answer); the T5 clip and the section-7 item-5 menu
  capture are the ones the night prompt says to skip.
- OPEN ITEMS (PR-116 1-5). (1) Whether to move the port's gates to the
  engine's strict rule, now that the reading is settled: 15066-15317 rows in
  2012 states would fire one feed later, 41 play legs plus the 2 object legs
  above currently pin the opposite rule, and the only evidence for the
  current rule is that it was the coherent-looking one when the flag
  direction was thought to be ambiguous. (2) A leg that puts a
  distance-fed accumulator exactly on a threshold: G2b is a survivor. (3) Do
  the 251 `WAIT`-carrying row lines build keyed ROW nodes (which would skip
  the compare entirely and be driven by 0x47e40 instead), or does 0x46b62
  register a separate event node? The vtable it stores is 0xa11c8 and the
  register call is 0x47d60; neither has been read. It decides whether the
  real boundary population is 15317 or 15066, and it is the first time this
  corpus shows a row form that does not go through the threshold. (4) What
  the handler does with the remainder it is handed at 0x52338 - the engine
  pays a row `acc - thresh` ticks at the moment it runs, and under the
  strict rule that value is a whole feed at a boundary row and not 0; this
  is the same clock question as PR-115's rows-per-step, with the boundary
  value attached. (5) The three zeroes: 0x5236b sits in 0x52360, which is
  vtable slot +0x1c in 4 of the 16 class tables and is also called directly
  at 0x4ff6b and 0x50003; 0x533b0 is in 0x532c0 and 0x5389e in 0x53850.
  Which events reset an accumulator mid-state, and whether any authored
  level relies on it, is unread.

## PR-117 — a distance-fed accumulator EXACTLY on a threshold is now a
tested case: leg 8 of `obj_motion_selftest` closes PR-116's open item 2 and
its G2b mutation is caught

- WHAT THIS PR DOES. One test-only leg (leg 8 of `obj_motion_selftest`)
  plus its summary string. No behaviour change: not one logic line of
  ported/ was touched, only a test and comments. It closes PR-116's open
  item 2, quoted verbatim (NEXT_STEPS.md:9455-9456): "(2) A leg that
  puts a distance-fed accumulator exactly on a threshold: G2b is a
  survivor." PR-116 had found that gap by mutation, not by
  inspection, and this PR is the fixture it asked for.
- THE LEG AND ITS ARITHMETIC. Fixture `[A_RUN] control=BY_X / F=100,0`
  with ONE row `1,100` - a walking state whose rows are fed by travelled
  distance, and a threshold of exactly one row's worth of units.
  `obj_walk` feeds `dist = |fx| * dt_ms / 4000.0` into `facc` and `xa`
  (ll_level.c:1101-1104), so:
  - call 1, dt = 2000: `dist` = 100 * 2000 / 4000 = 50.0. `facc` 50.0 is
    below the 100 threshold, so no row closes; the walk moves the object
    50 px (x 20 -> 70); and `row_t` / `row_rem` stay exactly 0, because
    `walk0` at :1169-1181 keeps a walking state away from
    `obj_row_tick` - the "one accumulator, one source" rule, now pinned
    from the other side.
  - call 2, dt = 2000: `facc` is EXACTLY 100.0, the stored threshold -
    `100 * 2000` and `/ 4000.0` are both exact in binary64, so this is a
    real equality and not a near miss. The port's rule closes the row,
    `facc` lands on 0.0, the end-of-list branch wraps `fi` back to 0 and
    skips the anchor snap (:1212 asks for the mode bit and the state is a
    walking one), so x reaches 120. Hand-derived, no game data, no frame.
- THE MUTATION, BEFORE AND AFTER (/tmp/opencode/mut/run117.sh, output
  /tmp/opencode/mut/run117.out). H0 is the control - the new tree with no
  patch: 0 build warnings, play rc=0 with 0 failures, mov rc=0 with 0
  failures. Then G2b, the same program PR-116 used
  (/tmp/opencode/mut/prog/g2b.py), which turns ll_level.c:1230
  `walk ? o->facc < (double)f->thresh` into `<=`. PR-116 recorded that
  this broke nothing anywhere; it now fails exactly one leg, the new one:
  "motion selftest: FAILED at exact equality: fi 0 facc 100 x 120 row_t
  0". The printed values are the mutant's and they say what the flip
  does: the row never closes, so `facc` is left sitting at 100.0, while
  x still reaches 120 because `obj_walk` moves the object independently of
  this gate. Nothing else changes - play rc=0 with 0 failures and every
  earlier object leg still passes.
- THE PLAYER SIDE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. /tmp/opencode/mut/prog/eq_player
  .py inserts one print at the loop-entry boundary of the player's row
  loop (ll_play.c:1286) that fires on `walk && p->facc == (double)thresh`.
  Built with 0 warnings; `./ll_level --play-selftest` rc=0, 0 failures,
  and 0 EQDIAG lines - no play leg of this repo lands a distance-fed
  accumulator on a threshold either. The obstacle is arithmetic, not
  fixture design: that feed is `p->vx * dt` with `dt = (double)dt_ms /
  1000.0` (ll_play.c:913, :1100, :1119), and 0.028 is not representable
  in binary64, so the shipped iteration step cannot hand an integer
  threshold exactly. A `dt_ms` of 1000 makes `dt` exactly 1.0, and then
  F=100 feeds exactly 100.0 in one step - that is arithmetic on the
  port's own code, not a test, and it is item 1.
- WHAT THIS PR DOES NOT CLAIM. That the engine fires at `facc == thresh`
  on a distance feed is not new evidence. PR-116 read the compare at
  0x52320-0x5232b, and that is the same code for every row whatever fed
  the accumulator: the feed is chosen by mode at the dispatcher 0x543a0,
  mode 0 writing [obj+0xa1] at 0x543d1. So the engine would keep the
  accumulator at this boundary and run the row one feed later - an
  inference from two verified readings, labelled as one, and still the
  owner's decision (PR-116 item 1). What a test can do is pin which side
  the PORT is on, and now the distance-fed side of it is pinned too.
- GATES (the same set as any ported/ change, since a test is code):
  `make` and `make win` rc=0, `make ll_level` 0 warnings,
  `./ll_level --play-selftest` and `--mov-selftest` rc=0 with 0 failures -
  the mov chain reaches leg 8, `obj_motion_selftest` is in it at :2981 -
  and both `make -k verify-all` passes, with the fixtures and
  fixture-free, EXIT=0 with the 23 named SKIP lines unchanged. The record
  of the runs is in the commit message and /tmp/opencode/pr117_gates.txt.
- OPEN ITEMS (PR-117 1-2). (1) A player-side leg for the same boundary.
  The probe says the case is untested there; its feed's arithmetic is why
  it is unreachable on the shipped 28 ms step; a leg would need a dyadic
  `dt_ms` (1000 is enough) and the play rig, and since that gate is ONE
  compare for both feeds any flip of it is already caught 41 ways by
  PR-116's G1 - so the value is in pinning the distance path itself, not
  the compare. (2) PR-116's items 1, 3, 4 and 5 are untouched and still
  stand: the strict-greater flip is an owner decision with a number on it
  (15066-15317 rows), the 251 `WAIT`-carrying row lines' node type is
  unread, what the row handler does with the remainder it is handed is
  unread, and which events run the three accumulator zeroes is unread.

## PR-118 — the boundary population re-measured for the DISTANCE-fed half:
the 100-unit divisor in the PR-116 census does not apply to a walking state,
and section 6 of the census tool says what does

- WHAT THIS PR IS. One new section (6) in `tools/re/mov_byx_gate.py`, plus
  this record and the two correction bullets in HANDOFF.md. No behaviour
  change: nothing under ported/ and no Makefile line is touched, and the
  only code in the commit is the census script, which no build or test
  leg runs. It came out of PR-117: that leg had to INVENT an `F=100,0` /
  `1,100` / `dt=2000` fixture to put a distance-fed accumulator exactly on a
  threshold, which raises the obvious question of whether any real authored
  row can land there, and on which of the grids this port really uses. The
  answer is measured now, and it corrects how PR-116's boundary figure
  should be read - so it goes in as a new record with the old wording
  quoted, exactly as PR-116 and PR-117 did it.
- WHAT IT MEASURES. `tools/re/mov_byx_gate.py` section 6, output
  `/tmp/opencode/pr118_census.txt` (275 lines; its sections 1-5 are
  BYTE-IDENTICAL to `/tmp/opencode/pr116_census.txt`, verified by diff).
  The walking states are selected by the port's own rule, the `walk`
  expression at ll_level.c:1169 (a `BY_X` token AND a non-zero first `F=`),
  not by the engine's mode word: 75 states, 992 rows, 57 files. Their
  stored thresholds are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 10 units. How many of them
  are an exact positive multiple of 100, the test section 5 uses:
  "0 of 992 rows, in 57 files".
- THE FEED, PER GRID. `obj_walk` feeds `dist = |fx| * dt_ms / 4000.0`
  (ll_level.c:1101-1104), and outside a selftest `obj_advance` is called
  with three dt values only: 20 ms (:6425, the play/PPM legs), 40 ms
  (:6432) and a measured frame dt (:6618); `LL_ITER_MS` = 28 is the grid
  every selftest uses. Section 6 asks, per walking state and grid, whether
  ANY whole number of identical calls lands a stored threshold exactly, in
  exact arithmetic (`fractions.Fraction`, k * |F| * dt / 4000 == t), and
  separately whether the port's own double accumulator reaches it by adding
  dt's rounded feed step by step. The measured result, as printed:
  - dt=20: 713 of 992 rows in 60 of 75 states reachable; the port's
    accumulator reaches it in 58 states, and in 2 states the two answers
    DISAGREE.
  - dt=40: 689 rows / 58 states; 56 states; the same 2 states disagree.
  - dt=28: 0 rows / 0 states, and no disagreement.
  - dt=2000 (PR-117's invented dt): 0 rows / 0 states.
- WHY 28 ms LANDS ON NOTHING, exactly. The per-call feed is
  `7|F| / 1000`, so landing an integer threshold t in k identical calls
  needs `k * 7|F| = 1000t`: the reachable t are exactly the multiples of
  `7|F| / gcd(7|F|, 1000)`. Section 6 prints that first-reachable value
  next to each group's actual threshold histogram, and the two never
  coincide: for the 48 states at |F|=100 (562 rows) only multiples of 7 are
  reachable, and those states author 2, 4, 6, 9 and 10 - never 7 or 14.
  Note that this is a coincidence failure, not an impossibility: a state at
  |F|=100 WOULD land a 7-unit row in exactly 10 calls. No such row is
  written anywhere in this corpus, so the column is zero.
- WHY 20 ms LANDS ON 713 OF THEM. At dt=20 the feed is `|F| / 200`, and
  |F|=100 - the largest group, 48 states and 562 rows - feeds exactly 1.0
  per call, so every integer threshold is a whole number of calls. That is
  the grid the play and PPM legs run on. So the distance-fed rows are not
  outside PR-116's boundary question; they have one, at a different divisor,
  and section 5's multiple-of-100 count does not include a single one of
  them.
- THE ACCUMULATOR ITSELF DRIFTS, in 2 states. Both are in
  `LONA.05_LEW.LON_LEW.MOV`: |F|=30 at dt=20 feeds 0.15 and a 3-unit row
  needs k = 20 calls. `20 * 0.15` is 3 exactly, but the port adds the
  rounded feed repeatedly: its accumulator holds 2.9999999999999991 after
  20 additions and crosses the threshold only on call 21, then hands
  itself a remainder of 0.14999999999999902 instead of 0. Verified in
  compiled C, not only in python: `/tmp/opencode/pr118/acc.c` mirrors
  obj_walk's feed line and the walking half of the row gate with the same
  expressions, built `-O2 -std=gnu11 -Wall -Wextra`, output
  `/tmp/opencode/pr118/acc.out`. The engine's accumulator is an integer
  dword (0x543d1 `add [obj+0xa1], eax`), so it cannot drift at all; what
  it drifts against here is not the engine but exact arithmetic - at that
  row the port fires one call LATER than its own documented feed law
  says. Nothing in either selftest chain tests it (the selftests run the
  28 ms grid, where no distance-fed row reaches a threshold at all), so
  it is a tested-behaviour gap, recorded as open item 1, and this PR did
  not add the leg.
- WHAT THIS DOES TO THE PR-116 FIGURES, stated precisely. Their arithmetic
  is right and their buckets are the ENGINE's modes (`word & 7`). The BY_X
  line, quoted verbatim (NEXT_STEPS.md:9409):
  "BY_X 67 of 1349, 66 states, 59 files"
  counts states whose control word reads mode 0, and the port
  distance-feeds only 75 of the 172 states in that bucket. The 67 rows
  that line counts are time-fed ones, so a feed of 100 does land them
  exactly and the sentence holds for them. What the wording does not
  support is reading the figure as the whole boundary
  population: the same record, at NEXT_STEPS.md:9445, states that a
  "strict-greater would shift 15066-15317 authored rows by one whole feed
  of 100 iterations" - that holds for the time-fed rows, whose feed IS the
  level's 100 per iteration. A distance-fed row's feed is its
  own per-call distance, never that 100. On the 20 ms grid 713 of the
  992 distance-fed rows sit on
  the same `cmp`/`jge` boundary PR-116 read at 0x52329-0x52334 - so the
  honest count of what a strict-greater flip would move is the 15066-15317
  figure PLUS a distance-fed population that depends on the caller's dt,
  not that figure alone. PR-116's own numbers are unchanged by this and no
  shipped record is edited; HANDOFF section 6 and its section-7 item-13
  bullet carry the qualification with the old wording quoted.
- OPEN ITEMS (PR-118 1-2). (1) A leg that pins the drift case: a walking
  fixture at an |F| whose dt=20 feed is NOT dyadic (30 -> 0.15) against a
  3-unit row, asserting the port's actual 21-call landing and the non-zero
  remainder. It would be the first leg to distinguish "the port follows its
  own feed law exactly" from "the port's accumulator drifts", and the
  existing `obj_motion_selftest` rig has everything it needs. (2) The
  measured 20 ms figure is for identical repeated calls. `ll_level.c:6618`
  passes a real frame dt, which varies; what a varying dt does to the same
  boundary (how often a landing is hit at all) is not measured, and the
  engine's own per-frame feed value in [obj+0xca] is still unread - so the
  engine-side count of distance-fed boundary rows cannot be given yet.
- GATES. `tools/` is touched, so the full set was run, transcript
  `/tmp/opencode/pr118_gates.txt`: `make` rc=0 with 0 warnings; `make win`
  rc=0 with 0 warnings; `make ll_level` rc=0 with 0 warnings;
  `./ll_level --play-selftest` rc=0 with 0 failures
  (`/tmp/opencode/pr118_play.txt`); `./ll_level --mov-selftest` rc=0 with
  0 failures (`/tmp/opencode/pr118_mov.txt`); `make -k verify-all
  DATA=/tmp/opencode/iso_stage/LEO HD=/tmp/opencode/hd_files` EXIT=0
  "ALL TESTS PASSED (linux + windows + llrs)"
  (`/tmp/opencode/pr118_verify_all.txt`) and the fixture-free
  `DATA=/tmp/opencode/nope HD=/tmp/opencode/nope` EXIT=0 with the same
  line (`/tmp/opencode/pr118_verify_none.txt`), whose 23 named SKIP lines
  are set-identical to the PR-110/111/112/114/115/116/117 baseline
  `/tmp/opencode/va_nope.log` (diff of the sorted SKIP lines: empty). The
  builds necessarily did not change between the PR-117 tree and this one

  final tree reproduced `/tmp/opencode/pr118_census.txt` byte-for-byte
  (`cmp` with the run before the docs edits), with sections 1-5 still
  byte-identical to `/tmp/opencode/pr116_census.txt`. No mutation runs:

## PR-119 — the accumulator drift PR-118 found is now tested: leg 9 of
`obj_motion_selftest` pins a distance-fed row landing ONE CALL LATE, with
the drift carried forward as its remainder

- WHAT THIS PR IS. One test-only leg, number 9, in `obj_motion_selftest`
  (`ported/ll_level.c`), plus the summary clause that names it. No
  behaviour change: not one logic line of the port is touched. It closes
  PR-118 open item 1, quoted verbatim (NEXT_STEPS.md:9648):
  "A leg that pins the drift case: a walking fixture at an |F| whose dt=20
  feed is NOT dyadic (30 -> 0.15) against a 3-unit row, asserting the
  port's actual 21-call landing and the non-zero remainder."
- THE FIXTURE, no game data and no window: `A_RUN`, `[A_RUN]` with
  `control=BY_X` and `F=30,0`, one row line `1,3`. Then 20 calls of
  `obj_advance(&e, 20)` and a 21st. The numbers are the ones PR-118
  measured in the corpus: the walk feed at :1101 is `|fx| * dt_ms /
  4000.0`, so a 20 ms call at F=30 feeds exactly 0.15 units and a 3-unit
  row needs exactly 20 calls - and 0.15 is not dyadic, which is what
  makes the accumulator drift at all. `dt=20` is not invented: it is the
  grid the play and PPM legs call `obj_advance` with (:6425).
- WHAT IS NOW PINNED, as the leg asserts it. After 20 calls the row has
  NOT run (`fi == 0`) and `facc` is 2.9999999999999991 - the leg checks
  `2.99 < facc < 3.0`, so an accumulator that held exact steps fails
  right there. The row closes on call 21, and the subtract at :1233 is
  left a remainder of 0.14999999999999902, which the leg checks as
  `0.14 < facc < 0.15`: never the 0.15 an exact feed would carry, never
  the 0.0 of a loop that drops the remainder. Those two values are the
  ones PR-118 derived by hand and confirmed in compiled C
  (`/tmp/opencode/pr118/acc.c`); the leg reproduces them exactly, so
  what was arithmetic in a census is now tested behaviour.
- A SECOND MECHANISM, FOUND BY WRITING THE LEG: by call 20 the object has
  already MOVED the whole three units (`x` 20 -> 23) while the row that
  needs three units has not run. `obj_walk` adds the same `dist` to two
  accumulators (:1103-1104), and only `xa` has its whole part taken away
  (:1105-1107) - and that subtraction re-draws the rounding at every
  pixel boundary. On that very call the position residual reached
  1.0000000000000002 and paid out its third whole pixel (leaving
  2.2204460492503131e-16 in `xa`) in the same step where `facc` came out
  at 2.9999999999999991: the same value added to two variables, landing
  on opposite sides of a whole unit. The leg asserts `x == 23` at both
  checks, so the divergence is pinned and not just described, and it is
  mirrored outside the test as well: `/tmp/opencode/pr119/xa.c` reproduces
  obj_walk's two lines with the same build flags and prints both
  accumulators at every call (`/tmp/opencode/pr119/xa.out`) - at call 19
  `x` is 22 with `xa` at 0.8500000000000002 and `facc` at
  2.8499999999999992, at call 20 `xa` reaches 1.0000000000000002, pays
  its third whole pixel and leaves 2.2204460492503131e-16 while `facc`
  comes out at 2.9999999999999991.
- MUTATIONS (/tmp/opencode/mut/run119.sh, transcript
  /tmp/opencode/pr119b_mut.txt): H0, the tree with no patch, clean. NOREM
  (carrying no remainder, `o->facc = 0.0` at :1233) fails ONLY leg 9's
  second check. EXACTF (the feed quantised to exact thousandths, an
  engine-like integer accumulator) lands on 3.0 at call 20 and fails ONLY
  leg 9's FIRST check. G2B (:1230 `<` -> `<=`, the PR-116/117 flip)
  fails only leg 8 and leaves leg 9 clean, which is the control that
  shows this leg is not a second copy of the PR-117 one: adding equality
  to the break condition changes nothing when the accumulator is already
  under the threshold, and at call 20 it is. `--play-selftest` reported
  0 failures under every one of those patches.
- WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE. Whether the ENGINE lands that row at call 20
  or 21 is still unknown: its accumulator is an integer dword (0x543d1
  `add [obj+0xa1], eax`) and cannot drift, but what it adds per frame is
  `[obj+0xca]`, still unread, so this leg pins the port against its own
  documented feed law and makes no claim about the engine. PR-118 open
  item 2 (a varying frame dt at :6618, and that unread `[obj+0xca]`) is
  unchanged by this PR, and PR-116 item 1, the strict-greater flip, stays
  the owner's decision. A new open item follows from the second
  mechanism above: nothing states which of the two accumulators the
  engine keeps for a walking state, so a case that would separate them
  (a state whose row threshold is not a whole number of pixels) is
  recorded as PR-119 item 1.
- OPEN ITEMS (PR-119 1-2). (1) Which of the two accumulators the ENGINE
  keeps for a walking state. The port has two (`facc` for the row gate,
  `xa` for whole pixels) and leg 9 shows they can disagree by a call at
  the same threshold; the engine's `[obj+0xa1]` is the one its row gate
  reads (0x52323) and PR-116 saw it added at 0x543d1, but whether that
  dword is the pixel counter's own accumulator or a separate one is not
  established - so no leg can yet separate "the engine lands that row at
  call 20" from "the engine lands it at call 21 too". What would
  establish it is a reading job at 0x543a0/0x543d1, not a capture:
  whether the dword that `add` feeds is the same field the engine's pixel
  advance truncates whole pixels out of, or a second one. The port's
  two-variable shape (one value, two accumulators, one of them truncated
  at every unit boundary) is the part with no source-side answer.
  (2) Carried from PR-118 item 2, unchanged by this PR: the measured
  boundary figures are for identical repeated calls, while
  `ll_level.c:6618` passes a real frame `dt`, and the value the engine
  adds per frame in `[obj+0xca]` is still unread.
- GATES. `ported/` is touched, so the full set was run on the exact bytes
  of this commit; transcript `/tmp/opencode/pr119b_gates.txt`, which

  "ALL TESTS PASSED (linux + windows + llrs)"
  (`/tmp/opencode/pr119b_verify_all.txt`) and the fixture-free

## PR-120 — the row gate's accumulator, read at byte level: it is its OWN
field, fed a value whose sub-pixel part is dropped at the divide, and the
port's fractional feed is now the one thing that separates it from the
engine

- WHAT THIS PR IS. A reading, with one mutation run against the shipped
  bytes as evidence. No code, no `Makefile`, no `tools/` change: nothing
  in the port moves. It answers PR-119 open item 1, quoted verbatim
  (NEXT_STEPS.md:9751):
  What would establish it is a reading job at 0x543a0/0x543d1, not a
  capture: whether the dword that `add` feeds is the same field the
  engine's pixel advance truncates whole pixels out of, or a second one.
- THE ANSWER: A THIRD FIELD, AND THE ROW GATE IS ITS ONLY CONSUMER. An
  indexed scan of the disassembled image over the object-code range
  0x52000..0x54fff lists every site naming `+0xa1` (transcript
  /tmp/opencode/pr120_dis.txt, every row `suspect=0`, and the ones that
  matter re-read with `leodb.py dis`, which disassembles the exact bytes
  and never trusts the index): the four feed sites 0x543d1 / 0x543e7 /
  0x54412 / 0x5443b that PR-116 listed, the set at 0x52118, the zeroes
  at 0x5236b / 0x533b0 / 0x5389e, the two loads the mode-2 and mode-3
  branches make at 0x54400 / 0x54429, and ONE read outside the feed
  branches: 0x52323, the load behind the compare PR-116 read at 0x52329
  (`39 d8 cmp eax,ebx`). So the answer to the
  quoted question is NEITHER of its two options: `[obj+0xa1]` is not a
  pixel counter and not the same field read twice - it is a counter whose
  only consumer anywhere is the row gate. Two notes on the method,
  worth keeping:
  the mode-2/3 branches write it through a register offset
  (`0x5440c: add ebx,0xa1` then `0x54414: mov [ebx],edi`, and the twin
  at 0x54435/0x5443d), which a scan for the literal text `+0xa1]` does
  not find; and the byte-level scan finds nothing in the position code,
  so PR-99 item 10's finding stands, quoted verbatim: "The position
  writer is still unread". What this reading adds is the site list:
  `[obj+0xca]` is READ at 0x5412c, 0x543c6, 0x54810 and 0x54836, its
  address is taken at 0x54830 (`lea`), and it is zeroed at 0x54e56; the
  0x54810/0x54830/0x54836 group is unread and is where to look next.
- WHAT THE FEED ACTUALLY ADDS, AND WHERE THE RESIDUE GOES. 0x543a0 is
  the mode dispatcher (0x543a6..0x543be reads `[obj+0x5c]`, the state
  list at `[obj+0x50]`, and `[state+0x12] & 7`, five-way jump table at
  0x54380). Mode 0, 0x543c6..0x543d1: `mov eax,[ebx+0xca]`, then
  `99` / `31 d0` / `29 d0` - cdq, xor, sub, the branchless absolute
  value - then `01 83 a1 00 00 00 add [ebx+0xa1],eax`; mode 1 the same
  shape on `[obj+0xce]` at 0x543dc..0x543e7. The value it adds is made
  a few instructions earlier in the same function that updates the
  velocity: 0x5434d `mov edx,[ecx+0xc2]`, 0x54353 `mov ebx,0x64`,
  0x54358/0x5435a/0x5435d the signed `idiv` by 100, 0x54365
  `mov [ecx+0xca],eax`, with the y twin at 0x5436b..0x54372. NEW, and
  it is the part nobody had written down: **the remainder is thrown away
  at the divide** - 0x5435f `mov edx,[ecx+0xc6]` overwrites `edx`
  before the x remainder could be stored, and the y remainder dies at
  the epilogue (0x54378 `pop ebp`). So the engine's accumulator is a
  SUM OF TRUNCATED STEPS, which is at most the distance travelled, not a
  truncated total of it - a difference that only shows up across a
  multi-row walk, and one that no port-side leg can see because the port
  never truncates.
- WHAT THAT BOUNDS, QUOTING PR-118'S OWN WORDING. Its section 6 derives
  the port's boundary law and its reachability claim, quoted verbatim
  (NEXT_STEPS.md:9595):
  "needs `k * 7|F| = 1000t`: the reachable t are exactly the multiples
  of `7|F| / gcd(7|F|, 1000)`"
  That law is the PORT'S feed, which is fractional. On the engine's
  feed the per-step amount is an integer q = trunc(|v_x|/100), so the
  thresholds reachable there are the multiples of q - and q = 0 is the
  case PR-99 item 9 already recorded ("a walk under 1 px/tick advances
  the frame list by nothing"). So the 713-at-dt=20 and 689-at-dt=40
  figures count the PORT's boundaries; turning them into engine figures
  needs q for each authored state, i.e. the `.MOV` `F=` to v_x
  relation, which is the half PR-118 left open, in its own words:
  the value the engine adds per frame in `[obj+0xca]` is still unread.
- PR-99 ITEM 9'S TEST, WHICH NOW EXISTS. Its closing sentence, quoted
  verbatim:
  That quantization is visible at low speeds and is worth a test of its
  own.
  It does now, as a mutation run against the shipped bytes:
  `prog/quant.py` replaces the walk feed with `o->facc +=
  (double)(int)dist`, which is the engine's `trunc(|v_x|/100)` shape at
  0x5434d..0x54365. Against `ported/ll_level.c` at sha256
  c3956398b6cc51f... (the bytes of PR-119), transcript
  /tmp/opencode/pr120_quant.txt: build rc=0 with 0 warnings,
  `--play-selftest` 0 failures, `--mov-selftest` exactly ONE failure -
  leg 9's first check, `facc 0` instead of 2.9999999999999991, because
  the 0.15 that fixture feeds per call truncates to 0 and the row never
  closes. Leg 8 passes under it: its fixture's step is `100*2000/4000` =
  50, a whole number, so truncation cannot touch it. So the port's
  fractional feed - the difference the code comment at :1073-1077 calls
  deliberate - is pinned by a leg, and no other leg in either chain
  notices the difference.
- OPEN ITEMS (PR-120 1-2). (1) The position writer, which PR-99 item 10
  named and this record narrows to 0x54810/0x54830/0x54836: what consumes
  `[obj+0xca]`, and whether the object's own coordinates are advanced by
  that truncated dword or by a path that keeps the hundredths. (2) The
  `.MOV` `F=` to v_x relation, needed to compute q per authored state
  and therefore to give any engine-side count of distance-fed boundary
  rows; carried from PR-118 item 2, unchanged by this reading.
- GATES. No code, no `Makefile`, no `tools/` or `.gitignore` line is in
  this commit, so the prompt's build gates do not apply and no build was
  run for it. What was run: the QUANT mutation above, against the bytes
  PR-119 shipped (`c3956398b6cc51f...`), after which `git status`
  reports `ported/` clean - the source is back byte-for-byte. The
  disassembly evidence is in /tmp/opencode/pr120_dis.txt: the source
  image's sha256, the indexed scan with its `suspect` flags, and the
  exact-byte `dis` of 0x543a0+0xa0 and 0x5434d+0x30. `leo.sqlite` is
  the derived index under /tmp, rebuilt in that session; nothing under
  git changed by it. No game data and no captured frame in this commit.


## PR-121 — the position writer, found: it adds the SAME truncated dword
PR-120 read and then clears it, so the engine's coordinates quantise the
way its row gate does

- WHAT THIS PR IS. A reading only: no `ported/`, no `Makefile`, no
  `tools/` line, nothing in the port moves. It closes PR-120 open item 1,
  quoted verbatim:
  "what consumes `[obj+0xca]`, and whether the object's own coordinates are
  advanced by that truncated dword or by a path that keeps the hundredths."
  and it answers PR-99 item 10, quoted verbatim:
  "0x54250 stores only `v/100` into +0xca/+0xce, and nothing read here uses
  the hundredths value for the position. The position writer is still unread
  - probably the same ground/terrain code that writes [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe]."
  All addresses below were read with `leodb.py dis`, which decodes the
  exact bytes; the transcript is /tmp/opencode/pr121_dis.txt (source
  image sha256, the `dis` of 0x547c0+0x40 and 0x54800+0x58).
- THE WRITER. 0x54804 `mov eax,[esi+0xce]` (the y delta), 0x5480a
  `mov ecx,[esi+0xea]` (a second y amount), 0x54810 `mov edx,[esi+0xca]`
  (the x delta, the field PR-120 read), 0x54816/0x54818 `mov edi,[esi]`
  and `mov ebp,[esi+0x4]` (the current pair), 0x5481b zeroes `[obj+0xea]`
  immediately after reading it, then 0x54825 `add eax,ecx`, 0x54827
  `add edi,edx`, 0x54829 `add ebp,eax`, and 0x5482b/0x5482d write them
  back: `mov [esi],edi`, `mov [esi+0x4],ebp`. The delta fields are then
  consumed in place: 0x54830 `lea eax,[esi+0xca]` + 0x54836
  `mov edx,[esi+0xca]` + 0x5483c `sub [eax],edx`, and the y twin at
  0x5483e/0x54844/0x5484a. So the answer to the quoted question is the
  first branch: the coordinates ARE advanced by that truncated dword, and
  there is no path that carries the hundredths into the move.
- THE SAME FIELD, TWO DIFFERENT USES. The row gate's feed takes `abs()`
  of `[obj+0xca]` (PR-120, 0x543cc..0x543cf); this writer takes it
  SIGNED - 0x54810 loads it, 0x54827 adds it, with no `cdq`/`xor`/`sub`
  between, which is what lets the object move left. And PR-120's scan
  found one zero of `+0xca`, a `mov [edx+0xca],0` at 0x54e56; here it is
  cleared by a second idiom, a self-subtract through a register offset
  (0x54830 `lea` + 0x54836 `mov` + 0x5483c `sub [eax],edx`), which is
  why an ops-text search for a `+0xca],0x0` store never listed it.
- WHAT THAT SETTLES. PR-99 item 9's arithmetic, quoted in part:
  "so a walk under 1 px/tick advances the frame list by nothing, and on the
  s=10/20Hz arithmetic above the worm contributes 1 px per tick, not 1.25."
  That sentence was about the row accumulator; on the coordinates it is
  the same law. The arithmetic of the divide at 0x5435d (PR-120) makes
  100 hundredths one pixel, so a velocity of 125 hundredths moves the
  object exactly 1 whole pixel a tick and drops the other quarter pixel
  every tick, with no carry - and the proof there is no carry is the
  self-subtract at 0x5483c/0x5484a clearing the delta after the move.
  The port's position path does the opposite: it accumulates the same
  fraction in `xa` and takes whole pixels out of it as they arrive
  (:1104-1106), so its steady-state speed is the exact velocity while the
  engine's is that velocity truncated per tick. That is the largest
  port-vs-engine difference in this area, and it is not a drift question:
  it is a quantisation the port does not model. The code comment at
  :1073-1077 records the feed half of it and not the coordinate half, so
  no comment in the port currently states this.
- NOT SETTLED: WHAT `[obj+0x0]`/`[obj+0x4]` ARE. The use here is
  coordinate-shaped - a pair read at 0x54816/0x54818, advanced by two
  delta fields, stored back at 0x5482b/0x5482d. One alternative IS
  ruled out in this very function: its method table is `[obj+0x8]`, which
  0x547eb loads and 0x547fa calls at slot +0xb8, so this class does not
  keep a table at +0x0/+0x4. Two reasons not to over-read the rest:
  0x547c2 `mov ebx,[eax]` + 0x547c6 `call [ebx]` treats offset 0 of the
  LINKED object as its method table, so offset 0 is a table in some other
  class; and NEXT_STEPS.md:6871 records a `TLewTunga2` ctor writing a
  pair at `[obj+0x0]` while working out real field offsets, which shows
  offset 0 is data in that class but is not a coordinate reading. The
  pair's identity needs the draw-side confirmation, and until it exists
  nothing here should be built on it.
- WHERE THE ONE-SHOT Y AMOUNT COMES FROM. `[obj+0xea]` is read and
  zeroed in the same breath (0x5480a/0x5481b) and has no x counterpart.
  A whole-image scan of the disassembled ops names 7 sites: 0x4549a
  `cmp eax,[edi+0xea]`, 0x454a8 `mov [edi+0xea],eax`, 0x4cee3
  `lea eax,[ebp+0xea]`, 0x4cf15 `mov ebx,[ebp+0xea]`, and the three here
  (0x5480a/0x5481b, plus 0x550aa `mov [eax+0xea],0`). Exactly one stores
  a computed value: 0x454a8, whose `eax` is the return of the call at
  0x45491 to 0x455a0, reached only past two guards (0x45496/0x45498
  `test`/`jg` and 0x4549a/0x454a0 `cmp`/`jg`), so it stores that result
  only when it is <= 0 and <= what is already there - a keep-the-smaller
  rule. And the block does it in a pair: 0x454a2 `mov [edi+0xe6],esi`
  stores a LINK there, two instructions before the amount. That is the
  same `[obj+0xe6]` this function copies into `[obj+0xa9]` at 0x547bc and
  then calls through (0x547c2/0x547c6, that object's slot +0, with
  `edx` = this object), clearing `[obj+0xa9]` at 0x547f0. So the y amount
  and the link arrive together and are consumed once. Caveat on the site
  list: 0x4cee3 takes the field's ADDRESS, so a store through that
  register would not name `+0xea`, and that pair of sites is a different
  code region and unread.
- CONTROL FLOW OF THE WRITE. The index gives four transfer targets of
  0x54804 - 0x546b3 `jne`, 0x547cf `je`, 0x547d5 `jmp`, and the
  fall-through after 0x54800 `or BYTE PTR [edi+0x2],0x4` - so within
  this tail of the function the coordinate advance is unconditional; what
  the tests choose are the flag bytes ([edi+0x1] bit 0x20 at 0x547d1,
  [edi+0x2] bit 0x4 at 0x54800; `edi` is set earlier and not established
  here) and whether the linked-object handoff at 0x547d7..0x547fa runs,
  which is entered only from 0x54760 `je` (after 0x54759
  `cmp [obj+0xe6],0`) and 0x54779 `jge`. What gates the function itself
  is unread: the index has no function entry covering 0x54804 (its
  nearest, 0x54560, ends by 0x545f4), and entry-list rows are hints, not
  proofs, so no claim here depends on one.
- OPEN ITEMS (PR-121 1-3). (1) Confirm `[obj+0x0]`/`[obj+0x4]` as world
  coordinates from the draw side and find every other writer of that
  pair, since this is one of possibly several. (2) Read 0x45480..0x454b0
  and 0x455a0: what is the amount 0x455a0 returns, what the `[obj+0xe6]`
  link is, and whether `[obj+0xea]` is the port's missing one-shot
  vertical push. (3) What `[obj+0xe2]` selects - it is compared with 0
  here and with 2 at 0x54766 - and which classes reach this tail.
- GATES. Docs only: no `ported/`, `Makefile`, `tools/` or `.gitignore`
  line is in this commit, so the prompt's build gates do not apply to it
  and no build was run for it. The evidence is /tmp/opencode/pr121_dis.txt
  (image sha256 + exact-byte `dis`) and the indexed scans quoted above,
  run against /tmp/opencode/leo.sqlite, a derived index under /tmp that
  changes nothing under git. No game data, no captured frame, no
  .github/workflows change, every added line <= 79 columns.


## PR-122 — where the one-shot vertical amount comes from: 0x455a0 is a
signed gap to a two-point surface segment, and the block that stores it
into `[obj+0xea]` is also the block that stores the `[obj+0xe6]` link

- WHAT THIS PR IS. A reading, no code, no behaviour. It closes PR-121
  open item 2, quoted verbatim:
  "Read 0x45480..0x454b0 and 0x455a0: what is the amount 0x455a0 returns, what
  the `[obj+0xe6]` link is, and whether `[obj+0xea]` is the port's missing
  one-shot vertical push."
  The addresses are all from `leodb.py dis` on the exact bytes; the
  transcript is /tmp/opencode/pr122_dis.txt (source image sha256 plus the
  full `dis` of 0x455a0, 0x45400+0x40 and 0x4543c+0x78).
- 0x455a0 IS A LINE-VERSUS-POINT y DIFFERENCE, AND ITS REMAINDER IS
  DROPPED LIKE PR-120's. Twenty-one instructions, read in full: args
  `eax` = point P, `edx` = point Q, `ebx` = point R, each a pair
  (`[p]`, `[p+4]`). 0x455a7/0x455aa compute `Q.y - P.y`, 0x455b1/0x455b3
  `R.x - P.x`, 0x455b5 `imul`, 0x455bc/0x455c1 `Q.x - P.x`, 0x455be
  `sar 0x1f` + 0x455c3 `idiv` - a signed divide whose remainder lands in
  `edx` and is overwritten by 0x455c5 `mov edx,[ecx+0x4]`, exactly the
  pattern PR-120 found at 0x5435f - then 0x455cb/0x455cd add `P.y` and
  subtract `R.y`. So the return value is `P.y + trunc((R.x - P.x) *
  (Q.y - P.y) / (Q.x - P.x)) - R.y`: the signed vertical distance from
  R up to the line through P and Q, truncated. There is no guard for a
  zero denominator in those 21 instructions, so the caller is
  responsible for the two points differing in x - a reason 0x45380,
  unread, has to be read before this is relied on numerically.
- THE CALLER BUILDS P AND Q OUT OF 13-BYTE RECORDS. In 0x45400 (the
  entry-list index calls it FUN_00045400; that is a hint, not a proof):
  0x4540c/0x4540f/0x45412 read `BYTE [[arg1+0x4]+0xc]` masked to 0xff
  and 0x45417/0x45419 `cmp`/`jg` branch to the epilogue when that count is
  GREATER than `ecx` - so the index is bounded by it - and `[arg1+0x4]`
  is a table whose records are 13 bytes apart with a count byte at +0xc -
  which is what the four `imul ...,0xd` at 0x4543c, 0x45440, 0x45481 and
  0x45485 scale. 0x45481..0x4548f (clean decode): `edx = ecx*13`, `dec
  ecx`, `ecx = (ecx-1)*13`, `eax = [[esi+0x4]]`, `add edx,eax`,
  `add eax,ecx` - so Q = base + i*13 and P = base + (i-1)*13, adjacent
  records; 0x4548b `mov ebx,ebp` puts the third point in `ebx` (arg3,
  saved at 0x4540a), 0x45491 `call 0x455a0`. The record index itself
  comes from a virtual call on the second argument: 0x45434 `mov
  ebx,[edi+0x8]`, 0x45439 `call [ebx+0x6c]`, whose `edx` return is
  scaled the same way at 0x4543c. A first call at 0x45468 builds the
  same pair through stack slots (0x45443..0x45464) and its third point
  is not established by that decode.
- THE GUARDS AND THE TWO STORES. After the 0x45468 call: 0x4546d `mov
  edx,[esp+0x18]` - that function has exactly one stack parameter (its
  single epilogue 0x454c0..0x454c6 is `add esp,0x8`, three pops, `ret
  0x4`, and every reject above branches there), so 0x45477 `sub eax,edx`
  subtracts that parameter from the first result. 0x45471 `mov
  ebx,[edi+0xa9]`, 0x45479 `cmp esi,ebx` +
  0x4547b `je 0x45481` - so when `arg1` IS the object's current link the
  following test is skipped - otherwise 0x4547d/0x4547f `test`/`jl`
  rejects a negative result. After the 0x45491 call: 0x45496/0x45498
  `test`/`jg` rejects a positive gap, 0x4549a/0x454a0 `cmp
  eax,[edi+0xea]`/`jg` rejects a gap larger than the stored one, and only
  then 0x454a2 `mov [edi+0xe6],esi` and 0x454a8 `mov [edi+0xea],eax`.
  So the link and the amount are stored together, the amount is a
  non-positive gap that is the smallest seen, and the link is `arg1` -
  the object that owns the record table. With PR-121's tail (0x54804
  adds `[obj+0xea]` into the y delta, clears it, and calls the linked
  object through its slot +0 at 0x547c2/0x547c6) the two halves now join
  into one mechanism: a surface provider is attached, a one-shot
  downward-or-zero correction is computed against a two-point segment, and
  the next position update applies and clears it.
- WHAT THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR. Nothing here names terrain. The shape
  fits a surface polyline and PR-99 item 10 guessed exactly that, quoted
  in part:
  "The position writer is still unread - probably the same ground/terrain code
  that writes [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe]."
  but that is a shape match, not a reading: what `[arg1+0x4]`'s table
  is, which class answers slot +0x6c with a record index, and what
  0x45380 (0x45423) selects are all unread, and the only caller the
  index lists for 0x45400 is a hint (0x4536f). For the port the contrast
  is concrete and worth recording: it has no geometric y path at all -
  y is written from the row's authored `dy=` directive (:1238) and reset
  to the object's base y (:831, :927, :1001, :1214) - so a
  slope-following push has no counterpart in the port and none of the
  shipped legs could detect one.
- OPEN ITEMS (PR-122 1-3). (1) Read 0x45380 and the slot +0x6c provider:
  what the 13-byte records are and which class answers with an index.
  (2) Who calls 0x45400 with which three points, and what its one stack
  parameter (the dword subtracted at 0x45477) is. (3) Whether `[obj+0xea]`'s
  sign convention (gap, stored only when <= 0) matches the engine's y
  axis as PR-121 read it, which needs the `[obj+0x0]`/`[obj+0x4]`
  identity from PR-121 item 1 first.
- GATES. Docs only: no `ported/`, `Makefile`, `tools/` or `.gitignore`
  line, so the prompt's build gates do not apply and no build was run.
  Evidence: /tmp/opencode/pr122_dis.txt (image sha256, `dis` of 0x455a0
  in full, 0x45400+0x40, 0x4543c+0x78, and the caller lists with their
  entry-list disclaimer). The port-side line references are from
  `ported/ll_level.c` as shipped (the bytes of PR-119, sha256
  c3956398b6cc51f..., unchanged since). No game data, no captured frame,
  no .github/workflows change, every added line <= 79 columns.


## PR-123 — the segment lookup behind PR-122's gap function: 0x45380 is a
linear x-search over an x-sorted record table that returns the segment
index, and the port already asks the same question of its .PLT ground

- WHAT THIS PR IS. A reading, no code, no behaviour. It takes PR-122 open
  item 1, quoted verbatim:
  "Read 0x45380 and the slot +0x6c provider: what the 13-byte records are and
  which class answers with an index."
  and closes its first half. 0x45380 is read in full here; the slot +0x6c
  provider is still unread, so this item is PARTLY closed. A second half
  of the question - what the records ARE - gains evidence rather than an
  answer: the same query already exists in the port, in `ll_play.c`, for
  the `.PLT` ground polylines, and the shapes match point for point.
  Everything is `leodb.py dis` on the exact bytes (transcript
  /tmp/opencode/pr123_dis.txt, with the image sha256, `dis` of 0x45380,
  0x453d0+0x30 and 0x453ed+0x24) plus `grep -n` against the shipped
  `ported/ll_play.c`/`ll_play.h`/`ll_level.c`.
- 0x45380 IS THE INDEX LOOKUP, AND ITS FAILURE VALUE IS 0. Seven pushes
  in, 43 bytes: `eax` = the table owner, saved to `ecx` at 0x45384;
  `edx` = the x to find, saved to `esi` at 0x45386 and re-read from that
  pointer at 0x45391, 0x4539d and 0x453b6 (a pointer to x, not x). Three
  bail-outs go to the epilogue at 0x453c4, which returns `eax` = 0:
  0x45388 `cmp DWORD PTR [owner+0x8],0x0` (an empty table), 0x45393/
  0x45395 `cmp`/`jl` when x is BELOW `[base]`, and 0x4539f/0x453a1 `cmp`
  /`jg` when x is ABOVE the dword at `base + count*13` - which is NOT
  inside the records, so the table keeps a further dword at that address.
  Between them: 0x4538e `mov eax,[owner+0x4]` is the base and 0x45397
  `imul edx,DWORD PTR [ecx+0x8],0xd` scales a DWORD record count by 13,
  confirming the 13-byte stride PR-122 inferred from four `imul ...,0xd`;
  the x of a record is at +0, and the byte at +0xc of a record is used
  elsewhere (0x4540f reads one as a count, 0x4504f/0x45053/0x451be
  move them) so +0xc is a per-record byte, not padding.
- THE SCAN, AND WHY THE ANSWER IS NEVER 0. 0x453a3..0x453bb walk the
  records in stride-13 order (`mov edx,0x1` and `mov eax,0xd` at
  0x453a3/0x453a8, `add eax,0xd` + `inc edx` at 0x453af/0x453b2, and at
  0x453b8 `cmp x, [base + k*13]` with `jg 0x453af`): the loop stops at
  the FIRST record whose x is >= x, and 0x453bd returns that 1-based
  index. So the return value satisfies 1 <= i <= count-1, and index 0 is
  not a record but the "not found" answer - which is exactly how both of
  the callers that the index lists treat it (0x4542c/0x4542e `test`/`je`
  in 0x45400, and 0x453db/0x453dd the same shape below). That is also
  what makes the pair PR-122 read safe: `i` and `i-1` are always both
  real records, so the two points of the segment exist.
- WHAT THE BOUNDS DO, AND DO NOT, GUARANTEE. Reading the dword at
  `base + count*13` as the upper bound only makes sense if the table's
  records are ordered by x - that is consistent with the scan, which
  stops at the first record at or above x, and with an upper sentinel;
  nothing here proves the ordering, only that the code assumes it. And no
  zero-denominator guard exists anywhere in this chain: the bounds say
  x(record i-1) < x(record i) is NOT excluded, so records sharing an x
  would make 0x455a0's divide by zero. Not observed, not excluded.
- THE SIBLING, SIXTEEN BYTES DOWN, RETURNS THE GAP DIRECTLY.
  0x453d0/0x453d1/0x453d2 `push ebx`, `push ecx`, `mov ecx,eax` (the
  table owner again), 0x453d4 `mov ebx,edx` (the point), then 0x453d6
  `call 0x45380` - the same unit the index labels FUN_00045380+0x56 (the
  entry list ends that body at 0x453c4, a hint, so describe the region
  by its bytes). 0x453db/0x453dd `test`/`je 0x453f5`, and 0x453f5 returns
  `eax` = 0x7fffffff for no match; otherwise 0x453df/0x453e3 `imul ...,0xd`
  build base+i*13 and base+(i-1)*13 in `edx` and `eax`, 0x453e6 `mov
  ecx,[ecx+0x4]` re-reads the base, 0x453e9/0x453eb add it, and 0x453ed
  `call 0x455a0`, whose return value is passed straight back (0x453f2/
  0x453f3/0x453f4 two pops, `ret`). So two near-identical clients of one
  table: this one computes the gap and hands it to its caller, 0x45400
  stores it into `[obj+0xea]` beside the `[obj+0xe6]` link. The INT_MAX
  the no-match path returns is the same shape as the port's own
  `best = 0x7fffffff` initialiser in `ll_plt_surface_at` (:143) and
  `ll_plt_first_below` (:167) - a similarity, not a reading.
- THIS IS A MODULE, NOT ONE FUNCTION. A scan of the disassembled ops in
  0x40000..0x46000 finds 21 sites that scale an index by 13, the first
  at 0x45012 (`imul eax,edx,0xd`) and including 0x45293
  `imul esi,DWORD PTR [esi+0x8],0xd` - the owner-count idiom again - and
  0x452e0/0x452e3. Byte reads of the record +0xc slot cluster in the
  same range. So the x-sorted 13-byte record table is used across that
  region, and 0x45380 is its shared lookup.
- THE PORT ASKS THE SAME QUESTION, AND ONLY THE PLAYER GETS THE ANSWER.
  In `ported/ll_play.c` as shipped (sha256 e1a390ddea926a02...,
  `ll_play.h` 71b0fedbd73a3088...): `ll_plt_parse` (:34) reads `.PLT`
  polylines, which the header documents as world-coordinate ground lines
  with x right and y DOWN, feet on top (`ll_play.h:54`), parsed from the
  HD install's ETAPY block (`ll_play.h:10`); `seg_y_at` (:123) is the
  same interpolation as 0x455a0's first term - `pl->p[k].y + dy * (x -
  x1) / (x2 - x1)` in C, which truncates toward zero like the engine's
  `idiv`, and it gives vertical segments their own special case at :126
  because a zero denominator is not allowed - and `ll_plt_surface_at`
  (:140) and `ll_plt_first_below` (:164) both scan every polyline for a
  covering segment and return found/not-found with `best = 0x7fffffff` as
  their not-found marker. That is the same query as 0x45380 (x to
  segment) plus 0x455a0 (y gap to that segment) with the search written
  as a scan instead of an indexed lookup. Who consumes it: the player,
  every step, inside `ll_player_step` (:905) which takes the ground as a
  parameter and calls those two queries at :1149 and :1173; a scene
  object only at placement, in `obj_settle` (`ll_level.c:1693`), which
  snaps a `CHECK_LN` object's base y to the first line below it
  (:1700, :1705). After placement, nothing: the per-tick y of an object
  is the authored `dy=` (:1238) and base-y resets (:831, :927, :1001,
  :1214). So the port has this geometry for its player and a one-time
  snap for its objects, while the engine's block PR-122 read re-derives
  the gap for an object and hands a one-shot correction to its position
  writer.
- WHAT THIS IS STILL NOT EVIDENCE FOR. The record table has not been
  matched to a `.PLT` file, and nothing here says it is one. The shapes
  agree (x-sorted polyline, y from a truncated linear interpolation, a
  found/not-found query with a large-value sentinel); the identities do
  not: 13-byte binary records with a dword count at `[owner+0x8]` and a
  byte at record +0xc is not the port's `.PLT` in-memory form
  (`ll_xy *p; int n`, per-polyline pointer + count), the engine reaches
  its table through a virtual call on another object (0x45434/0x45439
  `call [ebx+0x6c]`, unread), and the port's `.PLT` is text parsed from
  the HD tree. Also: PR-122's line saying the port "models no geometric y
  at all" is true only of the per-tick object path - the player path and
  the placement snap do use the ground polylines, as above. Both wording
  corrections live in this record; no shipped record was edited.
- OPEN ITEMS (PR-123 1-3). (1) Which class answers slot +0x6c with a
  record index, and what its table is - that is the unread half of
  PR-122 item 1, and it is the shortest remaining path to naming these
  records. (2) Whether any 13-byte record table in the image is built
  from ground lines: look for the code that WRITES such records (a store
  to `[base + k*13]` plus `[base + k*13 + 4]`, and the +0xc byte) and
  what feeds it. (3) Who calls the 0x453d0 sibling, and what its caller
  does with an INT_MAX answer - that would say whether "no segment here"
  is an everyday case.
- GATES. Docs only: no `ported/`, `Makefile`, `tools/` or `.gitignore`
  line is in this commit, so the prompt's build gates do not apply and no
  build was run. Evidence: /tmp/opencode/pr123_dis.txt (image sha256, the
  full `dis` of 0x45380, `dis` of 0x453d0+0x30 and 0x453ed+0x24, the
  caller lists with their entry-list disclaimer, the sha256 of the two
  `ll_play` files, and the `grep -n` line numbers quoted from them); the
  scans of 13-scaling sites and record-+0xc byte reads are queries
  against /tmp/opencode/leo.sqlite, a derived index under /tmp. No game
  data, no captured frame, no .github/workflows change, every added line
  <= 79 columns.


## PR-124 — the reference-capture catalog: every level in the 5 h
recording is now indexed by its own title card, R3 is split into
level-named files, the playlist is complete on disk, and R1's footage is
proved byte-identical to one of its episodes (DOCS ONLY, no code)

- WHAT THE OWNER ASKED, quoted: "in that catalog should be downloaded
  all movies, that 5h material should be splited, every file should be
  named correctly by level name", and then the shape of the document:
  "information about episodes is pointless, should be references to
  levels" / "on videos" / "names". So HANDOFF §3 gained a LEVEL INDEX
  keyed by the engine's own names, each level pointing at a file and a
  time range, instead of a catalogue of episode metadata.
- THE NAME EVIDENCE IS DATA, NOT VIEWING. Every LEVELDES record carries
  a `dir=` key naming its stage, and the port already reads that key
  (`ported/ll_level.c:5724`, `:5758`, `:6023`): ZARIA1.DES -> zaria.01,
  ZARIA2.DES -> zaria.02, ENA1.DES -> ena.03, ENA2.DES -> ena2,
  KADMAR1.DES -> kadmar.07, KADMAR2.DES -> kadmar2, KARA.DES ->
  kara.07, LONA.DES -> lona.05, RAN.DES -> ran.01, SADES.DES ->
  sades.06, TUNGA1.DES -> tunga.11, TUNGA2.DES -> tunga2.12,
  JUNCTION.DES -> junction. So the chapter name the card draws and the
  stage id the census uses are tied by the game's own key, not by my
  reading of a video.
- EACH CARD WAS THEN READ. "ZARIA I / first steps" at 1931 s, "ENA I /
  underwater journey" at 2711 s, "KADMAR I / ancient mysteries" at
  7230 s, "ENA II / pirate treasure" at 1587 s, "LONA / land of
  penguins" at 4465 s, "SADES / deep down" at 4947 s, "KADMAR II /
  egyptian dark" at 8629 s, "RAN / two weeks in a baloon" at 15372 s
  (the game's own spelling), "KARA / magic castle" at 15808 s, "TUNGA I
  / so close" at 17718 and 18889 s, "TUNGA II / the last battle" at
  16948 s, and inside the 480p set "ZARIA II / zar tropikow" at 49 s of

## PR-125 — the F/T-law video probe, round one. Both T != 40 fixtures
the data offered (ENA.03 RYBKA, LONA.05 PINGWIN) animate in place but
do NOT TRANSLATE until the lion is adjacent; the R3 camera holds dead
still for 20-30 s
windows and jumps discretely between them; the next-best fixture is
named with measured still windows. (no C change; two python probes
added to tools/re)

- THE QUESTION IS EXACTLY HANDOFF §7 item 13's, quoted there: law A
  (the port, v = |F|/4 px/s, PR-79's walk law) and law B (the engine
  loop, v = 10*F/T px/s once v's hundredths-of-a-px-per-tick units and
  25 ticks/s are applied) "differ only by a constant" at T=40 - and
  every object measured so far (worm F=100, rhino F=180) is T=40.
  "What separates the laws is a BY_X OBJECT at T other than 40."
- THE CENSUS FIRST. All 777 .MOV texts in /tmp/opencode/mov re-scanned
  (/tmp/opencode/pr125_byx.py): of 2318 states, 75 are BY_X with F!=0.
  Ranked by what a video could actually referee, against an R3 file on
  disk: RYBKA R1-R6 A_RUN = BY_X|FRAME_REV|CHECK_LEW|CH_DIR|DANGER
  F=100,0 T=20,0 in all six files (A 25 vs B 50 px/s, a factor 2);
  NINJA1-6 A_RUN/A_START2 F=100,0 T=30,3 (A 25 vs B 33.3, +33%) in
  KADMAR.07; PINGWIN A_RUN = BY_X|FRAME_REV|CHECK_ANI|CHECK_LN|
  CHECK_LEW|CH_DIR|DANGER F=75,0 T=50,10 (A 18.75 vs B 15) and YETI
  F=100 T=50 (A 25 vs B 20) in LONA.05. The lion's own A_WALK states
  carry T=20 and T=30 in several levels and were REJECTED as referee:
  the lion is the player, and the player's path through 0x54250 is
  unverified (item 8). KADMAR.07's ZOLW soldier A_RUN is BY_TIME, and
  KADMAR.07_0_0.MOV is a player-lion variant - neither discriminates.
- TWO PROBES JOIN tools/re. `video_stills.py` finds camera-STILL
  windows (decor-only column-shift; pixels that changed are objects
  and are excluded; drift is reported in game px/s). `video_lane_shift.py`
  measures net band translation inside such a window. The two
  estimators agree on ENA.03: `video_stills.py --max 8` flags
  20.5-50.0 s, and the independent per-frame masked-SAD estimator
  (/tmp/opencode/pr125/joint.py, 1318 consecutive-frame samples over
  the hand-picked 27.7-49.7 s window, saved as joint_val27.npz) sums
  to -10.7 half-resolution px over those 22 s - about -0.5 game px/s,
  i.e. the lock holds to well under 1 px/s. Both remain ESTIMATORS:
  hand-pick a window and eyeball it before trusting a number (a flat
  sand bank can fake drift).
- A CAMERA FACT ABOUT R3 ITSELF. The camera does not scroll smoothly.
  It holds dead still for long windows (ENA.03 20.5-50.0 s at mean
  drift 0.54 px/s; LONA.05_b 480.0-504.5 s at 0.35 px/s), then jumps
  at speeds that saturate the search. The whole-cut distribution is
  BIMODAL, not noisy: over ENA.03 5-785 s, 1547 guarded samples
  (/tmp/opencode/pr125/p50.py), drift runs at 0 for minutes at a
  stretch and saturates the search range (+/-12 shifts in the 160
  space = +/-96 px/s) at the jumps; p50 16, p90 p99 max 96. That p50
  is NOT a camera speed: between the locks the moving schools and
  bubbles contaminate the estimator - which is exactly why windows
  must be hand-picked, never averaged. CONSEQUENCE: any world-frame
  speed from video MUST be taken inside a still window; outside one,
  screen dx is not world dx.
- ENA.03, THE FIRST PROBE: NEGATIVE FOR THE LAW, NOT FOR THE MACHINE.
  Inside the lock the RYBKA schools sit at their .des rows (ena_zw3:
  340,100 / 380,130 / 440,160 ... 490,270) with ZERO translation:
  `video_lane_shift.py --band 90 300 0 400 --lag 40` over 28-49 s,
  304 frame pairs, best shift 0 px (sad 3.16, next best 5.07). And
  R1.MOV declares ONLY two states - A_RUN (BY_X, line 5) and
  A_ESCAPE (BY_TIME, F=0) - so a sitting fish IS in its A_RUN state;
  it simply does not translate there. They also MATERIALIZE on screen
  when the lion approaches - the water is empty before, and the first
  authored fish is at world x=340. So A_RUN's BY_X motion channel
  contributes 0 while the lion is far. The active stretch at 95-165 s
  is spawn/escape events with heavy occlusion - no clean A_RUN run
  anywhere in the file.
- LONA.05, THE SECOND PROBE: SAME SHAPE. .des (extracted with
  `llrs_cat1 /tmp/opencode/hd_files/ETAPY` - the iso_stage ETAPY has
  no level dirs) places four PINGWIN at x=326/606/682/715,
  bounds=270,370, scope=40. Inside the 480.0-504.5 s lock a black-blob
  track holds one penguin's x within +/-3 px over 44 frames, and
  `video_lane_shift.py --band 200 340 60 200 --lag 90` (277 pairs)
  gives best shift 0 (sad 9.38, next best 15.83): they WAVE in place.
  Only when the lion is adjacent (494-502 s) do they flee - apparent
  ~55-65 px/s, an ESTIMATE from thumbnail steps with multiplicative
  error, and A_RUN is PINGWIN's state 0 while the file declares no
  escape state (its full state list: A_RUN, A_DEAD, A_WALKINTO/
  OUTIGLO, A_WSP_LIN_*, A_ATAK, A_TURN), so whether that motion is
  A_RUN translation or the level's SURPRISE objects (LONASUR1/2.MOV)
  is untested - and 55-65 cannot referee 18.75 vs 15 anyway.
- THE STATE-MACHINE FACT BOTH PROBES TEACH. The two BY_X states are
  not idle states: RYBKA A_RUN (R1-R6 line 5: BY_X|FRAME_REV|
  CHECK_LEW|CH_DIR|DANGER), PINGWIN A_RUN (line 13: +CHECK_LN|
  CHECK_ANI), NINJA A_START2/A_RUN (NINJA1.MOV lines 51/72: BY_X|
  FRAME_REV|CHECK_LN|CHECK_LEW|CH_DIR) - all carry CHECK_LEW, and in
  the locked windows both objects ANIMATE (the penguin's in-place
  wave advances its animation rows over 44 tracked frames) while
  translating exactly zero; both flee or run only when the lion
  closes in. ZARIA's worms DID patrol while the player crossed their
  bounds (PR-79), so the proximity gate is per-object, not global.
  INFERENCE, stated as such: CHECK_LEW is a per-object "lion near"
  gate evaluated on the feed side, and while it is not satisfied the
  BY_X velocity contribution to [obj+0xa1] is held at 0; where the
  engine evaluates it is unread (cf. item 12's "whether the engine
  re-tests every object every tick is unread").
- THE FIXTURE PR-126 WILL USE. KADMAR.07 NINJA1-6, A_RUN/A_START2 =
  BY_X|FRAME_REV|CHECK_LN|CHECK_LEW|CH_DIR, F=100 T=30: A predicts
  25 px/s, B 33.3 - 33% apart, and ninjas are engine-spawned in the
  boss zone with visible runs. Its A_START2/A_RUN carry CHECK_LEW
  too, so PR-126 must measure runs with the lion ALREADY adjacent
  (PR-125's own state-machine finding is the method warning here).
  `video_stills.py --t0 700 --t1 820` on
  reference/video/levels/KADMAR.07.mkv measured the still windows:
  712.5-728.5 (16.0 s), 763.0-774.0 (11.0 s), 791.0-802.0 (11.0 s),
  and nine shorter runs. The blue-shield marching soldiers visible at
  ~766-778 are ZOLW and are dismissed (BY_TIME); YETI (T=50, bounds
  2000-2350, 20% delta) is the named backup.
- GATES. No `ported/`, `Makefile`, `.gitignore` or `.github/workflows`
  line changed: only this record, HANDOFF §3 (R3 note) + §7 item 13 +
  §8 T1, tools/re/README.md, and two new standalone python probes that
  no make target reads. All four legs were run on THIS tree: `make`
  rc=0 and `make win` rc=0 - the C tree is unchanged since PR-124,
  where the full clean warning-free build was made, so both legs say
  "up to date", which is the honest form of that statement here - and
  `make -k verify-all` ran full twice: with fixtures
  (DATA=/tmp/opencode/iso_stage/LEO HD=/tmp/opencode/hd_files) rc=0,
  0 FAIL, fixture-free (DATA=/tmp/opencode/nope HD=/tmp/opencode/nope)
  rc=0. Logs: pr125_make.txt, pr125_makewin.txt, pr125_vfix2.txt,
  pr125_vnofix2.txt (the earlier clean legs at the PR-124 tree are
  pr125_vfix.txt, pr125_vnofix.txt). No game data or video staged
  (reference/video is gitignored, nothing under /tmp staged); `git
  status` before the commit shows only HANDOFF.md, NEXT_STEPS.md,
  tools/re/README.md and the two .py files. Added doc prose lines are
  all <= 79 columns; the two tools/re/README.md table rows follow that
  file's existing table style (its committed rows run to 994 columns).
- EVIDENCE IN /tmp, as ever: pr125_byx.py (the census), and under
  pr125/ the probe history - bgmotion.py, lane_sad.py, penguin.py,
  joint.py (the calibration), the ENA frame sweeps, penguin tracks,
  kad_*.png and kk30_sheet.png (the 30 s contact sheet of KADMAR.07
  that located the ninja runs), lona_zw.des / ena_zw3.des /

## PR-126 — the placement join: the complete T!=40 surface, the NINJA
fixture WITHDRAWN, and the KADMAR.07 windows shown to be a scripted
scene. (one new python tool; no C change)

- WHY. Both law probes so far picked their fixture from the `.MOV`
  side alone. A class only reaches the screen if a level `.des`
  instantiates it, and nobody had counted that half. The join is now
  a tool, so the census is a tool output and not a claim:
  tools/re/des_census.py reads every ETAPY level's `.des` text (all
  103 dumped with `llrs_cat1`, named `<LEVEL>_<NAME>.DES`) and joins
  it by level+class against the `/tmp/opencode/mov` corpus.
- THE CENSUS, as printed by the tool: 103 `.des`, 777 `.MOV`, 75
  BY_X states with F!=0; 34 UNIQUE (level, class, state) rows are
  actually placed. 29 of the 34 have T=40, where the two laws give
  the same speed, and the complete law-discriminating surface of the
  shipped game is the remaining 5 rows across 4 classes: ENA.03
  RYBKA F=100 T=20 (16 placement lines - the r1-r6 fish in two
  clusters at x=340-490 and x=940-1090; the six `.mov` names match
  the six `.MOV` instances, which is why PR-125 read R1-R6),
  KADMAR.07 BOSS A_RUNA + A_RUNB F=75 T=20 (ONE instance:
  `BOSS,xxx,boss.mov,1328,243` in ZWIERZ1.DES, attached keys
  damage=30, bounds=1128,1440, scope=50,180, energy=200), LONA.05
  PINGWIN F=75 T=50 (4 positions), LONA.05 YETI F=100 T=50 (ONE
  instance at x=2100). Both PR-125 fixtures are on that list;
  nothing else is.
- NINJA IS AN ORPHAN - PR-125's NAMED REFEREE IS WITHDRAWN. No
  `.des` of any level places NINJA1-6, neither level `.LVM` script
  references them (0 hits in KADMAR1/KADMAR2), and no other `.MOV`
  text does (0 hits over the corpus): complete ANIMACJE data
  (seqs UJ01-UJ06, six instances) that NOTHING instantiates, so it
  can never be on any recording. The tool's true-orphan list has
  exactly two entries; the other is the dummy class `0` whose
  `.MOV` is the lion variant (PR-125 fact (3)). Their UJ01-UJ06
  seq names are the same art ZOLW/KOBRA/WAZ/PTAK use, so a class
  renamed with its old data left behind is the likely story (an
  inference, not measured).
- THE KADMAR.07 WINDOWS ARE A SCRIPTED SCENE, and the frame dump
  settles what is in them. Re-measured with the file's real name
  (`reference/video/levels/KADMAR.07.mkv` - there is no `_b` of
  it; 1280x720@60): the still windows reproduce exactly,
  763.0-774.0 and 791.0-802.0 among them. Frames inside:
  763-778 is ZOLW marching through the arches (BY_TIME - already
  dismissed); 791-802 is a PURE-BLACK room with a white-door arch
  (ANIBACK_DRZWI) and the BOSS figure in the middle of it - a
  lion-faced king, headdress, striped collar, purple robe:
  boss_track's mask centroid sits at x=315-322 with ZERO
  translation from 793.7 to 798.9 s (per-second span <= 7 px,
  0 px at 797) while the mask AREA oscillates 1700-3600 px -
  animating in place, the RYBKA/PINGWIN pattern, third object
  class - but with no lion in frame and no HUD, and 799.2-800.9
  the figure translates right x=316->589 at ~150 px/s while its
  hat/crown blob detaches and flies: neither law's T=20 speed
  (18.8/37.5), and an in-level scene driven by SEQ patch moves,
  NOT an A_RUNA/B run (inference from the no-HUD frame, named as
  such). 725 s inside the 712.5-728.5 window IS gameplay (HUD
  drawn): three stationary brown legged blobs - the camels
  (CAMEL, placed at x=1200, BY_TIME) - and no ninja anywhere.
  video_stills.py now carries the caveat in its docstring: a
  near-black room is a PSEUDO-still window (flat decor = flat
  column sums = shift 0 whatever the camera does); dump a frame
  from the middle of a window before spending a measurement on it.
- NO BOSS RUN IS ON FILM YET. 460-960 s of KADMAR.07.mkv were
  swept: 26 still windows in that range, the three quoted above
  included (605-687 repeats 5.5 s runs at
  0.0-0.64 px/s; 701.5-711.0; 859-874; 898.5-909; content
  unviewed except 725), none in the boss room. The rest of the
  file (0-460, 960-1455) was not swept - a pass is 26 min of

  backup; PINGWIN stays probed and inconclusive (the observed

- GATES. No `ported/`, `Makefile`, `.gitignore` or

## PR-127 — the Zax37 playlist renamed to level names on disk: the
11 episodes are complete (re-verified against YouTube today) and now
live in reference/video/zax37/ under the §3 index's own stage ids.
(NO CODE CHANGE; gitignored files renamed, docs updated)

- WHAT THE OWNER ASKED, quoted: "that playlist should be downloaded
  and placed in videos folder with proper names (it is in order of
  levels) i dont know why there is only one kadmar file". The
  download half of that was already done by PR-124; the naming half
  is what changed here, and the kadmar question has a clean answer:
  there is no missing file - the game has TWO Kadmar stages, and
  both are on disk twice over: `levels/KADMAR.07.mkv` + `zax37/
  KADMAR.07.mp4` (KADMAR I / ancient mysteries = "Starożytne

  (KADMAR II / egyptian dark = "Egipskie Ciemności" = ep.8). What
  does NOT exist is a `KADMAR*_b`: the `_b` files mark a SECOND
  visit in one sitting, and in the 5 h recording each Kadmar card
  fires exactly once (7 230 s and 8 629 s).
- THE PLAYLIST ITSELF WAS RE-VERIFIED LIVE: `yt-dlp -J
  --flat-playlist PL6B7604DEF5B643F9` returns 11 entries, the same
  ids PR-124 recorded, in the same order. Nothing was missing and
  nothing needed downloading.

  game's own card subtitle (proved for ep.2 by reading its card, and
  cross-checked against the game's shipped POL/ENG tables for every
  chapter - PR-124). So the rename maps chapter-subtitle -> stage id

  ENA.03 ENA2 LONA.05 SADES.06 KADMAR.07 KADMAR2 RAN.01 KARA.07

  checked against its new stage name (11/11 match; the check printed
