## PR-147 — THE CLIMB FEED LAW IS CLOSED ON THE ENGINE SIDE: THE

## BY_TY GUARD WORD IS THE PLAYER'S OWN VERTICAL INTENT, THE

## KEYBOARD WRITES IT AT +/-20, THE CONTACT NODE AT KIND 4

## OVERRIDES IT AT +/-10, AND PR-146'S KIND-4 LABEL IS CORRECTED

## (READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE; PR-138..146 precedent)

- WHY. After PR-146 closed the contact delivery, the climb line
  (HANDOFF item 15 G-9, section 8 T5) had exactly one clause left
  that was still READING rather than deciding: what drives the
  mode-4 (BY_TY) guard `cmp [obj+0xbe],0` at 0x5441b, what the
  guard's magnitude is, and what the input block the frame loop
  hands around actually contains (PR-145 open item 6, PR-108's
  "who fills the caller's two dwords", left open by PR-145). This
  unit reads those from the same image (sha256 edf19a12...) and
  closes them. Reading record only; no behaviour change.

- FINDING 1, THE CONTROL-KEYWORD ENCODING, BYTE-EXACT, AND THE
  FIVE-ENTRY JUMP TABLE. The token parser's compare chain
  (0x51b35..0x51da0, over the 23 keyword strings at
  0x9216e..0x9222f - BY_X, BY_Y, BY_TIME, BY_TX, BY_TY,
  FRAME_REV, SEQ_REV_X, SEQ_REV_Y, CHECK_ZW, CHECK_ANI, CHECK_LN,
  CHECK_ALL, CHECK_LEW, CHECK_BASE_LN, SOLID, CH_DIR, INV_V,
  DANGER, CHECK_ALL_PLANE, ANTI_SOLID, SOLID2, SEMI_SOLID,
  ANTI_POCISK; error string at 0x9223b) ORs these immediates into
  the state record's flag word: BY_X 0x1 (0x51b6f), BY_Y 0x2
  (0x51b89), BY_TIME 0x3 (0x51ba3), BY_TX 0x4 (0x51bbd), BY_TY
  0x5 (0x51bd7), FRAME_REV 0x8 (0x51bf1), SEQ_REV_X 0x10
  (0x51c0b), SEQ_REV_Y 0x20 (0x51c25), CHECK_ZW 0x80 (0x51c3f),
  CHECK_ANI 0x40 (0x51c57), CHECK_LN and CHECK_ALL both 0x1c0
  (0x51c71/0x51c8a). This confirms PR-108's five-value mode note
  item for item - BY_X -> mode 0 sets nothing visible because the
  first two compare arms share the same OR at 0x51b49/0x51b6f.
  The dispatcher's jump table at 0x54380 is FIVE dwords
  (byte-exact): idx0 0x543c6, idx1 0x543dc, idx2 0x543f2, idx3
  0x543fb, idx4 0x5441b, then data at +0x14. The mode-0 branch is
  the IMPLICIT mode: a state whose control word carries no keyword
  is fed by |v_x| (idx0), and mode 3 (BY_TX) has no guard while
  mode 2 (BY_TIME) is guarded on [obj+0xba] and FALLS THROUGH into
  the same body (0x543f2 -> 0x543fb). THE CONSTANT 100 HAS
  EXACTLY ONE WRITER: grep `+0x388]` over the image = 4 sites -
  the write `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x388],0x64` at 0x4c8b7 inside
  the entry at 0x4c8a2 (a clean prologue: push esi/edi/ebp, mov
  ebp,esp, sub esp,0x24c, sub ebp,0x12e - an init constructor)
  and three readers: 0x239d0 (the no-mode variant, +0xa0 in 31
  tables, PR-100), 0x54406, 0x5442f. The row-step sequence is
  confirmed end to end at exact bytes (0x521f0 entry): record
  lookup, condition any-bit test 0x5223c/0x495b0, the key-empty
  branch 0x522fc..0x5230c, THEN the feed call 0x52317, THEN the
  compare `mov eax,[rec+0x10]` / `cmp eax,[obj+0xa1]` /
  `jge 0x52354` (0x52320..0x5232b), the remainder `sub ebx,eax`
  handed to the row advance at [obj+0x44]+0x18 (0x52338; the
  entry it resolves to in the measured blocks is 0x52470, which
  writes the remainder straight back to [obj+0xa1] at 0x52118) -
  exactly the model the port ships (ll_play.c sections 4/7). The
  direction compute (PR-108's A^B at 0x52385/0x523a0) re-reads
  bit-exact against the new keyword table: A tests SEQ_REV_X
  (0x10), B tests SEQ_REV_Y (0x20).

- FINDING 2, THE INPUT BLOCK IS THE PLAYER'S OWN INTENT, AND THE
  GUARD WORD IS ITS VERTICAL AXIS. The class-table slot +0xcc is
  called at EXACTLY SEVEN sites (closed set, grep `call
  [reg+0xcc]`): 0x27e1d, 0x282a1, 0x344c8, 0x4010e, 0x4110c,
  0x41c01, 0x4aeca. The frame loop's own (0x4aeca): 0x4ae82 `mov
  eax,ds:0xa94f0` - when that global is zero the loop RETURNS 2
  (0x4ae8b, 0x4ae90); 0x4ae92 `lea edx,[esp+0x1f0]` (PR-106's
  12-byte block); 0x4aeb3 `mov eax,[ecx+0x394]` = the LION
  (PR-144's field); 0x4aec0 `mov ebx,[eax+8]`; 0x4aeca `call
  DWORD PTR [ebx+0xcc]`; and immediately after it 0x4aed0/0x4aedb
  = the step pump 0x52b80. So the engine hands the player's input
  block to the lion through its CONTACT METHOD, every frame,
  before stepping it. The block's producer 0x58690 has EXACTLY ONE
  call site in the image: the frame loop at 0x4ac6c (PR-106's
  `mov eax,0xcf400; call 0x58690`). THE CAPTURE READER 0x582f0
  (entry) maps the whole keyboard onto the block: it first zeroes
  words 0/1/2 (0x582f6..0x58303), gates on the singleton's enable
  byte (0x5830a `cmp BYTE PTR [eax],0`) and on 0x51320 (keyboard
  present), and reads through the keyed device object 0x1c530/
  0x1c550 (device immediate 0x13b at 0x58322; VMT array 0xce284 -
  internals not chased). Word 0 = the x-axis: Home/Left scancode
  0x24b -> -20 (0x58477), Right 0x24d -> +20 (0x58490). WORD 1 =
  the y-axis: Down 0x250 -> +20 (0x584a9), Up 0x248 -> -20
  (0x584c3) - so the engine's vertical intent is literally the
  player's Up/Down keys, +/-20, y+ = down (matches PR-99's sign).
  Word 2 and the flag bytes carry the buttons: Insert/Delete (0x8
  bits 6,7), F1..F10 ([+9] 0x1,0x2,0x40,0x80; [+0xa] 0x1,0x2,0x4,
  0x8), Tab ([+9]|4), Esc ([+8]|4 and |8), Space ([+8]|0x20 and
  |2), Ctrl ([+8]|0x10), LShift ([+8]|1), NumLock ([+9]|0x10,
  [+8]|0x808). WORDS 0 AND 1 ARE ONLY EVER 0, +20 OR -20 in the
  capture path. THE DEMO RECORD FORMAT (PR-145's open item 6,
  other half): 0x58690 treats the 0xcf400 singleton as an object -
  mode at [x+0xb], record arrays at [[x+0xf]]/[[x+0x2b]] with a
  0x10-byte stride, cursor [x+0x2f], current [x+0x2b], wrap when
  the cursor reaches `[rec+0xc]` (0x586c3..0x586dc) - and
  PLAYBACK copies a record's words +0/+4/+8 straight into the
  block (0x586a7..0x586b6): so a demo record IS a 12-byte input
  block plus a length word. Mode 1 runs the capture (0x586ed
  call 0x582f0) plus 0x58010 on [x+0x33]; when [x+0xb] == 1 it
  also replays the PREVIOUS record through 0x57fe0 (0x58708..
  0x58728) and merges via 0x225a0 (0x5875f) - the merge's
  internals are open item 3. [CORRECTED + CLOSED BY
  PR-188 F1: 0x57fe0 replays NOTHING - it DEDUPLICATES
  (match -> `inc [rec+0xc]`, difference -> append), and
  0x225a0 is the CAPACITY-GROWTH call when count == cap,
  not a merge - item 3's merge question dissolves. The
  '12-byte input block + length word' IS right: records
  are 16B = the 3 played words + the run count [rec+
  0xc]; playback reads only the first three (PR-106
  record CLOSED by PR-188 F1).]

- FINDING 3, THE INTENT WORDS AND THE THREE-KIND CONTACT CHAIN,
  WITH THEIR WRITE CENSUSES. 0x549f0 (entry 0x549f2): 0x549f7/
  0x549f9 `[obj+0xba] = [edx]` and 0x549ff/0x54a08 `[obj+0xbe] =
  [edx+4]` - both UNCONDITIONAL, from the CALLER'S block; Finding

  ([[obj+0xd2]+4], 0x54a16) = 1 -> the x chain (0x54a24..0x54af3:
  the ID test [head+0xc] vs [obj+0x6d], the getter [vt+0x68],
  the +-8 dead band around node+8, writing +10/-10/0); kind = 4 ->
  0x54aa2..0x54b47, the SAME shape but on the vertical: the
  getter's +4 (y, 0x54b05) compared against [head+0x1d] with the
  +-8 band, writing +10 (0x54b16, move down), -10 (0x54b3b, move
  up), 0 (0x54b47); kind = 2 -> the answer-set merge (0x54b65..
  0x54b84, PR-146). WRITE CENSUS, closed: [obj+0xba] is written
  at six sites (0x549f9 word0; 0x54a57 +10, 0x54a82 -10, 0x54a93
  0, 0x54ac3 +10, 0x54ae7 -10, 0x54af3 0) and read at 0x54108,
  0x542ab (the integrator's force), 0x543f2 (the BY_TIME guard),
  0x5495b (K_FWD/K_BKWD, gated on the facing byte [obj+0xb6] bit
  4), 0x54b51/0x54b5a. [obj+0xbe] is written at FOUR sites and
  nothing else (0x54a08 word1; 0x54b16 +10, 0x54b3b -10, 0x54b47
  0) and read at 0x54111, 0x542cd (the force), 0x5441b (THE
  MODE-4/BY_TY GUARD), 0x5499d/0x549ab (K_UP/K_DOWN by sign) and
  0x54b5a. THE CHAIN ORDER IS THE WIN: the block store happens
  first and the contact chain re-decides after it, all inside one
  call - while a kind-1/4 contact node exists, the intent is the
  engine's own +/-10 toward the node's position; otherwise it is
  the player's +/-20. (A side note, not chased: 0x54108/0x54111
  inside the called-from-many 0x54030 also COPY the two intents
  into a live set at [set-0x1c]/[set-0x18].)
  STRUCTURAL ODDITY, COUNTED NOT SMOOTHED: node+0x1d (the y the
  kind-4 chain compares) is the 30th byte, but the node builder's
  allocation is 0x1d bytes (0x3d5fc) - PR-146's node+0x10 answer
  set ends exactly at +0x1c. Either a DIFFERENT builder with a
  larger size builds the kind-1/4 nodes (PR-146 open item 1: who
  builds kinds 2/4 - still open), or the read crosses into the
  next allocation. The measurements themselves are unambiguous:
  node+8 is compared as an x, node+0xc compares against
  [obj+0x6d] (PR-108's ID field), node+0x10 is the answer set,
  node+0x1d is compared as a y.

- FINDING 4, THE AUTHORED A_WSP LAW, ENGINE DATA. A byte census
  over hd_files/ANIMACJE (1,961,080 bytes): BY_TY occurs 12 times,
  BY_TX 0 (the counted negative PR-108 asserted, now at byte
  level); member attribution by nearest preceding name marker:
  2LEW.MOV x4, LEWPL.MOV x4, one each at the offsets near
  KLADKA1.MOV, MIOTLA_W.MOV, XKALUZA.MOV (member boundaries are
  fuzzy; 12 blocks is the firm count). All eleven A_WSP/
  A_WSP_LIN blocks are identical in law: `control=BY_TY|
  CHECK_ALL|SEQ_REV_Y` (wire word 0x5|0x40|0x1c0 = 0x205),
  `F=0,100`, `T=160,50`, `G=0,0`, one seq=climb/climb_r (one
  variant adds ANTI_SOLID|FRAME_REV, seq=0024), and a row list
  `1,300`, `2..9,200`, `10,300` (10 rows; the LIN variants 8).
  The twelfth block - the A_DRAB one PR-109 quoted - carries
  T=1000,50 and rows `1..10,500`, seq=uj31. Under the law of
  Findings 1-3 this runs as: mode-4 guard = the vertical intent
  (the player's Up/Down, or the kind-4 chain's +/-10 toward the
  ladder's y); feed = exactly 100 per frame while it passes;
  threshold = the row's [rec+0x10] word, which the port reads
  from that row list (300 for row 1, 200 after, ll_seq) - so a
  BY_TY row advances after 3 and then 2 QUALIFYING frames, and
  the row stops dead the moment the vertical intent stops. The
  integrator side applies the same word as a force: 0x542cd
  `imul edx,[ecx+0xbe]` with the T1 pair, /20, added to v_y -
  with the authored T=160,50 a -10 intent is a -80-per-frame
  v_y increment against a 50%-per-frame drag. THE PORT'S CURRENT
  ROW MODEL IS UNCHANGED BY THIS (BY_TY is time-fed at 100/frame
  and the thresholds are already right); WHAT THE PORT DOES NOT
  HAVE is the guard and the intent values - which is now an
  implementation decision with the engine's numbers written down
  (+/-20 keyboard, +/-10 contact, +-8 dead band, 100 per frame),
  not a missing law.

## PR-148 — THE INPUT/GUARD LAW BECOMES BEHAVIOUR: THE PORT'S
## PLAYER NOW CARRIES THE ENGINE'S VERTICAL-INTENT WORD AND A
## BY_TY ROW IS FED ONLY WHILE IT IS HELD — AND THE SESSION'S
## 0x50252 "RISE LAW" CANDIDATE IS CAUGHT DEAD CODE (CODE PR,
## THE FIRST SINCE PR-140's `81eee9b`)

- WHY. PR-147 closed the climb feed law with ZERO open laws and
  said what remained was the implementation decision: give the
  port the guard and the intent word (the PR-147 Next entry, item
  (a)). This PR implements exactly that law as behaviour, with a
  hand-derived test (the re-pinned PR-108 leg) and a mutation
  battery. The second half of the reading that PR-147's Next
  handed to PR-148 - a claimed rise law at 0x50252, carried in the
  working notes but NEVER in a shipped record - was tested against
  the image first and REFUTED before it could be coded; the
  finding is corrected here, not hidden.

- FINDING 1, THE GUARD IS SHIPPED. Three parts, each a byte-exact
  copy of an engine fact PR-147 recorded:
  (i) `LL_CTRL_BY_TY = 0x20000u` and the parser now maps the
  `BY_TY` keyword to it (ll_play.c `ctrl_flag`, ll_play.h enum).
  The port's enum values have never been the wire values; the
  wire encoding (BY_TY = mode 5-in-bits-0..2, PR-147's
  0x51bd7) stays recorded where it was read.
  (ii) The player carries `p->vert_intent`, set every iteration
  from the held Up/Down keys with the engine's SIGN semantics
  (Up negative, y+ = down - the capture reader 0x582f0's own
  signs, PR-147) at the port's single intent scale
  (LL_PLAY_INTENT_FULL, PR-132's 10; the engine's keyboard word
  is +/-20 - that tension is named at the constant, not
  smoothed).
  (iii) Section 7's mode-4 feed guard: `control=BY_TY` states
  receive the 100-per-iteration feed ONLY while the word is
  non-zero, and the row compare runs regardless - the engine's
  order at 0x5441b is `cmp [obj+0xbe],0; je` (skip the ADD)
  and the step then compares [rec+0x10] against [obj+0xa1]
  (PR-147's 0x52317-then-0x52320 order), so a BY_TY row closes
  only on QUALIFYING iterations and the partial accumulator
  carries across the gap, exactly like [obj+0xa1]. The authored
  A_WSP rows (300 then 200, wire word 0x205) therefore advance
  after 3 and then 2 qualifying frames and stop the instant the
  intent stops - PR-147's law, now executable.
  NOT copied, deliberately: 0x543f2's guard of BY_TIME (mode 2)
  on the X-intent word (open item 2), and 0x542cd's use of the
  y-word as a v_y FORCE (open item 1). PR-102's "mode 2 carries
  no guard" stands as the port's behaviour; every video-verified
  leg since has run on that reading, and PR-147's own source for
  the guard (word0 = the arrows) makes it a behaviour-regression
  study, not a copy.

- FINDING 2, 0x50252 IS DEAD CODE IN THIS IMAGE, AND THE LION'S
  FRAME-LOOP +0x74 IS 0x50320. The working notes carried: "entry
  0x50252 (class slot +0x74, called on the LION at 0x4afea) is
  THE CLIMB RISE LAW, v_y*15/100 written into the position
  block." Three measurements refute it:
  (a) BYTE-EXACT TABLE: the LION's table 0x96960 has +0x74 =
  0x50320, not 0x50252 (struct read of 0x96960: +0x68 =
  0x23900, +0x74 = 0x50320, +0x78 = 0x50f80, +0xcc = 0x50340,
  +0xa0 = 0x543a0 - the last three match PR-144's readings,
  which anchors the read).
  (b) ZERO REFERENCES: a whole-image scan finds no rel32
  `call 0x50252` (0 hits), no dword pointing at 0x50252 (0
  hits), and text.asm quotes no such call. (The neighbours
  0x5024f/0x502b0 have no dword refs either - 0x502b0 is
  reached by a DIRECT call from 0x5032c, which is why a dword
  scan alone would miss it; the rel32 scan covers calls, so
  0x50252 is unreferenced both ways.)
  (c) WHAT ACTUALLY RUNS AT 0x4afea: 0x50320 gates on
  [obj+0x126] == 0, calls 0x502b0 - which tests the ODDNESS of
  [obj+0x102] and falls back to [obj+0xf2] - and when that
  returns zero calls 0x54c00, whose head (0x54c07..0x54c39:
  [obj+0xb5] as a signed byte, the [obj+0xb6] 0x2-and-0x1-bit
  tests, the [vt+0xbc] call) is a friction/ground-contact gate,
  not a rise.
  The *15/100 form at 0x50266 is real code but unreached; a
  pattern census (C1 E0 `shl eax,4` within 8 bytes of 29 D0
  `sub eax,edx`) finds 28 such sites image-wide, so the shape
  itself is a common multiply-by-15, not a signature of one law.
  CONSEQUENCE: no vertical MOTION was added to the port by this
  PR. The vertical position of a climbing lion stays unmodelled,
  and the path that could move it - this word as a v_y force at
  0x542cd plus whatever integrates v_y (the generic step
  0x54c00 is the candidate and is unread) - is open item 1.
  SELF-CORRECTION SCOPE: 0x50252 appears in NO shipped record
  (NEXT_STEPS and HANDOFF grep it zero times), so nothing needs
  re-editing; the error dies in this record. One shipped
  sentence DOES need narrowing: PR-147's "imul [ecx+0xbe] with
  the T1 pair /20 into v_y ... -80-per-frame" - at 0x542cd the
  multiplier is `[ebx+0x4]` of the same param struct whose
  +0x8 PR-132 read as the raised-to->=20 T word, and 0x542ab
  uses [ebx+0x8] for the x force. Which param field is the
  y-side multiplier (and whether it is the authored T pair at
  all) is UNREAD - the "-80" figure is conditional on that
  identification and is counted as open item 1's sub-question,
  not retracted (the instruction shape - intent * param/20 ->
  v_y - is byte-exact and stands).

- FINDING 3, THE RE-PINNED LEG (ll_play.c, the PR-108 leg,
  hand-derived, no game data). Three legs on authored-shaped
  fixtures:
  LEG 1 (the guard as behaviour): AC_DRAB raised, NO key ever
  held - the state is entered at list index 2 (PR-108's
  `A_WSP(3)=` entry-1 rule) and then 25 iterations change
  nothing: no feed (`row_t` stays exactly 0), no row advance, no
  wrap, no AC_BREAK_NEXT, and x, y, v_x, v_y never move. Under
  the old model the same loop advanced and wrapped at t=17. The
  final step lets AC_DRAB go and `A_FALL_DOWN(1)=!AC_DRAB`
  fires FROM A STATE WHOSE LIST NEVER TICKED - the transition
  pass is independent of the row pass, section 1 vs section 7,
  as the engine evaluates them separately.
  LEG 2 (guard held = the PR-108 spans, unchanged): Up held
  t=1..15, every iteration qualifies, rows close at
  t=2,4,6,8,10,12,14 with the entry at t=1 - the held-climb
  clock is IDENTICAL to the old ungated clock, which is the
  direct proof that the guard only ever SUBTRACTS feeds.
  LEG 3 (the gap): keys released t=16,17 - rows freeze at index
  9, the carried 100 of the 300-row survives untouched, no wrap
  at t=17 (the mutation that deletes the guard wraps HERE);
  Down held t=18: 100 + 100 = 200 < 300, no admit; t=19: 300
  -> wrap, index 0, AC_BREAK_NEXT armed and readable only on
  that step; t=20: a fresh 100 on the wrapped row. Up and Down
  qualify alike - the guard tests non-zero, exactly like the
  engine's cmp/je pair, and the sign is carried in the word for
  the force path (open item 1), unused by the clock.
  The PR-108 parser pins re-pin honestly: BY_TY leaves
  `ctrl_other` (2 -> 1, SEQ_REV_Y alone remains) and `ctrl`
  gains the new bit; `CHECK_ALL` still reaches ctrl as before.
  The selftest summary line was rewritten with the new
  behaviour text.

- WHAT THIS CLOSES / NARROWS. HANDOFF item 15's "implementation
  decision" is now HALF shipped: the guard and the word are in
  the port, and the authored BY_TY blocks now PARSE with a model
  bit. A sharper census comes with it: splitting the archive by
  BLOCK (not by string occurrence) counts exactly 12 BY_TY
  blocks across three state names - A_WSP x5, A_WSP_LIN x6,
  A_DRAB x1 - firm. Their MEMBER attribution, though, is
  anchoring-dependent: PR-147's string-offset anchor named
  KLADKA1/MIOTLA_W/XKALUZA for the last occurrences, the
  block-start anchor names F4ZDYBYA/DEMO/BALONIK instead (the

## PR-149 — THE NODE BUILDERS ARE PINNED AND THE 0x1d MYSTERY IS
## CLOSED (KIND-4 NODES ARE ALLOCATED 0x21); THE LADDER'S ANSWER
## METHOD IS READ AS A PREDICATE TREE; AND THE SECOND `LINA`
## LITERAL IS A FACTORY BRANCH - PR-141 ITEM 4 IS ANSWERED
## (READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE; PR-138..148 precedent)

- WHY. PR-148's Next handed PR-149 the node-shape pass first (who
  builds contact nodes kinds 1/2/4, and how a 0x1d-byte allocation
  can carry the field at node+0x1d - PR-147's open item 1), as the
  gate for the code PR that follows (the contact-answer route, now
  PR-150). The pass closed the item and then kept going down the
  ladder: its answer method read end to end at byte level, its
  construction chain, and the factory census that names LINA's
  class after all. No behaviour and no test changed, so by the
  PR-138..148 precedent no new test ships with this record.

- FINDING 1, THE NODE-SHAPE PASS, CLOSED. The builder ENTRY PR-147
  could not pin is pinned; three builders, byte-exact:
  (a) kind 1, entry 0x53eb0 (prologue `push esi; mov esi,eax` at
  0x53eb0/53eb1): [n+0]=0, [n+4]=1 (0x53eb9), [n+8]=edx,
  [n+0xc]=ebx, then the 13-byte set at [n+0x10..0x1c] is ZEROED
  (stores 0x53ec3..0x53ed2, the store list PR-147 measured). A
  second kind-1 builder at 0x53f00 carries the same stores
  (0x53f0d) - the two sites PR-146 quoted as the list setters'
  callees.
  (b) kind 2, entry 0x53f50: [n+4]=2 is BUILT (0x53f62), and the
  13 bytes are NOT zeroed - a caller-pushed block is COPIED IN
  (`mov ecx,0xc` + `rep movsd`/`rep movsb`, 0x53f6e..0x53f88):
  the answer-carrying builder. Its only rel32 caller is 0x3d66d.
  (c) kind 4: no builder - the kind-1 builder 0x53eb0 (called at
  0x24678) is PATCHED after the fact, [rec+4]=4 (0x24681) and
  [rec+0x1d]=edx (0x24688) - the write PR-146 quoted.
  THE ALLOCATION CENSUS, the item itself. 0x5c320 is the engine's
  general allocator (617 rel32 call sites - sizes must be read at
  each mov), and a whole-image byte scan (`mov eax,imm32` within
  16 bytes before a call to 0x5c320) finds exactly THREE sites
  sized 0x1d (0x1ef4c - a region that also calls the message
  queue 0x52b10, context unread; 0x3d5fc and 0x3d64f - the two
  node allocations inside the +0x78 contact entry 0x3d440, PR-147
  Finding 4) and exactly ONE site sized 0x21: 0x2465f, THREE
  INSTRUCTIONS BEFORE the kind-4 patch at 0x24681. So a kind-4
  contact node is 0x21 = 33 bytes and carries +0x1d..0x20 inside
  its own block; kind-1/2 nodes are 0x1d and the highest byte
  they own is +0x1c. And a whole-image grep for accesses through
  +0x1d: exactly ONE store exists, 0x24688 (in the kind-4 chain
  itself), and every register-based READ of +0x1d sits in the
  kind-4 handler 0x54aa2..0x54b4e (its y-compare pair, 0x54b11
  and 0x54b36; the other hits are stack slots or unrelated
  objects). The oddity was never an oddity: the allocation size
  follows the kind, exactly as far as the kind's reader reaches.
  Counted negatives, not smoothing: the scan's window is 16 bytes
  and one immediate could in principle hide beyond it; but the
  0x21 site sits in
  the kind-4 construction chain itself (one straight line:
  0x2465f alloc 0x21 -> 0x24672 `add ecx,0xd2` -> 0x24678 builder
  -> 0x24681 patch kind -> 0x24688 write +0x1d), which is the
  proof the
  census wanted. PR-147 open item 1 CLOSED (and PR-146's "the
  constructors write [rec+4]=1" NARROWED: only the kind-1
  builders write 1).
  WHO CALLS THE BUILDER CHAIN: 0x24678 sits inside a function at
  0x24440 - entry proven by its prologue (`push esi/edi/ebp; sub
  esp,0x40`) and reached from exactly ONE dword, 0x989ec, which
  lies inside the 0x988ec/0x988e4 class-table pair the PR-138
  census names as TLewEna (the ENA-level lion class, ctor
  0x24110) - so the chain is LION-side machinery, in the same
  table region whose ctor writes [obj+0x12a] (at `[this-0x12a]`,
  PR-138) - the exact field the chain's head gates on.
  [CORRECTED by PR-151 F1/F3, byte-checked this pass: the
  method entered at 0x24440 ENDS at its `ret 0x4` (0x244ba..

## PR-150 — THE LADDER'S ANSWER BECOMES BEHAVIOUR: THE FULL-EXTENT
## THEN 70%-PROBE PREDICATE PAIR, THE SINGLE ANSWER ROW, AND THE
## MERGED CATCH / LONE DRAB TAILS ARE SHIPPED AS CODE; THE PASS'S
## OWN THREE SELF-CORRECTIONS TO PR-149'S SHIPPED WORDING ARE
## RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN (CODE + READING RECORD)

- WHY. PR-149's Next named this as THE code pass: every input of
  the contact-answer route was pinned there (node shapes, the
  ladder's predicate tree, the merge chain), so the remaining
  question was implementation. The implementation forced three
  byte-level re-reads, and each re-read CORRECTED wording this
  session itself had shipped in PR-149 - the corrections are part
  of this record (Findings 1-3) and were also spliced into the
  PR-149 sections in place, per the session's correction
  discipline. The engine image is unchanged throughout (text.bin
  sha256 edf19a129e85efb8764457a0808e246ca4baf08a9111aa09be4ec9
  9ce6b8c40e).

- FINDING 1, THE ROW-INDEX SPACE IS CLOSED: [obj+0x5c] IS A
  1-BASED ROW POSITION, AND THE PORT'S CURSOR IS ITS 0-BASED
  TWIN (engine = fi + 1) [IDENTITY SUPERSEDED by PR-157 F3 +
  the 0x3f1dc re-read in PR-158 F2 (bracket inserted at the
  ledger recovery, PR-158): the gate reads [ecx+0x5c] with
  ecx = SELF, and the PR-157 census names the field the rows-
  array/STATE index - init 1 at 0x5321e, ENTER runs on rows[1]
  (0x539e6), the applier writes the TARGET RECORD INDEX at
  0x535ed, `( N )` goes to the state record's cursor [[rec]+4]
  at 0x53616, no row-advancement writer exists. By that law
  the gate values are STATE slots, not row positions. What
  STANDS under BOTH readings: this finding's proof (iii) (row-
  leading numbers = frame selectors), the (N) row-start law
  (PR-86/110), and every ZARIA.01 leg; the port's fi-model is
  KEPT (PR-158 F3)]. PR-149/150's first draft assumed the
  gate read some row ID tied to the authored leading numbers
  (drab's 1,2,3...11). The bytes close that. (a) The field
  indexes the CURRENT STATE's row-record table: 0x5523f/
  0x55242 calls class slot +0x44, and the base-class getter at
  that slot, 0x23920..0x2392e, is exactly `[[obj+0x50] +
  [obj+0x5c]*4] + 0x12` (PR-139 had already read that getter as
  the row-record read; this pass re-read it for the index
  question). (b) The transition apply 0x52000 walks the current
  state's transition list ([state+0x1a], count at +0x8, record
  stride 0x15, evaluator 0x47e40 per record), and on a match
  writes record+0xd (the target state) and record+0x11 - the
  AUTHORED `( N )` value, verbatim - into output slots; the
  second slot is the object's row cursor (0x52046..0x5204d).
  So N ADDRESSES the record table directly. (c) The authored
  data decides the rest: drab.MOV's A_UP has exactly ONE exit,
  `A_DROP(1)=K_GEN1`, while A_DROP's FIRST row line is `2,500`
  - under any global-ID keying (1) would land on an empty slot
  while (2) would be needed; under position keying (1) = the
  first line, exactly as PR-110's row law already equated
  `(1)` with the port's row 0. (d) Therefore the row lines'
  leading numbers (1,2,3...10,11) are FRAME SELECTORS (the
  drab table is one frame per drop step; obj_shape_elem feeds
  the same stored field to ll_mov_frame_ref), NOT row ids, and
  the near-contiguity is ladder art, not numbering. COROLLARY,
  the ladder's gate map, exact: cursor 1 (port fi 0 - A_UP's
  idle `1,0`, the drop's FIRST `2,500`, the park `11,0`) takes
  the FLAG branch (its 0x44ec0 child ANY-test never matches in
  the port - no child model - so it answers NOTHING and [self+
  0x66] bit 6 is never set, counted); cursor 2 (port fi 1 - the
  drop's `3,400,smpauto` row, 500 ms into the drop) is the
  ONLY answer row; cursor >= 3 (fi >= 2) falls to the inert
  exit at 0x3f217; cursor 0 = state start before any admit, no
  handler, never represented by the port. Corroboration found
  by the way: a second base-class gate at 0x238e4 treats row
  position 2 ("`cmp [eax+0x5c],0x2`") as unconditionally true
  in a test whose other arm is the class slot +0x8 rect test -
  the same second-row semantics, in the same base region as the
  +0x68 getter 0x23900; quoted, not chased (open item 7).

- FINDING 2, THE 0x49fb0 ARITHMETIC IS A SYMMETRIC CENTRAL-n%
  INSET - THE PR-149 WORDING WAS WRONG, CORRECTED IN PLACE. The
  shipped sentence ("`[p] += inset`, `[p+8] -= half` - asymmetric
  halving") misreads which register reaches the stores. Full
  trace, entry to exit (0x49fb0..0x49fe4, n set to 0x46 = 70 at
  0x3f278): eax = w = [p+8]-[p] (0x49fb6/0x49fb9); edx = n*w
  (imul 0x49fbb); ecx saves w; idiv 100 (0x49fca, TRUNCATION
  toward zero) -> inset; edx = w - inset = t (0x49fcc/0x49fce);
  eax = t, then `sar edx,31 / sub eax,edx / sar eax,1`
  (0x49fd0..0x49fd7) = t/2 TRUNCATED toward zero (checked at
  t = 13, -13, -1: all match C's `/2`); THEN BOTH stores use
  that same eax: `0x49fde add esi,eax` / `0x49fe0 sub edi,eax`
  with esi=[p], edi=[p+8] (0x49fd9/0x49fdb). The inset value
  never reaches a store - it is consumed forming t. The true
  law: half = trunc((w - trunc(w*n/100))/2), [p] += half,
  [p+8] -= half: a SYMMETRIC inset that keeps the CENTRAL n
  percent of the x-span (middle 70% for n=70; odd leftovers
  stay INSIDE the probe; w <= 3 leaves the block unchanged; the
  other two dwords [p+4]/[p+0xc] are never touched). C's two
  truncating divisions reproduce idiv and the sar-idiom exactly
  for both signs, so the port's blk_probe70 is the byte law
  with no normalisation.

- FINDING 3, THE PREDICATE ORDER IS FULL-FIRST, PROBE-SECOND -
  THE PR-149 WORDING HAD THEM SWAPPED, CORRECTED IN PLACE. The
  answer chain, verbatim operands (0x3f256..0x3f2b6): the four
  dwords [ecx+0xb1..0xbd] are copied to the stack block (esp..
  esp+0xc) with [esp+0x10] = 0x98274 (a table - unchased), and
  0x49fb0 runs on the COPY (0x3f28d/0x3f293); `add ecx,0xb1`
  (0x3f283) leaves ecx = the ladder's OWN un-inset block, and
  the FIRST slot +0x8 call gets `mov edx,ecx` (0x3f29b) - FULL
  extent; FALSE -> the inert exit 0x3f364 (0x3f2a4). Only the
  SECOND call gets `mov edx,esp` (0x3f2ad) - the PROBE; TRUE
  -> the merged tail (or dh,0x10 = bit 12 AC_DRAB_CATCH at
  0x3f2dc, or bh,0x4 = bit 10 AC_DRAB at 0x3f304, merged via
  0x49580 at 0x3f313, repnz-copied); FALSE -> `je 0x3f33f` =
  the AC_DRAB-alone tail (0x3f355). The PR-149 record had P2 =
  inset / P3 = full, which made its own text ask "when can P1
  be false while P3 is true?" - with the order corrected, the
  probe sits INSIDE the full extent by Findings 2+4 and all
  four PR-141 outcomes are consistent with ONE rectangle
  format: EDGE via the stored +0xc5 block; CATCH|DRAB inside
  the middle-70% band; DRAB alone inside the rung OUTSIDE the
  band; inert outside the rung. That resolves the standing
  "degenerate/ascending" worry the first draft of this note
  carried (deleted from the code comment before it shipped).

- FINDING 4, THE 0x23e00 SLOT IS A BOUNDS TEST OF TWO POINTS
  AGAINST ONE BLOCK, WHICH PINES THE WORD ROLES. Re-read whole
  (0x23e00..0x23e23): eax = p, edx = q; p[0] compared against
  q[0] (fail if jl) and q[8] (fail if jg); p[4] against q[4]
  (jl) and q[0xc] (jg); returns 1 or 0. INCLUSIVE bounds on
  all four sides (jl/jg pass equality). Two consequences this
  pass uses: (i) 0x49fb0's words 0 and 8 ARE the same pair the
  bounds test uses for x - the x-role of those words is now
  read, not inferred from arithmetic alone (the layout of the
  OTHER pair - y at 4/0xc - stays PR-149's open item 3, our
  item 1); (ii) a block whose x-words are INVERTED (q[0] >
  q[8]) can never satisfy the bounds test, so such a ladder
  answers INERT at every asker - the format the authored data
  uses is still open, but only ascending blocks can ever mean
  anything, and a leg pins the consequence. The asker side of
  every call stays PR-149's: the +0x68 getter hands the base
  family's self (0x23b60) or the lion's position block (0x23900
  = add eax,0xd6), and its first two dwords are p[0]/p[4] - so
  the port's asker point is the position point, and the lion
  asks through its own position block.

- THE CODE, AND WHAT EACH PART IS. New block in ported/
  ll_level.c above play_collide: ladder_class (the DRABINKA
  leaf filter - the one chain anchored end to end, PR-141);
  ll_blk/ll_pt + pt_in_blk (0x23e00 verbatim); blk_probe70
  (Finding 2, byte law, both truncations as C divisions);
  ladder_answer_core (the decision function: row gate by
  Finding 1's map, then P1 edge-first, P2 full-extent, P3
  probe -> merged/lone tails); blk_of_obj (the RUNG source:
  the SAME shape path play_collide's own two contact passes
  use - obj_shape_elem with its fi clamp and drawn polarity,
  then ll_seq_shape_bbox positioned at the object, with the
  no-margin-list skip rule ll_seq.h names); pt_of (the house
  position rounding); ladder_answer_for (the clamp, the
  ctor-shaped 1x1 fallback, the model-default edge, then the
  core). Two call sites in play_collide: the solid push pass
  and the non-solid PR-92 touch pass, both AFTER the shape
  meet and the push, mirroring the engine's answer-after-push
  order (0x552e0 -> 0x55230, PR-92); the answer is merged
  straight into the lion's pulse set - the port has no node
  list, and the node pop / merge-time row guard (0x54b6a:
  `[rec+8] == 0 || [rec+8] == [obj+0x5c]`) are item 4. The
  pulse lands after ll_player_step, so the NEXT iteration's
  transitions read it (verified against the player's own
  order: transitions evaluate first, p.sig zeroes mid-step
  after them, frame tails and this pass re-raise afterwards -
  the same window the PR-88 GEN pulses use).
  NAMED MODEL DEFAULTS (each a choice, each pinned by legs,
  none presented as read): the RUNG falls back to a 1x1 at the
  object when the object has no art/shape (the ctor's own
  1x1-default shape); the EDGE block is modelled as the same
  1x1 at the object - the ctor zeroes [obj+0xc9..0xd1] and
  NEVER stores +0xc5, so even the engine's default value there
  is un-read (PR-149), and a literal reading would be a
  garbage-dword degenerate at the world origin, unusable;
  P1's priority is a model behaviour of the shared chain,
  pinned as its own leg. WHAT THE CALL SITES DO NOT REPRODUCE
  (counted): the candidate walk is per-MOVER in the engine
  (0x52790 in 15 class units), while these passes run only
  while the LION is stepped and NOT in an ANTI_SOLID state
  (the port's existing contact gates) - object-object answers
  and mid-air asking are item 3, unchanged and now with this
  sharper edge.

## PR-151 — THE POST-TRANSITION HOOK IS THE PER-LEVEL BEHAVIOUR
## LAYER: THE kind-4 CONTACT SUPPLY IS A LION-CONTROLLER HOOK
## FEATURE (ENA/SADES-ERA CLASSES ONLY), THE ZARIA HOOK IS A
## TRANSITION REDIRECTOR, THE COMPANION LINK +0x112 IS THE
## STRONGEST K_GEN1 LEAD YET, AND THE NEXT ENTRY'S kind-4
## FRAMING IS CORRECTED (READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE;
## PR-138..149 PRECEDENT)

- WHY. The Next entry shipped with PR-150 named "the kind-4
  contact node and its +/-10 y-override" as the next CODE pass
  and claimed "the answer path can now PLANT a node". Before
  writing a line of code this pass checked that premise against
  the bytes, and it is wrong in one specific, checkable way:
  the answers of PR-150 plant kind-2 nodes (PR-149 F1 - the
  kind-2 builder 0x53f50 is the answer-COPYING one, and PR-150's
  own code note quotes that correctly), while the kind-4 nodes
  that the +/-10 y-override consumes are planted by something
  else entirely: a class-method hook at slot +0x90 that this
  project had never read. With the supply pinned, the ZARIA
  verdict is that ZARIA.01 supplies NO kind-4 contact at all -
  the third consecutive PR whose feature ZARIA data does not
  reach - so the kind-4 model code is deferred (see the new
  Next), and this pass ships as the reading record that closes
  the supply question and corrects the framing. The engine image
  is unchanged throughout (text.bin sha256 edf19a129e85efb8764
  457a0808e246ca4baf08a9111aa09be4ec99ce6b8c40e).

- FINDING 1, THE HOOK: THE CONTROLLER PIPELINE CALLS A
  PER-CLASS METHOD AFTER THE TRANSITION SCAN AND BEFORE THE
  LIVE-SET CLEAR. PR-132/133 read the compositor 0x536f0 end to
  end (the +0x8c key provider, the record key 0x523f0, the
  0x52000 transition scan with its (out1,out2) outputs, the
  0x535a0 record/row switch) but skipped what sits in the
  middle, and the port's model needs it. The full order now,
  0x53520..0x5359a verbatim: (a) copy the live set - [obj+0x60
  ..0x6b] plus the flag byte [obj+0x6c] - to a stack buffer
  (rep movs pair, 0x53531..0x53557); (b) evaluate the CURRENT
  row record's transition list [[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4]
  against that copy through 0x52000 (PR-150 F1b), writing the
  matched (row, N) pair to the caller's two out slots [TERMS
  FIXED by PR-157 F3, bracket inserted at the ledger recovery,
  PR-158: out1 = the TARGET STATE/record index (entry +0xd),
  out2 = the ROW index (entry +0x11); the applier writes
  [obj+0x5c] := out1 only on a state CHANGE (0x535ed) and the
  record cursor [[rec]+4] := out2 on the same state (0x53616)
  - every "row"/(N) comparison against [obj+0x5c] below is
  really a STATE-index comparison]; (c) call
  `[[obj+8]+0x90]` with (eax = self, edx = &out1, ebx = &out2)
  - THE HOOK; (d) 0x535a0 applies the (possibly rewritten) pair
  (PR-133's record/row switch); (e) 0x749a0 zeroes the 12/13-
  byte live set at [obj+0x60] (0x53583..0x5358e, the buffer
  address came from [esp+0x10] = [obj+0x60]). (d)+(e) confirm
  the port's shipped ordering (PR-88/150's window: transitions
  evaluate, then p->sig zeroes, later passes re-raise) - the
  engine clears only AFTER the scan and the hook. THE HOOK'S
  IMAGE-WIDE CALL SITES are exactly two: 0x5357d (this
  pipeline) and 0x3edaf (inside 0x3ed70, a method of another
  object family - reads [obj+0x40], calls +0x28/+0x84 first;
  unread, counted). Every class table has its own +0x90 slot,
  so the hook is the per-level behaviour layer. Read here: the
  base-chain hook 0x61670 (only its first arm, counted: if bit
  0x40 of the object's flag byte at [obj+0x0] is set, force
  (out1,out2) = (2,0) and clear [obj+0xb5]); the ZARIA-class
  hook (Finding 2); the ENA-class hook (Finding 3); the
  SADES-class hook 0x2e6a0 (Finding 3, two stores read by
  PR-108, body not read here). The per-table census of +0x90
  across all 24+ tables was NOT taken this pass (counted).

- FINDING 2, ZARIA'S HOOK IS A TRANSITION REDIRECTOR, READ
  WHOLE (0x1e250..0x1e2ef). The TLewZaria tables hold it at
  +0x90 (TLewZaria 0x96960 + 0x90 = 0x1e250; TLewZariaB's base
  0x97970 holds 0x61670, the base hook; ZARIA OVERRIDES it).
  With (out1,out2) at (edx,ebx), verbatim and in order:
  (a) if out1 == 4 and [obj+0x10e] * [obj+0x6d] > 0, call
  0x53670 - PR-108's facing flipper (it negates the facing
  [obj+0x6d] only when the state record's byte +0x15 has bit
  0x8, then invalidates); (b) if the current row [obj+0x5c]
  != 0xa and out1 == 0xa, subtract 0x1e = 30 from [obj+0xad] -
  the same field the ZARIA base ctor defaults to 0x1f4 = 500
  (PR-129): a per-redirect countdown bite; (c) if the armed
  flag [obj+0x12a] != 0, REWRITE the transition: out1 = 9,
  out2 = 0, clear [obj+0x12a] (a one-shot redirect of whatever
  transition just fired, to row 9 line 0 - the same field
  PR-145 quoted as armed by a type-0xc record in 0x52cc0's
  context; see Finding 5's correction); (d) if [obj+0x5c] == 9
  and set bit 2 (byte 0 bit 0x4 of [obj+0x60]) is set in the
  just-copied live set, set [obj+0x116] = 1 - the flag PR-70
  named from the kind-21 message and PR-104's death path reads;
  (e) if out1 == 0xc and global ds:0xcef64 == 0, or out1 ==
  0xb and ds:0xcef68 == 0, CANCEL the transition (out1 = the
  current row, out2 = 0); other values pass; (f) tail-call the
  base hook 0x61670. What ds:0xcef64 / ds:0xcef68 mean and who
  writes them is un-read (counted); [obj+0x10e] is written at
  0x24ce5/0x283d3 (regions unread, counted). The hook reads
  and rewrites the SAME pair 0x52000 wrote, so "row 9", "row
  10", "row 11/12" here are positions in this controller's own
  state script - a per-level veto layer over the state machine,
  in CODE, not in the .MOV.
  [ARMS THE REDIRECT: within the ZARIA region, 0x1e132 is a
  record handler (unreferenced as a table slot - reached how?
  counted) whose record+0x4 TYPE field dispatches: type 5 runs
  a static counter [ds:0xa94f4]++, [[ds:0xcef40]+0x38c] and
  0x44900, then posts through 0x52cc0 with edx = 9 (PR-129's
  dead +0x10 handler, read there); type 0xc writes [obj+0x12a]
  = 1 - THE ARM. Other [obj+0x12a] writers exist at
  0x2419d (ENA region), 0x2c28f/0x2c2ac (values 2/1) and -1
  writers at 0x2ba15/0x2bfc2 (KADMAR era); the ZARIA ctor
  zeroes it (0x1e0ba). No live ZARIA-path writer was found
  this pass - the only ZARIA-region arm store sits in the
  dead handler - so whether ZARIA's hook ever runs branch (c)
  at runtime is an OPEN question, counted as item 2.]

- FINDING 3, THE kind-4 CONTACT SUPPLY IS THE ENA-CLASS HOOK,
  AND THE SADES HOOK WRITES ITS ARRAY: PR-108/149's "chain at
  0x24678" IS FINDING 1'S HOOK. The TLewEna table 0x988ec +
  0x90 = 0x245b0 (the table identities now pinned: 0x988ec is
  TLewEna's, from PR-129's pair census; the slot arithmetic
  cross-checks - TLewEna + 0xcc = 0x989b8 = 0x50340, the +0xcc
  contact walker PR-108 recorded in "14 tables"). Its body,
  re-read: branch on the flag dword [self+0x0] (> 0x640) and a
  row-cursor window ([obj+0x5c] in 0xa..0xe, or == 0x11) that
  forces (out1,out2) = (1,0); then the zone pass, gated by
  [obj+0x12e] == 0 AND [obj+0x12a] != 0: read the array at
  [obj+0x136] (entry dwords 0/4/8; the third non-zero), take
  the LION SINGLETON ([ds:0xcef40]+0x394), write [lion+0x106]
  = 0, and for each entry build a kind-4 contact on the LION's
  list exactly as PR-108 recorded (builder 0x53eb0 with
  `add ecx,0xd2`, then the kind-4 patches [rec+4]=4,
  [rec+0x1d]=entry dword[2], x from entry dword[0]). THE
  ARRAY'S WRITER: the only [obj+0x136..0x13e] writer found is
  a per-level hook itself - 0x2e6a0, the TLewSades +0x90 slot
  (TLewSades 0x9c958 + 0x90), which PR-108 read setting the
  count to 1 and a value at [obj+0x13a]. So the array is
  RUNTIME state that per-level controller code maintains, not
  instantiated .des placement/attach data: PR-108's open
  question ("whether that [obj+0x136] array is the authored
  attach/child data ... PR-93's 0,0 entries") is ANSWERED -
  NO. And the ZARIA-era hooks never build kind-4 contacts:
  TLewZaria's hook (Finding 2) has no zone pass, and the
  ZARIA-base slot 0x61670 is the tiny flag-force hook. VERDICT
  for the port: no ZARIA-era controller plants a kind-4 node
  on the lion, so the +/-10 override has no supply at ZARIA -
  the model would be a no-op there, exactly as the ladder
  answer was, but WITHOUT a data path that could ever light it
  up in this level. The kind-4 code pass is therefore deferred
  to when the port reaches an ENA/SADES/TUNGA-era controller
  (the new Next). What the kind-4 contact MEANS at those
  levels (it pulls the lion's [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe] force
  pair +/-10 toward its stored x/y with the +/-8 dead band -
  PR-98/108 read that consumer exactly; its producer is now
  read too) stays a design note, not a ZARIA claim.

- FINDING 4, THE COMPANION LINK [obj+0x112] AND THE HAND-OFF
  METHOD +0x100 - THE STRONGEST K_GEN1 LEAD FOUND SO FAR. The
  ZARIA controller's ctor region (0x1e1a2..0x1e1db, inside the
  0x1e0a0 ZARIA ctor chain PR-129 read) LINKS a companion: it
  builds a query buffer (0x497b0, flags 0x400, seed pointer at
  [ds:0x961fc] = 0x1034c - the seed's format is unread,
  counted) and stores `0x4dcc0(<level singleton>, &query)` - a
  level-object SEARCH - into [obj+0x112]. Which named object
  ZARIA links this way is the first thing the next K_GEN1 pass
  should read (the seed format at 0x497b0's grammar decides
  it). The link's readers: the base +0x100 method 0x50c70
  (which the TLewZaria and TLewZariaB tables hold at +0x100,
  and the base pair 0xa2218 too) resolves it as `[[obj+0x112]]
  ` then `[[that+8]+0xdc]` (a per-class getter - the same
  getter slot PR-149 counted unread at 0x3f1cf's +0x3c family
  neighbourhood), and 0x50be6 guards a call path on
  [obj+0x112] != 0. THE HAND-OFF ITSELF: the ENA variant
  0x24440 (+0x100 at TLewEna) does the same resolution, then
  builds a 12-byte set with `or bl,0x40` into BYTE 6 = SET BIT
  54 = K_GEN1 (0x24492..0x2449f - the port's own LL_SIG_K_
  GEN1 number, PR-147's map) and 0x49580-ORs it into the
  RESOLVED OBJECT's live set [esi+0x60] (0x244a2..0x244a5),
  THEN tail-calls the base 0x50c70 (which calls slot +0x118
  with the companion, copies [self+0xb1] into [companion+0xb1]
  when the latter holds 0x14 = 20, and continues into [obj+
  0xee]/0xb5/0xe0/0x531b0 - partially read, counted). THIS IS
  THE FIRST RAISER OF K_GEN1 OUTSIDE the row GEN tails
  (PR-69) and the kind-9 messages (PR-70; PR-147's closed
  poster census) that this project has found - and it targets
  a named companion by construction, not the asker. Two
  cautions keep it a LEAD, not an answer: the ZARIA tables
  hold the BASE +0x100 (the K_GEN1 raise sits in the ENA
  variant's preamble, not in the base body - no ZARIA-path
  raise visible this pass); and the +0x100 method's two call
  sites (0x50c2a, inside a method guarded by [obj+0x112] != 0
  and the re-entry flag ds:0xcef4c, right after slot +0x110
  was called at the row cursor's value; and 0x41b6a, inside a
  method whose head dispatches on [obj+0x160] - an ENA-era
  mode switch) were not read to the point of naming WHEN they
  fire (both bodies counted, item 5). The K_GEN1 arm of
  PR-146/149/150 stays OPEN and named as the blocker - but its
  open list now has the companion query and the two +0x100
  bodies at the top, above the 0x238e4/0x52607 leads PR-150
  added.

- FINDING 5, A CORRECTION TO PR-129'S SHIPPED CENSUS SENTENCE,

  handler) does pass edx=9, but 0x3f77e passes edx=[self+0x4c]

  method 0x3f760, reached from a class-table dword at
  0xa0790 (the TLewTunga2 region, 0xa0624 pair - a different
  table base nearby, which class not pinned, counted): its
  body is a MESSAGE RECEIVER for message TYPE 0x1c (28) - if
  the received record's type dword [msg+4] == 0x1c and its
  third field is non-zero, it posts through 0x52cc0 with
  edx=[self+0x4c] (and 0x52bb0 first, unread). A class near
  the ladder's own code (the ladder answer method 0x3f1c0 ends
  at 0x3f37a; the TUNGA-era KLINA linals use the same .MOV
  shape - PR-150 F5) that receives type-28 messages and posts
  kind-9-shaped ones is squarely on the K_GEN1 road: counted
  as a lead, not read. The 14 sites for the future pass:
  0x1e185, 0x2475a, 0x247aa, 0x24807, 0x274b1, 0x33ee7,
  0x373f0, 0x374a9, 0x3dc5f, 0x3e54a, 0x3e727, 0x3f77e,
  0x45aed, 0x45b10 (the last two in the atc_on action region

## PR-152 — THE COMPANION HAND-OFF IS AN AUTHORED, GATED
## FEATURE: A PER-CLASS +0x104 ROW WINDOW (ZARIA: ROW
## POSITIONS 7-8 = THE `4,6,GEN AC_TIME` LINES OF A_WALK), A
## SIGNAL-FIELD MATCH ON THE CONSTANT 6, A KEY-REGISTRY
## COMPANION RESOLUTION (NOT A NAME SEARCH), AND THE FULL
## CANDIDATE CHAIN TO K_GEN1 NAMED LINK BY LINK (READING
## RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE; PR-138..151 PRECEDENT)

- WHY. PR-151's Next put the K_GEN1 arm reading pass first and
  named its lead order: (a) the companion-query grammar and the
  seed, (b) the two +0x100 call-site bodies, (c) the 0x52cc0
  sites, (d) the [obj+0x12a] arm. This pass read (a) and (b)
  and found the engine's answer to PR-151's open question
  "what makes +0x100 fire" - plus a correction to this
  session's own PR-151 framing of 0x4dcc0. The image is
  unchanged (text.bin sha256 edf19a129e85efb8764457a0808e24
  6ca4baf08a9111aa09be4ec99ce6b8c40e).

- FINDING 1, WHAT 0x4dcc0 IS (CORRECTING PR-151'S "LEVEL-
  OBJECT SEARCH" - PR-103'S READING WAS RIGHT). Re-read whole
  (0x4dcc0..0x4dd32+): 0x57a40 initializes a line-reader state
  (zeroes [st+0], sets [st+4] to the descriptor-list end
  0x96200 then to the root 0x961fc), then ONE comma-delimited
  token is read with the scanf-style format at 0x91f2a =
  ' %[^,\r\n] , ', and that token goes to the PLACEMENT
  FACTORY 0x4df10 (0x4dcdc) - exactly PR-103's "the readers of
  the placement grammar, the token is the line's first field".
  Then the rest of the line is split on '\' (literal 0x91f36),
  two 0x57a00 calls over the parsed parts, and the created
  object's +0x7c is called with the parsed x,y - PR-103's
  unread +0x7c, still unread. So PR-151 F4's "a level-object
  SEARCH" was WRONG (its F6-era wording, bracketed in place).
  THE AUTHORED PATTERN THIS SERVES: ZWIERZ1.DES (ZARIA.01, at
  /tmp/opencode/pr138/des/, re-read) carries SUB-LINES under
  animal placements - `POCISK,jajo.ani,jajo.mov,0,0` under
  both SEP2 and SEP, `PICT,panc.seq,20,29` under NOSOROG -
  and "read one line and run the factory on it" IS 0x4dcc0:
  the sub-line child-creation mechanism (the port joins these
  lines but never instantiates their children).

- FINDING 2, THE ZARIA CONSTRUCTOR CALL IS A KEY-REGISTRY
  RESOLUTION, NOT A NAMED-OBJECT LOOKUP. The ctor-region call
  (0x1e1a2..0x1e1db): a 0x18-byte state buffer is built with
  EVERYTHING ZERO except a pointer field at +0x9 = 0x961fc and
  a flag field at +0xb = 0x400; 0x497b0 is a token-list
  builder over a string at [q+5] (0x49a10 pre-fills via
  [[0xcef14]+0x14] when q[+1] != 0, 0x57990 appends NUL-
  delimited tokens): with the string NULL the name test at
  0x497c6..0x497de PASSES AS EMPTY, then [[0xcef14]+0xc] is
  called with edx=&q and its result stored at q[+1]; a zero
  result tail-calls 0x49620 - a GLOBAL last-query cache at
  ds:0xceedc that runs the descriptor's match routine,
  string-compares with 0x751b8 against the literal 0x91c68
  ('Second throw! %s\n' - an engine debug trace) and installs
  the state globally. And [ds:0xcef14] IS THE KEY-REGISTRY
  SINGLETON: 0x5c8c3 sets it to the static object at 0xcf3d8,
  whose initializer 0x5bf10 builds a descriptor list from the
  ROOT 0x961fc - whose first entry is (0x1034c, 0x57a00): an
  EXECUTABLE MATCH STUB AT 0x1034c IN .data (the "SQV" bytes
  at that address are code - `push ebx; sub esp,0x18; test
  cl,0x4; ...` - hand-written, decoded this pass with objdump
  on raw bytes because objdump's listing boundary hid it);
  bit 0x04 of its edx flag byte selects code-range tables
  (0x961c4, called through 0x74bc0/0x74be0) vs the name/
  registry branch (0x96138 control block + 0x57a00). THE
  DESCRIPTOR VOCABULARY IS THE SIGNAL VOCABULARY: the list
  continues at 0x9620c as 3-dword entries (-12, -10, -10, 1,
  ...), and 0x9627c holds (5, 0, 0x10000, 0x70000) - 5 =
  K_F5, 0x10000 = bit 16 = AC_RECT, 0x70000 = bits 16..18
  (PR-147's word model) in one entry. VERDICT for lead (a):
  ZARIA names its companion NOTHING in authored bytes - the
  name field is empty and the resolution is by key registry at
  runtime; "which object" cannot be answered statically (it
  needs the receiver-consumer trace, Finding 5's open item).
  Side negative while looking for the companion name: the
  literal LEWPL exists NOWHERE in the image (byte scan; only

  the session's label for the player's OWN .MOV text, not a
  factory name. ZARIA1.DES itself (extracted from the full-CD
  LEVELDES in LL.iso, now at /tmp/opencode/pr152/ld/) was

  lew.des` (controller class, .ani block, controller script)
  and there are NO sub-lines under it.

- FINDING 3, THE HAND-OFF MACHINERY AND ITS TWO PER-CLASS
  GATES. The block sequence 0x50af0..0x50c2c (entry head not
  pinned - counted) contains, after a live-set bit-0x04 clear
  and the [obj+0x116] set at a byte flag (0x50af0..0x50b08,
  the [obj+0x67] bit 0x20 - the PR-104-era draw flag), TWO
  entry-shaped blocks that both start by calling the
  `[[self.vt+0x104](self, [self+0x5c])` GATE GETTER:

  scan) and 0x50b85 (if the gate is FALSE, inert exit
  0x50c30). THE +0x104 GATE IS A PER-CLASS ROW-CURSOR WINDOW,
  read verbatim: TLewZaria 0x1e200 = true iff the row cursor
  is 7 or 8; TLewEna 0x24270: 5 or 6; TLewSades 0x2e190:
  0x1d/0x1e (29/30); TLewTunga2 0x612f0: 7 or 9; the base
  pair's 0x26f30 = `xor eax,eax; ret` = FALSE (no base-class
  hand-off). THEN the scan (0x50bb4..): `call
  [self.vt+0x108]` - A SECOND per-class getter - and when its
  value M is negative the CURRENT row's transition-record
  array [[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4] is scanned for a record
  whose +0x4 DWORD equals -M (`neg edx; mov eax,[record+4];
  cmp eax,edx`, 0x50bdd..0x50be4) [REFINED BY PR-159 F5: it
  is NOT a scan - no loop. It loads the CURRENT STATE RECORD
  [[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4] (0x50bd4-0x50bda) and compares
  ITS ROW CURSOR, [record+4], ONCE against -M (0x50be2) -
  the direct consumer PR-158 sought: the cursor can only ever
  hold an authored (N) written by a transition match (PR-159
  F1), so TLewZaria's -6 matches a state whose transition set
  (6). And there is a step (0) before this window: 0x50b9b
  tests [obj+0x9d] == 1 and on true calls [self.vt+0x114]
  (edx = the caller's [ebp-0x4] slot), falling through either
  way]; when M is non-negative the check is instead [obj+
  0x9d] == M (0x50bc8). On a match,
  with [self+0x112] != 0 and the re-entry flag ds:0xcef4c
  == 0, set ds:0xcef4c=1, call [self.vt+0x110](self,
  [self+0x5c]) (0x50c0a), and call [self.vt+0x100] (0x50c2a).
  If the companion is absent or the global counter [ds:0xa94f4]
  != 0, the (out1,out2) pair is ZEROED instead (0x50b61..
  0x50b7f) - part of PR-151 open item 9. THE +0x108 CENSUS,
  verbatim: TLewZaria and TLewZariaB `mov eax,0xfffffffa;
  ret` = -6 (match constant 6); SADES -4 (match 4); ENA2 and
  the BASE pair 0xa2218 +1 ([obj+0x9d] test); TUNGA2 -14
  (match 14); TLewEna a computation over the row cursor
  (`lea eax,[edx-5]; cmp eax,4; ...`, body unread). THE
  PORT'S SIGNAL ENUM maps those constants to NAMES (the
  ll_play.h enum: 6 = AC_DEADDUP, 4 = AC_DUP, 14 = AC_STONE,
  1 = AC_BLOK_Y) - but the enum names are the session's own
  best-guess tokens, so the HONEST claim is the NUMBER 6.
  AND 6 IS AN AUTHORED VALUE IN EXACTLY THE GATED ROWS:
  ZARIA's gate opens only at row POSITIONS 7-8 (the +0x104
  window), and in LEW.MOV (the ZARIA controller script,
  /tmp/opencode/mov/ZARIA.01_LEW.ZAR_LEW.MOV) the row lines
  AT POSITIONS 7-8 of the multi-row states carry exactly 6 as
  their second field: `[A_WALK]` pos 7 = `4,6,GEN AC_TIME`,

  pose ("row field 2 = 6", the row-gate field PR-150 item 6

## PR-153 — THE K_GEN1 CHAIN TRACE: THE MESSAGE QUEUE, ITS
## CONSUMER AND THE RECEIVER CENSUS (ZARIA'S "DEAD" HANDLER IS
## ALIVE - A DISASSEMBLY BOUNDARY ARTIFACT); THE ROW-RECORD
## LAYOUT CLOSES THE HAND-OFF LAW (FIELD 2 AT RECORD +0x4); THE
## STATE-MACHINE PIPELINE IS ONE TICK METHOD (0x536f0) THAT
## EVERY LION TICK CALLS; BIT-54 SETTER BYTE-VERIFIED; THE
## HAND-OFF RECEIVER'S ACTUAL EFFECTS NAMED (READING RECORD -
## NO CODE CHANGE; PR-138..152 PRECEDENT)

- WHY. PR-152's Next named two decisive gaps: (a) the record
  layout behind the hand-off scan, (b) the queue consumer +
  the posted node's type. Both closed - and the pass surfaced
  two corrections bigger than the questions asked. Image
  unchanged (text.bin sha256 edf19a129e85efb8764457a0808e24
  6ca4baf08a9111aa09be4ec99ce6b8c40e).

- FINDING 1, THE ROW-RECORD LAYOUT - HAND-OFF LAW CLOSED. The
  array [[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4] holds 72-byte records: the
  allocator 0x518f0 gives 0x48 and 0x517e0 copy-constructs
  from the parsed line (dword@+0x0 = field 1 = the FRAME
  SELECTOR per PR-133, dword@+0x4 = field 2 = PR-100's
  gate/threshold value, then word fields +0x8/+0xa/+0xc,
  dword +0xe...). The vtable is at +0x44 (0xa260c/0xa25d4
  sub-tables; 0x535a0,
  the row switch, calls slot +0x1c = row-ENTER and +0x20 =
  row-EXIT through it). So the hand-off scan's `mov eax,
  [record+0x4]` IS the authored second field: ZARIA's -6
  constant matches exactly the rows at POSITIONS 7-8 of
  A_WALK (`4,6,GEN AC_TIME`/`5,6,GEN AC_TIME`) and A_ZABLOK
  (`4,6`/`5,6`) - inside the +0x104 window - and no other
  ZARIA rows at those positions (A_JUMP 225/900, A_DEAD 400,
  ...). PR-152 open item 7 CLOSED at the layout level; "which
  state reaches rows 7-8 in play" stays (item 5 below). The
  two record systems are now separated for good: TRANSITION
  records (compiled `( N )=SIG` exits) are 21-byte blocks at
  [[obj+0x1a]], count [obj+0x22], walked by 0x52000 (stride
  0x15), kind byte +0xc -> EventSet::match 0x47e40 (a cs-
  table switch at 0x47e30 on [rec+0xc] 0..3), target +0xd,

## PR-154 — THE BIT-54 BRIDGE, PASS 1: THE STAMP OBJECT IS A
## PLACEMENT-LIST OBJECT, NOT A SIGNAL OBJECT (ITS CLASS 0x98278
## IS AN 8-BYTE TWO-DWORD RECORD; THE 0x44900 STAMP IS DEMO/
## COUNTDOWN BOOKKEEPING) - THE "ROW-55 STAMP" BRIDGE HYPOTH-
## ESIS IS CLOSED NEGATIVE; THE KIND-9 HIT-PIPELINE CENSUS IS
## COMPLETE (EXACTLY TWO kind-9 SITES, BOTH HAND-OFF ARMS) AND
## THE kind OBJECT IS THE ONLY UNEXPLORED FUNCTIONAL ARM OF A
## HAND-OFF; THE KIND TABLES ARE RUNTIME-ONLY (BSS, NEVER
## STATICALLY WRITTEN); THE "4 DYNAMIC-edx ENQUEUE SITES" ARE
## ALL CORRECTED - ONE IS THE STATIC TYPE-0xC POSTER AT THE
## PLAYER, AND A FIFTH ENQUEUE POSTS TYPE 5 ONTO A FRESH
## COPY-CLASS OBJECT; NODE KEY GETTERS CHAIN (PR-126 ITEM 3
## CLOSED - AUTHORED ROWS COMPOSE THEIR KEY THROUGH THE CHAIN)
(READING RECORD - NO CODE CHANGE; PR-138..153 PRECEDENT)

- WHY. PR-153's Next named the exact open question - who
  writes bit 54 (or the row-55 stamp) into the right object -
  and the four candidate threads (a)-(d). This pass pulls all
  four and closes two of them plus one PR-153 open item. Im-
  age unchanged (text.bin sha256 edf19a129e85efb8764457a0808
  e246ca4baf08a9111aa09be4ec99ce6b8c40e).

- FINDING 1, THE STAMP OBJECT IS A LIST, NOT A SIGNAL OBJECT.
  The class at 0x98278 (stored by ctor 0x443b0 at [t+0x14]
  and every +0x20,+0x2c,... up to [t+0x83] - a 10-item array
  of {0, class, 0} twelve-byte slots inside the 0x8c-byte ob-
  ject): its slots are +0x10 = 0x23ed0 (a FREE-path receiver:
  bit 2 of the flags -> free a shared EMPTY STRING whose des-
  ctor block is the TLewZaria table tail at 0x96854..0x96858,
  length 0; bit 1 -> 0x5c370 free-self), +0x14 = 0x23ea0 (a
  two-dword COPY: [dst]=[src], [dst+4]=[src+4], no vtable
  write), +0x18 = 0x23e00, +0x24 = 0x23e30 (a vector tail-
  trim over [obj+0x4]/+0x8/+0xc). So 0x98278 is the class of
  a TWO-DWORD RECORD with a plain copy verb - demo/counter
  record shape, not a lion. The 0x443b0 ctor never stores a
  class PAIR at [t+0x8]/[t+0xc] - those stay 0 (the factory
  0x4d612 alloc-then-construct stores no vtable either) - so
  the [[0xcef40]+0x38c] singleton is NOT a classed lion-style
  object. CONSEQUENCE: the PR-153 bridge reading "or the row-
  55 stamp" is CLOSED NEGATIVE - 0x44900's [t+0x5c]=55 and
  [t+0x6c]=count land in a list object with no receiver slot;
  the bit-54 question must be answered by a live-SET writer,
  not by a stamp. The builder block sits in the main-.des key
  chain AFTER the 'lew' compare (the compare method 0x76d20 at
  0x4d06f, literal 'lew' 0x91e59) and inside the 'demolist'
  region (literal 0x91e82 at 0x4d157); the 0x8c build at
  0x4d60d is guarded by a registry search whose query is the
  literal 'none' (0x4d5d6 -> 0x57c60, then 0x57dd0 with capa-
  city 0x42) - exact key attribution stays open (item 6).

- FINDING 2, THE kind-9 HIT-PIPELINE CENSUS IS COMPLETE. The
  14 sites of 0x52cc0, kind (edx) read raw-bytes-correct: 9 =
  EXACTLY TWO, 0x1e185 (ZARIA's receiver type-5 arm, PR-153)
  and 0x274b1 (the sibling 0x27470, PR-153); then 2 (0x2475a,
  0x247aa), 1 (0x24807), 0x31 (the 0x27470 pair), 0x18
  (0x33ee7), and the dynamic ones: [esi+0x8] (0x374a9), [ecx+
  0xee] (0x3e54a), [esi+0xf6] (0x3e727), [ebx+0x4c] (0x3f77e,
  PR-152's correction stands), [ebx+0x16] and [ebx+0x8]
  (0x45aed/0x45b10); 0x373f0/0x3dc5f unread (item 7). 0x56600
  (entry 0x56602 per its raw head - PR-153 already noted the
  boundary): if kind < ds:0xcf0b4, kind-object = ds:0xcf0ac
  [kind*4], then call [[self+8]+0x18](self, kind-obj). Only
  the LADDER table runs real code at +0x18 (0x3f0f0); every
  lion table is the bare-ret 0x23c60. So the kind-9 hit path
  exists ONLY for hand-off receivers, and its only functional
  arm is the kind-object passed into the companion's +0x18.

- FINDING 3, THE KIND TABLES ARE RUNTIME-ONLY. ds:0xcf0ac
  (array) and ds:0xcf0b4 (count) sit in the all-zero BSS
  block 0xcf090..0xcf0d0; an image-wide disp32 census finds
  EXACTLY two references (0x56604, 0x5660e - both inside
  0x56600), and an immediate-reference census over
  0xcf080..0xcf0e0 finds no builder either (only 0x567xx/
  0x60ea4 reads neighbours; 0x1cbb2 touches 0xcf084). Kind
  objects are created at runtime through a base-relative store
  not yet located (item 2). This does NOT close the path - it
  says the census cannot: a runtime kind table can hold a
  kind-9 object in play. THE DECIDING LEAD MOVES TO: which
  objects carry a non-bare-ret +0x18 (the ladder-table family
  among level-placed objects) and who builds the kind table.

- FINDING 4, A FOURTH 0x44900 CALL SITE INSIDE LION BASE CODE.
  0x50720 (raw-decoded; entry): pushes the object, edx=[obj+

  0x52bb0 read whole: kind 1 = position-delta move through the

  table's +0x10 slot): kinds != 0x10 -> 0x52bb0; kind 0x10 ->
  Finding 3.

  slot called with edx=2; then the demolist stamp:
  inc ds:0xa94f4 and 0x44900([[ds:0xcef40]+0x38c], edx=count)

- FINDING 3, THE GENERIC SIGNAL-DELIVERY LAW: kind-0x10 +
  magic token. At 0x53770's kind-0x10 arm: IF [rec+8] ==
  0x8138764 (a magic token - the same immediate appears at
  0x2882d) THEN bit-index byte = [rec+0xc]; build a one-bit

  PRNG raiser uses) and 0x49580-OR it into [self+0x60]. ANY
  receiver whose chain reaches 0x53770 can be handed ANY signal

  PR-144 item (3) ("can a full-HP object reach K_GEN1") is
  CLOSED YES through this path.

- FINDING 1, THE STATE-MACHINE CONSTRUCTOR IS A CLASS SLOT
  (+0x7C = 0x537f0, entry 0x537f2 - boundary rule again). A
  dword-slot census finds 141 tables holding it; DIRECT TABLE
  READS confirm TLewZaria 0x96960+0x7c, TLewZariaB 0x97a98,
  LINA's final pair 0xa1dfc, the LADDER pair 0x97cdc and BAL's
  0xa17dc ALL carry +0x7C=0x537f0 and +0x2c=0x53d80 - the
  base family universally. Base-ctor 0x531f2: [obj+0x50]=0
  (rows NOT built yet), [obj+0x58]=0, [obj+0x5c]=1 (INITIAL
  STATE = 1 - PR-70's "[+0x5c]==1 start state" now named),
  [obj+0x54]=ds:0xcf0e4 (the global default CONTEXT block);
  verb +0x2c (0x53d80) replaces that default with a PRIVATE
  0x28-byte block (0x5c320 + ctor 0x56620 edx=1; 0x53db0 re-
  stores the default and runs [[ctx+8]+0x14](edx=2) first).
  0x537f0 ITSELF: reads the placement record's remainder with
  0x49920 (custom scanf, see F5) using the class format ' %[^,],
  %[^,],%d,%d' = ANI, MOV, x, y; calls 0x53850, which regis-
  ters the object's OWN authored parameter entries; then the
  row builder 0x53974: count = [[list]+0x8]; (count+1)*4 bytes
  via 0x76a64 -> [obj+0x50]; zero via 0x749a0; for every pa-
  ram entry: key from the entry's name (0x57d30 mode edx=3,
  key formats ' %[^[\r
] ' = name up to '[' or EOL, ' [%[^]]]'
  = a bracket suffix), lookup 0x31f20 (registry 0xceff8 via
  [[ds:0xcef40]+0x398]'s class verb +0x4 / 0x10598 list-off-
  set walk, 8-byte entries); rows[i++] := the FOUND RECORD;
  [obj+0x58] := count [BINDING REFINED BY PR-159 F3: the
  store runs inside the helper 0x53480 - record := class verb
  +0x84, class verb +0x88 when that returns null (0x534a4-
  0x534b1); store INDEX := 0x53440(name): a scan of the ob-
  ject's OWN parameter-entry list [obj+0x3c] (count +8,
  stride 8, compare 0x76a69) with the position counter IN-
  CREMENTED BEFORE comparing (0x53460) -> 1-BASED position,
  0 if not found - the loop counter and the store index are
  different things; the row-builder loop (0x539aa-0x539cd)
  builds the key via 0x57d30 in mode edx=2 with the 0x922ba
  format. With (count+1)*4 zeroed: rows[0]=NULL and initial
  [obj+0x5c]=1 = the FIRST BOUND PARAM ENTRY - the state-
  index base is PROVEN 1-based]; then [[cls]+0x2c] (context),
  the entry
  rows[[obj]+0x5c] gets ITS class verb [[rec+0x44]+0x1c](rec)
  (ENTER), and the keys are consumed/marked (0x57a00 edx=1).
  So ROWS[STATE] = THE AUTHORED STATE RECORD, bound BY NAME AT
  PLACEMENT, and the pool is consumed as it binds.

- FINDING 2, THE REGISTRY: ds:0xceff8 HAS ONLY 7 REFERENCES
  image-wide (0x514f6/0x5150d/0x51a2c/0x51a8e = level-load key
  handling, 0x53861/0x539dd = F1's ctor, 0xa2340 static). The
  main-.des key chain 0x519xx reads keys 'sample' (%d), 'time_
  scale' (%d) - both 0x57a00-inserts - and 'seq': its 's'
  branch formats ' %[^ ,]%*[ ,]' to read a NAME, then

  and stores the result at ds:0xceff4. So authored 'seq NAME,

  'seq' occurs ZERO times in the extracted satellites (ANI2.
  DES, ZAR.BLK, LEVELDES, ETAPY, ANIMACJE greps) - ZARIA's

  ITSELF by PR-158 F2: the ladder answer method reads

## PR-159 — THE ROW CURSOR HAS NO INCREMENTER: ITS COMPLETE
## WRITER LAW IS CLOSED (a transition match at 0x53616, or the
## tail of the CLONE/ctor path at 0x300e6 - the 0x300d7 site
## that PR-157 F7 called a restart idiom IS object creation);
## ROW PROGRESS LIVES IN THE THRESHOLD/ACCUMULATOR ENTRY-WALK
## (PR-100/101) AND NEVER TOUCHES THE CURSOR; THE CURSOR'S
## BASE THEREFORE IS THE AUTHORED 1-BASED (N) - PR-157 F4's
## consumer-6 row shifts to the `3,6` line; A NEW LAW: THE
## TRANSITION PIPELINE SELF-RAISES AC_TIME FROM A PER-STATE
## MATCH-COUNT AGAINST A RECORD WORD (0x53626-0x5365c); THE
## rows[] BINDING HELPER PROVES THE STATE-INDEX SPACE 1-BASED
(READING; no code, no new test - the PR-138..158 precedent)

- WHY. PR-158's Next named the first read: WHO advances a
  state record's row cursor [[rec]+4] while playback runs -
  the applier only SETS it from the authored (N) and nobody
  increments it in any window read so far. The answer decided
  two open questions (the cursor's 0/1-based nature; PR-157
  F7's reset framing) and exposed a new engine law (a real
  AC_TIME mechanism) plus the rows[] binding helper.

- FINDING 1, THE COMPLETE WRITER LAW OF [[rec]+4] (the record
  = [[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4], the current state's row-array
  entry): exactly TWO writers exist in every window read, and
  NEITHER is an incrementer. (a) The transition applier's
  same-state arm, re-read whole (0x53602-0x53626): it loads
  [[obj+0x50]+[state]*4], reads the record's +4 cursor,
  compares it with the matched entry's row out-value
  (0x53612 `cmp esi,edx`), and when they DIFFER writes it
  (0x53616) and runs the class verb +0xac; when equal BOTH
  are skipped (0x53614 -> 0x53626). (b) 0x300d7-0x300e6 -
  the window PR-157 F7 called the "reset a state's row"
  idiom - is the TAIL OF A CLONE/CONSTRUCT PATH (0x30083-
  0x300f8): 0x5c320 alloc, 0x54030 ctor, four field copies
  (+0xee/+0xf2/+0xf6/+0xfa), a class pair store 0x9c05c/
  0x9c054 (0x300bf/0x300c6 - 0x9c05c is a base-family table:
  direct read gives +0x2c = 0x53d80 and +0x7c = 0x537f0,
  PR-157 F1's universal pair), and only THEN the tail:
  [esi+0x5c] := 1, rows[1]'s +4 cursor := 0, then a copy
  verb [[cls]+0x4] at 0x300fe. That is NEW-OBJECT INITIAL-
  IZATION, not mid-game state restart. Meanwhile row progress
  inside a state runs entirely in the threshold/accumulator
  entry-walk (PR-100/101's law at 0x522c1-0x5235c, re-ground
  verbatim this pass): the state record's class verb
  [[rec-class]+0x18] iterates entries by POINTER chain (the
  loop body 0x522fc-0x52336 reads the entry's class at
  [entry+4], gets a set via [entry-class+0xc], ORs it into
  the key through 0x49580, reads a threshold and gates on
  [obj+0xa1]) - the cursor is NEVER consulted. CONSEQUENCES:
  (i) PR-158 item 2 and its F4 question CLOSE: no row-
  advancement writer exists; the cursor is a pure SET-POSITION
  register [REFINED BY PR-160 F4: the cursor is what the row-
  walk INDEXES - rows live in a pointer vector at [[rec]+0x2e]
  and the verb reads entry = [[rec+0x2e array][cursor]] (0x522
  21-0x52229); an incrementer for the cursor is still NOT
  found (the entry/helper verbs are the candidates) [THE CAN-
  DIDATE WAS RIGHT - PR-162 F1: the helper verb 0x520c0 CON-
  TINUES at 0x5211e into a row-step tail (step 0x521d4-0x521
  d7, wrap 0x521c1-0x521c5, reverse 0x521a1-0x521b1) reached
  from the walk's PAID path (the +0x18 call at 0x52338)] so
  the "no writer" part of the
  writer law above stands only for the transition side].
  (ii) The cursor's BASE is the authored base: the
  only non-zero writer copies the authored (N) VERBATIM
  (0x52046 -> 0x53616), the authored (N) is 1-based (PR-86),
  and 0 is exactly the init value ("before any authored row",
  as PR-150's gate table observed). So consumer 6 (Finding 5,
  0x50be2) matches POSITION 6 = the `3,6` line of A_WALK, NOT
  index 6 (`4,6`): PR-157 F4's row-identity caveat resolves
  to the 1-based side; the numeric gate-6/threshold-6 coinci-
  dence (every A_WALK pose line carries field-2 6) is un-
  touched either way. (iii) PR-157 F7's "reset a state's row
  idiom" label and PR-158's restatements of it are corrected
  by brackets.

- FINDING 2, THE AC_TIME SELF-RAISER - A NEW ENGINE LAW
  (0x53626-0x5365c, verbatim): AFTER every same-state transi-
  tion match - including matches where 0x53612 skipped the
  cursor write - the applier reads rec = [[obj+0x50]+
  [obj+0x5c]*4], increments the OBJECT's step counter
  [obj+0x9d] (0x53629/0x53636/0x5363a), loads WORD [rec+0xc]
  (0x53643), and when it is nonzero AND <= the counter, sets
  live-set byte [obj+0x61] bit 1 - bit index 9 of the object
  signal set, i.e. AC_TIME (PR-145's bit-index = LL_SIG_*
  law; cross-checked against ll_play.h). The counter is zeroed
  on a STATE CHANGE (0x535c2, the different-state arm before

## PR-160 — THE STATE-BLOCK DIRECTIVE PARSER IS DECODED END TO
## END (0x51910 = a record-class verb; time= feeds the AC_TIME
## gate bounds; seq registers a block into the global pool; s
## inserts a NAMED-SEQUENCE ROW; control= enumerates 21 flags)
## AND WITH IT THE ENTIRE AC_TIME LAW CLOSES: ENTER ROLLS A
## RANDOM WORD BETWEEN THE AUTHORED time=min,max PAIRS VIA THE
## BORLAND LCG (0x76bcc), AND THE PR-159 MATCH-COUNTER GATES
## ON THAT ROLL; THE RECORD CLASS STRUCTURES DECODE (base
## 0xa25d4; the LADDER family at its own object-class table
## blob), THE ROW MODEL IS rows[[rec+0x2e]] INDEXED BY THE
## ROW CURSOR, THE [[rec]+8+0xa0] PRE-SCALE IS THE FRAME-
## ADVANCE MODE DISPATCHER THAT FEEDS THE [obj+0xa1] ACCUMU-
## LATOR (PR-100/101's mechanism, now named), AND THE RE-
## CORD+0xc GATE WORD'S ZEROER IS THE ENTER VERB ITSELF
(READING; no code, no new test - the PR-138..159 precedent;
the PR-159 items (2)/(3)/(4) CLOSE; a row-line-parser gap is
counted instead)

- WHY. PR-159's Next set two first reads: the row-walk verb
  body and the [rec+0xc] authoring chain. Both opened the
  same door - the record-class method tables - and behind it
  sat the whole authored-text directive layer PR-157 had
  hunted: the engine's parser reads the .MOV/state-block
  DIRECTIVES as plain text, 'seq NAME' is the sequence reg-
  istration mechanism, and time=min,max is verbatim the
  AC_TIME threshold pair.

- FINDING 1, THE RECORD-CLASS STRUCTURES AND THE RECORD
  FACTORIES. (a) State records carry their method-table
  POINTER at [rec+0x44]; the constant stores census (exact-
  pattern grep): the BASE record-class = 0xa25d4 (written at
  0x524cf, 0x52508) and a derived family at 0x97c9c (0x1e119,
  0x23115 - the TLewZaria-era region). (b) Records are made
  by the OBJECT-class verb +0x88 (PR-159 F3's fallback):
  base 0x55360 = 0x60-byte alloc + ctor 0x524d0 (which ends
  [rec+0x44]=0xa25d4); the LADDER class's +0x88 = 0x534c0 =
  0x48-byte alloc + ctor 0x51770. The +0x84 named-fetch verb
  is the NULL stub 0x23a90 for BOTH families - so ZARIA-era
  records are constructed fresh per object, never fetched
  from a name pool at binding time. (c) The LADDER record-
  class store at 0x97c9c lies INSIDE the LADDER object-class
  table blob (PR-156's pair at 0x97cdc): the walk verb 0x521f0
  appears at 0x97ca8, which is record-view +0x0c/+0x18-de-
  pending slots - the two views sit at a constant positional
  offset (+0x40) in that blob. Observed; the compile-time
  mechanism is not claimed. (d) Record ctor init (0x51770):
  [rec+0x0]=owner, [rec+0x4]=0 (row cursor), [rec+0xe]=
  0x3e8=1000 - the time_scale DEFAULT in a per-mille style
  (1000 = 1x) - [rec+0x12]=0 (control flags), [rec+0x16]=0
  (sample). (e) The base ctor region also holds 0x52500:
  copies WORDs +0x48..+0x5c FROM AN AUTHORED PARAM ENTRY
  (ebx=param entry; the F/T/G header fields of PR-79's map)
  INTO the record - PR-157 F7's "field-copy block whose 5c->
  58 copy contradicts [obj+0x58]=count" is this param-entry
  copy - the contradiction was only a mis-typed target; no
  object-copy is involved.

- FINDING 2, THE STATE-BLOCK DIRECTIVE PARSER - 0x51910, a
  record-class verb at +0x38 (called from a driver at
  0x52640), line-oriented: 0x76d20 compares the line head
  against directive names, then custom scanf 0x49920/0x498f0
  or tokenizer 0x57d30 reads the values. Full decode:
  time= -> '%hi' at [rec+0x8], ',%hi' at [rec+0xa] - the
  authored time=min,max pair IS the AC_TIME bound pair (the
  corpus shows time=10,20 / time=30,60 / time=50,100 / a
  single-value time=350 form too - the no-comma case's effect
  on +0xa is a small open item);
  sample= -> [rec+0x16]; time_scale= -> [rec+0xe];
  seq NAME -> REGISTERS the current block into the global
  pool ds:0xceff8 via the [[ds:0xcef40]+0x398] singleton's
  +0x4 verb (result parked at ds:0xceff4) - THE sequence
  registration mechanism PR-157 asked for;
  s NAME,N -> LOOKS UP the name in the same pool, allocates
  a 0x18-byte ROW ENTRY (ctor 0x515e0: +0x8=0, +0xc=0,
  +0x10=1 threshold default, +0x14=0, class 0xa2638; the 0x3e8
  argument to the ctor = the record's CURRENT time_scale [RE-
  ADDED BY PR-161 F1: plain row lines are the ID-KEYED VARIANT
  OF THIS SAME BUILDER - see the PR-161 record]), and APPENDS
  it to the rows vector at
  [rec+0x2e] - named-sequence rows;
  control= -> the FULL flag enumeration (21 names, exact
  strings) [THE FULL BIT MAP DECODED BY PR-162 F1d: BY_X sets
  NO bit; BY_Y=+0x12|0x1 ... SEQ_REV_X=0x10, SEQ_REV_Y=0x20
  (PR-95 CONFIRMED); the flag window is +0x12..+0x15 - see
  the PR-162 record]: BY_X BY_Y BY_TIME BY_TX BY_TY FRAME_REV
  SEQ_REV_X
  SEQ_REV_Y CHECK_ZW CHECK_ANI CHECK_LN CHECK_ALL CHECK_LEW
  CHECK_BASE_LN SOLID CH_DIR INV_V DANGER CHECK_ALL_PLANE
  ANTI_SOLID SOLID2 SEMI_SOLID ANTI_POCISK; the error path
  prints "Bledny control %s w pliku %s." ("Wrong control %s
  in file %s") - the parser carries the authored FILE NAME.
  ZARIA's extracted .MOV texts contain NO seq=/s= lines -
  their rows must come from the plain row lines; that parser
  is the counted gap (item 1).

- FINDING 3, THE AC_TIME LAW NOW FULLY CLOSED (joining PR-159
  F2): ENTER (record-class +0x1c; base 0x52360 -> 0x52070/
  0x52072) zeroes the owner's step counter [obj+0x9d] - the
  PR-159 "list-parent zeroer 0x52077" IS the ENTER body,
  [self+0] is the owner back-pointer - and computes
  [rec+0xc] = min + (max-min) * r / 32767 with r from
  0x76bcc = the classic Borland-C rand() LCG (state x*
  0x41c64e6d + 0x3039, output (x>>16)&0x7fff): A RANDOM
  ROLL IN THE AUTHORED RANGE AT STATE ENTRY. The PR-159 gate
  (WORD <= self-transition match count -> live-set AC_TIME)
  therefore means: after a random number of same-state trans-
  ition matches in [min,max], AC_TIME raises - and a state
  with NO time= line keeps [rec+0xc]=0 (ctor leaves it) so
  the gate NEVER raises it. ZARIA.01: zero time= lines in any
  ZARIA.01 authored text -> AC_TIME never self-raises there
  -> every ZARIA.01 leg unchanged; the port's PR-69 approxi-
  mation stays harmless but is now REPLACEABLE by the real
  law (Next: a candidate CODE pass - the port already parses
  time= per its PR-69 grammar). (Sub-question kept: the LAD-
  DER-family record ENTER override 0x4fef0 - does it roll too
  or deliberately not.)

- FINDING 4, THE ROW MODEL AND THE WALK VERB (0x521f0-0x35c,
  record-class +0x0c/+0x44; the helper at +0x18 is 0x520c0).
  (a) A state record's ROWS live in a vector at [rec+0x2e]

  CAUSE the step is lea+store); the HELPER does step the cur-
  sor - advance-on-threshold-pass] so the PR-159
  writer law holds but its "never touches the cursor" phras-
  ing is refined here. (b) Row entries: [entry+0x0]=payload,

  PER (verbs 0x55820/0x457e0/0x45800/0x45870/0x458e0 forward

  [entry-cls+0x8]; a keyed path copies the caller's 13B key,
  copies the object's live set (12B+1B, the 0x53520 shape),
  merges (0x49580) and tests the entry key with 0x47e40 - NO
  match ends the walk [ARMS CORRECTED BY PR-161 F2: the test
  is an INTERSECTION test (0x495b0 after the 13-byte dword-

  ED BY PR-162 F2: BOTH arms run the gate - the intersection

  other path runs the per-row gate:
  the walk calls [[owner]+8]+0xa0] - WHICH IS 0x543A0, THE
  FRAME-ADVANCE MODE DISPATCHER (the 0x54380 switch feeding
