      pair. The instrument was the problem, not the arithmetic: see
      THE LESSON below.

- WHAT THIS READ ESTABLISHES. The link PR-194 F(a) left open ("the
  RUNTIME that executes such a node was NOT found") and the question
  PR-194 F(b)/(b) and `## Next` scoped ("is the authored number the
  loop's RETURN, the exit word [level+0x4], or a level index?") are
  now read end to end. The answer: neither return nor index. The
  authored number is written into the current level object's +0x4
  slot; the level loop tests that slot against ZERO at the top of
  every iteration, and a nonzero makes the loop RETURN THE CONSTANT
  1, the same for every value; one copy of the number is published
  beside that code and read by NOTHING in the image. The values 1
  and 2 in the fixtures' 26 rows are behaviorally identical, and
  that code 1 is NOT the exit-4 leg - PR-190 pinned exit 4 as the
  menu result - so the two signals stay distinct.

- THE RUNTIME WAS ALREADY IN THE LEDGER, ONE CALL SHORT. PR-101
  recorded that 0x520c0 "takes the current node [[rec+0x2e]] +
  [rec+4]*4, calls the node's +0x4 method" (0x520cf-0x520e1), and
  PR-193/PR-100 fixed 0x520c0 as the `[[rec+0x44]+0x18]` handler,
  identical in all 16 record-class sub-tables, with no direct E8
  call anywhere (re-verified: zero call sites). What was never
  followed is where that call lands for an `end_level` row. It lands
  exactly where PR-194 F(a) already pointed: the parser at
  0x46bbd-0x46c01 builds a 0xc node whose class word is 0xa1048;
  class 0xa1048's slot +0x04 (table 0xa104c) is 0x45750; and
  0x520e1 is `mov ebx,[edi+0x4]; mov eax,edi; mov edx,esi; call
  DWORD PTR [ebx+0x4]` - the apply call, with the row node in eax
  and the record in edx.

- THE APPLY METHOD, EXACTLY. 0x45750-0x4576e:
  `mov ebx,ds:0xcef40; mov ecx,[eax+0x8]; mov [ebx+0x4],ecx` then
  if `[node+0x00]` is non-null, `mov eax,[node]; mov ebx,[ebx+0x4];
  call [ebx+0x4]` - it stores the node's number (the parser filled
  [node+0x8] through the `' %i '` format at 0x91998, PR-194 F(a))
  into the global object's +0x4, then recursively applies the rest
  of the row's directive chain through each next node's own class.
  It IGNORES edx (the remainder argument of the +0x18 handler's
  convention); PR-101's "[0x52118] rewrites the accumulator, so the
  carry lives in the object, not the node" is what makes that safe.

- THE +0x04 SLOT IS NOT ONE METHOD. Census of the 31-table run's
  slot +0x04 (PR-101's stride 0x18 census, same tables): 24
  DIFFERENT functions plus 0x457e0 x6 - every directive class has
  its own apply, and 0x45750 (write-then-walk) belongs to exactly
  one class, 0xa1048, the `end_level` class. The six 0x457e0
  classes are the pure-walk apply PR-101 described ("only walks"),
  and its chain recursion is 0x457e9->0x457ec. Full-image census of
  the apply pattern (`mov R2,[R1+0x4]` then `call [R2+0x4]` within
  6 instructions) finds exactly 4 sites: 0x45766 (0x45750's own
  recursion), 0x457e9 (0x457e0's recursion), 0x520da->0x520e1 (the
  row-apply above) and 0x510fc->0x51101 - that last on a DIFFERENT
  object shape (a byte cursor at [obj+0x8] walked through [obj],
  applying when a zero byte terminates); its object type is not
  identified here, counted below. The sibling row-steppers
  0x521f0/0x52360/0x523f0/0x52470 contain NO apply at all: their
  indirect calls are the PR-101 model's chain getters and record
  methods (+0x8/+0xc/+0x70/+0xa0/+0xa4/+0xa8/+0xac/+0x10/+0x18),
  so directive side effects run only through 0x520c0.

- WHO THE OBJECT IS, WITH THE IDENTITY CHAIN MEASURED. The
  ds:0xcef40 global holds the CURRENT LEVEL-SESSION OBJECT, and the
  loop's `this` is that same object:
  (1) 0x5d1f5 asks 0x5c320 for 0x3ea bytes and 0x5d233 runs the
      ctor 0x4a4c0 over it (PR-191: that ctor zeroes [obj+0] and
      [obj+4] and "the reader is 0x5d25e" - PR-191's exit-word
      language, confirmed as the field layout here);
  (2) inside that object's open sequence 0x4a5cf is the ONLY call
      to 0x223d0 anywhere; 0x223d0 returns the +0x3ce sub-view, and
      0x4a5d4 restores `lea ebx,[eax-0x3ce]` - the object base;
  (3) 0x4a5f3 stores that base to ds:0xcef40, installs the class
      table 0xa1350 at [obj+0x3e6] (PR-189's "manager" naming) and
      chains the previous global at [obj+0x39c] (0x4a5f9);
  (4) 0x5d24c loads the global and 0x5d251 calls 0x4abd0 with it in
      eax, so the loop's ecx and the global are the SAME object -
      `lea edi,[ecx+0x3ce]` at 0x4ac2b is the same view arithmetic;
  (5) teardown: the stubs' chain calls the object's +0x04 method
      with edx=2 (0x5d2a1-0x5d2ac, class 0xa1350's slot) and THEN
      nulls the global (0x5d2b6); 0x5e337-0x5e352 is the same
      destroy-then-null sequence for the other global holder, and
      0x3f74b is an unrelated fourth store to that global.
  Mention census over the whole image: 261 instruction sites mention
  ds:0xcef40 - 257 register-loads in 170 functions, 4 stores to the
  global itself. Accesses of the +0x4 slot in register form, entire
  image: ONE writer (0x4575b), the guard TEST (0x4ac55, a cmp
  against 0 - see below), one copy-OUT (0x5d25e), and nothing else:
  scanning every function that loads the global for any `[reg+0x4]`
  or bare `[reg]` read used as a source finds 5 functions and all
  5 are `lea` address arithmetic, not reads.

- THE LOOP'S OWN TEST, AND THE EXIT-CODE MAP. The level loop
  0x4abd0 (PR-106's law: exactly one E8 caller, 0x5d251) tests at
  the top of every iteration (0x4ac3b): first `[[ecx+0x394]+0x116]`
  nonzero -> ebx=3 and out; ELSE `cmp DWORD PTR [ecx+0x4],0x0`
  (0x4ac55): zero falls through into the frame body, NONZERO sets
  ebx=1 (0x4ac5b) and `jmp 0x4ae53` (0x4ac60) - straight to the
  epilogue, which ends `mov eax,ebx; ret`. So an `end_level` row's
  number makes the loop RETURN 1, identically for every value, 1 or
  2 alike. Two measured facts pin that as a real signal: within the
  body exactly ONE instruction loads the immediate 1 into ebx -
  0x4ac5b, this guard (the other immediates are 3 at 0x4ac4b, 2 at
  0x4ae8b, 4 at 0x4ae4e) - and the body contains NO store to the
  flag at all (zero `[reg]`/`[reg+4]` dword stores, zero
  ds:0xcef40 mentions), so the flag is never cleared mid-level and
  the exit lands on the first boundary after the row runs. Per
  level it starts 0: the ctor 0x4a4c0 zeroes [obj+4] (PR-191's
  reading, re-verified at byte level - 0x4a4c3 and 0x4a4cc are the
  two zeroing stores) on a freshly allocated 0x3ea block (0x5d1f5),
  so the flag cannot leak into the next level.
  THE 1->4 CONVERSION IS A DIFFERENT LEG. The frame-end test
  0x4ae45 `cmp ebx,0x1; jne 0x4ac3b` re-checks an ebx that came
  from a CALL: 0x4ae29 `call 0x603b0` then 0x4ae30 `mov ebx,eax`;
  its 1 is rewritten to 4 at 0x4ae4e. That is PR-190's exit-4 leg,
  "THE ESC MENU'S RESULT == 1 IS THE EXIT-4 SOURCE", reached only
  through the menu-result call and NEVER through the guard, whose
  jmp 0x4ac60 skips it. This is the one trap the reading nearly
  fell into: an earlier draft of THIS record claimed end_level
  returns 4, read off the frame-end test, and the guard's direct
  jump to the epilogue refutes it - corrected before commit, and
  stated here because the two legs look continuous in a linear
  listing. All four exits run through one epilogue: the body
  0x4abd0-0x4ae81 has EXACTLY ONE `ret` (0x4ae81), entered only at
  0x4ae53, from 0x4ac50 [3], 0x4ac60 [1, the guard], 0x4ae90 [2,
  when `ds:0xa94f0` is zero, 0x4ae82-0x4ae8b] and by the 0x4ae4e
  fall-through [4, menu]. PR-193's consumer table then applies as
  it recorded it: the stub at 0x5d3b5 dispatches on the code, and
  code 1 lands in its `mov eax,0x1` leg = CONTINUE WITHOUT RESET;
  code 4 is the `xor eax,eax` chain-stop (0x5d3ec).
- THE PUBLISHED PAIR, AND ITS ZERO READERS. 0x5d25e reloads the
  global AFTER the loop returns and copies N into the wrapper's local
  at [ebp-0x8]; 0x5d2d1-0x5d2dc (PR-193's out-pair store) then
  writes `[out+0x0]` = the loop's return and `[out+0x4]` = N. All
  14 call sites of 0x5d170 were enumerated: thirteen pass a LEVEL
  NAME in ebx from the block at 0x92631 - zaria1 zaria2 ena1 ena2
  lona sades kadmar1 kadmar2 ran kara junction tunga1 tunga2 (the
  ten plain stubs 0x5d3b0..0x5d7a0, plus three jump-table consumers
  at 0x5d891 [junction] 0x5d8c9 [tunga1] 0x5d940 [tunga2] - the
  TUNGA pair this whole read is about, and their shape is
  `dec eax; cmp eax,3; ja; jmp cs:[eax*4+...]` = a four-way table on
  code-minus-one); the 14th, 0x5eb11, takes the name from ITS
  caller, sets ds:0xa94f0=9 first, and reads NEITHER dword - it
  discards the pair. NOT ONE of the 14 reads the second stack dword:
  every consumer that reads at all reads the code, none reads the
  word, in any window. So the authored
  number's only live effect in the shipped engine is the nonzero
  test at 0x4ac55; the number itself leaves the level as data no
  code consumes.

- 0x98278, THE LAST UNREAD LEG OF PR-101'S WALK. `mov ecx,0x98278;
  call DWORD PTR [ecx+0x4]` at 0x520e6/0x520f6 is NOT a format
  string (PR-96's reading, made when 0x98278 was seen as a data
  value near the 0x3dbcc item lookup): the data at 0x98278 is a
  method table - [0x98278]=0x23ed0, [0x98278+0x04]=0x23ea0,
  [0x9827c+0x04]=0x23e00, adjacent to the level-bounds class table
  0x98274 that PR-190's law installs at [obj+0x14] - so the call is
  the +0x04 method of that table, 0x23ea0, with the record's two
  table views in edx/ebx as PR-101 described. READ, four
  instructions: 0x23ea0 `mov [eax],edx; mov [eax+0x4],ebx; ret` -
  it installs the two views into the dword block at eax (0x520eb
  points eax at 0x520c0's own stack scratch), i.e. the call
  MATERIALIZES a two-view cursor over the record right there; the
  same shape zero-defaulted at 0x23f00 (`mov [eax],0; mov [eax+4],0;
  mov [eax+8],0x98278; ret`) shows +0x8 is the table self-reference.
  What consumes that cursor is not read in this pass (counted), and
  the neighbours 0x23eb0 (a pair-copy that installs 0x98278 at
  +0x8) and 0x23ed0 (a dl-flag destroy/free leg) were noted, not
  followed.

- THE LESSON FOR THE NEXT WINDOW SEARCH. The exit word's writer sat
  inside a class-table METHOD reached only through an indirect call,
  storing through a register loaded 12 bytes earlier (two
  instructions between). No
  register-window pairing can rank that store above noise: replaying
  PR-194(c)'s stated shape (ds:0xcef40 mentions x `mov [reg+0x4],`
  stores, +-30 instructions) over the image gives 71 pairs, 29 of
  them with real registers, and 0x45752->0x4575b is among them - so
  the sentence "none pairs ..." is false as written, and the search
  that motivated it could not have succeeded. What DID find the
  writer was following the class model (PR-101/PR-153): row ->
  node class -> slot +0x04. Stated so no future pass re-runs the
  dead instrument.

- PORT CONSEQUENCE (for the scheduled [PORT]). The engine's own
  end-of-level contract is now: an authored `end_level <n>` row in a
  level's LEW.MOV (the lion's script; the fixtures' rows sit in the
  `A_EXIT`/`A_TUNGA1`/`A_TUNGA2` states PR-194 F(b) censused) runs
  as any other row, its apply stores n, and the level run ends at
  the NEXT frame boundary with the loop returning the constant 1 -
  PR-193's CONTINUE-WITHOUT-RESET leg - for every value of n. So
  the number selects nothing; the row's existence IS the exit.
  LEO_LEVEL_EXIT can therefore stop injecting codes: the real
  rows, run through the port's existing row walk, end the level.
  The pins to write a port against: any `end_level` row -> loop
  code 1, flag-only, no value semantics; the flag is per-level
  (ctor-zeroed) and never cleared mid-level; and exit 4 belongs to
  the MENU leg, so a level ending must not be modelled as a
  chain-stop.

CLOSES: the PR-199 scope in `## Next`; PR-198's PORT CONSEQUENCE
      paragraph - the port now implements that contract
CORRECTS: PR-194's block comment in ported/ll_level.c, "The port has
      no exit-word PRODUCER: ... its runtime executor was never read" -
      replaced in place, quoting that wording and naming PR-198/PR-199
      as the answer; PR-198's "LEO_LEVEL_EXIT can therefore stop
      injecting the codes" - true for the ONE outcome a real row
      produces only: the other three have no producer in the port, and
      none of the three levels that carry the rows can be run here, so
      the injection stays how all four are driven (measured below).

- WHAT SHIPPED, ONE PATH, EVERY STEP ANCHORED. (1) PARSER:
  `end_level <n>` in a row's directive chain now fills
  `ll_mov_fr.endlv` with the authored NUMBER - the analogue of the
  parse arm 0x46beb, which puts n through the `' %i '` format at
  0x91998 into [node+0x8] of a class-0xa1048 node (PR-194 F(a)). A
  tail with no number stays a counted directive, never a guess.
  (2) APPLY: the player's row admit - the point where a row becomes
  current, i.e. what the engine's 0x520e1 apply call reaches for that
  node - copies the number into `ll_player.exit_word`, exactly what
  0x45750 (`mov ebx,ds:0xcef40; mov ecx,[node+0x8]; mov [ebx+0x4],
  ecx`) does for the level object's +0x4 slot, and like the engine
  nothing ELSE happens: the apply ignores its remainder argument and
  the row's own chain still runs. (3) TEST: ll_level.c's play loop
  now compares that slot against zero at the TOP of its iteration,
  before any of the iteration's work - the 0x4ac55 position - and a
  nonzero hands loop code 1 to ll_stage_outcome (the 0x4ac5b
  ebx=1 + `jmp 0x4ae53` epilogue), prints a named producer line with
  the value and the addresses, and ENDS the level run there.
  (4) LIFE OF THE FLAG: never cleared by the loop (PR-198: the body
  has no store to the slot), zeroed where the engine's ctor 0x4a4c0
  zeroes it - the reset leg (stage_reset_to_authored -> play_spawn).
  A new named line makes the two producers distinguishable in any
  log: an injected CODE says "stage driver: exit N at tick T", a real
  row says "exit word <v> from an authored end_level row ...".

- THE DESIGN CALL, STATED NOT HIDDEN. The engine's field is ONE PER
  LEVEL OBJECT; the port's owner is the LION's state, because the
  lion's row walk is the only one the shipped data puts the directive
  in - all 26 rows live in `LEW.MOV` members (measured by the new
  census). That mapping is written at both fields, not implied. A
  SCENE OBJECT's row cannot reach the slot and stays counted. A
  literal `end_level 0` (which in the engine would CLEAR the slot)
  collapses into "no tail" - the parser cannot distinguish value 0
  from absence - and no shipped row does it (26 rows, values 1 and 2
  only), re-measured by the census leg. And the port ENDS the level
  run at the guard rather than pretending to continue: the engine's
  "run on, no reset" for code 1 is the CALLER's decision, and the
  caller re-enters the stage through a NEW level object, which the
  port has no equivalent of - the producer line names that limit.

- MEASURED - THE SHIPPED ROWS, THROUGH THE PORT'S OWN PARSER (new
  tool/endlevel_census.c + a verify-endlevel leg): 777 `.MOV` members
  of the HD ANIMACJE parsed by ll_mov_parse itself, 0 unreadable;
  exactly 3 members carry the tail and 26 rows total - 25 with value
  1, 1 with value 2, confirming PR-194 F(a) by an independent route.
  The members are LEVEL BLOCKS of the container, so the counts read
  per block: JUNCTION 1 `.MOV` member / 2 rows, TUNGA.11 48/12,
  TUNGA2.12 49/12 (the per-level `.MOV` counts sum to 777 - one
  member sits directly in a level block rather than under a leaf,
  and the census counts it too, never through a structure guess).
  Every row is named in the log: JUNCTION/LEW.JUN state 2 [A_TUNGA1]
  row 41 (authored frame 42, threshold 200) end_level 1;
  JUNCTION state 3 [A_TUNGA2] row 81 (frame 82, threshold 200)
  end_level 2;
  TUNGA.11/LEW.TUN state 9 [A_EXIT] rows 0-11 and
  TUNGA2.12/LEW.TUN state 32 [A_EXIT] rows 0-11, all `frame,6` -
  2 + 12 + 12 = the 26. And the levels every play leg DOES run
  carry ZERO such
  rows - RAN.01: 84 members, 0 rows; ZARIA.01: 33 members, 0 rows -
  which is what makes steps (2)/(3) inert on every existing frame
  pin.
- MEASURED - THE PATH DRIVEN END TO END ON RAN.01 (the level cannot
  carry a real row: see the CORRECTS note for why the three that do
  cannot be played here - JUNCTION's platformy=none.des declares 0
  polylines ("this level has NO ground"), and TUNGA's A_EXIT is armed
  only by `A_EXIT(x)=AC_RECT,AC_BLOK`, signals this port's object
  world does not raise). Injecting the tail on the level's OWN row -
  state 23 [A_WALK_FWD] row 1, the line becomes `2,6,end_level 2` -
  makes the guard fire: the row admits on tick 5, the loop ENDS at
  the top of tick 7 (reported as last completed tick 6, the same
  numbering as the injected codes), stage_apply answers exactly like
  an injected code 1 ("run on, NO reset (the engine's 0x5d3dc)"),
  and the 60-tick PPM is BYTE-IDENTICAL to (i) a 6-tick run of the
  same injected script - no extra iteration ran after the admit, the
  engine's own boundary shape; (ii) a run injected with value 1
  instead of 2 - the value selects nothing, PR-198's central finding,
  now demonstrated in the port; (iii) a 6-tick run with NO injection
  at all - carrying the tail changes not one byte of the simulation.
  An address that does not resolve (state 0 row 5 of a 30-state
  script) prints its own line and is byte-identical to the plain
  run; with no LEO_PLAY_ENDLV no driver line appears at all.
  ll_play_selftest adds the hermetic case: the flag lands EXACTLY on
  the admit of the carrying row and 60 further steps never clear it.
- WHY THE PROBE HAD TO NAME STATE 23, RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-FINDS IT
  THE HARD WAY. First probes injected on state 0 and did nothing,
  and the reason is the port's own correct behavior, not a dead
  path: RAN.01's lion spawns in state INDEX 22 (A_STAY, PR-83's
  declared-name spawn), state 0 (A_FLY_PTAKI1) is never current, and
  even A_STAY's single row is threshold-fed with no key effect, so
  no row there ever ADMITS while the lion stands. A_WALK_FWD's rows
  admit continuously while the walk script runs. The injection
  counter counts rows exactly as ll_mov_parse counts them, so the
  address is the shipped grammar, not a second indexing.

- THE PIN, TESTED RED FIRST. P5 in doc_census.py: the tracked .md
  set (via `git ls-files`, so untracked vendored material like SDL's
  own docs is out of scope by definition) must equal the declared
  standard - four living root docs, the generated index, the

  exactly as required: 7 files outside the set, and the missing
  archive README. After the moves: 16 tracked files, 16 in the
  standard, 8 archived, 0 outside. A missing REQUIRED file fails too
  (the check is two-way). P5 runs only in default mode: it measures
  the repository, not files handed to it. The failure message states
  WHERE content belongs, so the rule teaches instead of just
  rejecting.

  comments cite its sections directly (ported/main.c "PLAN 8b",

  set; HANDOFF's header line that called it "early milestones" was

  false claims fixed, see CORRECTS; ported/README's account was
  checked true: the Makefile does not build original/).
  tools/*/README.md and docs/RE_INDEX.md: allowed by shape and by
  name respectively.
- THE ARCHIVE RULES (docs/archive/README.md, the one new
  content-file): moved files are NEVER EDITED - their text, counts
  and line references stay frozen at the snapshots they name;
  corrections go in the README's table, never into the frozen file;
  `git mv` only, so `git log --follow` still works (git recorded
  all seven as renames, 100% similarity: the bytes did not move);
  every future arrival needs a record AND a table row in the same
  commit. One measured gotcha the README now states: the shas the
  archived files cite PREDATE the 2026-11-19 history override -
  c5be46c->4356d86, dfb2bf2->c6ca322, 4c48dd0->2a29f0a, a428cef
  unchanged - so old citations resolve through
  tools/history_override_2026-11-19.txt.
- THE HEADER FIXES, all width-safe: NEXT_STEPS now says
  "Numbering continues at PR-200" and points the P/E/M- and T- ids
  at the archive (read-only history; the live plan stays `## Next`);

  byte-identical): the moves touch no indexed address, field token

- FIX-FORWARD, RECORDED BECAUSE CI CAUGHT WHAT THE LOCAL GATE
  COULD NOT: the first CI run on this PR (44632489921) FAILED in
  verify-docs - not on the rule's judgment but on its instrument:
  P5's plain `git ls-files` hit git's safe.directory protection on
  the runner ("fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at
  '/__w/open-leo/open-leo'") because the checkout and the step
  process do not share a uid. Locally the guard never trips (the
  repo is owned by the invoking user) - the classic "works on the
  developer's machine" split, visible only because nothing else in
  the suite ever invoked git. Fixed in the same PR's follow-up: P5
  invokes `git -c safe.directory=*`, git's documented escape hatch,
  scoped to that one read-only call. Everything else about the run
  matched the local gate (same counts up to P5).

  construction (verify-docs remains ONE leg - P5 prints inside it,

  only greps for their names are prose in the journal and this
  PR's pointers, which were updated or are history.
- REVERT: revert the commit; the `git mv` records restore every
  path, and dropping P5 restores the old census exactly.

  clamp(T,.,130)*v/100` then `v += F*s/100` at the key intent
  s=10. For `F=100,` `T=50,` that is a drag of 0.50 and an
  increment of 10.0 hundredths-px, so the integrator's fixed
  point is exactly 20.0 hundredths-px per iteration = 20.0 px/s
  at the 20 Hz iteration clock PR-134 settled; during the ramp
  from rest the first 10 iterations average 19.8. Both ends of
  that band sit under every measured number below. The same
  arithmetic for the PINGWIN's `F=75` `T=50` pair is 15.0 px/s,
  and the pre-PR-135 F/4 law would say 18.75 - neither matches

## CHAIN MOVE ONTO THE 1:1 PLANE THEIR OWN .des NAMES

KIND: port

SUBSYSTEM: scene composition - the object -> tlo plane assignment

ADDRESSES: established, all at raw machine code (build/leo/leo.elf
      and leo.img; VA = file offset + 0xf000, and that VA is what
      build/decompiled/all/ names - LEO.EXE itself is a different,
      un-fixed-up address space and was not scanned):
  - 0x57500 (x law) and 0x57530 (y law): THE LAYER INDEX IS EDX.
    0x57503 `lea edx,[edx*4]`; 0x5750a `mov ebx,[eax+0x20]` (the
    per-layer percent table); 0x5750d `lea ecx,[ebx+edx]`; 0x57513
    `imul edx,[ecx]`; then 0x57516 `mov eax,[eax+0x1c]`, 0x57519
    `lea eax,[eax*4]`, 0x57522 `mov edi,[ebx]` as the divisor. So
    [scene+0x20] is the speed% table and [scene+0x1c] IS main_back;
    0x574e0 `mov ecx,[eax+0x20]; mov [ecx+edx*4],ebx` and 0x574f0
    `mov [eax+0x1c],edx` are their setters.
  - 0x52d67 / 0x52d72 `mov edx,[ebx+0x24]` feeding the 0x52d6a
    `call 0x57530` (again at 0x52e03, 0x52e26): THE FIELD THE
    LAYER IS READ FROM IS [obj+0x24] - the same field the
    collision-plane gate compares (PR-16x's [entry+0x24] ==

  - 0x23b90 = `mov [eax+0x24],edx; ret` is that field's setter:
    scanning leo.img for the 4-byte value 0x23b90 finds 211 data
    references (0x968d0 .. 0xa657c), EVERY one at (+0x04 mod 4)
    inside a table whose +0x00 slot holds a code pointer - verb
    +0x04 of 211 class tables. How a class declares its plane.
  - NOT the plane, and re-named as such: the placement pools.
    0x4cdf5..0x4ceb5, 0x4aaa0 and 0x4bb30 allocate/walk EXACTLY
    three pools at `[level+0x58] + id*4` with `id = [level+0x40]++`

- THE ANSWER FIRST, FROM THE LEVELS THEMSELVES: every shipped .des
  (12 of 13; CHEATS has none) carries `plany=` with EXACTLY one
  '|'-separated spec per tlo= layer - JUNCTION 1 ("TL"), KADMAR2 1
  ("TALABA"), KADMAR.07 2 ("T|TALAB"), LONA.05 2 ("T|TAAALAB"),
  ZARIA.01/.02, RAN.01, TUNGA.11, SADES.06, ENA.03 3, KARA.07 4
  ("T|TA|TALA|TB"), ENA2 4 ("T|T|TAAL|TBA"). The letter inventory
  over all of them is EXACTLY {T, A, L, B}: T once per spec, L
  once per level, B once (except JUNCTION, which authors no
  belka=), and A as often as the `animacje=` list has CELLS -
  counted: 3=3, 3=3, 3=3, 2=2, 3=3, 3=3, 5=5, 4=4, 4=4, 4=4, 3=3,
  0=0. THE LAW: the k-th A in reading order (layer 0 first, left
  to right inside a spec) is the k-th cell of that list, and it
  rides the layer whose spec carries that A. Cross-checks that
  make it a format and not a coincidence: the L letter sits on the
  main_back= spec on all 12 levels, and that spec is the 100,100
  speed pair; B also sits on a 100,100 spec (KARA.07 puts the
  belt on layer 3 while the lion is on layer 2 - the same 1:1
  math, both 100,100); a bare `none` cell in the MIDDLE of a list
  consumes a letter (RAN.01 `none,wulkany,dymy` = 3 A's) while a
  list that is ONLY a bare `none` names no cell (JUNCTION: "TL",
  0 A's).

## PR-209 — THE ENGINE RUNS `plany=` AS ITS OWN PER-LEVEL LETTER
## PROGRAM: `A` WALKS THE PLACEMENT POOL CELL THE SAME ORDINAL
## OUR PARSES USES; `T`/`L`/`B` DRIVE THE tlo/lion/belt; THE
## CONSUMER NEVER WRITES [obj+0x24], SO THE PLANE WRITER STAYS OPEN

KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: level flow - the engine's plany= interpreter
      (build/leo/leo.img 0x4af10 and its letter handlers), the
      placement-pool layout (0x4c720, 0x4cdd5..0x4ceb5, 0x4aaa0,
      0x4b360), and the class-table slot census correction;
      port-side: comments only, no behaviour change.
ADDRESSES: established, all at raw machine code (leodb `dis` =
      objdump over the exact bytes of build/leo/leo.img, VA =
      file offset + 0xf000, sha256 edf19a129e85efb8...; the DB
      was rebuilt this PR and its func table is the Ghidra list
      in build/decompiled/all/index.csv - the FUN_* names cited
      here are those VAs):
  - 0x4af10 THE PLANIES INTERPRETER (Ghidra FUN_0004af10).
    esi = the level manager; the string is [[esi]+0x30] (0x4af1d
    `lea ebp,[eax+0x30]`, 0x4af2a `mov ebp,[ebp]`). [level+0x3a0]
    is the gate: when nonzero the letter bodies are skipped
    (0x4af54/0x4afb1/0x4afe1/0x4b043 all test it) and 0x1cfd0 is
    called on entry (0x4af31). 0x4b076 uppercases the byte via
    0x76e98 and dispatches: cmp 0x42 -> 'B' at 0x4b008; cmp 0x4c
    -> 'L' at 0x4afe1; 'T' (0x54) at 0x4af54; 'A' (0x41) at
    0x4afb1; anything else 0x4b0a7 loads esi=0xa92d4, prints via
    the literal 0x91d2a "Bledny opis poziomu - plany" (the error
    string PR-59 found in the .des key table), then the report
    tail. [level+0x30] is filled by the loader: 0x4d230
    `mov edx,0x91eb4` (the literal "plany") then 0x4d259
    `call 0x57d30` with ecx=0, ebx=<value>, format ' %s' at
    0x91eba - ONE %s token, so a planies value carries no space
    (true of all 13 shipped values).
  - 'A' 0x4afb1: `mov edx,[esp+0x8]` (the A counter, 0 at entry),
    `mov eax,esi`, `lea ecx,[edx+0x1]`, `call 0x4b360`,
    `mov [esp+0x8],ecx` - EXACTLY one increment per 'A' letter,
    never reset per spec. 0x4b360 (bytes 0x4b360..0x4b3af):
    0x4b367 `lea edi,[edx*4]` (edi = k*4, held constant); the
    outer loop walks ecx = esi, esi+4, esi+8 (`lea ebp,[eax+0xc]`
    / `add ecx,4`) = the three key pools in order; each step
    0x4b37c `cmp esi,[ecx+0x44]` (that pool's cell count), then
    0x4b381 `mov eax,[ecx+0x58]` (the chain-heads array),
    0x4b384 `mov edx,[edi+eax]` = the chain head for cell k of
    that pool; the chain is +0x34 next, and for each entry
    0x4b399 `call [ebx+0x60]` (predicate), and if nonzero
    0x4b3a5 `call [ebx+0x74]` (activate).
  - THE POOLS, exact: 0x4cd6c..0x4ceb5 is inside the level .des
    loop. Key literals 0x91dda "zwierzaki" / 0x91de4 "animacje"
    / 0x91ded "ani_plat" each copy [level+0x40] into the global
    at 0xcef44 / 0xa94ec / 0xa94e8 (0x4cd85..0x4cdca) = that
    key's POOL ORDINAL. 0x4cdd5 `call 0x4c720` = the cell
    parser: it scans items with ' ' "%[^, " (literal 0x91d6c,
    8-byte-stride array, `lea edx,[eax*8]` at 0x4c735) and
    counts them. 0x4cdf0 `call 0x76a64` allocates count*4,
    0x4cdf8 `mov [esi+edx*4+0x58],eax` stores the chain-heads
    array at [level+0x58 + keyordinal*4], 0x4ce11 zeroes it,
    0x4ce3b `mov [edx+0x44],count` stores the cell count at
    [level+0x44 + keyordinal*4], the loop at 0x4ce52
    (`mov ebx,[ebp+0xe2]` cells, `add edx,8` per step) skips a
    cell equal to "none" (literal 0x91df6) and otherwise opens
    the file and calls 0x4dd50(eax=level, edx=[level+0x40],
    ecx=cell - 0x4dd58 `mov ebp,edx`, 0x4dd62 `mov edx,ecx`),
    which builds each entry (0x4aaa0 `call 0x4df10` factory,
    then 0x4aadd `call 0x52c10` = push onto chain
    [[level+0x58] + keyordinal*4 + cell*4]; the +0x34/+0x38
    links exact at 0x52c18..0x52c2c), and 0x4ceb5
    `inc DWORD PTR [esi+0x40]` - the ONLY increment, reached
    once per placement-KEY record: ONE POOL PER KEY, three
    pools, ids in .des record order.
  - 0x4b360's bound, read exactly: each of its three steps
    compares `[ecx+0x44]` - the CELL COUNT of the key's pool it
    is walking. Measured against the shipped data (the port's
    wiring dump gives the key order and every cell count): the
    minimum cell count across the three placement keys is >= the
    level's A count on EVERY one of the 13 levels - 3/3/3 vs 3
    (ZARIA.01, ZARIA.02 3/3/3, RAN.01 3/3/3, KARA.07 3/3/3),
    2/2/2 vs 2 (KADMAR.07), 3/2/3 vs 3 (KADMAR2, ENA2), 1/5/3
    vs 5 (TUNGA.11: min 1 - so letters 1..4 exceed the
    zwierzaki pool's bound; they still reach the 5-cell
    animacje and 3-cell ani_plat pools), 4/4/4 vs 4 (SADES.06,
    LONA.05, ENA.03), 1/1/1 vs 0 (JUNCTION). Every shipped
    letter therefore activates at least one real cell.
  - 'L' 0x4afe1: `mov eax,[esi+0x394]` = the LION object,
    `call [[lion+8]+0x74]` (the same activate verb), then
    `call 0x4b2f0(esi)`: walks [level+0x64] (a SECOND pool-heads
    array, PR-105 item 7's open half - its feeder is still
    unnamed) with the same +0x34 chain and the same +0x60/+0x74
    pair.
  - 'T' 0x4af54: edi = the T ordinal; the FIRST T (edi==0) calls
    0x57780([level+0x390] = the tlo controller, edx=0) and adds
    2 to the ordinal (0x4af78 `add edi,2` - the parser skips one
    extra character: NO shipped planies token has one, stated as
    a format caution); later T's call 0x57710 and add 1. Both
    callees: `mov ebx,level; mov ecx,edx; call 0x57500` (the
    PR-57 x-law getter) then /100 (0x57723 `mov esi,0x50`, idiv),
    0x5774a `mov eax,[ebx+0x44]` / 0x5774d `mov edi,[eax+ecx*4]`
    - the tlo controller shares the pool-array shape: the tlo
    LAYER objects live at [[level+0x390]+0x58 + layer*4], and
    0x5776a `call [[layer_obj+8]+0x08]` drives that layer with
    the computed offsets. The T ordinal = the tlo layer index:
    one T per spec, and the spec count really does equal the tlo
    count on all 13 levels (KADMAR2 is ONE tlo layer -
    "ll_level: parallax: 1 tlo layers" - its tlo= line lists
    plan_.pcm alone).
  - 'B' 0x4b008: gated by [[level+0x3ce]+8] != 0; loads the
    level .des string buffer (lea eax,[esi+0x3ce]) and 0xcef30,
    calls 0x4a170 (`mov eax,[0xcef2c]; add eax,[0xcf0e8];
    add eax,0x190` - a field of the main game struct), then
    0x49bd0([level+0x3b4], [level+0x3ce]+0, low16). Then if
    [level+0x3a0]==0 and [level+0x38c]!=0, `call 0x448c0` with
    eax = [level+0x38c] (the BELTA/HUD strip object). Only the
    field identities are established; 0x49bd0/0x448c0 bodies are
    NOT read (PR-16x's +0x24 pair at 0x23b80/0x23e00 is a
    different +0x24: those are table slot +0x330/+0x08 accessor
    thunks `mov eax,[eax+0x2c]` / `mov [eax+0x24],edx` /
    `mov eax,[eax+0x24]`).
  - CALL CONTEXT: 0x609d0 `mov eax,ds:0xcef40; call 0x4af10` -
    a thin thunk (its head 0x609c0 initializes a record via
    0x5f3d0 and stores the table 0xa2d6c at [rec+0x9c] first);
    and 0x4aeee inside the level-message handler (after
    `mov eax,0xcf068; call 0x563d0`). Per-invocation, not
    load-time.

- WHAT THE CONSUMER IS. planies is not a table the game consults
  to route objects; it is a PROGRAM the level manager runs, per
  invocation, over the string it parsed at load ([level+0x30],
  one ' %s' token). The four letters are commands: drive THIS
  tlo layer, activate the lion and the chain at [level+0x64],
  run the belt/HUD pair, activate pool cell k. The error branch
  prints the author-visible Polish sentence "Bledny opis poziomu
  - plany" - the format is authored data and the engine checks
  it at runtime.
- WHAT THE 'A' LETTER ACTUALLY DOES (the honest correction of
  this PR's own first reading). 'A' k is a BROADCAST over the
  three placement keys: for each key in .des record order it
  walks chain-heads[keyordinal][k] and runs the +0x60/+0x74
  pair on that cell's objects, skipping keys with fewer than k+1
  cells. It is NOT an "animacje cell k" command: with ZARIA's
  three 3-cell lists, the three letters step through cell 0 of
  ZWIERZ2, cell 1 of ANIPL2, cell 2 of ZWIERZ1 as well as the
  three animacje cells. What the DATA census adds (and it is a
  real, new law): sum(A) equals the MINIMUM cell count across
  the three keys on all 13 levels (3,3,3,2,3,3,5*,4,4,4,3,0;
  *TUNGA: min is 1, so there the letters overrun the short
  zwierzaki pool - the other two pools are covered exactly).
  The authors size planies by their own lists. The port's plane
  mapping (A k -> the plane of the k-th animacje cell) is
  unchanged by any of this: no pass read here writes a plane,
  and the PR-208 law stands on its data + film evidence.
- WHY THIS SHARPENS OI-109 INSTEAD OF CLOSING IT. The
  zwierzaki/ani_plat pools are allocated and chained exactly like
  animacje's, and planies' A letters reach them too (by cell,
  broadcast) - but never their PLANE: no handler writes
  [obj+0x24]. Their collision dispatch addresses each key's list
  by its stored global (0xcef44/0xa94e8/0xa94ec = that key's
  pool ordinal, PR-60's CHECK_ANI/CHECK_ZW paths), i.e. exactly
  the port's lvl_obj.src+entry model. The DRAW PLANE remains
  unwritten by any pass read so far: 0x4aaa0/0x4dd50 build and
  chain but write no +0x24. The next lead is concrete now: the
  accessors 0x23b80/0x23b90/0x23e00 (the +0x2c/+0x24 pair) and
  their 146 slot +0x04 call sites, or the entry-ctor family
  behind 0x4df10.
- CORRECTION SELF-TEST (what would have broken). PR-208's law
  survives because it was read from the data, not from a guess
  about the consumer; the ONLY claim of PR-208 that PR-209
  refutes is the slot +0x04 wording, and that refutation came
  from the tool the record itself named (`slots +0x04`, 158
  tables, three targets). The 211-value scan is kept as the
  measurement it was; its interpretation is fixed here.

- THE CORRECTED CAMERA LOCKS, AND THEY ARE LAW-FREE. y-curves at
  fixed x against the film, every camy 140..172 step 2, x=30,
  t=22.0, scored over the full frame minus the two screen-fixed
  overlay boxes (x>=285 y 53..128; bottom-left 0..44 y 150+),
  padded rows excluded: noobj/objon pairs 28.46/28.52 at 150,
  23.17/23.22 at 160, 22.83/22.87 at 162 (MIN), 23.48/23.54 at
  164, 25.22/25.28 at 168 - sharp to +-4 px, and the no-obj and
  obj-on curves agree within 0.1 over the whole range: the
  placed objects are worth ~0.05 MAD on the full frame, so the
  camera read CANNOT be a law artifact. Same at t=31.25: x at
  camy 215 -> 24.69@235, 24.72@240, 25.44@245; y at x=240 ->
  25.97@204, 23.79@214, 23.76@216 (MIN, shallow), 24.10@220,
  25.10@228.
- THE DISC MATCH (the close). PR-207's valid disc box at t=22.0,
  (279..287.8,131.5..141.8), sits ON the shipped law's design
  point: POCISK (310,298) draws 1:1 at camera (30,162) → origin
  (280,136), a 12x12 box (280..292,136..148): the film disc's
  left edge is within 1 px and its top edge within 4.5 px, and
  the chain MOVES (PR-207: kokos.mov is the bullet chain, jajo
  children spawn and fly), so a few px of travel is expected.
  The other two discs the port draws at that camera - the
  (95,320)/(115,320) pair at (65..77,158..170)/(85..97,158..
  170) - are absent from the film: those bullets had already
  flown; PR-207 recorded the same absence as a puzzle at every
  plane - it is exactly what a moving chain does. At t=31.25 the
  corrected camera (238,215) puts the design boxes at (72..84,
  83..95)+(84..96,83..95) vs measured (52.5..65.2,100.8..113.8)
  +(77..90.2,99..106.8): discs within a few px to ~20 px of
  design x = chain travel again, and the two y-laws coincide
  there as before. There is NO unexplained film disc left and
  NO plane evidence against the shipped law.
- WHY THE LANDMARK READERS FAILED THE FILM (the tool lesson,
  measured). A masked-union camera lock over only the 12 PICT
  landmark templates (opaque-mask MAD of the port's no-obj
  renders; harness /tmp/opencode/pr210/mland.py) is SHARP on
  port frames - self-tests: fed a render at the true camera
  (30,150) it ranks that camera first at MAD 0.000 with next
  candidate +4.4; fed a second render at (76,175) it lands
  (75,175) - 1 px - and nothing else - first. On the FILM at
  t=22.0 the same lock reports (76,175), 46/25 px away from
  the MAD lock: the plan templates match the film's background
  palm art, and the union mask there is only 3.6k px. The
  free-running --native NCC pass is worse: t=20..25 proposes
  plan6 seq matches at camx 54..290 / camy 296..412 (physically
  impossible drift), and t=72.5 proposes lisc1 at (1750,520).
  These are single-template ambiguities, the exact failure the
  tool's own docstring warns about: THRESH 0.55 is permissive
  for this film. Discard tier-2 reads; a film camera needs the
  full-frame MAD (obj-on or no-obj, they agree) or colour-
  anchored art edges.
- THE ANI3 TEST WINDOW, MEASURED (a second, independent plane
  hit - and its limits). The waterfall window (t=70.5/72.5/75)
  is the one ZARIA.01 stretch where an ANI3 cell is on screen:
  ANIBACK draws WAZ.SEQ (a 32 px water column, f0=-21 f2=-13)
  at layer 1, and the port draws its e0 at (168..199,28..61) at
  camera (1725,520) - measured by the obj-on/no-obj render
  difference (ANI .MOV art is not in the landmark atlas). The
  film's water, colour-segmented (pool/HUD rows masked): left
  edge 257 at t=70.5 AND t=72.5 (run 257..284, width 28 ~ the
  32 px art), and 185 at t=75 (run 185..233). Two laws'
  geometry, at the SAME frame:
  (a) shipped law: water left edge = 1613 - 0.85C + 21.25, and
      the 1:1 lisc4 crown (authored x 1870) sits 235.75 - 0.15C
      px RIGHT of the water edge: adjacency (0..25 px) needs C ~
      1405..1571, and the measured edge 257 needs C ~ 1620 -
      the film shows the palm crowns exactly adjacent, x ~
      250..320, and lisc1 (1776) at ~156 = the mid-frame palm.
      The edge positions at t=70.5/72.5 and t=75 imply
      camx ~1620 and ~1705: the water moved exactly 72 px in
      4.5 s = 0.85 x the implied camera run 85, and the 1:1
      inter-frame shifts (rock/grass bands, weak NCC 0.01-0.07)
      say 90-98 - a ratio 0.73..0.80, i.e. the L1 rate, not
      1.0.
  (b) PR-61's entry-index rule puts ani3 (cell 0) on LAYER 0:
      water edge = 1634 - 0.39C, which is on screen (0..320)
      only for C in 3315..4190 - impossible in this level
      (cam_xmax 1920). Under that rule the waterfall could
      NEVER have appeared in this window. The film shows it.
  So this window FITS the shipped law (a) and refutes the rule
  PR-208 replaced (b) - but its camera was never locked sharply
  by an independent method (the background-only full-frame scan
  is flat: 30.15 best vs 30.45 across +-50 px; the NCC reads
  failed), so it is recorded as SUPPORTING evidence, and the
  close above rests on t=22.0, where the lock IS sharp.
- AN UNMEASURED ANOMALY, NOTED NOT CLAIMED: at that window the

  the port's YMAX=500 clamp, and ZARIA.01 authors lisc2.seq at
  y=1546 - far outside its own 700-row world. Not pursued;
  if anyone re-opens level-bottom geometry, start there.
- WHY THIS CLOSES OI-108 AND NOT A RE-PIN. No port behaviour
  changed, so there is nothing to pin: the shipped law is
  already pinned (plany_selftest + lv_plany/lv_plany2, PR-208).
  What OI-108 held was a FILM contradiction; this PR measured
  it away. The method rule it adds (native /4+pad, never a
  direct 720->200 resize; full-frame MAD for cameras; colour
  edges for distinctive art; discard single-template reads) is
  now recorded in OI-108's closed row and in this record.

- WHAT YETI IS, BY BYTES. The name string 'YETI' sits at
  0x91247 and is used at exactly one factory branch, 0x38498:
  strcmp-guarded, allocation 0x130 (0x384a8), constructor
  0x73e50 — which stores the method-table views 0x9f298 into
  [obj+8] and 0x9f290 into [obj+0xc] (0x73e55/0x73e5c). The
  second view is the same cells shifted by -8; every slot
  below is stated in the [obj+8] view (the view PR-130's
  +0xa0 census used), read from build/leo/leo.elf bytes.
- THE YETI TABLE, FULL MAP (0x9f298): +0x10 = 0x54560, the
  per-class event handler (jump dispatch on [edx+0x4]; code 5
  is handled one layer up, at 0x3d8f0, which sets the terrain
  word [obj+0x6d] and ORs [obj+0x66]|0x40; codes >=6 set or
  accumulate the position-delta words [obj+0xc2]/[obj+0xc6]
  at 0x54593/0x5459c/0x545aa); +0xa0 = 0x543a0, the feed
  dispatcher (PR-99/100, unchanged); +0xc0/+0xc4 = 0x54fe0/
  0x55020, a [obj+0xb6]-gated contact pair; +0xc8 = 0x54250,
  THE INTEGRATOR; +0xcc = 0x549f0, the generic input-apply;
  and in the same table's extended half +0x1c8 = 0x52590,
  0x52590's record PARSER, +0x1f4 = 0x52680, the merge: the
  state record is the object, so PR-98's "rec" offsets are
  object offsets on this class. The same parser/merge pair,
  at a constant +0x2c slot spacing, occurs in 62 of the 189
  detected class tables (0x9f298 among them) — a census read
  from the .elf, not from the stale .img-backed index rows.
- THE AXIS LAW, PROVEN (closes OI-107 lead 1, pair seconds):
  the parser stores the pairs F= -> +0x50/+0x54, T= -> +0x58/
  +0x5c (clamp 130 at 0x525f8/0x52610), G= -> +0x48/+0x4c;
  the merge copies them into the runtime ctx block as F ->
  ctx+0x0/+0x4, T -> ctx+0x8/+0xc, G -> ctx+0x10/+0x14, and
  the node handler 0x45d50 folds selector-matched node pairs
  into ctx+0x18/+0x1c (the target-velocity pair). The
  integrator then takes its x legs from ctx+0x0/ctx+0x8 (drag
  x, force x; the intent multiply is the imul at 0x542ab) and
  its y legs from ctx+0x4/ctx+0xc (0x542cd), and the
  velocity-SET leg at 0x54170 reads ctx+0x18 (x) and
  ctx+0x1c (y). FIRST = X, SECOND = Y. The authored YETI
  data corroborates: F=100,0 (force on x only), T=50,5,
  G=0,100 (a 100-scale force on y in every state - a
  gravity-like term), and no FC/F/I row in A_RUN. So the
  seconds of T=50,5 / F=100,0 are the Y axis and CANNOT
  scale the ground x walk: lead 1 is DEAD.
- THE PER-FRAME PHYSICS STEP, ONE DISPATCH: 0x52750 runs a
  record pair-then-integrate: it calls [obj+0x44]+0x2c and
  +0x30 (ctx methods; [obj+0x44] is a ctx built by 0x524e0,
  which allocs, tags class 0xa25d4 (0x524e8), and runs
  0x52540 - that copies the authored field block +0x48/0x4c/
  0x50/0x54/0x58/0x5c, the G, F and T pairs, out of the
  source record at 0x5250f-0x52530), then calls
  the integrator at [[obj]]+8 slot +0xc8 (the call at
  0x52774 — the ONLY +0xc8 slot-dispatch in the image), then
  [obj+0x44]+0x34. 0x52750 has exactly 10 call sites:
  0x23fc8, 0x264a8, 0x2701d, 0x2c3ad, 0x2df08, 0x31fd8,
  0x33c98, 0x3620d, 0x4fff1, 0x61238 — ten per-class frame
  drivers; their call rate is the open question below. The
  integrator is also called directly at 0x24731, 0x321fe and
  0x33348; only 0x33348 (the family whose class tables,
  0x9cfd0/0x9d088/0x9d168/0x9d220/0x9d2ac/0x9d338/0x9d460,
  carry 0x33310 at the +0xc8 slot instead of 0x54250) edits
  the ctx G term before integrating (+/- 5*[obj+0xf2] into
  ctx+0x10 for states 3/5). YETI's slot is plain 0x54250:
  that adjustment never touches it. The integrator sits in
  150 of the 189 detected class tables, at the +0xc8 slot in
  113 of them — it is the shared physics step for creatures,
  exactly as PR-133 found for the lion; the two-view trap is
  that a slot number written for the 0x9f290-style view is 8
  lower in the [obj+8] view (the mid-PR scratch "+0xd0" was
  that shift).
- s IS BOUNDED AND MULTIPLE-OF-5 ON EVERY PATH (closes
  OI-107 lead 2, partial intent above 10): the integrator
  reads the intent pair from [obj+0xba] (x, imul at 0x542ab)
  and [obj+0xbe] (y, 0x542cd). In the whole image the ONLY
  writer of those two fields is the input-apply 0x549f0: it
  copies the caller's IN pair (0x549f9/0x54a08) and its
  contact-node dead-band branches store only the constants
  10 (0x54a57), -10 (0x54a82/0x54ac3) and 0 (0x54a93/
  0x54ae7). Every call site of the input-apply slot (+0xcc
  in this view; the lion's is reached from the level loop at
  0x4aeca, PR-132 bounded that IN) builds IN with |s| <= 10
  in multiples of 5, and the only non-binary builders are:
  0x27d60, a target-chase driver that reads dx=[obj+0x126]-x
  and dy=[obj+0x12a]-y and passes IN = (round(10*dx/(|dx|+
  |dy|)), round(10*dy/(|dx|+|dy|))) — the 10.0 double at
  ds:0x909ef, a 1-norm normalisation that reaches |IN.x|=10
  ONLY when dy=0 — and 0x34495, which passes IN.x = 10 times
  the class +0x70 getter (for YETI that getter is 0x239f0,
  `mov eax,[eax+0x6d]` — the terrain WORD, so 0, 10, 20...),
  IN.y = 0. Also dead as candidates: the T-raise gate inside
  the integrator fires only for T_x < 20 (authored 50), and
  A_RUN authors no FC row, so the 0x54170 target leg is zero
  for the walk. A ground walk at 22.0-24.9 px/s under this
  law needs s = 11.0..12.5 — NO s on any path is 12.5 or
  even non-multiple-of-5. Lead 2 is DEAD.
- WHAT THE LAW ACTUALLY IS FOR YETI (re-derived from these
  bytes, matches the shipped port, PR-135): steady x speed =
  5*F_x*s/T_x per STEP = 10*s units at the authored pair —
  a pure multiple of the intent, with the register fixed
  (F_x/T_x = 2). The port runs the same law at its 50 ms
  step and predicts 20.0 px/s at s=10. The film's 22.0-24.9
  is the SAME law with 1.1-1.25 steps where the port counts
  1 — so the 1.25 is now a pure steps-per-second question,
  not a register question. The remaining read is the STEP
  RATE: how often the ten 0x52750 call sites run per display
  frame, against the display cadence PR-134 bounded. That is
  the row's ONE named lead.
- WHY NOTHING IS PINNED: no behaviour changed; PR-135's port
  law is confirmed as the engine's x law by this reading, and
  a steps-per-second contradiction cannot be pinned until the
  step-rate read resolves it. The 22.0 burst remains the one
  a future PR must explain; the 24.9/24.9/25.0 cluster and
  its |F|/4 = 25.0 coincidence are still unexplained and
  still recorded in the row.
- TOOLING CAVEAT, STATED ONCE: every class-table and
  data-segment number in this record is read from
  build/leo/leo.elf program headers. build/leo/leo.img holds

- THE ONE PLANE-WRITER FOR PLACED OBJECTS. Entry 0x4b1d0
  (eax = the level object) has exactly ONE call site in the
  image, 0x4d764, in the level-load flow between
  `mov DWORD PTR [level+0x64],0` (0x4d75d) and the object
  wiring that follows; the same flow builds the lion at
  0x4d668 (builder 0x4dde0, creature ctors 0x1fef0/0x25510/
  ...) and sets the lion's plane at 0x4d68b (below). The
  pass walks POOL OCCURRENCE IDS 0..2 (the same ids
  [level+0x40] hands out, one per placement-key record,
  0x4ceb5 `inc [level+0x40]`; the three key literals are
  'zwierzaki' 0x91dda, 'animacje' 0x91de4, 'ani_plat'
  0x91ded, whose last id each level stores at 0x4cd85 ->
  ds:0xcef44, 0x4cda6 -> ds:0xa94ec, 0x4cdc7 -> ds:0xa94e8;
  every shipped level carries exactly the three keys, so
  ids 0,1,2 cover every pool). For id k it reads the cell
  count [[level+k*4]+0x44] (0x4b22d; written at 0x4ce3b)
  and the head array [[level+k*4]+0x58] (0x4b274; allocated
  at 0x4cdf5 and zeroed at 0x4ce0a, one head per parsed
  list token), and for cell c in [0,count): it scans the
  level's planies string - the pointer at [level+0x30], the
  SAME program the letter consumer 0x4af10 interprets
  (0x4af1d/0x4af2a fetch the identical pointer) - counting
  the '|' bytes (0x7c, inc at 0x4b266) up to the (c+1)-th
  'A' byte (0x41, inc at 0x4b255; the scan runs while the
  A-count-minus-1 is below c, 0x4b268-0x4b26a, and ends at
  the strlen precomputed at 0x4b1dc). The count of '|' is
  PLAIN edx = the plane value; when the string has fewer
  than c+1 A's the scan stops at the end and the value is
  the total '|' count - the LAST segment index. Then it
  walks the chain at head[c] (0x4b27f, chain link +0x34 at
  0x4b289) and calls class-table slot +0x5c on every entry
  (0x4b282/0x4b286). One string scan per cell index, the
  same for all three pools.
- ENTRY i OF A LIST IS CELL i, RAW. The list parser at
  0x4cd6c..0x4ceb5: per key record it parses the token list
  (0x4cdd5 -> count at [ebp+0xe2]), allocates count heads
  (0x4cdf5), then for token i (loop 0x4ce52..0x4ceb3,
  ebx = i at 0x4ce78): if the token does NOT contain the
  literal 0x91df6 - which reads, from the .elf, as 'none'
  (0x4ce5d) - it opens the named .des (0x4a910) and calls
  0x4dd50(eax=level, edx=[level+0x40], ebx=i); 0x4dd50
  parses the file and calls 0x4aaa0 per entry line; 0x4aaa0
  constructs the object at 0x4aac3 (0x4df10) and chains it
  at [[level+id*4]+0x58]+i*4 via 0x52c10 at 0x4aadd. A
  'none' token leaves its cell an EMPTY HEAD and the next
  token still gets its own index: cell indices are raw
  token positions, 'none' consumes a slot. Neither 0x4dd50
  nor 0x4aaa0 writes [obj+0x24] - PR-209's wording holds.
- THE SET VERB IS SLOT +0x5c. A census of every detected
  class table long enough for the slot (from
  build/leo/leo.elf bytes): 177 tables have +0x5c, 150 of
  them hold 0x23b90, `mov [eax+0x24],edx; ret` - the plain
  store. The variants are propagation verbs, and they are
  exactly why the word needs a verb at all: 0x1ecb0 sets
  its own [obj+0x24] then dispatches +0x5c with the same
  value to the partner at [obj+0x120]; 0x332f0 sets itself
  then dispatches to the object at [obj+0xee]; 0x554f0
  sets itself then walks a child array [obj+0x40] x count
  [obj+0x3c] (0x554f9/0x55513); 0x531b0 copies ANOTHER
  object's plane - it calls [B]+8 slot +0x5c with
  edx = [A+0x24] (0x531bc-0x531c1). The whole dispatch
  surface is the ten `call DWORD PTR [reg+0x5c]` sites in
  the image, and all ten are now accounted for: three are
  those helpers' own bodies (0x1ecbd, 0x332fd, 0x55513),
  one is 0x531b0's body (0x531c1), one is the level-load
  pass (0x4b286), one is the LION: 0x4d688-0x4d68b sets
  [lion+0x24] = [[level+0x390]+0x1c] - the scene struct's
  main_back, the reference layer (PR-208's [scene+0x1c],
  setter 0x574f0) - and four are CREATION-TIME
  INHERITANCE: a child built through the 0x4dcc0 factory
  (registry ds:0xcef40) and hooked into its owner's
  [owner+0x112]/[owner+0x12a] takes its creator's
  [obj+0x24] (0x24026-0x2402b, 0x33d03-0x33d0f,
  0x362c1-0x362c7, 0x362ec-0x362f2). Direct stores to an
  object's +0x24 outside 0x23b90 exist only in 0x332f1 and
  0x554f9 (the helpers); every other +0x24 store in the
  text is a stack local or another structure's field
  (checked one by one: 0x1f2fb/0x4c931/0x528bc/0x52950/
  0x55bca/0x5663a/0x5729b/0x594ac/0x594b8/0x5957e/0x5958b/
  0x5f1f6 and the rest - struct inits beside class tags
  0x98278/0xa2550/0xa26c8, list bookkeeping, [esp+0x24]).
- THE LETTERS ARE THE ACTIVATION PROGRAM, THE PIPES ARE THE
  PLANES. The consumer 0x4af10 walks the same string byte
  by byte: 'T' drives the tlo layers through 0x57780/
  0x57710, 'A' at the k-th occurrence calls 0x4b360(level,
  k) (0x4afb1-0x4afc9), which walks cell k of EVERY pool
  (0x4b37c-0x4b384 index the same [level+4j+0x44]/
  [level+4j+0x58]) and for each chained entry runs verb
  +0x60 (0x4b399 - 0x23b80, the [obj+0x2c] getter, the
  predicate) and, if nonzero, verb +0x74 (0x4b3a5); 'L'
  runs the same pair on the [level+0x64] chain (0x4b2f0..
  0x4b317). So PR-209's "the pass ACTIVATES; it never
  writes [obj+0x24]" stands - and the reason no shipped
  planies spec NAMES zwierzaki= or ani_plat= is that the
  letters never named a key's plane: the program's
  SEGMENTS do, for all three keys at once, through cell
  index = A ordinal.
- THE DATA, MEASURED. ZARIA.01 `plany=T|TA|TALAB`, lists
  `zwierzaki=none,zwierz2.des,zwierz1.des` and
  `ani_plat=none,anipl2.des,none`: 3 A's at segment
  positions 1,2,2, so cell 0 of any pool -> plane 1, cells
  1,2 (and any cell past the last A) -> plane 2. KAMIEN
  (ZWIERZ2, cell 1) rides plane 2, ZWIERZ1 (NOSOROG/PAJAK/
  SEP, cell 2) rides plane 2, ANIPL2 (cell 1) rides plane
  2; the lion's plane is main_back = 2 (0x4d68b; the port
  itself reports "parallax: 3 tlo layers, reference 2").
  The animals sharing the lion's collision plane is a CON-
  SEQUENCE OF THE LAW, not a coincidence (this is what the
  OI-109 row could only call evidence). LONA.05 `T|
  TAAALAB`: all 4 A's sit in segment 1, so every cell of
  every pool - ZWIERZ.DES (FOKA/PINGWIN/YETI at cell 2)
  and ANIPL2/ANIPL22/ANIPL3 (cells 1,2,3) - rides plane 1,
  and the lion's reference layer is 1. KADMAR2 `TALABA`:
  no '|' at all, every plane 0 - PLAT1 (cell 0) and the
  three animacje cells included. TUNGA.11 `T|TA|ATALABA`
  and ENA2 `T|T|TAAL|TBA` give cell planes 1,2,2,2,2 and
  2,2,3 - exactly the maps the shipped port already
  computes for animacje= in its PR-208 planies reader: the
  port's animacje law WAS the engine's law, and it extends
  verbatim to the other two keys.
- WHERE THE PORT DIFFERS (measured with the read-only
  LEO_OBJ_POS probe on the fixtures): the port keeps the
  PR-61 model "plane = the cell's RAW token index" for the
  two un-lettered keys, which agrees with the segment law
  only where the segment number happens to equal the index.
  ZARIA.01: port KAMIEN layer=1, engine plane 2; port
  ZWIERZ1 layer=2 = engine 2 (the agreement the row called

- THE QUESTION, VERBATIM (OI-078, since PR-150): "the
  per-frame setter of the lion's contact target [obj+0xd2]".
  The answer is NO - there is no per-frame setter, and the
  wording came from reading the consumer as if it were fed
  continuously.
- EVERY WRITER, RE-COUNTED FROM THE ELF BYTES. A word-store
  sweep finds exactly two direct stores to [obj+0xd2], both
  zero: 0x5415b (a copy/assign tail that clears the head) and
  0x54e88; plus the pop's head rewrite at 0x551fc (0x551f0 =
  pop one node, and when the list goes empty call
  [[obj+8]+0x3c] and set [obj+0x106]=1 - PR-99's edge). The
  only appends go through the node builder 0x53f00 (node =
  16-byte header + a 13-byte zeroed answer set, the 0x1d-byte
  allocation, header [n+0]=0, [n+4]=1, [n+8]=pointer,
  [n+0xc]=count - PR-146 finding (d)). In this image 0x53f00
  has exactly TWO call sites and no table holds its address:
  0x3d618 (PR-146's asker-append inside the +0x78 entry
  0x3d440) and 0x1ef71, which this PR reads.
- THE NEW ONE, 0x1ee20, AND ITS CLASS SLOT. 0x1ee20's address
  appears in exactly one place in the whole image: the dword
  at 0x97050 = THE LION BASE CLASS TABLE 0x96874 + 0x7dc. So
  the pair-touch handler below is the LION base's method at
  slot +0x7dc, and the lion's contact list is written by the
  lion's own class, whenever it is paired with another object.
  Inside (0x1ee20..0x1ef79): call [[other+8]+0x3c] (is-enemy,
  PR-99's signature), then [[other+8]+0x4c] for the other's
  4-dword rectangle, its record from [[self.vt+0x68]] - 0x64
  (0x98278 sentinel), 0x4a050 with an 0xc-dword key made of
  the lion's own first rectangle, then the overlap test
  0x28622-0x28637; on success [obj+0x106]=1 (0x3d5f6's
  field), and if the other's [obj+0] == 2 a node (0x5c320
  (lion, 0x1d, 1)) is appended at lion+0xd2 by 0x53f00 with
  ebx=1, after [[0xcef40]+0x394]+0x106 = 0 and the other's
  [[vt+0x68]]-0x64 as the node's +8 pointer. The same
  handler's other branch calls 0x52b10 - the plain 16-byte
  push into [obj+0x10], the list the CHECK_ masks walk
  (PR-102) - not the contact list. The gate value [obj+0]==2
  is named open (rectangle format, below).
- THE ONLY READER PATH FOUND, 0x28590 (0x9a390 + 0x134): it
  runs only when BOTH sides' state slots [obj+0x5c] equal 4,
  with the lion side read as [[0xcef40]+0x394]; it calls the
  other's +0x3c (is-enemy) and +0x4c (rectangle), then
  0x3d440 at 0x28682, which appends the node to THE ASKER's
  list (PR-146 finding (c)) - so that append is a generic
  contact-entry behaviour, not a lion path: 0x3d440 sits at
  +0x78 in exactly two class tables, 0x96a88 and 0x99e64,
  neither a lion table.
- THE LION CLASS FAMILY DOES THIS INSTEAD: the LION base's
  +0x78 is the variant 0x3d990 (5 tables: 0x968ec, 0x991e4,
  0x9a1ac, 0x9adc0, 0x9e7b8 - bases 0x96874, 0x991dc,
  0x9a1a4, 0x9ad48, 0x9e740), and TLewZaria (0x96960)
  overrides +0x7dc with 0x531b0, which appends NOTHING: it
  calls [[asker+8]+0x5c] with edx = [self+0x24] - THE PLANE
  WORD PR-213 just shipped - then 0x4b140 and
  0x4aa70(level, ecx, edx).
- 0x4b140 IS A SECOND CONSUMER OF THE PLANIES STRING, and the
  first one outside the level load. With the level in esi and
  the object in edi: if edi == [level+0x394] (the lion,
  PR-60's field) it walks [level+0x30] - the planies string,
  PR-209's field - counting 'A' (0x41) until the first 'L'
  (0x4c) and returning that count, 0 when there is no 'L';
  otherwise it returns the first index 0..4 for which 0x4b0f0
  is true, and 0x4b0f0 tests exactly the pool law:
  i < [level+0x44 + k*4] AND [[level+0x58 + k*4] + i*4] != 0
  for the three keys in order. 0x4aa70 then resolves
  (key, cell) to the cell object through
  0x52c10([[level+0x58]+key*4][cell*4]) - the same chain
  walk as PR-212's loader. So for ZARIA ("T|TA|TALAB") the
  lion's plane by this reading is 2 = the segment holding the
  'L', which is the same number PR-213's cell_plane gives the
  lion's own placements; TLewZaria's +0x7dc answers a pair
  ask by matching the asker's plane to the lion's and then
  enumerating the placement cells of that plane.
- WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE COLLISION WORK: PR-213 said
  "[obj+0x24] is the collision-equality word; no consumer
  beyond the draw insert and the gate is known". This PR
  names a third consumer: the +0x7dc pair-answer responder
  keys on it ([[asker+8]+0x5c](edx=[self+0x24]) in 0x531b0),
  and its result decides which placement cells the ZARIA lion
  answers for. That is OI-110's consumer half, opened
  narrowed.
- WHAT STAYS OPEN, NAMED (OI-078's rectangle half): 0x1ee20
  gates on a RUNTIME object's [obj+0] == 2, while 0x28590 and
  0x1ee20's own key build read [obj+0]/[obj+4] and
  [rec+0]/[rec+4] as rectangle x/y (0x28601's `lea ecx,
  [eax-0x14]` is a width/height adjust). Which object has
  [obj+0]==2, and what the authored row-start numbers do on
  screen (PR-102 item 4), are unmeasured; PR-102's BY_TY
  finding says every climb/hang state feeds vertically, and
  the lion still does not climb at ZARIA x=180, so the
  climb's blocking term is not this contact list.
- RISK: none to the build (no code touched). The reading risk
  is slot arithmetic: 0x97050 as LION base +0x7dc and 0x9a4c4
  as 0x9a390 + 0x134 follow PR-99's anchored two-table pair
  rule and PR-146's independent anchor (+0x8c = the key
  provider 0x54910 for 0x96a88); the +0x78/+0x7dc values at
  the five lion bases were read straight from the ELF.
- REVERT: revert this commit; this record, the OI-078 row
  rewrite, the OI-110 row narrowing, the section 8 status
  block, the header numbering line and the regenerated index
  go back together; nothing else was touched.

- FAILING TEST FIRST, MEASURED. The new leg went in before the
  code: with the leg present and the arm NOT implemented,
  ./ll_level --play-selftest failed five checks, at the exact
  steps the seek is due -
    seek to (3) from row 1: port fi 1/t 230, want fi 3/t 160
    the step after:          port fi 2/t 90,  want fi 4/t 190
    seek to (2):             port fi 3/t 120, want fi 2/t 50
    seek (9), over-range:    port fi 4/t 150, want fi 1/t 80
    the step after:          port fi 5/t 180, want fi 1/t 180
  (the last pair is the purest: the SAME carry 180, the
  difference is entirely the row index). With the arm in, all
  eight steps measure the expected values and the whole
  selftest is green. The leg's numbers were derived from
  runs, not on paper: the first draft of the leg was wrong in
  three places (it double-counted the iteration's own feed
  and mis-added 190+100 against the 240 gate) and had to be
  re-derived from the U-print trace of the implemented path.
- WHAT THE ENGINE DOES, AND WHY THE PORT WAS WRONG. PR-174
  read the applier's same-index arm verbatim (0x53602-
  0x53626): it opens by writing the transition's row field
  ([entry+0x11], PR-103: the authored N minus one, -1 when
  the `( )` part is absent) into the CURRENT record's row
  cursor, and PR-172 settled it inlines nothing else - no
  ENTER, so the row feed [obj+0xa1] and its carry survive.
  The object side got that in PR-174; the lion's side kept
  PR-83's "a self-target leaves the state running untouched",
  which was written before PR-107/PR-174 and correctly
  refuses the RE-ENTER but wrongly throws the row away.
  PR-174's own census sized the miss: of the 101 authored
  self-target seeks with entry >= 2, 77 are LION-class lines
  and ALL 20 of ZARIA.01's are in the lion's own scripts -
  the object-side fix could not reach one of them. This PR
  is the half that can move ZARIA.
- THE DATA FOR THE ABSENT TOKEN (a census, not a guess). New
  scratch tool /tmp/opencode/rowseek_census.c (same method as
  PR-174's: it LINKS ported/ll_play.c and counts through
  ll_mov_parse, so the counts are what the port's parser
  stores), over HD ANIMACJE: 217 self-target transition
  lines; 22 of them carry a HELD DIRECTION condition
  (K_FWD/K_BKWD), 19 of those with no numeric token, 3 with
  "(1)", 0 with a numeric token >= 2; 195 on event-like
  conditions (AC_TIME, K_FIRE, AC_BREAK_NEXT, K_GENn...).
  The held-direction ones are walk states (ZARIA.01/LEW.ZAR
  state 4 twice, KADMAR2/LEW.KAD 0 and 4, TUNGA2.12, ENA.03,
  SADES.06 19/21/23, KADMAR.07). Under the "absent token
  writes the top" reading, holding an arrow would re-seek
  those states to row 0 on every iteration - the walk would
  never advance past its first pose - and PR-79/PR-134's
  video measurements (the lion's 12 poses at 2.4 iterations
  each, the worm's 9 at 3.2) are exactly those lists running.
  So the port refuses the write for a non-numeric token. The
  engine-side reading of the same fact is the open half
  above: either its row-setter's negative refusal (0x52381)
  also guards this path in effect, or a held arrow is not a
  level condition. Both give this port's behaviour.
- NOT OBSERVABLE ON ANY SHIPPED LEG, AND SAID SO. verify-all
  is 65 ok with fixtures, byte-identical, and 13 ok + 21
  named SKIPs without them: no shipped play/level/cutscene
  leg runs a state whose self-target line fires inside a
  pinned window (ZARIA's are gated on K_FIRE/AC_TIME/AC_DUP
  pulses in the fight and death states, and the play legs
  never reach those rows). This is law-completion plus the
  removal of a wrong model, not a video fix; the first place
  it is expected to show is the fight/death row sequences
  when FOCUS 1's ZARIA legs get there.
- RISK: the selftest leg is the only pin that changed
  behaviour; no fixture pin encoded the old values. The
  guard `entry > 0` is deliberate and asymmetric with the
  object path (see OPENS): if the engine's raw -1 really

  side must follow, and the leg's LEG A flips. Reading risk
  is confined to that question; the numeric-token half is
  PR-174's already-shipped reading of the same bytes.

  state is index 1 = the child-ANY branch. The leg was fixed
  to declare a throw-away state first so the block under test
  is index 2; the model, not the leg, was right.
- THE LOADER, WHICH IS WHAT WAS MISSING. The engine parses a
  .MOV in this order: 0x53905 loops ` %[^[` (0x922b0) over the
  text BEFORE the first block and pushes each name into the
  vector at [obj+0x3c] (8-byte entries: the grow call 0x53949,
  count++ at 0x53959, the element write 0x5396d); its length
  goes to [obj+0x58] at 0x53977; 0x5397a allocs length+1
  four-byte slots and stores them at [obj+0x50]. Then 0x539aa
  scans ` [%[^]]]` (0x922ba) once per declared entry and calls
  0x53480 for each block, which resolves the block's name with
  0x53440 and stores the constructed record at
  [[obj+0x50] + that_index*4] (0x534b6). 0x53440 is a linear
  walk of the name vector (count test 0x53452, entry load
  0x5345d, compare 0x53461 through 0x76a69) and RETURNS
  position+1 on a hit (0x5346a: ebx was already incremented
  before the compare) and 0 on a miss (0x53471). Three
  independent details pin the one-based reading: the record-
  ctor loop starts at byte 4, i.e. slot 1 (0x533de
  `mov ebx,0x4`); the object ctor writes [obj+0x5c] = 1
  (0x538ab); and the ENTER verb runs [[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4]
  straight after (0x539e6..0x539fb). 0x53440 has exactly three
  callers - this block handler, 0x3fe1c and the transition
  parser 0x51e0b - so the same one-based number is what a
  transition like `A_DROP(1)=` writes when it fires.
- WHY THE HEADER SCAN IS SAFE WITHOUT READING ITS DELIMITERS.
  The scan at 0x53915 goes through 0x57d30, which composes the
  real format from a template at 0xa9510, so its exact
  delimiter set was NOT read. It does not matter for the port:
  the vector is keyed by NAME, not by position - 0x53440
  compares strings - so a vector holding one blob could not
  work (every record would land in slot 0 and the ctor's index
  1 would run an empty slot). And the shipped texts have the
  shape the port assumes: one name per line, 768 of 777 with
  the header count exactly equal to the block count, 9 with a
  shorter header (their extra blocks are index 0), 0 with a
  longer one, longest header 40 names, so the port's
  LMOV_MAXST 64 never truncates a real script.
- THE GATE ITSELF, RE-READ. 0x3f1c6 `mov ecx,eax` makes ecx =
  SELF; 0x3f1d1 first runs the ASKER's +0x3c (is-enemy) gate,
  unchanged. 0x3f1dc loads [self+0x5c]. `cmp 1` (0x3f1df) runs
  the asker's +0x4c rectangle, the child list [self+0xa5]
  through the 0x44ec0 ANY-test, and on a hit sets [self+0x66]
  bit 6 (0x3f203..0x3f20c) - no signal at all - then jumps to
  the inert exit. `cmp 2` (0x3f214) is the P1/P2/P3 tree the
  port already ports; anything else falls through 0x3f217 to
  0x3f364. So DRAB.MOV's A_UP asks its CHILDREN, A_DOWN asks
  the LION, and A_DROP - the unrolling rope - answers nobody.
  That is a coherent mechanic (a rope that is still unspooling
  cannot be grabbed) and it is now the shipped model.
- WHAT THE FIXTURES PIN. L4's DRAB_MOV is ZARIA.01's real
  file: the declared list A_UP, A_DOWN, A_DROP and the block
  order A_UP, A_DROP, A_DOWN, the shipped `A_DROP(1)=K_GEN1`
  and `A_DOWN(1)=AC_BREAK_NEXT` arms, only the row numbers
  trimmed. It carries two discriminators: block 1 (A_DROP) must
  NOT answer and block 0 of a second fixture (the second
  declared state written FIRST) MUST answer, so no
  block-order or row-cursor model passes. L5 pins the numbers
  the parser itself computes, including the case-folded
  A_Go/A_GO shape the one shipped file uses and the
  not-declared 0.
- AT ZARIA.01 NOTHING OBSERVABLE CHANGES, and the probe says

- RISK: the answer's PREDICATE tree is untouched, so the risk

        treats the remaining names as non-bit node ops, and the
        most-used of them (K_NEVER, 159 rows in the authored
        texts) is built without any bit at all: K_ANY
        by filling the
        12-byte set with the fill byte 0xff at 0x749a0,
        zeroing words 0-1 and writing word 1 = 0x2001f8
        (0x48037-0x48048), K_NEVER by leaving the zeroed set
        and OR-ing bits 5/6 into BYTE 4 of the data (0x4806f-

        arm at 0x47e40, named by its own error string at
        0x47fc3-0x47fe1, "Bledna komenda %s w pliku %s" with
        0x919ca = "TEventSet::match") reads: it switches on
        [set+0xc], NOT on byte 4, and jumps out of range for
        anything above 3. The port's LL_SIG_* enum
        matches those 68 ordinals name for name. (3) The node
        the two row arms build: the directive chain is 0x45df0,
        its `GEN` arm 0x46af4-0x46b34 and its `Wait` arm
        0x46b62-0x46ba2. Both allocate 0x15 bytes, both call
        the same node ctor 0x45770 and both parse the operand
        with the clause parser 0x47d60 into the 12-byte
        TEventSet at [node+0x8]; they differ only in the class
        word written at [node+0x4] - 0xa11e0 for `GEN`,
        0xa11c8 for `Wait`. Their vtables answer the row step's
        two slots: 0xa11c8 +0x8 = 0x45970 (copy the node's own
        [node+0x8] out, do not call the operand) and +0xc =
        0x45870 (call the operand node's +0xc, else hand back
        an EMPTY set); 0xa11e0 +0x8 = 0x45800 (call the operand
        node's +0x8, else EMPTY). A clause atom the clause
        parser wraps at 0x47d00-0x47d42 also takes class
        0xa11e0, and its +0xc is 0x45920: run the operand node,
        then OR the atom's own [node+0x8] into the result - the
        raising shape the port's `GEN` model (PR-88) matches.
        The row step 0x521f0 reads row [rec+0x4] from the list
        at rec+0x2e, calls its slot +0x8 at 0x52235, calls the
        any-nonzero test 0x495b2 at 0x5223c and admits ONLY on
        empty (0x5224b); a row with no clause therefore returns
        empty from 0x45800/0x45870 and is admitted, while an
        un-negated `Wait K_GEN1` copies out a non-empty set and
        its row is never admitted. 0x522bc then OR-s that
        result with the caller's key set and [obj+0x60]
        (0x49582) and 0x522e6 (0x47e40) tests the union before
        0x52303 may call slot +0xc; 0x5230c OR-s that result
        into [obj+0x60]. The row clock is [rec+0xa1] and
        0x52362 is its feeder: it writes [rec+0x4] = 0 and
        [rec+0xa1] = 100. 0x5222c is `mov esi,[ebx+0x4]` with
        ebx = [rec+0x2e][idx], i.e. the row record's OWN node
        list head at [row+0x0]: the row-line parser 0x51660
        calls the directive chain 0x45df0 and PREPENDS each
        returned node there (0x516e2-0x516e6), so the row's
        test call reaches the LAST keyword written on the line,
        and a row with no tail tests EMPTY and runs. (4b) The
        clause parser atom wrapper at 0x47d00-0x47d42 calls
        the node ctor 0x45780, which sets [node+0x0] = 0,
        [node+0x4] = the class word and clones the operand
        through its class's slot +0x14 into [node+0x0]; the
        record ctor 0x51700 is the state record's, and 0x45750
        (the end_level apply, PR-198) writes the authored
        number to [[0xcef40]+4] - the level's exit word,
        byte-for-byte as PR-199 models it. (5) The second test
        0x47e40 takes two EventSets (eax, edx) and switches on
        the FLAG byte at
        [eax+0xc] through the table at 0x47e30: flag 0 (0x47e63)
        AND-s them (0x49552) and returns TRUE when the
        intersection is NON-empty; flag 1 (0x47edc) AND-s and
        returns TRUE when it is EMPTY (0x495b0); flag 2
        (0x47f42) returns TRUE when the AND is empty; flag 3
        (0x47fb2) returns TRUE when the two sets are
        byte-identical (`repz cmps` over 12 bytes). So that arm
        IS a live-set test - the object's [obj+0x60] and the
        caller's key are one operand, the clause the other, and
        the clause's flag byte picks ANY / NONE / EQUAL. Whether
        the row's own node (the entry at [row+0x4], the object
        0x45800 delegates through) composes the `Wait` clause
        that way is the reading PR-218 takes; nothing in the
        port acts on it yet.

MEASURED: (a) THE MODE BYTE. The clause parser 0x47d60 clears
  it first: 0x47d73 `mov BYTE PTR [esi+0xc],0x0` right after
  the zero-fill 0x749a0. Then per operand it tests the token's
  first byte at 0x47db2-0x47dd0: `!` (0x21) writes 1 (0x47dce
  -> 0x47dc8), `*` (0x2a) writes 2 (0x47db6 -> 0x47dc2), `|`
  (0x7c) writes 3 (0x47db8 -> 0x47dbc); a COMMA writes nothing,
  it only adds a second signal to the same clause - this
  corrects this PR's own first draft, which had `,` at mode 1.
  (b) WHAT THE MODES MEAN. TEventSet::match 0x47e40 (its own
  name, in the out-of-range error path 0x47fd8 through the
  string 0x919ca) reads [self+0xc], `cmp 3 / ja` out of range,
  and jumps the table at 0x47e30. mode 0 (0x47e63) ANDs the
  two sets (0x49550 -> 0x49552) and returns true when that AND
  EQUALS the clause byte for byte (`repz cmps` + `sete` at
  0x47ec1-0x47ecc), i.e. the clause is a SUBSET of the set it
  is handed; mode 1 (0x47edc) returns 0x495b0 of the AND, i.e.
  true when it is EMPTY (shares nothing); mode 2 (0x47f42)
  returns the negation of the same call, i.e. true when it is
  NOT empty (shares something); mode 3 (0x47fb2) is byte
  equality of the two sets. 0x495b0 itself (whose entry is 2
  bytes before the 0x495b2 my PR-217 note quoted - an
  alignment artifact of the dump, the same trap as PR-153) is
  the empty test: it answers 1 only when all three data dwords
  are zero. (c) THE TWO PATHS. 0x52229 takes the ROW object
  from [rec+0x2e][rec+0x4] and 0x52235 calls its test slot
  +0x8; the row class 0xa2638 IS the chain delegate 0x45800, so
  the call walks the row's directive chain, where the ctor
  0x45780 stores the operand at [node+0x0] under the base class
  word 0xa1000 and 0x45800/0x45870 answer with the operand's
  answer (0x45800 with an EMPTY set when there is no operand),
  while a clause node composes: 0x45970 and 0x45920 call the
  chain getter 0x45870 and OR their own [node+0x8] in (0x49580
  at 0x4593c). 0x5223c then tests that answer and `je 0x522fc`
  sends the NON-EMPTY one to 0x52303/0x5230c: the execute slot,
  its result OR-ed into the CALLER's set - and the row runs only
  if its authored frame [row+0x10] is BELOW the object's clock
  [obj+0xa1] (0x52320-0x5232b), the difference being its budget
  at 0x52338. Only an EMPTY answer falls through to 0x52251,
  which copies the caller's key and the object's own EventSet
  [obj+0x60] (12 data bytes plus the mode byte copied
  separately), ORs them at 0x522bc and calls match at 0x522e6;
  a 0 answer SKIPS the row (0x522ed -> 0x52354) and a 1 answer
  runs it with a ZERO budget (0x522ef -> 0x52338). (d) THE
  SHIPPED DATA against that law: of the 251 captured clauses
  230 carry no operator (mode 0) and 21 carry `!` (mode 1);
  `*` and `|` appear in ZERO rows, so modes 2 and 3 are never
  authored. Every one of those clauses leaves a NON-empty set -
  K_NEVER is not empty at all, 0x4806f-0x4807d OR-s 0x60 into
  data BYTE 4, and K_ANY OR-s the mask 0x2001f8 into dword 1
  at 0x48037-0x48048 - so not ONE shipped row reaches match
  with a clause, and the clause-less rows that do reach it
  carry an empty clause, which is a subset of anything: the
  second test never refuses a shipped row. What a clause DOES
  change is the path: a row that carries one is gated by the
  frame/clock compare at 0x52320, a row that carries none runs
  at once with a zero budget. (e) THE CENSUS, through the port's
  own parser and pinned by verify-endlevel: 161 of the 251
  captured operands get NO signal bit from the comparator 0x48000
  - 161 of them K_NEVER, 0 K_ANY, 0 unknown - after this PR's
  parser fix; before it 2 were counted as unknown because the
  token carried a trailing space. 0 rows name `K_ANY` (its only
  authored use, `WAIT |K_ANY,rdir` in LONA.05, is a two-token
  clause the parser still refuses to capture) and the token
  `rdir` is a row DIRECTIVE name in neither table.
FAILING TEST FIRST, MEASURED RED: obj_rowgate_selftest grew an
  `op` column and two legs before the code did, and
  `./ll_level --mov-selftest` said `row gate selftest: FAILED
  SADES.06's [A_RUN] row WAIT K_NEVER ;,smpauto: the clause
