MEASURED: (a) THE ROW OBJECT. The ctor entry is 0x515e0 (PR-217
  quoted 0x515e2, a 2-byte dump artifact, the same one as
  0x495b0/0x495b2 in PR-218): push esi, push edi, call the node
  ctor 0x45770, then [row+0x8] = 0, [row+0xc] = 0,
  [row+0x10] = 1, [row+0x14] = 0, the class word 0xa2638 at
  [row+0x4], push the caller's text argument (it sits at
  [esp+0xc] behind the two pushes, and the ctor ends `ret 4`),
  call 0x51660. The clone 0x51622-0x51655 allocates 0x18 bytes,
  calls 0x45780 and copies +0x8, +0xc, +0x10, +0x14. (b) THE
  LINE PARSER. 0x51660's FIRST act is a scan of the row text
  with the format at 0x92115 - the bytes there are `%hi` (the
  neighbours in the same string block are `time` at 0x92119,
  `,%hi` at 0x92122, `sample` at 0x92127 and `time_scale`
  0x92131), and it writes that FIRST number straight into
  [row+0x10]. Then 0x51679-0x5168f: `mov ebp,[esi+0x10]`,
  `mov edx,[esp+0x10]`, `imul edx,ebp`, `mov ebp,0x3e8`,
  `idiv ebp`, `mov [esi+0x10],eax` - the value is multiplied by
  a factor taken from the caller's frame and divided by 1000.
  That is PR-110's `* time_scale / 1000` and it is the only
  such site in the image. The second value is handled at
  0x51692-0x516d2: its magnitude goes to [row+0xc] with a sign
  flag at [row+0x14] (0x51696 writes 1, 0x516c7 writes 0), and
  when it is ZERO the engine stores no zero - 0x516af-0x516c2
  reads a key string at [scene+0x398] (ds:0xcef40 is the scene
  block), looks it up through 0x44110 against the same name
  tables the clause parser uses (0x961fc/0x96200) and stores
  the answer at [row+0x8]. The directive chain call and the
  prepend are at 0x516d5-0x516e6 exactly as PR-217 read them.
  (c) THE CLOCK. The field the row step compares against
  (0x52320-0x5232b, `mov eax,[row+0x10]` / `mov ebx,
  [obj+0xa1]` / `cmp eax,ebx` / `jge 0x52354`) is the OBJECT's
  [obj+0xa1], not the state record's. Its writers are: the
  row-run verb 0x520c0 at 0x52114-0x52118, which sets it to the
  budget the row step handed it in ebx (clock - frame on the
  clause path, 0 on the clause-less path); the row reset at
  0x5236b, which writes 0; and 0x533b0/0x5389e, which write 0
  at construction. Its feeder is 0x543a0, the object verb held
  at +0xa0 of the LION class table: it reads the current state
  record's control bits `[rec+0x12] & 7`, jumps the table at
  0x54380 and adds, by case, |[obj+0xca]| (0x543c6-0x543d1),
  |[obj+0xce]| (0x543dc-0x543e7), or the scene's frame delta
  [scene+0x388] gated by [obj+0xba] / [obj+0xbe]
  (0x543f2-0x54414, 0x5441b-0x5443d) - the port's own
  distance-fed versus wall-time-fed split (PR-110, PR-114), now
  with the field names and the switch that picks between them.
  (d) THE ROW-RUN VERB. 0x520c0 is the record class 0xa260c's
  +0x18, reached as `call DWORD PTR [esi+0x18]` with
  esi = [rec+0x44] - the record's own class word, which is also
  what makes 0xa11c8 = 0xa11c0+8 and 0xa11e0 = 0xa11d8+8 in
  PR-218's note. It clones the row (0x520e1), composes the key
  with the global 0x98278 (0x520e6-0x520f2), calls the class's
  +0x28 (0x52100), sets the clock (0x52118), runs the row
  through its class's +0x10 with edx = 6 and a local mode at
  [esp+0xc] (0x52124-0x5213d), tests that mode against 6
  (0x52140), then does the frame-list end/walk: 0x521b6-0x521d4
  compares [list+0x8] - 1 against the cursor and OR-s bit 4 or
  bit 8 into the CALLER's set byte 0 (0x521a1, 0x521c1) -
  PR-135's list-end bit, seen by the NEXT step's key
  composition, now named. (e) A THIRD CHAIN
  VERB. The row class 0xa2638 answers +0x00 = 0x55820,
  +0x04 = 0x457e0, +0x08 = 0x45800, +0x0c = 0x45870,
  +0x10 = 0x458e0, +0x14 = the clone 0x51620, and 0x458e0 is
  another chain walker: `mov esi,[eax]`, and if there is an
  operand `movsx edx,dl` (the mode number, 6 from 0x52138) and
  `call [operand_class+0x10]`. Both directive families carry the
  same entry (0xa11c0+0x18 and 0xa11d8+0x18 are 0x458e0), and
  the call is made with ebx = &rec+0x4 (the row cursor) and
  ecx = a local mode that 0x52140 compares against 6. So this
  verb does not read the row's authored numbers at all; which
  verb applies them, and which field it applies as the time, is
  the half OI-112 leaves open. (f) THE DATA. The shipped row
  grammar puts an index first and a time second: KADMAR.07 `_0_0.MOV`

MEASURED: (a) THE RECORD. The state record is 0x48 bytes

  the GLOBAL 0xceff4 (0x51a35). (c) THE ROWS. 0x51eb0 first
  scans the row line's leading number with `%d,` (0x92156,
  0x51aa1). Then at 0x51f37-0x51f54: `mov eax,[rec+0xe]`,
  `mov edx,[eax+0xe]`, `push edx` - the record's time_scale IS
  the row ctor's scale factor, read from the record, not from a
  line position - then `lea eax,[esp+4]`, `call 0x57fd0`
  (0x57fd0 = `mov eax,[eax]` + a jump into the string copy at
  0x76fa3: the ctor's first argument is a COPY of the line),
  `mov ebx,ds:0xceff4` (0x51f48 - the sequence's default just
  registered), ecx = the copy, edx = the line, `call 0x515e0`.
  Inside 0x515e0's line parser 0x51660 the ONE scan is
  `%hi` (0x92115) into [row+0x10] (0x51662-0x51676) and the
  multiply/divide by the caller's factor is 0x51679-0x5168f, so
  `[row+0x10] = first * [rec+0xe] / 1000`. The value handed in
  ebx goes to [row+0x8] (0x5169e/0x516cf) and the second
  authored number to [row+0xc] with the sign flag at
  [row+0x14], 0 replaced by 0x44110's registry answer (0x516bd)
  exactly as PR-219 read. (d) THE GATE IS A COMPARE, NOT A
  SUBTRACTION. 0x52320-0x5232b: `mov eax,[row+0x10]`,
  `mov ebx,[obj+0xa1]`, `cmp eax,ebx`, `jge 0x52354` - if the
  clock has NOT reached [row+0x10] the step runs nothing at
  all. When it has, 0x52334 computes `ebx = [obj+0xa1] -
  [row+0x10]`, the OVERSHOOT, and passes it as the budget to
  the row-run verb 0x520c0 at 0x52338; the row step's other
  path (a row whose clause matched, 0x522fc-0x5232b) runs the
  row's directives first, feeds the clock at 0x52317, and then
  makes the same compare with ebx = 0. Nothing decrements
  [obj+0xa1] here; only the reset 0x5236b and construction
  write 0 (PR-219). (e) THE CONTROL BITS, NAMED. The `control=`
  branch 0x51b0d takes the first token with ` %[^,| \r\n\t]`
  (0x9215d) and OR-s a bit into [rec+0x12]: BY_X = 1 (0x51b6f),
  BY_Y = 2 (0x51b89), BY_TIME = 4 (0x51ba3), BY_TX = 8

  (0x51c3f), SEQ_REV_X = 0x40 (0x51c25), SEQ_REV_Y = 0x80
  (0x51c0b), more at [rec+0x13] (0x51c59). That is the byte
  0x543a0 masks with 7, and its table 0x54380 is case 0 ->
  |[obj+0xca]|, 1 -> |[obj+0xce]|, 2 -> 0x543fb, 3 -> 0x543f2,
  4 -> 0x5441b: BY_X feeds the clock with the distance walked
  in X, BY_Y in Y, and the remaining cases take the scene
  frame-delta paths. The port's LL_CTRL_BY_TIME = 1 /
  LL_CTRL_BY_X = 2 are its own vocabulary and do not equal
  these values; cases 3 and 4 differ only in their guard

  adding `[scene+0x388]` to [obj+0xa1]. (f) THE DATA.
  KADMAR.07 `_0_0.MOV` 112-127 is

  `1,1000,gen K_GEN1`, `2,400`, ... - the first column counts

  number the row step's compare actually gates on, is OI-112"

CODE: no: this PR ships no code. It reads, and it re-opens what
  PR-220 seemed to settle.
HOOKS: none new, none touched.
MEASURED: (a) THE PARSE DESTINATION. The raw bytes of 0x51660
  are `push esi; push edi; push ebp; mov esi,eax; mov edi,edx;
  add eax,0x10; push eax; push 0x92115; push edx;
  call 0x49920; add esp,0xc` - THREE pushes and one cleanup of
  0xc, so the scan gets exactly its three cdecl arguments (the
  line, the format `%hi`, ONE destination, [row+0x10]). The
  helper 0x49920 pushes the caller's EDX and EBX and the local
  format pointer, then calls 0x49870, which calls the scanf
  pointer stored at `[eax+4]` through `call DWORD PTR [edi]`
  (0x4987c); every other caller of 0x49920 in the image
  (0x1f579, 0x2787e, 0x5194e, 0x52640, 0x51aa1 to name four)
  reads the parsed values back from the destination memory and
  never from a register. There is no second destination for the
  row line: the ctor parses one number, the first, and scales it
  into [row+0x10] (0x51679-0x5168f, PR-220). (b) THE FLAG AND
  THE DEFAULT. After that scan EAX is the scanf return: 0x51692
  `test ecx,ecx; jge 0x516ad`, and the raw bytes show the value
  compared is followed by `inc ecx` (0x5169d), `mov [esi+0x8],
  ebx`, `mov [esi+0xc],eax` after `neg eax` (0x516a6-0x516a8) -
  i.e. the "second number" it stores is +2 or -2, and 0x516ad's
  `jne 0x516c7` branch stores `dec ecx` = -1 with
  [row+0x14] = 0, while the zero case writes [row+0xc] = 0 and
  takes [row+0x8] from 0x44110 (0x516bd). A store of the
  CONSTANT 2 / -2 / -1 with a flag is what a scan count
  produces, not what a parsed value produces. What IS the
  caller's value is EBX, preserved across the scan by the
  helper: the row-list builder passes `mov ebx,ds:0xceff4`
  (0x51f48) - the sequence default of PR-220's (b) - and the
  other row-ctor caller (0x51ac1) passes the object looked up
  by name through the settings block (0x51a76 registers the
  empty key at 0x57d30, 0x51a86 reads the settings block's
  name-table field, 0x51a92 calls its +0x4 verb with the token
  scanned from the line); 0x92143 is the bytes `seq` of the
  settings branch, so both callers hand the row a looked-up
  default, never a row-line number. (c) THE GRAMMAR, COUNTED.
  Across the 777 extracted .MOV texts every row line has exactly
  two numbers: 18617 match `<n>,<m>`, 0 are a bare single
  number, 2617 have a negative first value and the largest
  absolute first value in the whole set is 82 (ENA.03_ROZGW
  `-5,4`, `-6,4`, `-7,4`, `-8,4`, then `-7,4`, `-6,4` - the
  first column walks up and DOWN). No engine path reads a second
  row-line number. (d) THE ROW REPEATS ON ANSWER 6.
  0x52120 zeroes the local answer, 0x52138 sets edx = 6 and
  0x5213d calls the row's +0x10 (the chain verb 0x458e0, which
  forwards the mode to the operand's own +0x10 with ebx =
  &rec+0x4, the row cursor); 0x52140 `cmp DWORD PTR [esp+0xc],
  0x6; je 0x521da` - when the answer IS 6 the walk at
  0x52195-0x521d4 is skipped ENTIRELY and [rec+0x4] keeps its
  value: the row will be run again. Otherwise the walk runs:
  with a negative cursor 0x521a1 OR-s bit 8 and sets the cursor
  to count-1 (0x521a5-0x521a9), at the last entry 0x521c1 OR-s
  bit 4 and zeroes it, otherwise 0x521d4 adds one. That is
  PR-135's list-end bit and PR-95's SEQ_REV walk with their
  addresses, and it says the row's length is decided by its
  chain answering 6, not by a stored duration. (e) WHERE NUMBERS
  ARE READ. The base node class 0xa0f28 (create 0x46d70, clone
  0x459b0, test 0x45800, execute 0x45870, chain 0x458e0,
  0x47c90) has verbs that DO read their node's arguments:
  0x45d50 calls the chain (0x458e0) and then, if the answer
  equals the byte at [node+0x10], adds [node+0x8] to *[ebx] and
  [node+0xc] to *[ecx] (0x45d6e-0x45d7e); 0x45d90 and 0x45dc0
  call the chain and if the answer is 6 write *[ebx] =
  [node+0x8] or *[ebx] += [node+0x8] and set the answer to 6
  (0x45dad-0x45db3, 0x45ddd-0x45de2). So directive nodes carry
  their authored numbers in their OWN +0x8/+0xc and gate on
  their +0x10 - which is where the row line's other numbers must
  be parsed, not into the row.
OPENS: OI-112, again, and narrowed further: where does the second
  authored number of a row line go? Nothing in the row ctor
  parses it and no class verb of the row, the node base or the
  record (PR-220 (f)) reads [row+0x8]/[row+0xc]. The two
  candidates PR-221 did not settle: the clause/directive node
  family (0xa11c0's test is 0x45970, 0xa11d8's execute is
  0x45920, and the `Wait`-clause rows are exactly the ones the
  engine leaves at answer 6 - PR-218's "the clause selects the
  path, never refuses the row" needs rereading against (d)), and
  a per-row counter the engine may keep in the CLONE it makes at
  0x520e1 rather than in the row. The port's `.thresh` model is
  NOT contradicted by this PR - its fixtures pin it and pass -
  but its claimed engine source (`%hi` into node+0x10,
  ported/ll_play.c:524) is now known to be the FIRST number,
  and the second number's engine site is unnamed. Do not move
  behaviour before that is settled.
CLOSES: nothing in the register.
CORRECTS: PR-220's (b)/(c) sentence "The SECOND value is handled
  at 0x51692-0x516d2: its magnitude goes to [row+0xc] with a
  sign flag at [row+0x14]" - those store sites are right, and
  what they store is not the second authored number: the parse
  destination of 0x51660 holds exactly one address, so no second
  number is parsed, and the values stored there are ±2/-1 plus a
  flag from the scan's result, with [row+0x8] taken from the
  caller's default (the sequence's, or a name lookup).
  PR-220's claim that KADMAR.07's `[A_DEAD]` durations are
  "100/1000 unscaled" is therefore unsupported: those numbers
  have no engine consumer named yet. PR-110's note that the
  engine "reads %hi into node+0x10 first" stays correct; the
  port's own row parse (`%d,%d`, frame from the first, thresh
  from the second, ported/ll_play.c:521) is NOT the engine's
  read of those two fields.

HOOKS: none new, none touched.
MEASURED: (a) THE VOCABULARY. The engine's directive keywords
  sit in one string block at 0x91847-0x91990, scanned with
  ` %[^,| \r\n\t]` (0x91844) and matched by 0x76a69 against the
  token in [ebp-0x8]: `rev`, `zero_v`, `zero`, `zero_t`,
  `vol_music`, `smp` (` %i`), `smp2` (` %i , %i`), `smp3`
  (` %i , %i , %i`), `smpauto`, `smpauto2`, `smpprior` (` %d`),
  `vol`, `smp_loop`, `smp_unloop`, `smp_stop`, `atc_on`,
  `atc_off`, `lock`, `lock2`, `unlock`, `unlock2`, `ground_on`,
  `ground_off`, `chdir`, `ldir`, `rdir`, `pos` (` %i , %i`),
  `goto` (`%d`), `gotorel`, `goto_rel`, `I` (` %i,%i`), `F`,
  `IC`, `FC`, `M` (` %i,%i`), `MOVE`, `GEN`, `Wait`. Every
  argument set is read by a scan with THAT format into the node
  (e.g. 0x46beb-0x46bf9: an 0xc-byte node, class word 0xa1048
  at [node+0x4], `push 0x91998` = `%d`, `call 0x49920`).
  (b) AN UNKNOWN WORD ENDS THE ROW'S TAIL. 0x46c1c: when the
  token matches no keyword, the engine reports it through
  0x496b0 against the format string at 0x9199d with the text
  pointer at [esi+5] and the global 0xa92d4, calls 0x49620, and
  returns EBX = 0 (0x46c55) - the chain build stops there
  (0x516e8 `test ebx,ebx; jne 0x516d5`). So digits after the
  row's second field are never consumed: the shipped texts
  confirm it, 0 row lines have a bare number as their third
  field. (c) THE SHIPPED TAILS, COUNTED over the 777 .MOV
  texts, field 3 of `<n>,<m>,<tail>`: `smpauto` 370,
  `GEN K_GEN1` 288, `ATC_OFF` 242, `ATC_ON` 235,
  `GEN AC_PLAT_OFF` 181, `M` with a 0 first argument 172,
  `WAIT K_NEVER` 157, `F` with 0 99, `lock` 92, `unlock` 66,
  `GEN AC_TIME` 60, `F` with -300/-330/-250 36/36/36,
  `zero` 30, `WAIT K_GEN1` 25. (Field splitting is on commas,
  so a tail's argument may be glued to its word, `M0`/`F0`.)
  The port counts this set as "modeled / captured / counted"
  already; what this PR adds is that the engine's own keyword
  spellings are the lower/mixed-case forms (`atc_on`, `ground_on`,
  `smpauto`, `Wait`) and that its own scan format for `M` and
  `I` is `%i,%i` with `%i`, not `%d`. (d) THE NODES AND THE
  ANSWER-6 CARRIERS. Clause nodes are allocated by their create
  verbs - 0x46c70 (`GEN`, class 0xa11e0) and 0x46cf0 (`Wait`,
  class 0xa11c8) both allocate 0x8 + 0xc and copy the parsed
  EventSet through 0x47d60; the base clause node 0xa0f28 is
  allocated by 0x47c90 (0x8 bytes, class word at [node+0x4]).
  The node base table's sibling sub-tables override +0x10 with
  the verbs that answer 6: 0xa1038 → 0x45dc0 (`*[ebx] +=
  [node+0x8]`, answer ← 6) and 0xa1040 → 0x45d90 (`*[ebx] =
  [node+0x8]`, answer ← 6) - the second is the `goto` jump on
  the row cursor EBX = &rec+0x4 (PR-221 (d)), the first a
  cursor delta - and 0xa1098 → 0x45d50, which after its own
  chain checks the answer against the node's trigger byte
  [node+0x10] and then adds [node+0x8] to *[ebx] and
  [node+0xc] to *[ecx]. A row is therefore re-run (cursor held,
  0x52140) exactly while one of ITS OWN directive nodes answers
  6, not while a clock says so. (e) WHERE THE ROW CURSOR IS
  PLACED ON STATE ENTRY. The record's row-reset verb (class
  0xa260c +0x1c = 0x52360) rolls the `time=` default through
  0x52070 (PR-220), zeroes [obj+0xa1] (0x5236b), sets
  [obj+0x99] = 1, and then PLACES THE CURSOR: for edx >= 0 it
  writes [rec+0x4] = edx, or with the state's 0x10/0x20 exit
  bits XOR-ed into the choice, [rec+0x4] = [list+0x8] - edx - 1
  (0x523bc-0x523cb). The rolled `time=`/sequence-default number
  is used as a ROW INDEX: entering a state starts it at row k,
  or at count-1-k.
OPENS: OI-112 again, narrowed further. What this PR could NOT
  settle: the first step of the chain builder is not a keyword
  compare but a FIELD SPLIT. 0x45df0 at 0x45dfc-0x45e18 calls
  0x57d30 with EBX = the static defaults table 0x961fc, EDX = 1,
  ECX = the pattern 0x91844 (the bytes are ` , %[^,| \r\n\t]` -
  a comma separator THEN the token class, so the "pattern" is
  what separates fields, and the token class is the keyword
  scan), and the text in EAX, then 0x45e20-0x45e38 treats a
  NULL or empty first field as "no more text" (0x45e3a-0x45e55:
  an empty node) and otherwise takes the result at [ebp-0x8] to
  the keyword compares (0x45e7d: `mov edx,0x91852` = the string
  `rev`, the first word of the table, then `call 0x76a69`).
  0x57d30 is now read: it copies a static 125-entry scratch
  table from 0xa9510 to the stack, dispatches on EDX through a
  jump table at 0x57d20 - 0 = bare scan 0x49920, 1 = bare scan
  0x498f0, 2 = separator-stripping 0x49950, 3 = 0x499b0 - to
  fill the scratch with the scan's values, and hands the array
  to 0x57990, which frees the previous string (0x579e0) and
  copies the new one out a wide-character-at-a-time copy
  (0x579c2-0x579d8). Its callers include the settings-block
  readers 0x51a1f/0x51a76 (EBX = the block object, PR-221's
  sequence default), the clause parser 0x47d97 (EBX = 0x961fc
  with the format 0x919bc, mode 0) and 0x44480 (EBX = 0x961fc,
  mode 3). 0x961fc is STATIC data whose own fields point at
  0x96200 - the defaults block of that settings/string object,
  132 code sites name it, and 0x57a00 stamps the class word
  0x96200 on the objects that hold these strings. So the
  engine reads a row line as comma-separated fields, first
  field = the first authored number, then a keyword token, and
  the exact use of the array vs. the table at 0x961fc inside
  0x57990 is the first thing the next PR should read. The named
  lead for the keyword arguments: the scan helpers differ.
  0x49920/0x498f0 are BARE scans
  (they pass the caller's format straight through), but
  0x49950/0x499b0 first strip separators in a loop (`%c` at
  0x91cda, then 0x91ce1/0x91cf1, 0x4996d-0x49980) and only then
  apply the real format - a format like ` %[^,| \r\n\t]` only
  behaves as "skip the separator, take the next token" through
  THAT kind of helper. And the unknown-word report is the string
  at 0x9199d, `Bledna komenda %s w` - the engine's own "bad
  command" diagnostic. OI-112's
  second-authored-number question is unchanged and stands as
  written: no path in the row ctor, the row chain build or any
  class verb consumes it, and the shipped data never puts a bare
  number where a directive word would be.
CLOSES: nothing in the register.
CORRECTS: PR-221's OPEN paragraph named "the clause/directive
  node family" as an unsettled candidate for where a row's
  numbers go: this PR reads that family and closes that part -
  clause nodes hold only the 12-byte set plus the mode byte
  (0x46c70/0x46cf0 allocate 0x8+0xc), and the numbers a row
  tail carries belong to the keyword-argument nodes (`M`/`I`/
  `pos`/`goto`/`smp`), which is where the port's `dx,dy`
  already comes from. It also narrows PR-217's/PR-218's note
  that a `Wait` tail is "the same ctor/parser as GEN": the
  creates are separate (0x46cf0 vs 0x46c70, classes 0xa11c8 vs
  0xa11e0) even though the clause parser at 0x47d60 is shared.

CODE: no: this PR ships no code.
HOOKS: none new, none touched.
MEASURED: (a) HOW A CLASS TABLE IS ADDRESSED. A node's class
  word IS its create verb: the 0x18-byte table at that address
  is create/+0x04 clone/+0x08 test/+0x0c execute/+0x10 chain/
  +0x14 a sixth verb. That reads cleanly on the two tables whose
  numbering PR-219/PR-220 had already pinned from use - the
  RECORD 0xa260c = 0x51910 (its +0x00, the block-settings
  dispatcher)/0x23c90/0x559c0/0x521f0 (row step)/0x23c80/0x518f0
  - and the ROW 0xa2638 = 0x55820 (row ctor)/0x457e0/0x45800/
  0x45870/0x458e0/0x51620 (its clone) - and it makes PR-220's
  "node base 0xa1000 = 0x457b0/0x457e0/0x45800/0x45870/0x458e0,
  the Wait word 0xa11c0 = ... and the GEN word 0xa11d8" wrong:
  0xa11c0 is the 5th slot of the `ground_on`-family table 0xa10b0
  (0x458e0) and 0xa11d8 is the `Wait` clause's chain slot
  (0xa11c8 + 0x10), not tables. 0xa1000 is the base NODE class
  only in the sense that the node ctor 0x45780 stamps it at
  [node+0x4]; the region is a list of 0x18-byte per-directive
  tables. (b) THE FULL VOCABULARY, read as the builder's own compare
  sequence (every `mov edx,<word>` + `call 0x76a69` pair in
  0x45df0-0x46d80, in address order): `rev` 0x45e85, `zero_v`
  0x45ec9, `zero` 0x45f0d, `zero_t` 0x45f51, `vol_music` 0x45f95,
  `smp` 0x45fef, `smp2` 0x4604d, `smp3` 0x460af, `smpauto`
  0x4611a, `smpauto2` 0x46162, `smpprior` 0x461c1, `vol` 0x4621c,
  `smp_loop` 0x4627f, `smp_unloop` 0x462e5, `smp_stop` 0x4632d,
  `atc_on` 0x46375, `atc_off` 0x463c5, `lock` 0x46412, `lock2`
  0x46462, `unlock` 0x464b9, `unlock2` 0x46506, `ground_on`
  0x4655a, `ground_off` 0x465b1, `chdir` 0x46605, `ldir` 0x4664d,
  `rdir` 0x46695, `pos` 0x466dd, `goto` 0x46740, `gotorel`
  0x467a6, `goto_rel` 0x46816, `I` 0x46882, `F` 0x468e6, `IC`
  0x4694e, `FC` 0x469b6, `M` 0x46a1e, `MOVE` 0x46a81, `GEN`
  0x46aeb, `Wait` 0x46b59, `end_level` 0x46bc7 - 39 keywords,
  and the chain ends at 0x46c1c for anything else. PAIRING a
  keyword to the class it stores is only safe where the store
  sits in that keyword's own branch: verified - `rev` -> 0xa0f28
  (the base CLAUSE node: no operand, set inline at [node+0x8]),
  `zero_v` -> 0xa0fa0, `zero`/`zero_t` -> 0xa0f88, `smpauto`/
  `atc_on`/`atc_off` -> 0xa10f0 (the builder stores 1 into
  [node+0x8], 0x46393-0x4639f), `lock`/`lock2`/`unlock`/
  `unlock2`/`ground_on`/`ground_off` -> 0xa10d8 with a second
  class 0xa10a8 (and 0xa10c0) chosen in the same branch for the
  no-argument forms, `chdir` -> 0xa0f40, `ldir` -> 0xa0f58,
  `rdir` -> 0xa0f70, `F` -> 0xa1090, `MOVE` -> 0xa1060, `Wait`
  -> 0xa11c8 (0x46b99), `GEN` -> 0xa11e0 (0x46b28), and
  `end_level` -> 0xa1048 (create 0x46c70, the `%i` scan at
  0x46beb with format 0x91998), which is the node PR-194/PR-199
  named. NOT paired: `smp`/`smp2`/`smp3`/`smpauto2`/`smpprior`/
  `vol`/`smp_loop`/`smp_unloop`/`smp_stop`/`pos`/`goto`/
  `gotorel`/`goto_rel`/`I`/`IC`/`FC`/`M` - their branches share
  the 0x46100-0x46c00 range and pairing needs a branch walk, so
  no class is claimed for them here.
  (c) WHERE THE
  ARGUMENTS AND ANSWER-6 LIVE. Since the chain walk calls the
  operand's +0x10 slot and a directive's table is 0x18 long, the
  verbs PR-221/PR-222 found - 0x45d90 (`*[ebx] = [node+0x8]`,
  answer <- 6), 0x45dc0 (`*[ebx] += [node+0x8]`, answer <- 6),
  0x45d50 (gate on [node+0x10], then apply [node+0x8]/[node+0xc])
  - are the +0x14 (6th) verbs of directive classes: 0xa1048 +0x14
  = 0x45d90 (`end_level`: `*[ebx] = [node+0x8]`, so THE ROW
  CURSOR IS SET TO THE AUTHORED NUMBER and the answer becomes 6),
  0xa1030 +0x14 = 0x45dc0 (a cursor delta), 0xa1090 +0x14 =
  0x45d50 (the class `F` builds, gated on [node+0x10]). So a
  row is held by a DIRECTIVE its own line carries, not by a
  clock, and `Wait`/`GEN` clause nodes do NOT hold it: their
  +0x10 chain verb is the base chain walker 0x458e0 and they have
  no operand (the node ctor 0x45780 writes 0 at [node+0] and only
  clones an operand when the ctor is given one; the clause parser
  0x47d60 fills the set INLINE at [node+0x8]). (d) THE CLAUSE
  VERBS, cleanly split: a clause node's TEST (+0x08) answers with
  its own authored set - 0x45970 copies [node+0x8..0xc] - while
  its EXECUTE (+0x0c) is the base delegate 0x45870, which with no
  operand returns an EMPTY set: a `Wait` tests and raises nothing.
  The `GEN` clause 0xa11e0 keeps the base test 0x45800 but its
  execute is 0x45920: it calls the base execute 0x45870 and ORs
  its own [node+0x8] in through 0x49580 - which is the engine's
  raise path for `GEN <signal>`: the row step's non-empty branch
  0x522fc calls the row's execute and ORs the result into the
  CALLER's set at 0x5230c (a 12-byte local zeroed at 0x52207).
  (e) THE ENGINE'S SIGNAL-RAISE MESSAGE, and the port's ordinals
  confirmed against it: the handler 0x53772 tests the message
  type 0x10 and the tag 0x8138764, reads the payload BYTE at
  [msg+0xc] as a SIGNAL INDEX, and ORs `1 << (idx % 32)` into
  DWORD PTR [obj+0x60 + 4*(idx >> 5)] (0x53790-0x537d2), then
  ORs the whole local set into [obj+0x60] through 0x49580 - the
  68-signal TEventSet of PR-88, raised one bit at a time. Its
  senders call 0x4bc40 with EBX = the message type and the
  payload pushed: 0x2c5cd sends 0x21 with tag 0x8138764 and
  0x2c611 sends 0x1c, 0x2c651 sends 0x1b - which are EXACTLY
  this port's LL_SIG_K_FWD = 36, LL_SIG_K_UP = 28,
  LL_SIG_K_DOWN = 27, so the port's signal ordinals are the
  engine's own message payload numbers (PR-88's table confirmed
  from the raising side for the first time). The record's +0x28
  verb 0x518f0 also names a field: it allocates the 0x48-byte
  record, calls the state ctor 0x517e0 and writes the ARGUMENT
  into [rec+0x0], which the row step reads as the owner at
  0x52214/0x52311/0x5232d ([obj+0xa1] the clock, [obj+0x8] its
  class) - the record knows its object from creation.
OPENS: OI-078 stays open, narrowed to one named question: NO
  sender of 0x10/0x8138764 passes 54 = K_GEN1 - all 22 call
  sites of 0x4bc40 use small AC_* indexes (7, 0x12, 0x13, 0x19,
  0x1a, 0x1b, 0x1c, 0x21) or a value loaded from an object field
  (0x1f45c, 0x34a7f, 0x3a1cf: `[obj+0xee]`, `[obj+0xf2]`), and

  set rather than a signal near the top of the table.
  OI-112 unchanged: the
  second authored number still has no consumer, and (b) makes it

CLOSES: nothing in the register.
CORRECTS: PR-220's (f) - "for a NODE the class word is the table

  singly-linked queue at [obj+0x10] to its tail node (0x52b13-
  0x52b20; the head cell itself holds no message), allocates a
  0x10-byte node, writes link=0, [msg+4]=type, [msg+8]=tag,
  [msg+0xc]=payload (0x52b30-0x52b3c) and links it. Receiver in
  eax, type in edx, tag in ebx, payload in ecx. Pump 0x52b50:
  for every queued message calls the RECEIVER's vtable slot +0x10
  (0x52b67); 0x52b80 is the frame step: vtable +0x14 first, then
  the pump, then vtable +0x00 if [obj+0x28] is set. Base message
  handler 0x52bb0: dispatches
  on the TAG at [msg+4]: tag 1 adds a position delta (edx=[msg+
  8], ecx=[msg+0xc] into [obj+0x50]/[obj+0x54], 0x52bc6-0x52bd7),
  tag 0xe stores [msg+8] into the object named by [msg+0xc]
  ([obj+0x30]), tag 0x21 writes 1 to [obj+0x28]; anything else
  is ignored. 0x53772 (b) is a derived +0x10 handler that ends
  with 0x52bb0 in its non-signal branch, so 0x52bb0 is the base
  version of the same slot. The engine's tag numbers ARE the
  signal numbers of
  this port's table: 0x21 = 33 = LL_SIG_K_FWD.
  (b) THE SIGNAL FAMILY. A signal message is type 0x10 with tag
  0x8138764 and payload = signal index; the handler 0x53772
  checks BOTH (0x5377b, 0x53780) and ORs the bit. The magic tag
  occurs at EXACTLY SIX producer sites in the whole image
  (0x2882d, 0x2c5e1, 0x2c613, 0x2c653, 0x2c99a, 0x3eacf) plus
  that one check - so the set of raisers is closed and small.
  (c) THE RAISERS, one by one. Broadcast helper 0x4bc40:
  receiver=eax (the scene), type=edx, tag=ebx, selector=ecx
  (0=every object; otherwise match [obj]'s vtable+0xc = class id,
  0x4bcc1-0x4bcc9), extra pushed arg = payload written to [msg+
  0xc]; it delivers by calling 0x52b10 per object (0x4bcd7).
  Signal sends through it: 0x2c5cd raises 0x21=33 (K_FWD) when
  [obj+0x5c]=2 and the one-shot latch ds:0xcec70 is 0; 0x2c611
  raises 0x1c=28 (K_UP); 0x2c651 raises 0x1b=27 (K_DOWN). The
  three indexes are EXACTLY LL_SIG_K_FWD/K_UP/K_DOWN, confirming
  PR-88's ordinals from the raising side. Direct enqueues:
  0x2c99f raises signal 0x15=21 on [0xcef40+0x394]; 0x3a1dc
  raises signal 0x1e=30 on the object itself (payload =
  [obj+0xf6]) when its [obj+0xee] equals [obj+0xf2]. Synthetic
  stack message + direct vtable+0x10 call at 0x2882d-0x2885a:
  type 0x10, tag magic, signal 0x0a=10. The collision loop
  0x3eac6-0x3eaf4 builds the same synthetic shape (0x3eabd type
  0x10, 0x3eacf tag, 0x3eae3 signal 0x39=57) and calls the
  collided object's handler for every entry of its neighbour list
  ([obj+0x3c], count [x+0x3c], index via 0x55760).
  (d) NON-SIGNAL SENDS. A plain message has type = the signal/
  tag number and tag 0 (or a subsystem constant): e.g. 0x1ea52/
  0x1ea65 enqueue tag-27 then tag-13(payload 100) on the object
  after a vtable+0x8 probe fails, and 0x1eab9 first checks
  vtable+0xc (= class id, compared to ds:0xceba4). This CORRECTS
  PR-224's (e): the field-fed sites 0x1f454, 0x34a7f etc. pass
  their subsystem constant in EDX = the TYPE slot (ds:0xcebfc,
  ds:0xced04, 0x967f4) with tag 0, so they were NEVER signal
  raises - the "field-fed sender" candidate of PR-224 is closed.
  (e) OTHER SET WRITES (not messages): at a collision the engine
  ORs 4 into the object's set (0x3edff/0x3ee01), ORs in the set
  at [[obj+0x3c]+0x60] (0x3ee04-0x3ee11 - the CURRENT STATE
  object carries a TEventSet at +0x60), and vtable+0x8c (base
  0x536f0) merges its result into [obj+0x60] every frame
  (0x536ff-0x53725).
OPENS: OI-078 narrowed hard: the raise senders are CLOSED and

  carried set at [[obj+0x3c]+0x60] (0x3ee04) - what the state

  or the shipped `.MOV` maps the WORD `K_GEN1` to an index among

  [obj+0x60] (0x53705-0x53725). This PR finds the other side:
  102 class vtables in 0x9a000-0xa2500 hold 0x54910 at slot +0x
  8c (verified samples 0x9a1c0, 0x9a700, 0xa1c10) - the ordinary
  scene-object classes implement the slot as a SIGNAL PROVIDER,
  and the frame refresh calls it on every object every frame.
  (b) THE PROVIDER'S LAW, 0x54910-0x549e6, machine code, bit by
  bit. Build a 12-byte TEventSet (mode byte 0, 0x5491d-0x5492c),
  then: if [obj+0xa5] bit 0x1 set, raise 33 = K_FWD (0x54931-
  0x5493a: OR 0x80 into byte 4 = dword 1 bit 1 = index 33); if
  bit 0x10 set, raise 41 = this port's K_F6 slot (OR 1 into
  byte 5, 0x5493f-0x54948); if bit 0x20 set, RAISE 54 = K_GEN1
  (OR 0x20 into byte 6 = dword 1 bit 22, 0x5494d-0x54956). If
  [obj+0xba] != 0: test [obj+0xb6] bit 0x10 - clear raises 35
  (`add al,0x23` = 35 = K_BKWD, 0x54964-0x54970) and set raises
  36 = K_FWD; if [obj+0xbe] < 0 raise bit 29, if > 0 raise bit
  30 (0x5499d-0x549b4). Finally copy the 12 bytes + mode byte to
  the caller (0x549c8-0x549d8). THE DRABINKA'S WAIT K_GEN1 HAS
  ITS ENGINE RAISER: bit 0x20 of the object dword at +0xa5,
  evaluated continuously by the frame refresh - no message and no
  `GEN` row is needed, which is why no sender passes 54.
  (c) WHERE THE TESTED FLAGS COME FROM. [obj+0xb6] bit 0x10 is
  maintained at 0x54bb0-0x54bd4: `setl` of (edx * [obj+0x6d]),
  shifted 4, OR-ed into that dword - the SIGN of the object's
  word at +0x6d (its speed). [obj+0xa5] is initialized 0
  (0x2b6a0), copied by the object clone (0x2b840), and read as
  an INDEX into a table at [obj+0xa9] elsewhere (0x2b727,
  0x2b81b) - the same dword plays both roles; the bit-0x20
  writer is NOT found yet (no `or ...,0x20` exists; the dword
  sites are 0x2b840 clone-copy and 0x54be9, which stores
  [[ecx+0x8]] - a different class).
  (d) THE MIRROR FLAG AND `rev`. State records carry flag word
  +0x12; bit 0x800 (tested as `test dh,0x8` on the WORD,
  0x5367b-0x5367e) is the state MIRROR flag: on entry the
  engine does `neg DWORD PTR [obj+0x6d]` and calls vtable+0x54

  it loads the row's object at [node+0x0] (stored by 0x518f0,

  tail flips the object's speed sign, exactly the PR-222 keyword
  `rev` 0x45e85 / class 0xa0f28 whose execute was the base
  delegate: this is what that execute DOES. (The port's mirror
  model - frame sign XOR facing, PR-82 - draws the same fact;
  the engine additionally flips the SPEED word.)
  (e) THE STATE'S ROW CHAIN. [obj+0x50] is an array of state

  whose payload holds an OBJECT POINTER puts the target's class

  therefore means: "attached to an object whose class vtable
  address low byte has bit 0x20 set" - true for every class
  table in the 0x9a778-style range, statically inspectable.

  layout: [msg+8]=ebx, [msg+0xc]=ecx). So AC_RECT means "my

  message. (b) THE HANDLER'S STORES. PR-228's +0xfc arm 0x50dc7
  passes edx=[[msg+8]] - THE OTHER OBJECT'S POINTER ITSELF - and
  ebx=[msg+0xc]. Raw bytes decode the entry 0x549f0 exactly:
  `push ebx; push ecx; push esi; mov ebx,eax; mov ecx,edx;
  mov eax,[edx]; mov [ebx+0xba],eax; mov eax,[edx+4];
  mov [ebx+0xbe],eax; ...` and at 0x54be6-0x54be9
  `mov eax,[ecx+0x8]; mov [ebx+0xa5],eax` (ecx is still the
  other object) - so [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe] = the other object's
  first two dwords and [obj+0xa5] = THE OTHER OBJECT'S WORD AT
  +0x8. The block also gates on [other+4] being 1 (0x54a1b) or 2
  (0x54b65) and calls [[other]+0x68] (0x54a40). The stored word
  lands exactly in the byte the provider (PR-226) tests.

  vtable: it is the KIND METHOD TABLE - 0x9a754 is a table of

  0x453d0, 0x45400 - the very helpers of PR-88/PR-227) and
  0x54a40 calls [[obj+0x8]+0x68] on the carried object (kind-
  family verb, e.g. 0x504e0 in class 0xa21e8). PR-221's
  `call [vtable+0xc]` compared against ds:0xceba4 = 0x96fd8 is
  THIS word (the "class id" PR-225 used loosely). (d) THE BIT
  LAW, FINALLY. Provider: bit 0x1 -> 33 (K_FWD), bit 0x10 -> 41,
  bit 0x20 -> 54 (K_GEN1). Kind-pointer low bytes, measured

then the class verb [[kind]+0x9c], then 0x55230. THE
+0x78 CENSUS: 0x552e0 x78, 0x3df00 x23, 0x50f80 x15,

(0xa2510) - 0x3d990 x5, 0x3d440 exactly 2 (0x96a88/

ebx = the context/requester edi, edx = request block):

clause, signal message, K_GEN1, AC_RECT, AC_DRAB, K_GEN4,

CODE: no: this PR ships no code. A PORT attempt made during
this work (the current row's `Wait` clause OR-ed into the
transition-test key) was MEASURED against the bytes and
REFUTED before commit - see (c) - so it is not shipped and
no test of it ships.
HOOKS: none new, none touched.
MEASURED: (a) THE DRIVER. The per-step key of an object is
built in 0x536f0 in this order: the provider at [[obj kind]
+0x8c] OR-ed into [obj+0x60] (0x5370c, PR-227/238), then
0x5371c calls the record driver 0x523f0(record, out = a
local) and 0x53725 OR-s its answer into [obj+0x60]; then
the row-index verb [[kind]+0x54] seeds a row output
(0x5372f-0x53733) that the scan 0x53520 -> 0x52000
overwrites with the matched row (0x53560/0x5204a), and
0x535a0 applies the state and row it is handed. 0x523f0
(eax = the record, edx = the out set) runs, in order:
[[rec+0x44]+0x8] = 0x52750 (the fixed
record-class table 0xa25d4, PR-107), [[rec+0x44]+0xc] =
0x521f0 (the row step, (c)), then the OWNER's kind-table
+0xa8 and +0xac with the same out (0x52416/0x52423), then
[[rec+0x44]+0x10] = 0x23c80 (a getter) - and returns the
out. For the placed DRABINKA (kind table 0x97cdc, PR-238)
those two owner verbs are 0x23940 and 0x23930: both are a
bare `ret` - they contribute NOTHING (measured, not
assumed).
(b) THE WORLD-GATHER 0x52750. It builds a context struct in
its own frame and only THE LAST verb writes the caller's
out. 0x5275e -> 0x52680 (+0x2c) fills that struct from the
OWNER's state fields: [obj+0x50] (the state-record vector),
[obj+0x54], [obj+0x58] (its count, PR-216), [obj+0x5c]
(the live state id), [obj+0x48]/[obj+0x4c], then queries
the CURRENT ROW's verb +0x10 three times with modes 1, 3,
2 (0x526e9/0x5272a/0x5273d - the class 0xa2638 chain walk
0x458e0; for a row whose only node is a `Wait` node the
chain stops at the node and its operand is null, so nothing
is written); 0x5276a -> +0x30 = 0x2b4d0 (unread, same
struct, NOT the out); 0x52774 -> the OWNER kind-table +0xc8
= 0x54560 for the placed rope (unread, same struct); and
0x52783 -> +0x34 = 0x52790, THE ASK CHANNEL: it starts
from an EMPTY set and OR-s into it (i) 0x4bd30 when
[[rec+0x13] bit 2] (0x527b3/0x527cb), (ii) 0x4b890 when
[[rec+0x12] bit 0x40] (0x527db/0x527ef), (iii) 0x4b870
when [[rec+0x12] bit 0x80] (0x52805/0x5281f) - each called
with the LEVEL (ds:0xcef40), the owner object and the
record's bit 0x8000 - and COPIES length+12 bytes to the
out (0x52833-0x52850). Those gate bits are the authored
`control=` names: the parse arms 0x51b6f-0x51d2b write them
([rec+0x12] |= 1,2,3,4,8,0x10,0x20,0x80,0x40; [rec+0x13]
|= 1,2,0x40,4,8,0x10,0x20,0x80; one name OR-s the WORD
0x1c0 at 0x51c73). ZARIA.01's rope declares
control=BY_TIME, so its ask channel is OFF: measured
negative for the ladder chain.
(c) THE ROW-STEP PATH SPLIT, and the `Wait` clause is NOT a
key source. 0x521f0 takes the caller's set as its out
([esp+0x68]). It reads the current row
[[rec+0x2e]+[rec+4]*4] (0x52221-0x52229) and calls its
TEST slot +0x8 (0x52235; the 0xa2638 chain walker 0x45800
hands back the first node's answer - for a `Wait` node that
is 0x45972, which copies the node's own [node+0x8] clause
and never calls an operand, PR-218). 0x5223c (0x495b0)
tests that answer for emptiness and 0x5224b branches:
NON-EMPTY -> 0x522fc, the EXECUTE slot +0xc (0x52303, the
chain walker 0x45870) and 0x5230c OR-s what EXECUTE returns
into the caller's set; then the owner verb +0xa0 (0x52317)
and the row may advance only when the authored threshold
[row+0x10] is BELOW the object clock [obj+0xa1] (0x52320-
0x5232b), the difference being the budget handed to the
advance verb [[rec+0x44]+0x18] = 0x520c0 (0x52338).
EMPTY -> the caller's set and [obj+0x60] are copied and
OR-ed (0x52251-0x522bc) and TEventSet::match 0x47e40 is
handed the row's (empty) clause (0x522e6): an empty clause
is a subset of anything, so the row runs, and it advances
through the SAME 0x520c0 with a ZERO budget (0x522f8). A
`Wait` node's own execute is the chain walker 0x45870 with
a null operand, which returns an EMPTY set (0x4587b-0x4588d
-> the empty-set path at 0x4588d): so a `Wait` clause adds
NOTHING to the caller's set and never reaches [obj+0x60] -
the model "the current row's clause feeds the transition
key" is REFUTED. The clause's only observable effect is the
path split above, which is what PR-218 recorded and this
confirms at the node level; how 0x520c0 spends the budget
(difference vs zero) stays open.
(d) THE GEN CHANNEL, confirmed as the port models it: a GEN
node's execute (class 0xa11e0 +0xc = 0x45920) = the chain
operand's answer OR the node's own clause at [node+0x8]
(0x45934), and the row step OR-s that into the caller's set
(0x5230c) - so `GEN` raises on the object that RUNS the
row, and 0x53725 puts it in [obj+0x60].
(e) THE K_GEN1 (bit 54) FEED CENSUS, extending PR-234. No
instruction writes bit 54 directly (no `+0x66],0x40` write
exists). Signal messages DO feed [obj+0x60]: the receiver
0x53770 (the placed rope's kind-table +0x10) takes a
message of type 0x10 with tag 0x8138764, builds a set from
the payload byte [msg+0xc] (0x537a0-0x537cf, the
dword[i>>5] bit i%32 math of PR-236) and OR-s it into
[obj+0x60] (0x537cf-0x537d4) - so one such message is a
complete feed. But the engine's FIVE signal-message
builders never send 54: 0x287a0 sends payload 0xa = AC_DRAB
to the sender's PARENT (0x2882d-0x2885a, PR-218), the
0x2c4a0 family broadcasts payloads 0x21/0x1c/0x1b gated on
the sender's state id and row (0x2c5e1/0x2c613/0x2c653,
via 0x4bc40), and 0x3e980 sends payload 0x39 = K_GEN4 to
every item of a list (0x3eacf-0x3eaf1).
(f) THE LION'S ANSWER VERB 0x27f30 (kind table 0x99828
+0x78, PR-237): it answers only when the ASKED lion is at
state 1, the requester has a PARENT ([[requester kind]+0x3c
= 0x23c10], 0x27f4a) and the requester's state id is 0x10
(0x27f57); its act is to OR bit 17 = AC_RECT into THE
LION'S OWN live set [lion+0x60] (0x27f6d-0x27f7d) and then
defer to the base verb 0x3df00 (0x3df3b): 0x3df00 refuses
when asked == requester, calls the asked's class verb +0xd8
(0x3df16) and on true 0x45320 with [asked+0xee] (a
position-scale helper: 0x541f0 + [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce],
also called by the 0x1e560 pair-touch family at
0x1e596/0x1e985), then the base 0x552e0.
OPENS: OI-078's rope feed is now narrowed to named unread
verbs, all on the record path: 0x2b4d0 (record class +0x30)

0x3f1c0 (the placed DRABINKA's own +0x78, PR-238) at the
ASKED's first declared state ([asked+0x5c] == 1, A_UP -
0x3f1dc/0x3f1e2) runs its FLAG branch: the requester must
have a PARENT ([[requester kind]+0x3c] = 0x23c10, 0x3f1e9,
false -> the empty tail at 0x3f364), and 0x44ec0 must
answer true for the pair ([asked+0xa5], the requester's
[[requester kind]+0x4c] object - 0x23a20 for the LION,
KAMIEN and 0x9a44c tables) (0x3f1e4-0x3f1fb). When it does,
0x3f203-0x3f20c is EXACTLY a signal raise on the ASKED:
`mov ah,[ecx+0x66]; add ecx,0x64; or ah,0x40; mov
[ecx+2],ah` - byte 6 of the 12-byte live set at
[asked+0x60], mask 0x40 = BIT 54 = K_GEN1. Then it jumps to
the tail and ANSWERS NOTHING. That is the signal the same
state's own authored exit tests: ZARIA.01's `[A_UP]` line
`A_DROP(1)=K_GEN1` (PR-149/216), matched in the next step
against [obj+0x60] (0x53725 -> 0x53520 -> 0x52000,
PR-239). So OI-078's question "what raises K_GEN1 on a
DRABINKA" is ANSWERED: the ladder's own ask answer does,
when it is asked by an object that has a parent and whose
[[kind]+0x4c] object matches one of the ladder's contact
elements. The port already located this store and counted it
as an unmodelled flag ("sets [self+0x66] bit 6", ll_level.c
4782/4965/5601); what was missing was that bit 6 of byte 6
IS signal 54 = K_GEN1. The same store appears in the KAMIEN
answer 0x3d440 at 0x3d4e2-0x3d4e5 (PR-236/237's step (4)) -
also a raise of K_GEN1 on the ASKED, not a "child-ANY bit".
(b) 0x44ec0, THE ANY-TEST, read whole: eax = the vector
header (here [asked+0xa5]), edx = the object to match. It
walks [[hdr]] as 12-byte elements while the index is below
the count at [hdr+4] ([asked+0xa9]) (0x44ec9/0x44ee3/
0x44ed4-0x44edd) and calls each element's class verb +0x8
with edx (0x44eea); true on the first that answers, false
when the count is not > 0. It is a pure test: it writes
nothing.
(c) THE LAST TWO PER-STEP CHANNELS, RULED OUT for the
placed rope: the record-class +0x30 verb (called by the
world-gather at 0x5276a) is 0x2b4d0, a bare `ret`; the
OWNER kind-table +0xc8 verb (0x52774) is 0x54560 for table
0x97cdc - a MESSAGE HANDLER (a switch on [msg+4]: 6/7 write
[obj+0x6d]/[obj+0x71] (0x545de-0x545eb), 0xc/0xd accumulate
into [obj+0xc2]/[obj+0xc6] (0x545a7-0x545bb), other arms
OR [obj+0xb6] bits 4/8 or zero those fields, 0x1b forwards
through [obj+0xa9]) - it NEVER writes [obj+0x60]. With
PR-239's negatives (the provider slot 0x23a60, the owner
+0xa8/+0xac bare `ret`s, the control-gated ask channel off
for control=BY_TIME) the rope's live set is fed only by
(1) its own answer-verb raise (a), (2) signal messages
(none sends 54, PR-239 (e)), (3) its own GEN rows (none
authored).
(d) THE BASE MESSAGE HANDLER 0x52bb0 (what the signal
receiver 0x53770 falls back to at 0x537dd for any other
type) dispatches on [msg+4] (0x52bb3): type < 0xe ->
0x52bf9, where type 1 is the position arm (0x52bc6-0x52bd7:
[obj+0] += [msg+8], [obj+4] += [msg+0xc], then the [[kind]
+0x54] verb); type == 0xe -> 0x52bef/0x52bf2: `[obj+0x30] =
[msg+8]` - the PARENT store, exactly as PR-236 measured;
type 0x21 -> 0x52be4: `[obj+0x28] = 1` - PR-225's
frame-step flag is ALSO settable by a message, a second
feed of that gate (its senders are open).

DRABINKA) - ANSWERED, and the row now turns to the port of

2 of the 186 tables carry it), the KAMIEN-family 0x96a88's =
0x1e4a0; the common values are 0x23c60 (50 tables) and
0x40eb0 (30). 0x3f0f0 calls 0x44f10 on the header at
[obj+0xa5]: 0x49920 with the format "%d" (0x91828) writes the
COUNT into [obj+0xa9], 0x44f32-0x44f4a allocates count*12+4
bytes, stores the base in [obj+0xa5], then per element calls
0x4a0b0 and consumes a separator with the format "d %c"
(0x9182b); 0x4a0b0's own format slots 0x91d0f/0x91d15 hold a
NUL, so the number scan is inside 0x49920/0x498f0 (NOT READ).
Then 0x44e90 (0x3f110) walks the elements and ADDS [obj+0]
and [obj+4] to element+0 / element+4: the authored numbers are
RELATIVE to the placement and become ABSOLUTE ONCE, at build
time. The second line is parsed by 0x49f90 with the format
"%d,%d;%d,%d" (0x91d00) into the header at [obj+0xb1] and
0x3f124-0x3f14e offsets that rectangle by the placement too:
for ZARIA.01's ladder, x 203..233, y 540..670 - it reaches
the authored ground line, while the port collides with the
art bbox 42x48 at (180,510). The object ctor of the same
class (the name-factory branch 0x1f8f3-0x1f947, which writes
[obj+8] = 0x97cdc and [obj+0xc] = 0x97cd4) pre-initialises
[obj+0xa9] = 0, [obj+0xad] = 0x97f50, [obj+0xb1..0xc0] =
1,1,1,1 with [obj+0xc1] = 0x98274 and a second header at
[obj+0xc5] with [obj+0xd5] = 0x98274. (c) THE VECTOR IS AN
OBJECT: 0x97f50 is a method table - [0] = 0x44e40,
[+4] = 0x44ec0 (PR-240's ANY-test), [+8] = 0x44f10,
[+0x1c] = 0x23e00 - so [obj+0xa5] = {base, count, the vector
class table 0x97f50}, which is what PR-239's "[obj+0xad] =
0x97f50" was. The ELEMENT class: table 0x98274 (ctor
0x23e30 = "the centre of a rectangle", setter 0x23ea0 =
`mov [eax],edx; mov [eax+4],ebx`), and each element stores
the descriptor 0x98278 = table+4 at element+8, so the
ANY-test's `call [[elem+8]+8]` = dword 0x98280 = 0x23e00,
which is a POINT-IN-RECTANGLE: element.x within
[edx+0..edx+8] and element.y within [edx+4..edx+0xc]. So
0x44ec0 asks: is any of MY authored contact points inside the
asker's rectangle. (d) THE ASKER'S RECTANGLE IS UNIVERSAL:
all 186 kind tables have +0x4c = 0x23a20 = `add eax,0x75;
ret` - the rectangle is the plain field [obj+0x75..0x84]
(x0,y0,x1,y1). (e) THE GATE IS A CLASS GATE, NOT A PARENT:
+0x3c is 0x23c10 (`xor eax,eax`, fails) in 171 tables and
0x230a0 (`mov eax,1`, passes) in 15. The name factory
resolves one of those 15 at 0x1fef4-0x1ff15: the name
TLewZaria (0x9078b) allocates 0x12e bytes, calls the ctor
0x1e0a0 and writes [obj+8] = 0x96960 - THE ZARIA LION IS ONE
OF THE 15, so the gate is "the asker is a lion-class".

its first declared state (PR-216) with ONE contact point at
(180+33, 510-3) = (213,507); when the lion's own rectangle
contains that point, the ladder raises K_GEN1 on itself

what the jump-on-a-ladder half of OI-078 is for.

MEASURED: (a) THE ASK IS A RECORD-CLASS CHANNEL, AND ITS
FLAGS ARE ROW BITS. 0x52790 is a method of the placed
rope's OWN class table - its slot +0x14 at 0x97cd0 is
0x52790 (the rope table 0x97cdc reads: +0x10 = 0x53770 the
signal receiver, +0x14 = 0x52790; PR-238's factory chain
0x1f8ac/0x23248 -> 0x97cdc). 0x52790 reads its row-step
argument at bits of its word [esi+0x12]: bit 0x20000 (byte
[+0x13] bit 1) -> the ASK branch 0x527b3-0x527cb, bit 0x40
-> 0x4b890 at 0x527db-0x527f5, bit 0x80 -> a third branch
at 0x52805. The ask call 0x4bd30 takes: out-packet edx =
the local 12-byte set, this eax = the level singleton
[ds:0xcef40], ebx = the row-step's own OBJECT word [esi],
ecx = the SAME word masked with 0x8000. Every branch's
answer is OR-merged into the caller's set (0x49580,
0x527d6/0x52800) and copied out at 0x527b7-0x527e9, i.e.
the answer joins the set the transition key is built from -
the channel 0x523f0's +0x10 verb (0x5242e-0x52435, PR-239's
key composition, called per step at 0x5371c).
(b) THE CANDIDATE WALK 0x4bd30, read whole: it walks the
chain [[ebx+0x64]] -> [rec+0x34] (0x4bd6c-0x4bd76), keeps a
candidate only if its kind verb +0x60 answers true
(0x4bd81; the rope's is 0x23140, the lion's 0x238e0) AND
[rec+0x24] equals the candidate's own layer [cand+0x24]
(0x4bd8c) AND the candidate is not the requester itself
(0x4bd98), then calls the CANDIDATE's verb +0x78 with
this = candidate, ebx = the requester (0x4bda0-0x4bda9) and
ecx = the input set, and ORs each answer (0x4bdb6 ->
0x495b0 tests whether anything arrived). With no matching
candidate it falls through at 0x4bdf6 to `this`'s member at
[[0xcef40+0x394]] and calls THAT object's +0x78. The
sibling ask verb 0x553e0 asks an object's CHILD vector
instead ([obj+0x3c] count, [obj+0x40] vector, 0x55412-
0x5542b); it is the +0x1c verb of the element class whose
descriptor 0x98278 is at 0x98eb0, and its callers are the
element proxy 0x1eba0 (slot +0x78 of the ELEMENT-child class
0x978dc, built by ctor 0x1ec00) and 0x380d0.
(c) THE PARENT GATE'S SITE, CORRECTED. Inside the ladder
answer 0x3f1c0 the +0x3c call is at 0x3f1d1 - on ebx, THE
REQUESTER, at the ENTRY, before the state switch - not at
0x3f1e9 (PR-240's citation); 0x3f1e9 is the requester's
+0x4c rectangle getter, already modelled by PR-243. With
that correction PR-242(e) reads exactly right: re-censused
over the kind tables (the set whose +0x4c = 0x23a20, 186 of
them), +0x3c is 0x23c10 (`xor eax,eax`) in 171 and 0x230a0
(`mov eax,1`) in 15, and the lion table 0x96960 is one of
the 15 - its site 0x9699c = 0x96960+0x3c. So the ladder
answers ONLY for a requester of those 15 classes; the placed
rope's OWN +0x3c is the single 0x23270 (at 0x97ce8, 0x231d0
shares it): `mov eax,ds:0xceeac` - a global object built
once in the 22-object block at 0x3d0f0-0x3d1d2 (globals
0xcee60..0xceeb0; the store at 0x3d1c3, never rewritten),
so the rope never fails its own gate but is asked as a
candidate only through some requester's chain.
(d) THE STATE-2 BRANCH OF THE SAME VERB (0x3f214): with
[self+0x5c] == 2 - ZARIA.01's rope has exactly the declared
states A_UP=1, A_DOWN=2, A_DROP=3, so that is A_DOWN, the
hanging state - it takes the REQUESTER's position through
its +0x68 getter (0x3f222), tests it with the element verb
+0x8 (the PR-242/243 point-in-rectangle) against the rope's
FIRST authored element, and answers `or byte [edx+1],0x1` -
BIT 8 of the signal table. Otherwise it builds a 4-field
vector from the authored rectangle at [self+0xb1..0xbd] (the
rect PR-242 measured: ZARIA.01 x 203..233, y 540..670) with
0x49fb0 using the class descriptor 0x98274 (0x3f256-0x3f293),
tests the position against it the same way (0x3f29f), and
answers `or byte [edx+1],0x10` - BIT 12; if even the second
test fails (0x3f33f) it answers `or byte [edx+1],0x4` - BIT
10. The signal names are shipped at 0x919ec in table order:
bit 8 = AC_DRABK, bit 10 = AC_DRAB, bit 12 = AC_TIME - the
bit convention matches the port's enum (ll_play.h 237-262)
exactly. So a hanging rope ANSWERS with the rope-grab
signals, keyed on the requester's position inside its own
authored element or rectangle.
(e) THE AUTHORED LION SIDE EXISTS AND READS THOSE NAMES:
ZARIA.01's LEW.MOV line 328 `A_WSP(1)=AC_BREAK_NEXT,AC_DRAB`
and line 363 `A_FALL_DOWN(1)=!AC_DRAB`; LONA.05's LEW.MOV
lines 58/59 `A_WSP_LIN_UP(1)=K_UP,AC_DRAB` and
`A_WSP_LIN_DOWN(1)=K_DOWN,AC_DRABK` (and 152/153 again);
AC_TIME is consumed by the lion's A_DRAP (line 134
`A_DRAP(1)=AC_TIME`) and many other states. That is the
other half of OI-078 authored end to end: the rope answers,
the answer enters the requester's key set through (a)/(b),
and the lion's authored transitions read it.
(f) THE PORT NEEDS NO CHANGE FROM (c): both ladder ask
sites in play_collide run only when the LION is in contact,
and the lion class is one of the 15 that pass the 0x3f1d1
gate, so the gate is already satisfied by construction -
counted here, not coded.

## OPENS IT (CHECK_ALL IMPLIES IT), THE CANDIDATE FILTER IS
## THE CONTACT-NODE FIELD [obj+0x2c], AND THE AUTHORED RECT
## FILTERS CANDIDATES TOO
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: state control words / the ask channel - THE THREE
ROW-STEP CHANNELS ARE THE CONTROL WORD'S CHECK_* BITS, AND
THE CANDIDATE FILTER IS THE OBJECT'S CONTACT-NODE FIELD
ADDRESSES: 0x527b3, 0x527db, 0x527cb, 0x527c5, 0x527f5,
0x52805, 0x5281f, 0x523f0, 0x52435, 0x536f0, 0x5371c,
0x52790, 0x4bd8c, 0x4bd91, 0x4bd96, 0x4bd81, 0x23b80,
0x23140, 0x23145, 0x9216e, 0x51b49, 0x51b56, 0x51b6f,
0x51b78, 0x51b89, 0x51c62, 0x51c73, 0x51c8f, 0x51d1a,
0x921c6, 0x921d0, 0x92202, 0x9185d, 0x97cdc, 0x97cd0,
0x96960, 0x53670, 0x9a44c
NAMES: ask channel, CHECK_LEW, CHECK_ZW, CHECK_ALL_PLANE,
CHECK_ALL, contact node, [obj+0x2c], candidate filter,
control word, row-step, OI-078, OI-113
CODE: no: this PR ships no code.
HOOKS: none new, none touched.
MEASURED: (a) THE ASK IS A CONTROL-WORD CHANNEL. The record
driver 0x536f0 (the placed rope's kind-table slot +0x14)
builds the transition key every step at 0x5371c through
0x523f0, and that composition calls the record-class +0x10
verb at 0x5242e-0x52435 with the object's live set; for the
placed rope's class that verb is 0x52790 (the dword at
0x97cd0, the word just BELOW the kind table 0x97cdc, PR-244
read it as a +0x14 slot - see CORRECTS). 0x52790 then
switches on the SAME record's control word [esi+0x12..] -
the field PR-230's keyword table fills:
  bit 0x200 (engine CHECK_LEW, the port's LL_CTRL_CHECK_LEW
    = 0x8000) -> the ASK branch 0x527b3, delivery walk
    0x4bd30 at 0x527cb;
  bit 0x8000 (engine CHECK_ZW, port LL_CTRL_CHECK_ZW) ->
    0x4b890 at 0x527db-0x527f5;
  bit 0x8000000 (engine CHECK_ALL_PLANE, port
    LL_CTRL_CHECK_ALL_PLANE) -> 0x4b870 at
    0x52805-0x5281f;
  and the layer argument handed to the walk is exactly that
  bit: `mov ecx,[esi+0x12]; and ecx,0x8000` (0x527c0-
  0x527c5). So PR-239's "control-gated ask channel" is
  fully named: the channel bit is the control word's
  CHECK_LEW, and CHECK_ALL sets it - 0x51c73 `or WORD
  PTR [esi+0x12],0x1c0` covers the engine bits 0x40 ANI /
  0x80 ZW / 0x100 LN / 0x200 LEW, i.e. the engine's
  CHECK_ALL = ANI + ZW + LN + LEW.
(b) THE SHIPPED DATA DECIDES IT: ZARIA.01's DRABINKA and
LINA states are all bare `control=BY_TIME` - no CHECK_LEW,
so those records NEVER ask; the ZARIA.01 lion's states carry
CHECK_ALL (LEW.MOV 52/74/101/215) or CHECK_ANI|CHECK_ZW|
CHECK_BASE_LN (40) - CHECK_BASE_LN is engine bit 0x400000,
a fifth, different bit (0x51ca9). So the ask that can reach
a ladder runs from the LION's states, per step, over the
lion's candidate chain - which is exactly the shape PR-150
modelled (the ask sites sit in the lion's contact path), now
with its enabling bit named. OI-113 item 1 grows one more
entry: the port's ctrl_flag CHECK_ALL (ll_play.c, set by
PR-231 to CHECK_ANI|CHECK_ZW|CHECK_LN) does NOT set its
LL_CTRL_CHECK_LEW bit, while the engine's CHECK_ALL does -
no port code tests CHECK_LEW today, so nothing moves; the
ask port must set it.
(c) THE CANDIDATE FILTER IS THE CONTACT-NODE FIELD. The
walk's first gate 0x4bd81 calls the candidate's kind verb
+0x60; 156 of the 186 kind tables answer with 0x23b80 =
`mov eax,[eax+0x2c]; ret` - the object's contact-node field
(PR-149's node list head), set to 1 at 9 sites
(0x2b809/0x2db80/0x36610/0x3f7a0/0x52926/0x59b2e/0x604e6/
0x60b81/0x60f4a). So a candidate is only asked if something
has planted a contact node in it - the pair contact, again,
is what opens the channel; the second gate 0x4bd8c-0x4bd96
requires the candidate's layer [cand+0x24] to equal the
record's [rec+0x24] unless the mask (CHECK_ALL_PLANE) is
zero, in which case the candidate is skipped.
(d) THE CONTROL BITS RE-READ, ONE CORRECTION: the chain
0x51b49-0x51d93 compares BY_X FIRST and on a match sets
NOTHING (0x51b56 jumps straight to the end); BY_Y sets bit
0x1 (0x51b6f), BY_TIME 0x2 (0x51b89), BY_TX 0x3, BY_TY 0x4,
then 0x8/0x10/0x20/0x40/0x80 as PR-230 lists. PR-239(e)'s
"BY_X = 1, BY_Y = 2, BY_TIME = 4" shifted the chain by one
name. (The engine's BY_X is the walk mode 0x543a0 selects
for distance-clock feeding; the port's model names stay as
they are.)
OPENS: what writes [[obj+0x64]], the chain the walk follows
(the rope's own +0x64 verb is 0x23140 - the RECT-INTERSECT
test of the authored rectangle at [obj+0xb1..0xbd] against
the requester's live box, writing its result into [obj+0x2c]
at 0x23140-0x23174: a SECOND live use of that rectangle, on
top of PR-244's state-2 answer, and the strongest evidence
yet that the authored rect, not the art bbox, is the
engine's collision box); the bodies of 0x4b890 (the
CHECK_ZW ask) and 0x4b870 (the CHECK_ALL_PLANE ask); what
[rec+0x24] holds and how it tracks [obj+0x24]; the 9
writers of [obj+0x2c]; PR-244's list (the element-child
class 0x978dc, [0xcef40+0x394], 0xceeac) and PR-243's.
CLOSES: none; OI-078's ask half is now fully named, and
OI-113 gains the CHECK_ALL/CHECK_LEW entry.
CORRECTS: PR-244 three times: (i) the ASK branch is gated
by control-word bit 0x200, not 0x20000; (ii) 0x52790 is not
"slot +0x14" of the kind table 0x97cdc - it sits at 0x97cd0,
0xc bytes BELOW it; (iii) "AC_TIME = bit 12" stands but the
branch description should read bit 0x10 of packet byte 1 =
engine-table position 12. PR-239(e) once: the control chain
starts at BY_X = default (sets nothing); BY_Y = 0x1,
BY_TIME = 0x2 (0x51b56-0x51b8d), so the PR-230 table - not
the PR-239 letter list - is the right one to use.

at [obj+0xa5]), 0x44e90 (points made ABSOLUTE by adding the
placement x,y), then `lea ecx,[esi+0xb1]` -> 0x49f90 (four
numbers through the 0x49920 scan engine, reader at 0x91d00)
and then 0x3f124-0x3f14b adds the placement x,y to all four
words: [obj+0xb1]=x0, [obj+0xb5]=y0, [obj+0xb9]=x1,
[obj+0xbd]=y1, ABSOLUTE - the port's place_rect stores the
same four in the same order, so PR-246's reader matches the
engine. Then 0x3f159 writes the THIRD block: [obj+0xc5]=v,
[obj+0xc9]=y-0x50, [obj+0xcd]=v, [obj+0xd1]=y, and 0x3f178
resizes a container to ([obj+0xb9]-[obj+0xb1]+1) elements
made absolute - counted, not modelled (npair stands).
(b) CORRECTION, the intersection verb is table slot +0x64,
not +0x60: 0x97cdc's slots are +0x3c 0x23c10, +0x4c 0x23a20
(the box getter, PR-242/245 confirmed), +0x60 0x23b80 (the
plain [obj+0x2c] getter - the same verb 156 classes use),
+0x64 0x23140, +0x68 0x23b60, +0x78 0x3f1c0. The walk's
filter 0x4bd81 therefore calls +0x60 for the ladder too:
it only READS the contact-node field.
(c) WHO WRITES IT - the broad phase 0x4b970 (called at
0x4aeac between 0x222d0 and 0x4ba90): it reads the layer
count [[obj+0x390]+0x18], allocates 20 bytes per layer, and
for each layer index calls 0x57530/0x57500 (the scene's
per-layer origin transform) and 0x4b940, which writes a rect
(X-0xa0, Y-0x78, X+0x1e0, Y+0x140) - 640x440, the SCREEN
window of that layer. Then it calls [[class]+0x64] (eax =
the instance, edx = that rect) for every instance of the
object's CLASS CHAIN ([obj+0], [obj+4], [obj+8] -> count at
[class+0x44], instances at [class+0x58], chained by
[obj+0x34]) and for every object in [obj+0x64] (0x4ba6e);
0x23140 answers authored-rect-intersects-that-window and
writes it to [obj+0x2c] (0x23176). Census of slot +0x64:
0x23940 = an EMPTY ret (always yes) in 109 tables, 0x53490
in 21, 0x23ba0 in 16, 0x23bd0 in 4, 0x37380 in 2, and
0x23140 in exactly 2 - 0x97cdc and 0xa1dfc, the ladder
family only. So the authored rectangle is the object's
ACTIVE-WINDOW box (a culling/contact flag), NOT the test
against the asker: PR-246's filter (authored rect vs the
asker's live box) is not what the engine does, and the
model the port needs is "the ask is not gated by the
authored rect; the authored rect gates whether the object
counts as in-play".
(d) THE WALK'S LIST IS THE WORLD'S: 0x527bb loads eax =
ds:0xcef40 and 0x4bd61 reads [[eax]+0x64] - the global
scene object's list, not the requester's (correcting
PR-244); the requester travels in ebx (0x527c6 `mov ebx,
[esi]` = the record's owner object), its layer is
[requester+0x24] compared with [candidate+0x24] at 0x4bd8c
unless the CHECK_ALL_PLANE-masked bit is non-zero
(0x4bd91), and self is skipped at 0x4bd98. Only THEN comes
the answer call [candidate class+0x78] with ebx = the
requester (0x4bda9) - the ladder's 0x3f1c0.
(e) THE ASKER'S RECTANGLE IS THE LIVE BOX, AND IT IS RUN-
TIME STATE: 0x3f1e9 calls the requester's +0x4c verb; for
the lion (0x96960) and the ladder (0x97cdc) alike that verb
is 0x23a20 = `add eax,0x75; ret`, and 0x44ec0 hands the
result to the element verb +0x8 = 0x23e00, whose compare
order fixes the layout: [edx]=x0, [edx+4]=y0, [edx+8]=x1,
[edx+0xc]=y1 - the same layout as the authored rectangle.
The two-object collision helpers 0x52f66 and 0x530dc take
BOTH boxes the same way (+0x4c on each) and compare x0/y0/
x1/y1 the same way. In 201,475 instructions only two name
that field: the getter 0x23a20 and the writer wrapper
0x23a51 (`lea edx,[eax+0x75]; call 0x534e0`). 0x534e0
fills box[0]/box[4] from the class verb +0x68's object -
the lion's is 0x23900 = `add eax,0xd6` (the lion's own
frame field), the ladder's is 0x23b60 = `ret` (itself),
then chains +0x48, +0x33 and +0x50 for the rest. So the
box the point gate tests is built from the CURRENT FRAME,
never authored - which is exactly the model the port's
player_shape_box (the SEQ shape bbox) stands in for.

branch). PR-224's "middle band (smp/vol/goto/I/M...) NOT
pair-verified" is pair-verified for I/F/IC/FC/M with this.
(b) THE MERGE'S THREE QUERIES, exact out slots (0x52680,
the record-class merge; the table 0xa25d4 is at 0xa2600 at

-> block+0x18/0x1c (0x526e9); id 3 'IC' -> block+0x0/0x4,

0x5270b `cmp DWORD PTR [eax+0x95],0`); id 2 'I' ->
block+0x20/0x24 (0x52731 `lea ebp,[esi+0x18]` OUTSIDE the
gate, 0x5273d with edx=2 writes ebp+8/+0xc, i.e. the pair
AFTER the pull pair). The integrator's velocity-SET leg
0x5433a/0x54348 reads block+0x18 x (times the terrain word
[obj+0x6d]) and block+0x1c y, and 0x54170 is the soft
pull: for a positive limit it moves v only while v < limit,
stepping by the limit and clamping exactly to it; for a
negative limit (the y launch) it applies only while
-v <= -limit, i.e. while the velocity has not yet reached
the target. So the pull channel carries the header-pair
copy plus ΣFC plus (when [obj+0x95] is set) ΣF; the 'I'
pair lands in block+0x20/0x24, whose consumer I have NOT
found (OPENS). (c) THE ONE-SHOT GATE, the [obj+0x95]
lifecycle end to end: the state-record step 0x521f0 clears
it at its head (0x52217) and sets it at 0x5234a, three
instructions after the row handler `[[rec+0x44]+0x18]`
(0x52338) and the class verb +0xa4 (0x52341) - and that
block is the row-admission tail: 0x52320 reads the current
node's threshold [node+0x10], 0x52323 the distance
accumulator [obj+0xa1], 0x5232b `cmp/jge` skips the whole
tail when the threshold was NOT crossed. So the flag means
"a row was admitted on THIS state step", reset every step -
PR-98's item 6 and PR-100's reading, with the whole writer
census now measured in one function plus the two sibling
state-entry paths (0x535d1, 0x538b7, both right after their
`mov [obj+0xa1],0`). (d) THE CURRENT-ROW SCOPE, closing
PR-98's INFERENCE (its item 3): the merge takes the node
chain 0x5268e `lea edi,[eax+0x2e]` / `mov edi,[edi]` /
`mov edi,[edi+[A+0x4]*4]` and the step takes the same
chain 0x52221-0x52229 - the head table is AT [rec+0x2e],
indexed by the row cursor [rec+0x4]; the cursor is moved
only by the id-6 query family of 0x520c0 and the `end_level`
directive (PR-101). The sums are of the CURRENT ROW's
directives, not of the state. (e) WHAT THE SHIPPED JUMP IS
UNDER THIS LAW, arithmetic on the authored constants of
ZARIA.01 LEW.MOV [A_JUMP] (T=20,1, G=0,55; rows 1,75,
F 0,350 / 2,75,F 0,350 / 2,75,I 150,-1200 / 2,100 / 3,150,
FC 30,0 / ...), run through the integrator order
(v += G; v -= T*v/100; then the pull) with the one-shot
rule of (c), at the port's 20 Hz iteration clock: the two
F rows dip the lion ~7 px down, the I row sets v_y = -1200
(-12 px/iter) ONCE, G_y=55 and the T_y=1 drag decay it,
apex 50 px above the take-off at iteration 15, back level
at iteration ~30. Applying the 'I' pull on EVERY iteration
the row is current instead (the cursor may hold one chain

pre-drag and post-drag value - a drag that never reaches
zero leaves the residue. (b) 0x54358-0x54372 write
[obj+0xca] = idiv(v_x,100) and [obj+0xce] = idiv(v_y,100),
and 0x54827-0x54829 add those WHOLE numbers to the
position. NOTHING carries the idiv remainder: a part of a px
in one iteration is dropped. [obj+0xe2]/[obj+0xe6]/
[obj+0xea] is not a sub-pixel accumulator - it is the SEQ
step-motion verb, set at 0x4549a-0x454ba and consumed at
0x54759-0x547c8. (c) C's signed / is x86 idiv, so the port
needs no rounding helper. (d) CONSEQUENCES, MEASURED ON REAL
DATA, none of them fitted: the authored A_JUMP words apex at
exactly 100 px (was 108) and the tool's closed form agrees;
ZARIA's A_WALK register settles at 250 = F*s/T and his body
walks 2 px an iteration, 3 iterations per 6-unit pose; the
worm pair (100,40) settles at 125 and walks 1 px, 4
iterations per pose; a released key leaves a 4 px slide and a
residue that never zeroes, which then feeds the 0x54170
pulls; an FC pair pulls the register in ITS unit, so the
punch's FC 100 is a 1 px step (the punch moved 14 px under
the old reading, now 3). PR-134's video counts are 2.4 and
3.2 iterations per pose - 20% and 25% faster than this - and
that difference is the truncation, not a constant to tune:
either the engine keeps the remainder somewhere this read did
not find, or the BY_X feed is not the post-truncation step.
Named at OI-015. (e) What the truncation exposes downstream:
A_DRAP's own G=0,250 with T_y=15 has terminal
idiv(25000,15) = 1666 = 16 px an iteration, and the port's
ground query looks only at the position it stands on THIS
iteration, so a jump that ends in A_DRAP walks straight
through the authored grass (668 at 70, 688 at 71, the line
at 681). The engine's ground answer is the shape-box test
(FUN_00042a70, the push-out 0x42de0); a one-point query
cannot reproduce it. (f) OI-078 moves the WRONG way and this
record says so: at the new 2 px walk the press lands at x=189
and the apex at 189,550, so the ask now spans the ladder
point's x (168,517..215,583 against 213,507) and misses its
y by 10 px where PR-254 was 2 px away. The ladder's art hangs
510..558 and its point is 3 px above that, 143 px above the
walk line - more than A_JUMP's own words measure.

0x3f355, 0x3e060, 0x3e0a8, 0x4bc40, 0x52b10, 0x53770,
0x54910, 0x506d6, 0x1f468, 0x3457c, 0x34a71, 0x34a9a,

AC_DRAB, AC_DRAB_CATCH, AC_SPOKUJ, AC_ENEMY, K_UP, K_DOWN,
K_FWD, K_BKWD, K_JUMP, K_FIRE, K_F1, [obj+0xad],

no expectation to pin first. The leg OI-078's row points
at - an A_WSP entry fed by AC_ONAIR - would pin a line
this level can never take, and (e) is what says so.
MEASURED: (a) THE SET AND ITS WRITERS. A signal mask is 12
bytes plus a count byte at +0xc, built on the stack by
0x749a0 (the count in ebx) and merged by 0x49580, which
OR-s three dwords src into dst: 69 call sites. Nothing
OR-s an immediate into a live set anywhere in the image;
the only direct writes are register read-modify-write at
two sites (0x3f203 `mov ah,[obj+0x66] / or ah,0x40 /
mov [obj+0x66],ah`, PR-241's flag branch, and 0x3b601),
and the record path reaches the same merge: 0x53770 takes a
record of kind 0x10 tagged 0x8138764 whose +0xc byte is the
signal ORDINAL and raises it through 0x49580.
(b) THE ANSWER VERB RETURNS, IT DOES NOT RAISE. 0x3f1c0
writes its caller's buffer: 0x3f2dc puts 0x10 at mask byte
+1 (bit 12 = AC_DRAB_CATCH) and 0x3f313 merges 0x04 at +1
(bit 10 = AC_DRAB) into it; the no-catch path 0x3f355
writes 0x04 at +1 alone. PR-245/246's packet is confirmed
at byte level - `set 1400` and `set 400` in the port's own
probe words - and NEITHER packet carries AC_ONAIR.
(c) WHERE A RETURNED MASK LANDS. 0x553f0..0x5542b walks an
object's [obj+0x3c] count of array elements at [obj+0x40],
calls each element's class verb +0x78 and OR-s each
returned mask into the accumulator; the single-pair form
0x55250..0x552d1 does the same and adds a byte-0 0x80 mask
(bit 7 = AC_ENEMY). So the answer packet does reach a live
set. Counted: which member's set that accumulator is, was
NOT read; the port keeps applying it to the player's
one-tick vector (PR-92's model).
(d) A SECOND AC_DRAB_CATCH RAISER, new to this project:
0x55130, the mask builder the lion's own +0x78 entry
0x50f80 calls, asks 0x550c0 and then compares the two
members' [obj+0xad] words - the greater wins: byte 2 bit 0
(bit 16 = AC_DRAB_CATCH), the other branch gives bit 7 =
AC_ENEMY. [obj+0xad] is the same counter the K_GEN1 gate at
0x50df4 tests against 100. Named, not modelled.
(e) AC_ONAIR HAS NO POSTER IN ZARIA.01. Bit 18 is byte 2
bit 2 of the middle dword, so a literal raise is a
0x00040000 dword or a 0x04 byte at mask +2. The image holds
6 uses of 0x00040000 and not one is a mask; every 0x04 byte
write at a mask base sits at +1 (AC_DRAB: 0x3f304, 0x3f355,
0x28805, 0x2c460, 0x36a1f, 0x37ab0, 0x37dfd, 0x3c2b9), at
+3 (bit 26 = AC_SPOKUJ - and 0x3e0a8/0x3e0b5 raise it onto
ANOTHER object, [ecx+0x112]+0x60, an "attached object"
field not named here), or at +7 (bit 58, 0x2e417). The only
sites that carry 0x12 as a value are the broadcaster
0x4bc40 at 0x1f468 - the class 0x977f0 entry, JBRANCH's
sub-object, gated on [self+0x5c] == 9 and the pair pass -
0x3457c, 0x34a71, 0x34a9a (the KBLOKZ class 0x9de64) and
0x3a20d (the XCHG class 0x9fb24, ctor 0x3a110). ZARIA.01
ships no script and places no object of any of those
classes: its placement list is DRABINKA, LINA, KORONA, BAL,
POCISK, KAMIEN, SEP, SEP2, RYBA, WODA, ZARROW, LICHA,
PALMA, PAJAK, NOSOROG, KATAPULT, PICT, ANITAB, ANIBACK.
That lion is never told it is on air.
(f) THE CHAIN THE PORT DOES REACH, measured at HEAD with

unrolls; from 127 the DOWNED ladder answers at index 2 with

`A_DRAP(1)=AC_TIME` row takes A_WALK -> A_DRAP and

ladder stance, live for the first time. A second script
reaches `A_TURN_BACK -> A_WSP` at 153 and its climb rows
admit at the authored 300,200,... - and all 17 of its ticks
read `pos 214,648`: the climb runs IN PLACE.
(g) WHAT OWNS THAT MOTION is PR-148's open item 1, and

mask - [obj+0xa5] bit 0 -> bit 39 K_FIRE, bit 4 -> bit 40

MEASURED: (a) THE SET. The live set is 12 mask bytes at
[obj+0x60]..[obj+0x6b] plus the op byte at [obj+0x6c], and
the class names itself: the branch at 0x47fd8 pushes
0x919ca, whose string is "TEventSet::match :Bledna
operacja" ("invalid operation"). Four operations, all
three-dword loops on that
layout: 0x49550 AND-into-place, 0x49580 OR-into-place,
0x495b2 "are all three dwords zero" (entered as 0x495b0,
the padding before it, from 4 sites), 0x495e2 clears a
transition ENTRY: memset 12 bytes through 0x749a0, zero the
byte at +0xc, zero the dwords at +0xd and +0x11 - a
TEventSet plus its two payload dwords.
(b) THE BYTE AT +0xc IS A MATCH OPERATION, NOT A COUNT.
0x47e40 = TEventSet::match(A = eax, B = edx) reads A's byte
at +0xc, `cmp al,3; ja 0x47fd8` to the error string, and
jumps through the table at 0x47e30: op 0 (0x47e63) copies B,
ANDs A into it with 0x49550, and `repz cmps` compares 12
bytes with A - TRUE when A AND B == A, i.e. A is a SUBSET of
B; op 1 (0x47edc) does the same AND and returns 0x495b0's
answer directly - TRUE when the intersection is EMPTY
(disjoint); op 2 (0x47fb2) compares the two 12-byte masks
directly - EXACT equality; op 3 (0x47f42) ANDs and returns
the negation of 0x495b0 - TRUE when the intersection is NOT
empty. So one test routine carries the positive and the
negative form of a signal condition, and the compiled
condition's own op byte selects which.
(c) WHERE IT IS USED. TEventSet::match has exactly TWO call
sites in the image, 0x52033 and 0x522e6. 0x52033 is inside
0x52000, a transition-list walker: entries are 21 bytes (the
`add ebx,0x15` stride) at [[record+0x1a]] with a count at
[record+0x22], laid out {12 mask bytes, op byte at +0xc,
dword at +0xd, dword at +0x11} - the same 21 bytes 0x495e2
clears, i.e. a TEventSet plus two payload dwords - and the
walk takes the FIRST entry whose set matches, copies those
two payload dwords out to the caller's two output pointers,
and then calls [[record+0x44]+0x4]. Here A is the ENTRY, so
the compiled entry's own op byte selects the operation.
PR-100's row step is the other user, and its shape is now
read: 0x52221-0x52235 loads the current row
[[ctx+0x2e] + [ctx+4]*4] and calls its class slot +8 to make
the row's AUTHORED CONDITION key into [esp+0x40]; 0x5223c
asks 0x495b0 whether that key is EMPTY (no bits at all) -
empty takes 0x52251, where the caller's key (arg at
[esp+0x68], e.g. 0x54910's input key) and the object's live
blob ([ebp+0]+0x60, op byte at +0x6c, read at 0x5228d and
merged by 0x49580 at 0x522bc) are ORed into one buffer,
keeping the CALLER's op byte; then 0x522e6 calls
match(A = the row's condition key, B = that merged live
key). So in both users the op byte that decides the test
belongs to the COMPILED condition, not to the live set.
(d) RAISED BITS ARE NEVER LOWERED. The raise sites OR a bit
straight into the blob: 0x3f203-0x3f20c and 0x3b5f3-0x3b601
are both `mov ah,[obj+0x66] / or ah,0x40 / mov [obj+0x66],ah`
= bit 54 = K_GEN1, the first one being 0x3f1c0's flag branch
the port already models. The per-frame assembler 0x536f0 does
not rebuild the blob either: it calls the class hook
[[obj+8]+0x8c] and ORs the answer into [obj+0x60], then
builds the current record's key with 0x523f0 and ORs THAT in
too - no memset, no zeroing, before or after. Every write
that zeroes those bytes on an object is a construction or
reset path: 0x32535 and 0x32825 sit immediately after
`call 0x52860` (the allocator) and each is followed by the
class's vtable installs at +0x8/+0xc; 0x4457b-0x44590 zeroes
+0x58, +0x5c, +0x60, +0x64 as one block. The dedicated
clear 0x495e2 is UNREACHABLE in the shipped image: a
little-endian scan of the whole image finds 0 sites holding
that address, and a scan of every rel32 call/jmp encoding
finds 0 sites whose target is it.
(e) THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is the port's, not the engine's.
ll_play.c:1327 `p->sig = 0;  /* one-tick pulses */` and the
object-side `o->sig = 0` sites make every signal in this
port a one-iteration pulse, so a row conditioned on `!AC_DRAB`
is TRUE on any iteration where nothing re-raised it. PR-259's
probe shows exactly that ending the climb: the ladder's
answer verb says nothing on ticks 297 and 298, nothing is
raised on those iterations, and A_WSP's authored
`A_FALL_DOWN(1)=!AC_DRAB` row takes the lion down. In the
image that silence changes nothing: the bit raised on tick 296
is still in the blob when the row is evaluated, because no
code lowers it. The chain-break is the port's clear.
(f) THE KEY BUILDERS, and a correction to PR-88's wording.
0x48000 compares the token case-insensitively (0x76a69
upcases) against the four special names first - 'AC_K_ANY'
(0x919ec), 'K_ANY' (0x919f5), 'AC_K_NEVER' (0x919fb),
'K_NEVER' (0x91a06) - and for those two a MASK is built
directly: K_ANY memsets 12 bytes (0x749a0) then `or
DWORD PTR [base+4], 0x2001f8` = signals 35,36,37,38,39 and
53 = K_BKWD, K_FWD, K_UP, K_DOWN, K_FIRE and K_JUMP; K_NEVER
`or BYTE PTR [base+4], 0x60` = signals 37 and 38 = K_UP,
K_DOWN. Every other name is a chain of string compares
against the block at 0x91a0e and, on a hit, `mov al,
<the name's ordinal>` and the /32 ADDRESSING inlined (0x480e4
is AC_BLOK_Y with al = 1, 0x48131 AC_BREAK_NEXT with al = 2:
`shr 5` picks the dword, `idiv 0x20` and `shl eax,1:rem`
pick the bit, OR into that dword). So PR-88's "EXPLICIT
constant per name" is right about the ORDINAL and wrong about
the constant: no mask literal is ever stored, and the only
real mask constants in the function are K_ANY and K_NEVER.
The port's ll_sig_id plus `1ull << bit` is already the
addressing, and PR-88's "K_ANY/K_NEVER are not bits" stands -
they have no ordinal - but they are not merely node-op tags:
they carry whole masks. 0x54910 builds its input key on the
stack the same way and its mapping is now read end to end:
memset 12 at 0x5492c with op byte 0 (subset) at +0xc, then
[obj+0xa5] bit 0 -> bit 39 K_FIRE, bit 4 -> 40 K_ALT, bit 5
-> 53 K_JUMP (0x54931-0x54956, direct byte ORs), [obj+0xb6]
bit 4 -> 36 K_FWD else 35 K_BKWD (`sete` + `add al,0x23`
then the /32 addressing, 0x54964-0x5499a), and the VERTICAL
INTENT WORD: [obj+0xbe] < 0 -> 37 K_UP (0x5499d), > 0 -> 38
K_DOWN (0x549ab). K_ANY is exactly those six keys minus
K_ALT. The 12 bytes plus the op byte are then copied to the
caller at 0x549c8-0x549d8, so a caller's key carries its own
op with it.
(g) A TRAP FOR THE NEXT READER OF THESE OFFSETS. +0x60 is
overloaded: 0x65154/0x6562c read and write +0x62/+0x66 of a
session-state record with a jump table at 0x65080, 0x5da60-

structure whose own fields are at +0x4..+0x18, and the whole

esp-relative LOCALS at +0x62/+0x66/+0x6a. Every claim about
the signal blob has to name the base register and the guard
chain that makes it an object.

## PR-261 — AN AUTHORED TRANSITION CONDITION IS COMPILED
## INTO A TEventSet: '!' IS DISJOINT, '|' IS ANY, ',' IS ALL,
## AND THE PORT'S GRAMMAR DIFFERS ON SEVEN SHIPPED CLAUSES
```

SUBSYSTEM: the transition condition of a .MOV state block -
the authored text to the 21-byte entry the record walk
matches, and what the engine's four operations mean for this
port's condition grammar (parse_cond / obj_cond_true).
ADDRESSES: 0x47d50, 0x47d60, 0x47d73, 0x47d8c, 0x47d9c,
0x47da9,
0x47db2, 0x47dbc, 0x47dc2, 0x47dc8, 0x47dd2, 0x47de0, 0x47dfd,
0x48000, 0x495e2, 0x49610, 0x51e07, 0x51e13, 0x51e2a, 0x51e36,
0x51e43, 0x51e54, 0x51e8f, 0x52000, 0x52033, 0x53440, 0x53815,
0x57d30, 0x57fd0, 0x919bc, 0x9225c, 0x9229c, 0x922ba
