## PR-312 — THE OBJECTS' PHYSICS STEP: `+0xac` IS A GROUND QUERY,
## AN ATTACH LAW AND A CARRY-AND-SNAP, AND IT RUNS FOR 108 OF THE
## 151 CLASSES - INCLUDING EVERY LION - BUT NOT FOR THE LADDER
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the object class slot +0xac: what its body 0x546a0
does, how often it is installed, and the field triple its result
travels through; the contact-list insert 0x45320/0x45400 that also
fills that triple; and the interpolation it uses. FOCUS 1 asked
what could move a rider whose own state authors no motion: this is
the named mechanism.
ADDRESSES: 0x546a0, 0x54706, 0x54759, 0x54804, 0x45320, 0x45400,
0x45380, 0x453d2, 0x455a0, 0x49580, 0x4b430, 0x4b600, 0x4b7f0,
0x23930, 0x52a00, 0x45120, 0x541f0, 0x98278, 0x96874,
0x96960, 0x96d1c, 0x97cdc, 0x99ff0, 0x1e970, 0x749a0, 0xcef40
NAMES: physics step, ground query, attach, detach, carry, snap,
clearance, contact list, polyline, segment count, flag byte,
control word, AC_ONAIR, AC_DRECT, TLewZaria, TLewZariaB, DRABINKA,
KATAPULT, WSPRECT, OI-078, OI-018, PR-304, PR-305, PR-307,
PR-308, PR-311, ll_plt_first_below, ladder_answer_core
CODE: no: image and class-table reading only; nothing under
`ported/` changed, so no red leg is owed and none was written.
HOOKS: PR-311's OPENS (i) - "what writing a contact-list entry
with mode 2 does, and who reads that list back" - and the FOCUS-1
rule that a mechanism must be read in the engine, not inferred.
MEASURED: (a) WHO RUNS IT. The class slot +0xac holds 0x546a0 in
108 of the 151 factory-census classes, including TLewZaria (its
+0xac cell is 0x96a0c), the lion base class 0x96874, PLATF, WINDA,
SCHODY..4 and the enemies; 24 classes hold the empty stub 0x23930
- the whole ladder family (DRABINKA 0x97cdc, LINA, KDRABINA,
KATAPULT, PALMA, DZWIGNIA) - 5 hold 0x52a00 (the WSPRECT family),
3 hold 0x45120, and one holds 0x45400. So a rider runs this step
and a ladder does not.
(b) ITS SHAPE. `test BYTE [obj+0xb6],0x2; jne 0x54804` - the
queries are skipped when that bit is set, but the carry at 0x54804
still runs. Then the current state record is read through
[[obj+0x50] + [obj+0x5c]*4] and its control word at state+0x12
selects: bit 0x4000 -> call 0x4b600 with ecx = 0 and then 0x4b430;
bit 0x0100 -> 0x4b600 with ecx = 2, then 0x4b430, then 0x4b7f0.
All three are called with eax = ds:0xcef40 (the world object) and
their result is passed to 0x49580, which ORs three dwords into the
12-byte signal set the verb was handed (that is the set shape with
its mode byte at +0xc, PR-296) - so a ground query RAISES SIGNALS.
(c) THE RESULT TRAVELS IN A TRIPLE ON THE OBJECT: [obj+0xe6] = the
surface found, [obj+0xe2] = that surface's flag byte, [obj+0xea] =
the signed clearance, and [obj+0xa9] = the surface currently
attached. The law at 0x54759: no surface found -> if one was
attached, call its class [+0x4] (leave), clear [obj+0xa9], call
the object's own [+0xb8], set flag bit [edi+0x2] |= 4. Surface
found -> if kind == 2 and [obj+0xc6] < 0x58c it is ignored too;
otherwise if nothing is attached set [edi] |= 0x10, store it, call
its class [+0x0] (enter) and the object's [+0xb4]; if a DIFFERENT
one was attached, call the old one's [+0x4] first. Then kind != 0
sets [edi+0x1] |= 0x20.
(d) THE CARRY, 0x54804: pos.x += [obj+0xca]; pos.y += [obj+0xce]
+ [obj+0xea]; then [obj+0xea] and [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] are
zeroed. So a rider is moved by the surface's per-frame delta and
by the clearance to it - the only channel FOCUS 1 had left, and it
is a snap to a polyline, not an authored rise.
(e) HOW A CONTACT LIST BECOMES A SURFACE. The ask verbs pass their
own [obj+0xa5] list, and the insert 0x45320 first asks the object
for its point through 0x541f0 with the {0,0,0x98278} triple
(PR-308's provider pre-seed), adds [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce], then
calls 0x45400, which treats the list as a polyline of 13-byte
records (x at +0, y at +4, flag byte at +0xc): a mode gate on the
FIRST entry's flag byte, then 0x45380 finds the segment whose
x-span contains the point, and 0x455a0 returns (interpolated Y at
that x) - Q.y; the best (nearest non-positive) candidate is
stored in the triple of (c). 0x453d2 returns 0x7fffffff when no
segment covers x. So the catapult's mode 2 (PR-311) is a filter
value on that flag byte, and the flag byte is the same byte the
.PT text reader fills from the point separator (0x451a1 stores 1
for `;`).
OPENS: 0x4b430 / 0x4b600 / 0x4b7f0 first - the three ground queries
against the world object: which polylines of the level they walk,
and how the mode argument and the per-point flag byte filter them.
This is now the direct route to the ZARIA.01 platform line. Second,
what the state control-word bits 0x4000 and 0x0100 are in the
`control=` vocabulary the port parses. Third, the signals the
queries raise - does one of them name AC_ONAIR / AC_DRECT, the two
the level's own exit chain waits for (OI-018)? Fourth, the object's
own [+0xb4]/[+0xb8] verbs and the surface's [+0x0]/[+0x4] class
verbs. Fifth, F1's capture read still stands as plan step one.
CLOSES: the FOCUS-1 question "is there any mechanism left that
moves a rider with no authored motion" - yes, and it is now read
at the level of its fields and arithmetic; and PR-311's OPENS (i).
CORRECTS: PR-305, whose reading of the +0xac cell as "ENTER" is
kept as a measurement (the ladder family really does hold the
empty stub 0x23930 there) but is the wrong role: for 108 of the
151 classes the slot is the per-frame ground/attach/carry step.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no
red leg by the rule PR-245 states, and no suite run. The last full
no-Windows suite run is PR-298's, rc=0 with 69 green verdict lines;
since then only comments in ported/ have changed.

## PR-313 — THE THREE GROUND QUERIES THE PHYSICS STEP CALLS:
## A BLOCKADE PUSH, AN ASK SWEEP, A CEILING TEST - AND THE
## NAMED SIGNALS THEY RAISE, INCLUDING AC_ONAIR
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: 0x4b430, 0x4b600 and 0x4b7f0, the queries PR-312 found
gated by the state control word inside the physics step 0x546a0;
the world arrays they walk; their sibling nearest-object searches
0x4b6d0/0x4b762; and the signal bits the step itself raises, read
against the port's own LL_SIG_* table.
ADDRESSES: 0x546a0, 0x4b430, 0x4b500, 0x4b600, 0x4b6d0, 0x4b762,
0x4b7f0, 0x4b870, 0x45620, 0x534e0, 0x541f0, 0x49580, 0x749a0,
0x44370, 0x44540, 0x98274, 0x98278, 0xcef40, 0xcef44, 0xa94e8,
0x287a0, 0x23930
NAMES: AC_BLOK, AC_DUP, AC_DUP_CD, AC_ONAIR, AC_UP_DUP, AC_DRAB,
blokady, blockade, ceiling, floor, nearest, penetration, push,
ask sweep, world arrays, control word, OI-018, OI-079, OI-078,
PR-312, PR-305, PR-308, LL_SIG_AC_ONAIR, LL_SIG_AC_DUP
CODE: no: machine-code reading; the port's signal enum was READ
as a name table, nothing under `ported/` was changed, so no red
leg is owed.
HOOKS: PR-312's OPENS first item (the three queries), second item
(the control-word bits) and third item (whether they raise
AC_ONAIR / AC_DRECT - the pair ZARIA.01's exit chain waits for,
OI-018).
MEASURED: (a) THE BLOCKADE QUERY 0x4b430. It builds the object's
own RECT (a local rect object of class 0x98274, filled through
0x534e0), adds the pending delta [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] to all four
edges, then walks an array whose base is at [arg+0x70] and whose
count is at [arg+0x7c], stride 0x14, entry x at +0x4, y at +0x8,
length at +0x10, calling 0x45620 per entry. 0x45620 accepts an
entry whose x lies inside the rect's x-span and whose y..y+len
crosses the rect's y-span AND which is more than 1 px from the
farther x edge; on accept it adds (entry.x - that edge) into
[obj+0xca] - a SIDEWAYS PUSH through the same pending-delta field
the carry reads - and returns 1. First match wins. The query then
composes the answer: an EMPTY set if nothing matched, and with the
set's byte 0 OR-ed with 0x1 = signal bit 0 = AC_BLOK if something
did (the name matches the behaviour exactly).
(b) THE ASK SWEEP 0x4b600, the one the control word runs in mode 0
or 2. It takes the object's POINT through the +0xb0 provider
(0x541f0 with the {0,0,0x98278} triple, PR-308), adds the pending
delta, and if a surface is attached at [obj+0xa9] it asks THAT
first, through the surface's class [+0x8] verb with ecx = 2. Then
it walks a second array, base [arg+0x74], count [arg+0x80],
stride 0xc, whose entries hold an object pointer at +0x0, and
calls each entry's class [+0x1c] verb with eax = that object,
edx = the world, ecx = the asking object, ebx = &point. The
collected answer is composed at 0x4b500 with the mode from the
control word and a global from ds:0xa94e8.
(c) THE CEILING/FLOOR SEARCHES 0x4b6d0 and 0x4b762 walk the same
second array and, for every entry, ask it through its class
[+0x14] verb with the object's own [+0x6c] result, keeping the
best: 0x4b6d0 requires a NEGATIVE answer and keeps the largest
(starting at 0x80000001), 0x4b762 requires a POSITIVE one and
keeps the smallest (starting at 0x7fffffff); both write the chosen
entry's address out. 0x4b7f0 is the third query: it walks a THIRD
array, base [arg+0x78], count [arg+0x84], stride 0x14, whose
entry at +0x10 names an object, calls that object's class [+0x4]
verb, and on a non-zero answer composes an empty set with byte 3
OR-ed with 0x2 = signal bit 25 = AC_UP_DUP.
(d) THE SIGNALS ARE NAMED NOW. Matching the byte index and bit
mask against the port's own enum in ported/ll_play.h (AC_BLOK = 0
.. AC_KOLO = 34): the blockade query raises AC_BLOK, and the
physics step of PR-312 raises, on the surface branch, byte 0 mask
0x10 = bit 4 = AC_DUP when it ATTACHES, byte 1 mask 0x20 = bit 13
= AC_DUP_CD when the surface's kind byte is not 0, and byte 2 mask
0x4 = bit 18 = AC_ONAIR when no surface was found at all (or the
attached one was left). So OI-018's AC_ONAIR has a producer and it
is the ground query FAILING: ZARIA.01's exit chain A_DRAP /
A_PRE_JUMP -> A_WPAD waits on AC_ONAIR,AC_DRECT, i.e. on the lion
having no ground under him. And OI-079's AC_DUP producer is the
attach branch of 0x546a0, not a row-tail directive.
(e) THE WSPRECT ANSWER, one site, read only as far as its signal:
its ask verb 0x287a0 ends by clearing the set's mode byte, calling
0x749a0 with ebx = 0xc and OR-ing byte 1 mask 0x4 = bit 10 =
AC_DRAB - the ladder signal, from a RECTANGLE class.
(f) The three arrays are separate from the contact lists of
PR-312: their base/count pairs (+0x70/+0x7c, +0x74/+0x80,
+0x78/+0x84) are written together at 0x44599..0x4460f, a setup
that parses config text through 0x4a0b0 and builds the runtime
arrays in 0x44370 - that producer is named, NOT read here.
OPENS: 0x44370 / 0x44540 - which level-config block becomes which
of the three arrays, and the entry layout of each; then the
+0x1c / +0x14 / +0x8 / +0x4 verbs a queried object answers with
(which is how a ladder or a platform reports itself as ground);
then AC_DRECT, which is NOT raised by any of the three queries
read here; then whether AC_ONAIR's producer being the missing
ground is what the port's LL_PLAY_GRAVITY stand-in replaces.
Fifth, F1's capture read still stands as plan step one.
CLOSES: PR-312's first three opens: the queries are read at the
level of their arrays, their verbs, their arithmetic and their
signals; AC_ONAIR and AC_DUP have named producers (OI-018,
OI-079).
CORRECTS: none. PR-312's reading of the same bits as "0x10
(landed), 0x20 (kind != 0), 4 (airborne)" is unchanged as bytes;
they are now named AC_DUP, AC_DUP_CD and AC_ONAIR.

## PR-316 — PLAN STEP F2 AND F3 ANSWERED AT ONCE: `pos` SETS THE
## POSITION THROUGH THE OBJECT'S CLASS +0x4 VERB, `lock`/`unlock`
## ARE A FLAGGED PAIR, AND `end_level` IS THE WRITER OF
## [world+0x4] - THE LAST OF WHICH OI-046 HAD ALREADY CLOSED
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the .MOV state-directive node classes - the apply of
`pos`, `lock`, `unlock`, `rdir` and `end_level`, which this port
counts and acts on none of - read through the parser's dispatch,
the node classes, and the object verbs they call.
ADDRESSES: 0x466d6, 0x46ef0, 0x45a30, 0x457e0, 0x45c50, 0x54f40,
0x54f90, 0x45a10, 0x45750, 0xa11b0, 0xa10d8, 0xa0f70, 0xa1048,
0xa10f0, 0x91940, 0x91901, 0x9190c, 0x9193b, 0x9198e, 0x23850,
0x23ea0, 0x53df0, 0x55070, 0x5c320, 0x49920, 0x57a00, 0xcef40,
0x96874, 0x96960, 0x97cdc
NAMES: pos, lock, unlock, rdir, ldir, end_level, set position,
locked flag, direction word, level end, node class, apply verb,
A_WPAD, A_WYJSCIE, OI-078, PR-194, PR-198, PR-199, PR-305,
PR-309, PR-312, ll_player_step
CODE: no: machine-code reading only; nothing under `ported/`
changed, so no red leg is owed and none was written.
HOOKS: plan step F2 (the apply of the directives the exit needs)
and F3 (who writes [level+0x4]). PR-309 named the exit chain and
the two `pos` lines; PR-312 named [obj+0xb6] bit 2 as a physics
skip and PR-305 named the class +0x54 cell.
MEASURED: (a) THE DISPATCH. One parser function compares the
directive names and, for each match, allocates a node and stores
its class word, then appends it with 0x57a00. `lock` (the name at
0x91901, compared at 0x46408) allocates 12 bytes and stores
0xa10d8; `rdir` (0x9193b, compared at 0x4668e) allocates 8 bytes
and stores 0xa0f70; `pos` (0x91940, compared at 0x466d6)
allocates 16 bytes, stores 0xa11b0 at [node+0xc] and then calls
0x49920 with the format string at 0x91944 and two output slots at
[node+0x8] and [node+0xc] - the authored `pos 1020,692` pair.
(The end_level node 0xa1048 and its table were read at
PR-198/199.)
(b) THE NODE SHAPE AND THE APPLY SLOT. A node is {link at +0x0,
class word at +0x4, payload at +0x8}. Each node class differs
from its siblings at exactly two slots, +0x4 and +0x1c, and the
+0x4 bodies are the semantic ones (0x45750 end_level, 0x45c50
lock, 0x45a10 rdir, 0x45a30 pos); every one of them first calls
the shared helper 0x457e0, which walks [node+0x0] and calls the
OWNING object's class +0x4 verb - so a directive runs against a
specific object, and that object is reached from the node. That
+0.4-is-the-apply reading is INFERRED from this shape and from
the bodies; the executor's call site in the level loop was not
read, and PR-198/199 point at other verbs of 0xa1048 (0x45d90 as
its sixth), so a [port] step must re-confirm the call site.
(c) `pos` IS A POSITION SETTER. 0x45a30 reads the target object
from the context ([ecx] then [that+0x8] = its class word), takes
edx = [node+0x8] and ebx = [node+0xc], and calls the target's
class +0x4 verb. For the lion classes (0x96874 and TLewZaria
0x96960) that cell is 0x23850, five instructions: `mov [eax],edx`
- [obj+0x0], the x the physics step and the ask protocol both
read - `mov [eax+0x4],ebx`, then `call [class+0x54]`: the
row/animation verb PR-305 named (0x55070 for the lion family,
0x53df0 for the ladder family). So `pos x,y` teleports the object
and refreshes its row - with no carry, no clearance and no
signal: it does not go through the physics step at all. The
DRABINKA class holds a different setter, 0x23ea0.
(d) `lock` AND `unlock` ARE A FLAGGED PAIR. 0x45c50 branches on
[node+0x8] (the authored `lock` / `unlock` argument) to 0x54f40 or
0x54f90. Both first call the class +0xbc verb as a guard and
check [obj+0xb6] bit 1; 0x54f40 proceeds only when that bit is
clear, and at the end sets `or BYTE [obj+0xb6],0x1`; 0x54f90
proceeds only when it is set. In both, the body is the same trio:
the class +0x48 verb, the class +0x50 verb, and then the class
+0x4 verb of the holder read at [[+0x48 result]+0x33]. Note the
neighbouring bit: PR-312 found the physics step skipping its
queries on [obj+0xb6] bit 2 - bit 1 is this authored lock.
(e) `rdir` sets a direction word: its apply 0x45a10 writes
[obj+0x6d] = 1 (the same field 0x545e5 writes from [edx+0x8]).
`ldir` was not opened further than its name at 0x91936.
(f) `end_level`, AND PLAN STEP F3 WAS ALREADY CLOSED. The body
at 0x45750 - the +0x4 slot of the end_level node class 0xa1048 -
loads the world object ds:0xcef40 and stores the node's
[node+0x8] argument into [world+0x4]. This is the same site and
field PR-198 read ("0x45750 -> the exit word at [mgr+0x4]"), so
this confirms OI-046's contract from the node-class side and adds
nothing to it: the plan step F3 that PR-310 wrote was a duplicate
of a CLOSED row. What is new here is only that ZARIA.01's own
lion script has no `end_level` row, so that node never runs for
this level.
OPENS: the port's apply for these five first - the smallest
honest one is `pos`, five instructions with an obvious test: the
authored `pos 1020,692` must put the lion at x 1020, y 692 and
then run the class +0x54 verb. Second, what [world+0x4] drives in
the level loop (F3b). Third, the [obj+0xbc] guard verb and the
+0x48 / +0x50 / +0x33 trio behind lock. Fourth, AC_DRECT, still
unnamed (F4).
CLOSES: plan step F2 for pos/lock/unlock/rdir, and PR-309's "this
port counts pos, lock, unlock, ldir, rdir and goto without acting
on any of them" now has the engine side measured for four of the
six. It also closes plan step F3 as a mis-scope: that question is
OI-046, CLOSED by PR-198/PR-199.
CORRECTS: PR-310 - its plan list item "F3 read what ends THIS
level: the writer of [level+0x4]" restates OI-046, which PR-198
and PR-199 closed and the port implements; the item is replaced in
T5 by the open half, what the exit word drives. PR-305's cell map
is used as measured: its +0x4 object slot is now named the
position setter, and its +0x54 frame/row verb is exactly what the
setter calls after moving.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no
red leg by the rule PR-245 states, and no suite run. The last full
no-Windows suite run is PR-298's, rc=0 with 69 green verdict lines;
since then only comments in ported/ have changed.
```

failing test first") on the reading plan step F2 shipped a turn ago
(PR-316); FOCUS 1, whose authored end is the A_WYJSCIE walk-off
that opens with this directive.
MEASURED: (a) THE CENSUS, RE-MEASURED HERE. Over the 777 extracted
`.MOV` texts the word appears in EXACTLY 4 rows in 3 files, and
BOTH spellings are shipped: `0,0,pos 1020,692` as the third row of
`[A_WYJSCIE]` in ZARIA.01_LEW.ZAR_LEW.MOV and in
ZARIA.01_LEW.ZAR_LEWPL.MOV, `1,250,POS 220,140,GEN K_GEN1` in
RAN.01_LEW.RAN_LEW.MOV `[A_DEAD]` and `15,300,POS 200,140` in its
`[A_DEAD1]`. No shipped row carries an `M` tail beside a `pos`.
(b) THE NODE. The parse arm 0x466d6-0x46718 asks for 0x10 bytes,
runs the node ctor 0x45770, writes the class word 0xa11b0 at
[node+0x4] and reads the pair through 0x49920 with the format at
0x91944 into [node+0x8] (x) and [node+0xc] (y).
(c) THE APPLY AND ITS ARGUMENT CONVENTION. 0x45a30 saves the node
in ebx and the second argument in ecx, calls the shared prologue
0x457e0, then takes the object from that argument: `mov eax,[ecx]`
and `mov esi,[eax+0x8]` - the CLASS WORD of the object the context
carries - and calls `esi+0x4` with edx = [node+0x8] and ebx =
[node+0xc]. For the lion classes 0x96874 and TLewZaria 0x96960
that slot is 0x23850, four instructions: `mov [eax],edx`,
`mov [eax+0x4],ebx`, `call [edx+0x54]` - write [obj+0x0]/[obj+0x4]
and refresh. The DRABINKA class 0x97cdc holds a different setter,
0x23ea0, so the slot is per-class, not one global setter.
(d) THE REFRESH. 0x55070 (the lion class's +0x54) is
`lea edx,[obj+0xd6]; call [class+0xb0]` - the presented-point
provider of the ask path (PR-313) - then `lea edx,[obj+0x89]; call
0x541f0`, then `call [class+0x98]`. So a `pos` re-derives the
point the ground queries use. It does NOT touch the velocity
registers, [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] or any signal: the directive
bypasses the physics step 0x546a0 of PR-312 completely.
(e) THE CHAIN, EXACTLY. 0x457e0 is `ebx = [eax+0x0]` and, if
non-null, `eax = that link; call [[link]+0x4]+0x4` - the PARENT
link's +0x4 with the SAME second argument, not the owner object;
0x45870 (the +0xc verb every one of these classes shares) walks
the same link into its +0xc and, when the link is empty, builds an
empty 12-byte set through 0x749a0 with ebx = 0xc. The list is a
chain in both slots and the object always arrives as the argument.
(f) THE PORT'S APPLY, RED FIRST. The new selftest leg parses the
two shipped shapes in one fixture - the upper-case RAN.01 row with
its trailing `GEN K_GEN1` and the authored `pos 1020,692` - and
then runs the player on a ground line at 692 + the contact offset,
so the authored point is an exactly-grounded point and the physics
pass neither adds nor removes anything there. Derived expectation,
from PR-110's row clock (100 units a feed): the 250-unit first row
holds iterations 0-2, so the pair must appear on iteration 3 and
nowhere before; on iteration 4 (a row with no `pos`) the position
must be unchanged, because it is a set and not a delta; on
iteration 6, where the list wraps and row 0 is admitted again, its
`POS 220,140` must re-apply, because the engine re-runs a row's
chain every time it runs the row. Controls: with the parse arm
disabled 5 checks fail (2 parse + 3 runtime); with only the apply
disabled exactly the 3 runtime checks fail; with both in, the leg
is green and `--mov-selftest` stays green.
(g) WHAT DOES NOT MOVE. The ZARIA.01 level probe is unchanged, and
its "frame directive(s) the model does not act on" count stays 52
before and after: that count covers the PLACEMENT scripts, not the
lion's own `ZAR_LEW`, so the shipped exit row was never in it.
(h) THE EXIT SITS IN A HOLE. Reading `zaria_a.plt` for the
authored point: the terrain across the exit column runs
(953,654) (994,644) (1007,646) (1051,633), then NOTHING until
(1115,662) - a 64 px gap - and the same file authors a catch-all
line (-100,1500)-(3000,1500). The authored `pos 1020,692` is 39
px below the terrain at x 1007 and 59 px below it at x 1051, inside
that gap column: the level drops its lion through the floor it

MEASURED: (a) THE TOOL, AND WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT SEE.
  tools/re/signal_raise_census.py reads the signal names from THIS
  port's own LL_SIG_* enum in ported/ll_play.h (PR-88 verified that
  table 68/68 against the engine's name block), so its output
  cannot drift from the port's bit numbers. It walks every
  instruction row for the two shapes a raise has: bit N lives at
  byte N/8 of a signal set, bit N%8, and a set is reached either
  as an answer buffer (displacement 0x0..0xb, the 12-byte buffer
  0x749a0 builds with ebx=0xc) or as the live field
  [obj+0x60..0x6b]. Over the whole .text it prints 194 candidate
  sites and names each one's enclosing function. Its blind spot is
  stated in the tool and here: it sees writes of a CONSTANT mask
  only, and a bit also arrives by a register merge - PR-313's two
  AC_ONAIR raisers 0x36165/0x2b327 and the set-OR sites
  0x49580/0x53725 are exactly that form, and the census does not
  print them. So "no raiser" from this tool means no
  constant-mask raiser.
  (b) AC_DRECT (bit 19 = byte 2, mask 0x8) HAS EXACTLY TWO such
  raisers in the whole image: 0x40d99 and 0x286ec. Both are class
  +0x78 ASK VERBS of the rectangle family, reached from the ask
  walk 0x4b500 (PR-312/PR-313), and both raise into the ASKER'S
  answer buffer, not into their own live set: the verb calls
  0x749a0 with edx=0, ebx=0xc to build the 12-byte buffer, stores
  0 at [buffer+0xc], then OR-s the bit into it.
  (c) THE `DRECT` CLASS. The placement factory 0x4df10 compares the
  entry line's first field against its name block (0x91f75 'RECT',
  0x91f7a 'DRECT', 0x91f80 'DRECT2', the names loaded by
  0x4e15c and its neighbours) and installs the class table by
  immediate store: RECT 0xa15ac at 0x4e147, DRECT 0xa1638 at
  0x4e1aa, DRECT2 0xa16c4 at 0x4e20d - and the same three again
  from the level-descriptor parser's own factory 0x4ea10 at
  0x4eb9a / 0x4ec6a / 0x4ed3a (0x4ea10 is called from 0x4c8a0, the
  `.des` key parser, at 0x4d7e4/0x4d7f1). The DRECT table: ctor
  0x4ebb0, +0x18 = 0x40c90, +0x78 = 0x40d50 in the cell 0xa16b0.
  The +0x18 verb is the AUTHORED RECTANGLE: 0x40c90 does
  `add eax,0x3c` and calls 0x49f90, which pushes the format at
  0x91d00 - `%d,%d;%d,%d` - into the field parser 0x49920. The
  numbers on the placement line become the box at
  [obj+0x3c..0x49]: x0, y0, x1, y1.
  (d) THE GATE, READ AT 0x40d50. eax = the DRECT instance, ebx =

  asker's class +0x3c verb - PR-303/PR-304's ASKABLE probe -

  geometry object whose own class +0x8 verb, called with

  authored-rectangle class 0x98274 that +0x8 verb is 0x23e00, the
  contain test the port already prints for authored contact
  points: x within [box.x0..box.x1] and y within [box.y0..box.y1].
  Only then bit 19.
  (e) THE SIBLINGS, SAME SHAPE. RECT's verb 0x40cf0 (cell 0xa1624)
  drops gates (1) and (2) and raises AC_RECT (byte 2, mask 0x2) at

  (f) THE DATA, COUNTED WITH COMMITTED TOOLS. tools/re/llrs_tree

NAMES: the class verb +0x10, opcodes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 0xd, 0x1b,
  `MOVE`, `zero`, `chdir`, `ldir`, `rdir`, `[obj+0xc2]`,
  `[obj+0xc6]`, `[obj+0x6d]`, `[obj+0x71]`, `[obj+0xb6]`,
  `[obj+0xa9]`, `[obj+0xd6]`, `[obj+0x5c]`, `[obj+0xfe]`,
  `[obj+0x126]`, `[obj+0x12a]`, AC_DRECT, AC_RECT, AC_DRAB,
  command_post_census.py, signal_raise_census.py
CODE: yes: one new read-only tool, tools/re/command_post_census.py
  (a census of the poster's call sites over the leodb `insn` table),
  and one comment correction in ported/ll_level.c - the PR-225 note
  that called 0x2885a the lion's vtable+0x10; no behaviour change.
HOOKS: none
MEASURED: (a) THE BUS. 0x52b10 is a poster: eax = the object, edx =
  a command opcode, ebx and ecx = two payload ints. It builds a
  4-word message - [msg+0x4] = the opcode, [msg+8] and [msg+0xc] =
  the ints - and calls `[[obj+8]+0x10]`. This is the same message
  layout PR-235 read for the SIGNAL message (0x2883f-0x2885a builds
  type 0x10 with payload 0xa = AC_DRAB and calls the same verb), so
  the signal posts and the object commands are one bus, not two.
  tools/re/command_post_census.py counts the poster's call sites:
  66 of them, with the opcode each one loads - 0x1 x7, 0x2 x5,
  0x5 x7, 0x8 x5, 0xa, 0xb, 0xc, 0xd x4, 0xf x5, 0x10, 0x11,
  0x12 x2, 0x14, 0x15 x4, 0x19 x11, 0x1b x5, 0x1d, 0x1e, 0x21,
  and 2 sites whose opcode is computed. The tool states its
  heuristic (the last `mov edx, ...` in the 48 bytes before the
  call) in its own header.
  (b) THE BASE HANDLER'S MAP. 0x54560 is the +0x10 verb most object
  classes install: 87 dword cells in the image hold it, and every
  one the class-table join locates sits at table+0x10. Reading it
  end to end: opcode 2 ASSIGNS
  `[obj+0xc2]`/`[obj+0xc6]` from the two payload ints (0x54593 /
  0x5459c); opcode 0xd ADDS to both (0x545aa / 0x545bb); opcode 8
  ZEROES both (0x545f4 / 0x545fe); opcode 6 writes `[obj+0x6d]`
  and `[obj+0x71]` (0x545de) - the same field the `rdir` directive
  writes straight out at 0x45a1a (PR-316, through its node class
  0xa0f70's +0x4 verb 0x45a10); which directive posts opcode 6 is
  NOT established here. Opcodes 3 and 4 set bit 2 and bit 3 of
  `[obj+0xb6]` (0x545c6 / 0x545d2) - bit 2 is the physics-skip
  flag of PR-316; opcode 0x1b runs the `[obj+0xa9]` surface
  attach/detach block, which is where PR-318's AC_DUP (0x54785),
  AC_DUP_CD (0x547d1) and candidate AC_ONAIR (0x54800) sites are.
  Every other opcode - including the signal type 0x10 - falls
  through to 0x53770 (0x5463a / 0x54652 / 0x54675 / 0x5468d).
  (c) THE LION IS ON THIS BUS. The LION class 0x96874 has +0x10 =
  0x3d8f0, which handles opcode 5 itself (writes `[obj+0x6d]` and
  sets a bit at `[obj+0x66]`) and chains EVERY other opcode to
  0x54560 at 0x3d906. The other lion table 0x96960 has +0x10 =
  0x1e130, whose unhandled path is 0x50d60 - a second handler with
  its own jump table at 0x50d20 over opcodes 9..0x15 and a special
  case for opcode 1 when `[obj+0x126]` is non-zero. So the pair is
  reachable on the lion through 0x3d8f0, and nothing in the physics
  step of PR-312/313 writes it.
  (d) THE PAIR IS A COMMAND-WRITTEN (x,y) OFFSET. Opcode-2 posters:
  0x1e952, 0x1f3ce, 0x3e03d, 0x3e446, 0x3e840. Opcode-8 posters:
  0x1f3b6, 0x3e01e, 0x3e364, 0x3e424, 0x45a84. Opcode-0xd posters:
  0x1ea65, 0x1eaef, 0x3c3b8, 0x53ba4. The 0x1exxx family is the
  level-geometry path that also instantiates the KILOF_PL family
  (0x1f870, PR-318); the 0x3cxxx/0x3exxx family is the
  contact/attachment code PR-235 walked (its pair loop 0x3eac6);
  0x45a84 sits in a `.MOV` directive apply, 0x45a6f, which
  resolves its target through 0x457e0 and posts opcode 8 with both
  payload ints zero; 0x53ba4 is inside 0x53ae0, the function that
  compares two objects' class +0x44 verbs (the kind word PR-312
  named) and then posts opcode 0xd. Together with the zeroing at
  every state start (0x5042e/0x50438, PR-318), that is the whole
  write set. Its readers are two: the AC_DRECT gate's boolean test
  at 0x40d65, and the point-provider verbs 0x27350 (installed at
  +0xe8, cell 0x9a634, of the class 0x9a54c that the ctors
  0x2703e/0x2743f build) and 0x36732, which return the asker's
  +0x68 provider's point plus `[obj+0xc2] * 15 / 100` plus
  `[obj+0x6d] * 60` plus `[obj+0xfe]`, the first gated on the
  current record index `[obj+0x5c] == 0x12` and the second on
  `0x1f <= [obj+0x5c] <= 0x26` (PR-235's record-index field).
  (e) WHAT `MOVE` MOVES. The name is at 0x91980; the directive
  parser's arm at 0x46a77 allocates 0x10 bytes, installs the node
  class 0xa1078, and parses the pair with the format at 0x91979 (`
  %i,%i`) into node+0x8/node+0xc. The node's apply, 0xa1078+0x04 =
  0x45ce0, resolves the target through the shared 0x457e0 (PR-316)
  and posts OPCODE 1 with the two ints - so `MOVE` is not what
  writes the pair. Opcode 1 on the classes that install 0x28880
  (cell 0x9a000) reads `[obj+0x3c]/[+0x40]/[+0x44]/[+0x48]` - the
  AUTHORED RECTANGLE the RECT-family classes parse their placement
  numbers into (PR-318) - and offsets it by the payload. So the
  authored rectangle of a placed rectangle-class object is movable
  by a script, and that is what `MOVE x,y` does to it.
  (f) THE AC_DRECT GATE IS NOW FULLY READ EXCEPT ITS UNIT QUESTION.
  The asker's +0x68 verb, which PR-318's gate calls, is the point
  provider: for the lion classes the cell (0x96874+0x68 = 0x968dc,
  0x96960+0x68 = 0x969c8) holds 0x23900, which is `add eax,0xd6;
  ret` - a pointer to the PRESENTED POINT of PR-305. So the gate
  is exactly: the lion's presented point lies inside the placed
  DRECT's authored box, AND `[lion+0xc6]` is positive, AND the
  asker is ASKABLE. What OI-119 still owes is which of the
  opcode-2/0xd posters can run against the lion and in what unit -

  0x49920, 0x46764, 0x46777, 0x467dd, 0x467e3, 0x4684d, 0x46853,

  0x45870, 0x457b0, 0x47710, 0x47770, 0x477d0, 0x47800, 0x521f0,

  0x91955, 0x9195d, 0x9185d, 0x91862, 0x98278, 0x76bcc
NAMES: goto, gotorel, goto_rel, GOTO, GOTO_REL, GOTOREL, zero,
  zero_t, [rec+4], [row+0x10], [obj+0xa1], [obj+0x99], [obj+0x71],
  answer-6, row cursor, A_DEAD, A_KILOF, A_PODCIAG, A_WYJSCIE,
  A_SPADANIE, SEQ_REV_X, SEQ_REV_Y, AC_BREAK_NEXT, 0xa1030,
  0xa1018, 0x45d90, 0x45dc0, ll_mov_fr
CODE: no: the diff is .md only; the model this read opens (F2b)
  belongs to the row-advance path, not to this PR.
HOOKS: none
MEASURED: (a) THE PARSE, 0x46739/0x4679c/0x4680c. All three arms:
  case-insensitive name match (0x76a69) against 'goto' (0x9194d),
  'gotorel' (0x91955), 'goto_rel' (0x9195d); a 12-byte node
  (0x5c320, 0xc) initialized by 0x45770 ([node+0]=0, [node+4]=
  0xa1000 base); the operand read by 0x49920 with '%d' (0x91952)
  into [node+8]. The arms differ in two instructions each:
  `goto` writes descriptor 0xa1030 (0x46764) and then DECREASES
  the stored value (0x46777-0x46780) - the authored row number is
  1-based, the engine stores the 0-based cursor index; `gotorel`
  writes 0xa1018 (0x467e3) and decrements then INCREMENTS back
  (0x467dd, 0x467ea-0x467ee) so the authored delta is kept
  verbatim; `goto_rel` is instruction-for-instruction the same
  (0x4684d-0x4685e). So gotorel and goto_rel are aliases, and
  only `goto` compiles to an absolute index. Nothing else about
  the three names differs - case twins GOTO (64), GOTO_REL (29),
  GOTOREL (10) and the lowercase spellings (25/6/1) all parse.
  (b) THE DESCRIPTOR TABLES. 0xa1030 and 0xa1018 are six-verb
  tables (+0x00 clone 0x47710/0x47770, +0x04 EXECUTE = the base
  chain delegate 0x457e0 - these nodes do NOTHING in the row's
  execute pass, +0x08 TEST 0x45800, +0x0c EXECUTE-walk 0x45870,
  +0x10 the ADVANCE verb 0x45d90/0x45dc0, +0x14 a copy builder
  0x47800/0x477d0). Node fields: +0 next sibling in the row's
  directive chain, +4 the descriptor, +8 the authored operand.
  (c) THE ADVANCE DRIVER, 0x521f0 -> 0x520c0. The row step hands
  the advance verb 0x520c0 (the record class 0xa260c's +0x18) a
  budget = clock - threshold, exactly as PR-219 read; 0x520c0
  walks the row chain's +0x04 verbs first (0x520e1 - pos/lock/
  ldir act there, goto is inert there), composes and scans the
  transition sets (0x520e6-0x52112, the empty-set composer
  0x98278), stores the carry [obj+0xa1] = budget (0x52114-
  0x52118), and then at 0x52124-0x5213d calls the row
  descriptor's (+0x10) = 0x458e0, which walks every child's
  +0x10 verb with eax=node, ebx=&[rec+4] (the row cursor),
  ecx=&answer (init 0) and dl=6. Absolute 0x45d90: after
  walking the siblings, if dl==6 it writes *[cursor] =
  [node+8] and sets the answer to 6; relative 0x45dc0: *[cursor]
  += [node+8], answer 6. At 0x52140 an answer of 6 SKIPS the
  step entirely - a goto row never wraps and never raises the
  list bits. (d) THE STEP ITSELF, now read end to end.
  Non-reversed (0x521b6): cursor == count-1 -> OR byte 0 bit 0x4
  (AC_BREAK_NEXT, verified constant 0x2 = bit index 2) into the
  caller's signal set and cursor = 0; else cursor+1. Reversed
  (0x52195-0x521b4): cursor == 0 -> OR byte 0 bit 0x8 (bit
  index 3, a name this port's 68-bit ledger has no verified
  constant for) and cursor = count-1; else cursor-1. The
  reversed test (0x5214b-0x52193) is an XOR of three terms:
  (the object's class +0x70 verb answering -1 AND [rec+0x12]
  bit 0x10 = SEQ_REV_X), ([obj+0x71] == -1 AND [rec+0x12] bit
  0x20 = SEQ_REV_Y), and ([obj+0x99] == -1 - the row-reset
  entry 0x52360 writes it 1 at 0x52377, so that term is off
  under normal running). No clamping after a relative jump:
  authored `1,0,GOTOREL -1` at row 1 leaves cursor = -1, and
  `gotorel 0` (KADMAR2's A_SPADANIE, A_RUN) re-enters the same
  row forever - the hold-without-a-clock pattern. (e) THE
  CORPUS, 777 texts: 135 goto lines in 102 states - goto 89
  (25 goto + 64 GOTO), GOTO_REL family 35, GOTOREL 11; two of
  the 135 sit on `;`-commented lines (SADES.06 BUTLA). ZARIA
  uses them for its ROW LISTS: the lion's A_DEAD (`27,400,
  GOTO_REL -3` - the death anim loops its last four rows
  instead of wrapping), A_KILOF, A_DRAP, A_LOOKUP, A_FIGHT,
  A_FIGHT_DOWN, A_BORRING, A_FG_PACKA(_DN), plus RYBA, KAMIEN
  1-3, SEP, SEP2, SPLYW. (f) THE RIDER QUESTION, NEGATIVE: F2
  asked whether this family could move a rider whose state
  authors no motion. It cannot - the verbs write only [rec+4],
  never a position word - and neither A_PODCIAG nor A_WPAD nor
  A_WYJSCIE carries a single goto line. The last candidate
  motion source for the lift is gone; the lift stays where
  PR-284/PR-286 left it. (g) THE ZERO FAMILY, found by the
  correction in CORRECTS: names 'zero' (0x9185d) and 'zero_t'
  (0x91862) build 8-byte nodes (no operand) on descriptor
  0xa0f88 at parser arms 0x45f05/0x45f49; its +0x04 verb
  0x45a50 walks the rest of the chain, then calls 0x52070(rec),
  which zeroes [obj+0x9d] and writes WORD [rec+0xc] =
  0x76bcc's-scaled ramp (rec+0xa - rec+8)/0x7fff + rec+8 (the
  plain move when [rec+0xa] == 0). 31 `zero` and 1 `zero_v`
  lines exist; what the [rec+8]/[rec+0xa]/[rec+0xc] triple and
  [obj+0x9d] ARE stays unread - named below.
OPENS: the port's row clock has no cursor-jump and never steps
  backwards - modelling the answer-6 protocol (ll_mov_fr gaining
  the goto pair, and a row-close that rewrites fi instead of
  fi+1/wrap when one is present) is the F2b port lead this read
  exists to open; what [rec+8]/[rec+0xa]/[rec+0xc] and
  [obj+0x9d] mean (the `zero`/`zero_t` law above is shape, not
  semantics); the class +0x70 verb and the -1 sentinels at
  [obj+0x70]-answer/[obj+0x71]/[obj+0x99] (who sets -1, and the
  name of signal bit index 3); whether the engine clamps a
  negative or past-end cursor anywhere else (the reads here show
  none); and the chain order inside one row: each +0x10 verb
  walks its SIBLINGS before applying itself (0x45d90 calls
  0x458e0 first), so with two gotos on one row the FIRST
  authored one wins - unverified against authored data because
  no shipped row carries two.
CLOSES: HANDOFF section 8 T5 step F2, the last unmodelled half
  of the six exit directives - all six are now read (`pos`
  PR-316/317, `lock`/`unlock`/`ldir`/`rdir` PR-320/PR-321,
  goto family this PR), and the rider clause is closed as a
  measured negative. OI-111 gains the advance law; the ladder
  thread's remaining work is F1b/F6's AC_ONAIR raise path, the
  ly_exit leg, and the new F2b port lead named in HANDOFF.
CORRECTS: PR-224's descriptor attribution for the answer-6
  verbs: `0xa1048 +0x14 = 0x45d90 (end_level ... THE ROW CURSOR
  IS SET ...)` and `0xa1030 +0x14 = 0x45dc0` are off by one
  table - 0x45d90 sits at 0xa1030+0x10, the ABSOLUTE-goto
  descriptor (and its stored value is authored minus one, not
  the authored number), 0x45dc0 at 0xa1018+0x10, the relative
  one; end_level's own descriptor 0xa1048 holds the base chain
  walk 0x458e0 at +0x10 and acts only through its +0x04 verb

  row touches the cursor. `0xa1090 +0x14 = 0x45d50` (the F-row
  hold) is the right class at the wrong slot: 0x45d50 sits at
  0xa1090+0x10. PR-320's `0x52070 is called from the ADJACENT
  0x45a50, the apply of the goto-family name that follows pos`:
  0x45a50 is not goto - it is the +0x04 verb of descriptor
  0xa0f88, installed by the `zero`/`zero_t` parser arms
  0x45f05/0x45f49; the real goto descriptors carry no custom
  execute verb at all (+0x04 is the base 0x457e0), which is

GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code changed

  parser census block in ll_play.c.
ADDRESSES: 0x46739, 0x4679c, 0x4680c, 0x46777, 0x467dd, 0x49920,
  0x91952, 0xa1018, 0xa1030, 0x45d90, 0x45dc0, 0x520c0, 0x52135,
  0x52140, 0x521b6, 0x52195, 0x54170
NAMES: goto, gotorel, goto_rel, GOTO, GOTO_REL, GOTOREL, goto,
  gotocmd, gotoval, answer-6, A_DEAD, A_KILOF, A_END, A_G1, A_G2,
  gotocmd, apply_row_pull, LL_SIG_AC_BREAK_NEXT
CODE: yes: two fields in ll_mov_fr (gotocmd/gotoval), one parser
  arm covering the three names, the answer-6 branch at the row
  close in ll_player_step, and the census-comment move from counted
  to modeled; no new tools.
HOOKS: none
MEASURED: (a) THE MODEL. Parse: one arm matches goto/gotorel/
  goto_rel case-insensitively (the corpus carries GOTO 64, goto
  25, GOTO_REL 35, GOTOREL 11 - PR-322's census) and reads '%d';
  `goto` stores gotocmd=1 with gotoval = authored minus one,
  mirroring 0x46777-0x46780, gotorel/goto_rel store gotocmd=2
  with the verbatim delta, mirroring the dec-inc pair at
  0x467dd/0x467ea-0x467ee. Row close (the same point where
  pos/lock/ldir apply, i.e. PR-322's 0x520c0 +0x04 pass): when
  the closing row carries the word, the cursor step of 0x45d90/
  0x45dc0 runs instead of the normal step - fi = gotoval, or
  fi += gotoval - and the +1/wrap branch is skipped ENTIRELY,
  exactly the 0x52140 answer-6 skip: no wrap, and no AC_BREAK_
  NEXT. The row entering through the jump has its one-shot I/F
  pull applied through the existing PR-253 admit path. The
  engine writes the cursor without clamping (PR-322); the port
  clamps to [0, nfr-1] as a NAMED safety net for the engine's
  undefined out-of-table read - no shipped PLAYER row reaches
  it (the only one, KADMAR2_SCHODY's `1,0,GOTOREL -1`, is an
  object state). (b) THE LEGS, red first (4 failures before the
  arms). G1: row 0 `goto 4` with an `I 100,0` row as the
  fourth - the parse stores 3, closing row 0 on iteration 0
  puts the cursor there, and that row's pull is in force from
  iteration 1: x walks 301, 302, 303 while the word-less
  control fixture stands at 300 through its iteration 1 (the
  pull row only reaches it there at iteration 3); the v
  register is asserted at 100. G2 is the A_DEAD shape: the
  last row `GOTO_REL -3` re-enters row 2, and the state's

  branch off - exactly 2 (G1's x line, G2's transition);
  dropping the parse-time minus-one - exactly 1, G1's parse

  so the parse check is what pins 0x46777's arithmetic).
  All pre-existing legs, PR-321's LK/D legs included, stayed
  green: the goto branch is inert for word-less rows.

  obj+0xa9, obj+0xe6, obj+0xe2, obj+0x3c, obj+0x10, obj+0x78,
  obj+0x68, obj+0x8, obj+0xbc, ll_play_v_step, ll_play_pull,
  ll_play_v_raw, LL_PLAY_RAW_VDIV, A_WPAD, A_WYJSCIE, A_JUMP,
  A_JUMP_S, A_FALL_DOWN, A_TURN, A_PRE_JUMP, A_DRAP, A_WALK, OI-119,
  F6, OI-078
CODE: no: only .md rows changed (this record, HANDOFF section 8 T5
  (6), OI-119, OI-078). No new tool: every reading is leodb dis over
  exact bytes, and the data lines are tools/extract_record.py output.
HOOKS: none new. Shipped read-only paths only: leodb dis/sql
  (PR-106 index), tools/extract_record.py for ZARIA.01 ANI2.DES, and
  this port's own LL_SIG_* enum to number the bits the engine raises.
MEASURED: (a) THE PAIR IS A VELOCITY, AND THE PHYSICS STEP WRITES IT.
  0x54250 (eax = the object, edx = a per-class parameter block, held
  in ebx) runs one integration pass over exactly this pair. verbatim:
  a class +0xbc guard answers first (0x5425c), and when it answers
  true and the block word [ebx+8] is under 20 and bit 2 of [obj+0xb6]
  is clear, that word is raised to 20 (0x54266-0x54275). Then, at
  0x5427c: edi = ([ebx+8] * [obj+0xc2]) / 100 and esi = ([ebx+0xc] *
  [obj+0xc6]) / 100 (the divisor is loaded as 0x64 at 0x54286) - the
  two drag terms. Then the two force terms: eax = ([ebx+0x0] *
  [obj+0xba]) / 20 + [obj+0x6d] * [ebx+0x10] and [obj+0xc2] is
  INCREMENTED by it (0x542ab-0x542c7); [obj+0xc6] is incremented by
  ([ebx+0x4] * [obj+0xbe]) / 20 + [ebx+0x14] (0x542cd-0x542fa) -
  [obj+0x6d], the facing word of ldir/rdir, scales the x side only,
  and [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe] are the intent words PR-147/PR-148 read.
  Then the drag is subtracted and a sign flip is killed: [obj+0xc2] =
  old - edi, and if old * new < 0 it is set to 0 (0x54300-0x54322),
  the same for y at 0x54325-0x54337. Finally 0x54170 ramps the pair
  toward the block's ceiling words [ebx+0x18] (mirrored) and
  [ebx+0x1c] - the not-an-assignment law this port already ships as
  ll_play_pull. This is the body PR-253/PR-256 read for the player and
  shipped as ll_play_v_step: drag = v*T/100, post = v + add, out =
  post - drag, out = 0 when post * out < 0 - an instruction-for-
  instruction match with 0x5427c-0x54337.
  (b) THE UNIT IS 1/100 px PER ITERATION, AND THREE SITES SAY SO.
  (i) The same function ends by storing [obj+0xc2]/100 to [obj+0xca]
  and [obj+0xc6]/100 to [obj+0xce] (0x5434d-0x54372) - the very
  per-iteration step words PR-98's mode switch at 0x543a0 consumes and
  that PR-320 already traced into the point at [obj+0x14a]. (ii) The
  surface pass compares the pair against a constant: 0x5476f is
  `cmp DWORD PTR [obj+0xc6],0x58c` (1420) inside the branch that
  decides whether to attach the object to a found surface, reached only
  when [obj+0xe2] is 2 - a fall speed of 14.2 px per iteration above
  which the attach is skipped. (iii) The point-provider verbs PR-319
  read offset a point by `[obj+0xc2] * 15 / 100`, a velocity scale,
  not an offset scale. And the pair's other two writers are the ramp
  0x54170 and the command handler, not a position store.
  (c) WHO ELSE TOUCHES IT, EXACTLY. The command handler 0x54560 is the
  base class +0x10 verb, and the opcode test is a tree, not a table:
  opcode 2 assigns both (0x54590-0x5459c, reached through 0x54680),
  opcode 0xd adds to both (0x545a7-0x545bb, reached through 0x54577),
  opcode 8 zeroes both (0x545f4, reached through 0x54649), opcode 6
  writes [obj+0x6d] and [obj+0x71] (0x545de), opcodes 3 and 4 set
  bits 4 and 8 of [obj+0xb6] (0x545c6/0x545d2), opcode 0x1b swaps the
  surface link [obj+0xa9] (0x5460e), and everything else falls to
  0x53770. The level-script dispatcher 0x50d60 posts into it at
  0x50e53; the lion's own class 0x96874 chains to it (PR-319's
  0x3d8f0 at 0x3d906). And every state entry zeroes the pair:
  0x5042e/0x50438 sit immediately after the [class+0x4] state call of
  0x50420 and immediately before the [obj+0x6d] = 1 facing default at
  0x50442, which is the same block PR-321 read for ldir/rdir.
  (d) THE THREE RECTANGLE ASK VERBS DIFFER BY ONE TEST, AND IT IS THE
  SIGN. All three take eax = the placed rectangle object (its authored
  box is [self+0x3c], written by the +0x18 verb 0x40c90 through the
  `%d,%d;%d,%d` format at 0x91d00, PR-318), ebx = the asker, edx =
  the answer buffer, and all three build the buffer through 0x749a0
  with ebx = 0xc and raise into it. RECT at 0x40cf0 runs ONLY the
  geometry test - the asker's +0x68 getter, for the lion 0x23900 which
  returns the block at [lion+0xd6], and that block's class +0x8 verb,
  0x23e00, against `lea edx,[self+0x3c]` - and raises byte 2 mask 0x2
  at 0x40d23 (bit 17, LL_SIG_AC_RECT). DRECT2 at 0x40dc0 adds the
  asker's ASKABLE probe ([asker+8]+0x3c at 0x40dce) and raises byte 2
  mask 0x10 at 0x40dff (bit 20, AC_DRECT2). DRECT at 0x40d50 runs the
  SAME two tests and ONE more: 0x40d65 loads [asker+0xc6], 0x40d6b
  tests it and 0x40d6d refuses when it is <= 0, before raising byte 2
  mask 0x8 at 0x40d99 (bit 19, AC_DRECT). So AC_DRECT is
  AC_DRECT2-plus-falling: the verb answers only while the asker's own
  y-velocity is positive, and PR-99's sign makes positive y DOWN.
  (e) THE DATA AND WHO ASKS IT. ZARIA.01 ANI2.DES carries the shipped
  set's only DRECT (line 18, `DRECT,988,645;1340,750`) next to a
  RECT (line 19) and a KILOF_PL (line 20); that box contains the
  A_WYJSCIE exit point 1020,692 of PR-317 and spans the three
  ZWODOSPD mushroom platforms. SEVEN states of the ZARIA.01 lion
  script ask it, all with the same transition and no others in the
  file: A_JUMP_S line 53, A_JUMP 78, A_FALL_DOWN 105, A_WALK 131,
  A_TURN 219, A_PRE_JUMP 402, A_DRAP 473, each `A_WPAD(1)=AC_ONAIR,
  AC_DRECT` (the ZAR_LEWPL.MOV twin carries the same seven at lines
  52/76/102/128/216/399/470). AC_DRECT appears in 5 of the 777 .MOV
  files in the extracted script set and AC_DRECT2 in 2 (SADES.06,
  TUNGA.11 - the two levels PR-318 found place DRECT2 objects), so the
  velocity-gated verb is the rare one and it belongs to this level's
  exit. A_WPAD then runs eleven rows behind `lock`/`unlock` (PR-321's
  window) and its list end feeds AC_BREAK_NEXT into A_WYJSCIE, whose
  first rows are `lock`, `ldir`, `pos 1020,692`, `wait AC_TIME`.
  (f) WHY THIS IS A PORT GAP, NOT AN ENGINE ONE. The gate's input
  already exists in this port under a name: ll_play.c keeps exactly
  this register (p->vx/p->vy in px per second, ll_play_v_raw converting
  to the 1/100 integer, PR-256) and ll_play_v_step is the pass of
  section (a). What the port has NO path for is the other side of the
  ask: a DRECT placement line becomes st->poly (ll_level.c:9807,
  counted as a polyline, exactly as PR-318 (g) reported), so no object
  with an authored box at [obj+0x3c] exists for the walk 0x4b500 to
  ask, and nothing in the port raises bits 17/19/20. F6's port half
  is now named without a guess in it: place the rectangle-class objects
  the `.des` lines name, run the 0x40d50 verb's three tests against
  them, and raise AC_DRECT into the lion's live set.
OPENS: the parameter block of 0x54250 - which authored words its
  +0x0/+0x4/+0x8/+0xc/+0x10/+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c are (the F and T words
  are named for the x pair by PR-132, the rest is not), and what the
  class +0xbc guard at 0x5425c asks (PR-132's conditional T-raise
  question, unchanged); which classes reach 0x54250 at all - the three
  call sites 0x24731/0x321fe/0x33348 were never named by class; the
  0x54860 decay block OI-119 already names; the surface words
  [obj+0xa9]/[obj+0xe6]/[obj+0xe2] and their kinds, which decide when
  AC_ONAIR (0x54800), AC_DUP (0x54785) and AC_DUP_CD (0x547d1) fire
  and are the second half of the exit chain's AC_ONAIR term; and on
  the port side, whether a DRECT object is askable in the sense of the
  +0x3c probe, which decides whether gate (1) of 0x40d50 ever passes.
CLOSES: OI-119. The pair is the object's velocity register in 1/100
  px per iteration, x at +0xc2 and y at +0xc6, written by the physics
  step, the ramp verb and the command opcodes, zeroed at every state
  entry; and the AC_DRECT gate's `[asker+0xc6] > 0` is "the asker is
  moving down", which is the whole difference between DRECT and
  DRECT2. That unblocks the F6 leg of HANDOFF section 8 T5 (6): the
  exit chain A_JUMP/A_JUMP_S/A_FALL_DOWN/A_WALK/A_TURN/A_PRE_JUMP/
  A_DRAP -> A_WPAD -> A_WYJSCIE is now walkable in the port as far as

CORRECTS: PR-319, twice. Its "THE PAIR IS A COMMAND-WRITTEN (x,y)

MEASURED: (a) ONE RECORD PARSER, EIGHT CLASS TABLES. The +0x18
  verb of eight class tables is the same three instructions:
  0x40c90 `add eax,0x3c; call 0x49f90; ret`, and 0x49f90 is a
  four-slot scan - it pushes eax, eax+4, eax+8, eax+0xc and the
  format 0x91d00 `%d,%d;%d,%d , ` to the wrapper 0x49920. So a
  three-field `.des` line `TOKEN,x0,y0;x1,y1` fills the record at
  [obj+0x3c..0x48], and the ctor zeroes that record before the
  line is read (0x29458-0x2947c zeroes +0x3c, +0x40, +0x44, +0x48
  and stores the 0x98274 string pointer at +0x4c). leodb's dword
  read finds +0x18 = 0x40c90 in exactly eight tables, and they are
  the primary half of eight adjacent pairs - every class stores
  two vtables (BRECT: 0x99668 to [obj+0x8] and 0x99660 to
  [obj+0xc], stores 0x29480/0x29487; the same adjacency for
  KILOF_PL 0x96b88/0x96b80, BICZRECT 0x99f64/0x99f5c, WSPRECT
  0x99ff0/0x99fe8, KRA1 0x9ec8c/0x9ec84 stores 0x38905/0x3890c,
  RECT 0xa15ac/0xa15a4, DRECT 0xa1638/0xa1630, DRECT2
  0xa16c4/0xa16bc). Only the primary of each pair parses through
  0x40c90: the second of the BICZRECT pair has +0x18 = 0x40ca0, a
  neighbour this record did not read. Each class is named by the
  installer branch that compares its token through 0x76a69 and
  stores the vtables: KILOF_PL ('KILOF_PL' 0x90741 at 0x1fba6,
  store 0x1fbf4); BRECT ('BRECT' 0x90a40 at 0x2956d, store
  0x295bb); BICZRECT ('BICZRECT' 0x90a46 at 0x295cf, store
  0x2961d); WSPRECT ('WSPRECT' 0x90a4f at 0x29631, store
  0x2967f); KRA1 ('KRA1' 0x91291 at 0x387f5); RECT ('RECT'
  0x91f75, store 0x4e147); DRECT ('DRECT' 0x91f7a, store
  0x4e1aa); DRECT2 ('DRECT2' 0x91f80, store 0x4e20d).
  (b) THE SIGNAL IS THE CLASS'S, NOT THE ASK'S. All eight +0x78
  verbs share one body shape - the asker's ASKABLE probe
  `[edx+0x3c]` (0x286ae, 0x2871f, 0x1e3ae), a class-specific gate,
  then the asker's point through its +0x68 or +0x6c getter and the
  element verb `[eax+8]` against `lea edx,[ecx+0x3c]` (0x23e00,
  PR-318/PR-319), then the answer-buffer build 0x749a0 with
  ebx = 0xc, and a raise into that buffer. The RAISED BIT differs
  by class: BICZRECT 0x286a0 raises byte 2 mask 8 = AC_DRECT at
  0x286ec, so AC_DRECT has TWO raisers (PR-326 read the DRECT
  verb 0x40d50's raise at 0x40d99); BRECT 0x28710 raises byte 2
  mask 2 = AC_RECT at 0x28772, so AC_RECT has two too (the RECT
  verb's 0x40d23); WSPRECT 0x287a0 raises AC_DRAB at 0x28805;
  KRA1 0x37ea0 raises AC_KILOF at 0x37ed7 and AC_BECZKA at
  0x37f3a; and KILOF_PL 0x1e3a0 raises AC_KILOF at 0x1e42b. The
  gates differ as much as the bits, and none of them is the
  geometry-only test PR-326 called RECT's: BICZRECT requires the
  asker's class +0x70 verb to return -1 (0x286ba `call
  [edx+0x70]`, 0x286bd `cmp eax,0xffffffff`, 0x286c0 leaves
  unless equal) - the same
  verb slot PR-322's reverse-row law reads (OI-111); KILOF_PL
  requires it to be > 0 (0x1e3f1, 0x1e3f6 `jle`); BRECT tests the
  asker's state index instead (0x28726 `cmp [ebx+0x5c],9` /
  0x2872e `cmp eax,0xd`) and picks the +0x6c getter inside 9..13,
  the +0x68 getter outside it. Only the RECT verb 0x40cf0 raises
  on geometry alone (PR-326 (d)).
  (c) ONE RAISER THE CENSUS TOOL DOES NOT SEE. 0x1e42b raises
  through a register (`mov ah,[ecx+4]` / `add ecx,4` / `or ah,1` /
  `mov [ecx],ah`), and tools/re/signal_raise_census.py matches the
  memory form `or BYTE PTR [reg+d],imm`, so it reported no raise
  for the KILOF_PL verb at all and AC_KILOF looked like a KRA1
  signal. The complete AC_KILOF set is three sites: 0x1e42b (the
  KILOF_PL ask), 0x37ed7 (the KRA1 ask) and 0x75390, which is a
  command-style body, not an ask verb (0x75384 tests [eax+8],
  writes 3 to [edx+0x1c] when present, then raises byte 1 mask 1
  and calls 0x79450) - its caller was not read.
  (d) WHICH OF THESE THE SHIPPED DATA PLACES, AND IN WHICH FORM.
  Over the 103 `.des` text files llrs_cat1 dumps for both

  string 'KRY' (LONA.05_ANI3 line 12) exists nowhere in the
  engine - a leodb str read over the whole table finds no 'KRY',
  only 'Program wykryl zmiany...', so that line places nothing.
  (e) WHAT THIS DOES TO F6b, AND THE CONTROL LEVEL. ZARIA.01
  authors exactly two boxes of this family - the DRECT that
  answers the seven `A_WPAD(1)=AC_ONAIR,AC_DRECT` asks and the
  KILOF_PL, the only placed object in reach of the A_DRAP ask of
  line 462 (`A_KILOF(1)=K_FIRE,AC_KILOF,K_F4`, the same line at

  not exist: a placed object carrying an authored box at

  and the KILOF_PL ask additionally needs the class +0x70 verb to

  control: its lion asks AC_KILOF from seven states (LON_LEW.MOV
  lines 146, 147, 202, 249, 282, 318, 352) and the level places
  NO KILOF_PL, but it does place 21 KRA1 objects, whose class
  verb 0x37ea0 raises AC_KILOF - so one ask name reaches the
  player through two different classes in two levels, exactly as
  section (b) says it must.
  (f) THE ASKER'S SIDE OF THE GATES, AND THE TABLE THAT REALLY
  RUNS. The ask verbs read the asker's vtable at [asker+0x8], so
  every gate is the ASKER's class verb, not the box's: the ASKABLE
  probe is [asker+8]+0x3c (0x40d5e), the direction test is
  [asker+8]+0x70 (0x1e3f1, 0x286ba), and the two point getters are
  [asker+8]+0x68 = 0x23900, the presented point [obj+0xd6]
  (PR-319), and [asker+8]+0x6c = 0x23a10 `add eax,0x89`, the
  frozen anchor pair PR-305 read. And the table that answers is
  NOT 0x96874: that pair, 0x96874/0x9686c, is the BASE every class
  chains to - the same two addresses are stored by the ctors of
  TLewZariaB, TLewEna2 and TABLICZKALONA (stores 0x2020e/0x20215,
  0x26e3f, 0x38dde) - and its +0x3c verb is 0x23c10
  `xor eax,eax; ret`, the not-askable default. The ZARIA lion's
  own pair is 0x97a98/0x97a90, stored into [obj+0x8]/[obj+0xc] at
  0x1ff49/0x1ff50 in the branch whose token compare is
  'TLewZariaB' (0x90795) at 0x1ff26. In it +0x3c = 0x230a0
  `mov eax,1; ret` - the lion IS askable, so the DRECT, DRECT2,
  BICZRECT and BRECT probes pass; +0x68 = 0x23900 and +0x6c =
  0x23a10, the two points PR-319/PR-305 named; +0x70 = 0x239f0
  `mov eax,[obj+0x6d]; ret`, PR-321's facing word; +0x18 =
  0x23c60 and +0x10 = 0x1e130, not the base's 0x3d8f0. So the
  BICZRECT ask answers only for a lion facing LEFT and the
  KILOF_PL ask only for one facing RIGHT (-1/+1, PR-321's
  ldir/rdir), and PR-322's reverse-row test `class +0x70 verb
  == -1` is that same facing-left read on whichever class it is
  called on. It also settles which point each ask tests: the
  PRESENTED point for RECT, DRECT, DRECT2 and KILOF_PL, the FROZEN
  ANCHOR for BICZRECT, and for BRECT the anchor while the asker's
  declared state is 9..13 and the presented point outside it.
OPENS: whether the `1 -4,0;37,0` row of an art placement is the
  text the +0x18 verb scans, and whether 0x23e00 then reads it
  relative to the object's position (the KRA1/KRA2 form); the
  caller of the non-ask AC_KILOF raiser 0x75390 and what
  `[edx+0x1c] = 3` means; the bodies of the WSPRECT 0x287a0 and

  census tool and did not read; which lion-variant table this port
  should read as the player's - it read TLewZariaB's 0x97a98, the
  other TLew* classes are not compared here; and why BRECT and
  WSPRECT exist in the engine yet are placed by no shipped `.des`.
CLOSES: nothing. It narrows OI-018 to the semantics of AC_ONAIR,
  AC_DUP and AC_EDGE: the raisers of AC_RECT, AC_DRECT, AC_DRECT2,
  AC_KILOF and AC_BECZKA are counted per class, with the gate and
  raise site of six of the eight ask verbs read; and it closes
  PR-326's open half about the ASKABLE probe - the lion's own
  +0x3c verb 0x230a0 returns 1, and its direction word is the
  [obj+0x6d] this port already models.
CORRECTS: PR-326, twice, and one tool. Its framing of AC_DRECT as
  belonging to the DRECT class alone is too narrow - the BICZRECT
  ask verb 0x286a0 raises the same bit under a different gate and
  AC_RECT has a second raiser at 0x28772 (its "the shipped set's
  only DRECT" stands). Its "the lion's own class 0x96874" names
  the BASE pair 0x96874/0x9686c, which the classes chain to and
  whose +0x3c is the not-askable default 0x23c10; the ZARIA lion's
  own pair is 0x97a98/0x97a90, which is where PR-319's 0x23900
  and PR-305's [obj+0x89] actually come from - those readings
  stand, the attribution did not. And
  tools/re/signal_raise_census.py under-reports AC_KILOF: the
  KILOF_PL verb 0x1e3a0 does raise, at 0x1e42b, in a register
  form the tool does not match.

  legs run in every configuration.
MEASURED: (a) WHAT THE READER DID BEFORE. `TOKEN,x0,y0;x1,y1` has three
  commas, so it fell past the entry grammar into `else if (strchr(line,
  ';')) st->poly++;` - the polyline branch. Every one of the 18 shipped
  box lines PR-327 counted (1 in ZARIA.01_ANI2 line 18 and 2 more in
  lines 19-20, 7 in SADES.06_ANIM, 2 in TUNGA.11_ANI2, 1 in
  TUNGA2.12_ANIM, 1 in KADMAR.07_ANI1, 7 DRECT2 elsewhere in
  SADES.06_ANIM) was counted as ground noise and placed nothing. That is
  what PR-318/PR-326 reported and it was true of the code then.
  (b) RED FIRST. The new legs feed the reader a fixture `.des` of 15
  lines built from the shipped lines verbatim. Before the code: `0
  rectangle-class lines, expected 10`, `objects total 1, expected 11`,
  `polyline lines 13, expected 3` and ten "no object of class X carries
  the authored box" lines. After it, all ten boxes stand.
  (c) MUTATIONS, five, each caught by the named legs (this leg is
  data-free, so it runs in the fixture-free configuration too): M1b the
  box read as a CHILD of the entry before it, PR-95's rule applied here
  (6 legs fail, first "no object of class BICZRECT carries the authored
  box 218,345;230,368" - the KADMAR.07 shape is a box line sitting in
  another object's property block); M2 the box sorted to low/high like
  place_rect does for the ladder (2, first "no object of class RECT
  carries the authored box 900,300;800,250"); M3 one class record per
  line instead of per class (1: "3 class record(s) for RECT with 1
  instance(s), expected 1 and 3"); M4 the class-token check dropped, any
  first field accepted (5: "12 rectangle-class lines, expected 10" -
  ZONE and KRY join, which PR-327 excludes); M5 the entry grammar's
  world-bounds rule applied to a box (6: "9, expected 10" - TUNGA.11
  authors `RECT,-10,200;50,500`).
  (d) THE THREE MODEL FACTS THE CODE KEEPS, EACH READ IN PR-327.
  Absolute: 0x40c90 is `add eax,0x3c; call 0x49f90; ret`, and 0x49f90
  only pushes the four output pointers and the format 0x91d00
  `%d,%d;%d,%d , ` to 0x49920 - there is no add of the placement, unlike
  the ladder's own record verb 0x3f0f0, which reads the same shape and
  then adds the placement at 0x3f124-0x3f14b (PR-246). place_rect keeps
  that offset rule; place_rect_class writes the authored numbers as they
  stand, and the leg pins the difference on the KADMAR.07 case (a pulled
  box would read 246,387;258,410). Unsorted: nothing in the verb orders
  the edges, so an authored box that runs backwards is kept as written
  and simply matches nothing under 0x23e00 - the engine's behaviour, not
  a port choice. One class record, many instances: the class token names
  the object's script the way DRABINKA does (ladder_class), so three
  RECT lines share one class record with ninst = 3 and stay three
  objects - the engine's one table per class and one instance per line.
  (e) WHAT THEY ARE NOT. They have no script, no art, no states, so
  every path that gates on sc->mov steps over them: the fixture count
  line stays "68 animated object(s), 18 static image(s)" for TUNGA.11
  because the two boxes are counted as neither, and the listing names
  them for what they are ("obj DRECT2[rectangle class]: no script, no
  art - the line authors the box 510,400;820,600 and nothing else").
  The per-level report now prints its own line for them ("authored scene
  TUNGA.11: 2 rectangle-class line(s) ... placed as objects carrying the
  class token and the authored box at [obj+0x3c]; nothing asks them
  yet"), and the bounded "more placement(s) advanced" proof line moves
  from 74 to 76 because the scene holds 88 placements instead of 86.
  (f) NOT IN THIS GRAMMAR, LEGGED AS NEGATIVES. ZONE
  (`ZONE,5044,444;5056,456`): its +0x18 verb is 0x41c50, which does the
  same 0x49f90 scan and then reads `id= %d` (0x91689) - not one of the
  eight. KRY: no such string exists in the engine. KRA1/KRA2 are in the
  token table (the engine's class name at 0x91291 is in the eight), but
  their shipped lines are five-field ART placements whose box sits in a
  following `1 -4,0;37,0` row, so they go through the entry grammar. A
  token whose numbers are not four numbers - `DRECT,988,645`,
  `DRECT,988,645;1340` - places nothing and stays counted as it was.
OPENS: the ask itself - nothing in the port calls the class verb
  0x40cf0/0x40d50/0x40dc0/0x1e3a0/0x286a0, so no AC_RECT, AC_DRECT,
  AC_DRECT2 or AC_KILOF is raised - that is the next step, and PR-327
  already names every gate and PR-326 the velocity input this port has;
  the position of such an object (the line authors none, so the port
  keeps 0 and the box absolute - the engine's own default for those
  fields was never read); whether the `1 -4,0;37,0` row of a KRA1/KRA2
  art line is the text their +0x18 verb scans, and whether 0x23e00 then

  (the class +0x60 verb, PR-247) does with a box like this; and whether

CLOSES: nothing. It finishes the placement half of F6b as HANDOFF

CORRECTS: PR-318 and PR-326 on the port side, in the tense they were

MEASURED: (a) WHAT WAS MISSING. PR-328 placed the 18 shipped box
  lines; nothing called a class answer verb, so no AC_RECT,
  AC_DRECT, AC_DRECT2 or AC_KILOF could ever be live and the exit

  (b) WHERE THE ASK COMES FROM, READ IN FULL. 0x523f0, the per-step
  key builder, asks through the record class's +0x10 verb (0x52790
  for the placed family), which switches on the requester state's
  CHECK_* control words (PR-245). One walk found by its [vt+0x78]
  call sites (only 4 in the whole image: 0x4b5be, 0x4bda9, 0x4be09,
  0x55421) is 0x4b500: it iterates instance arrays (0x4b581), filters
  each candidate by its class +0x60 (0x4b59a), skips self (0x4b5af),
  matches planes unless the flag at [esp+0x54] is set (0x4b5a1, fed
  by CHECK_ALL_PLANE), and calls [class+0x78] at 0x4b5be with
  eax = candidate, ebx = requester; the 12-byte answer it returns is
  merged into the requester's set by 0x49580 at 0x4b5c5. That is the
  same +0x78 entry PR-147/PR-249 read for the ladder.
  (c) THE BITS ARE THE SIGNAL INDEXES. The success paths write
  `or BYTE PTR [ans+0x2], 0x2` (0x40d23), 0x8 (0x40d99), 0x10
  (0x40dff) and, in the register form at 0x1e422-0x1e42b, `or ah,1`
  into BYTE [ans+0x4]. Those are bit positions 17, 19, 20 and 32 -
  exactly LL_SIG_AC_RECT, LL_SIG_AC_DRECT, LL_SIG_AC_DRECT2 and
  LL_SIG_AC_KILOF of the PR-69 signal table, which is the engine's

  (d) THE VERB GATES, EACH READ: RECT 0x40cf0 has NO probe at all,
  only the requester's presented point against the box; DRECT2
  0x40dc0 = askable probe + geometry; DRECT 0x40d50 = probe +

## PR-330 — THE .MOV LINE IS READ THROUGH ONE CHAINED CURSOR, SO AN
## `s <seq>` LINE IS A ROW TOO: 206 WERE UNREAD, AND ZARIA.01'S LION
## RAN A TWO-ROW FALL WHERE THE GAME AUTHORS THREE
```
KIND: port
SUBSYSTEM: the row-line test of the .MOV parser - ported/ll_play.c's
  ll_mov_parse and the new shared ll_mov_row_line - and the row count
  of the object census in ported/ll_level.c and its end-level row
  injector. It is the read that makes the F6 exit thread of HANDOFF
  section 8 T5 (6) walkable: A_FALL_DOWN is the state the surface-link
  raiser of the next step reaches, and its authored row list was short
  by one row, so the state's own row tokens addressed the wrong rows.
ADDRESSES: 0x51910, 0x51921, 0x51926, 0x51929, 0x961fc, 0x92115,
  0x92119, 0x9211e, 0x92122, 0x92126, 0x92127, 0x9212e, 0x92131,
  0x9213c, 0x9213f, 0x92146, 0x92148, 0x92156, 0x9215a, 0x92162,
  0x51933, 0x51944, 0x51948, 0x51956, 0x5195a, 0x51960, 0x519ab,
  0x519c3, 0x51a4e, 0x51a55, 0x51a64, 0x51a6a, 0x57d30, 0x51a7b,
  0x51a86, 0x51a8c, 0x51a92, 0x51a95, 0x51a9a, 0x49920,
  0x51ab7, 0x51ac1, 0x51ac9, 0x51af7, 0x21e80, 0x515e0, 0xa2638,
  0x51660, 0x51679, 0x5168d, 0x51692, 0x51696, 0x5169e, 0x516a3,
  0x516a8, 0x516af, 0x516c2, 0x516cf, 0x516d2, 0x44110, 0x516d5,
  0x45df0, 0x76d20, 0x76a69, 0x51eb0, 0x51f37, 0x51f3e,
  0x51f48, 0x51f54, 0x3e8, 0xcef40, 0xceff4, 0xceff8
NAMES: s, seq, time, time_scale, sample, control, BY_TIME, FRAME_REV,
  ll_mov_row_line, ll_mov_parse, ll_mov_st, seq_switch, no_scale,
  ll_mov_fr, ll_mov_row_start, A_FALL_DOWN, A_TO_BOR, A_LISC_END,
  A_PUT_BOMB, A_WSP_LIN_DOWN2, A_BORING4, T_TELEPORT1, T_TELEPORT2,
  A_DEAD, A_RUN, A_WSP, A_DRAP, A_LOOKDOWN, ZARIA.01, ZARIA.02,
  TUNGA.11, TUNGA2.12, KADMAR.07, KARA.07, LONA.05, ENA.03,
  SADES.06, F6, OI-120, OI-111
CODE: yes: ported/ll_play.c (ll_mov_row_line, the row branch of
  ll_mov_parse, the time_scale pass, and the LEG S block added to
  --play-selftest), ported/ll_play.h (that declaration,
  ll_mov_st.seq_switch, ll_mov_fr.no_scale) and ported/ll_level.c
  (the census field, its report clause, and PR-199's end-level row
  injector now calling the shared test). Makefile: the PR-278
  ladder-descend leg re-pinned for the third row; no leg added or
  removed, so the fixture count stays 71.
HOOKS: none new. The re-pinned leg runs under the existing
  LEO_PLAY_SCRIPT / LEO_PLAY_ASK / LEO_LEVEL_PPM / LEO_LEVEL_PPM_TICK
  knobs; the data-free legs ride --play-selftest, which verify-play
  already requires.
MEASURED: (a) WHAT THE PORT ASKED, AND WHAT THE ENGINE ASKS. The port
  required a line to BEGIN with the number pair, sscanf(line, "%d,%d").
  The engine never looks at a line head. Its state-block reader 0x51910
  builds ONE character cursor in its prologue - 0x51921 loads the
  stream vtable 0x961fc, 0x51926/0x51929 store it at [ebp-0x1c] with
  a zero at [ebp-0x20] - and every scan after that consumes from where
  the previous one stopped. The `time` arm shows the chaining
  outright: it reads "%hi" (0x9211e) at 0x51948 into [st+0x8] and
  then ",%hi" (0x92122) at 0x5195a into [st+0xa] of the SAME line.
  Its first step is the token " %[^,| \r\n\t]" (0x92162) compared by
  the plain byte comparator 0x76d20 - NOT the case-folding 0x76a69
  that names states - against the field names time (0x92119), sample
  (0x92127), time_scale (0x92131), seq (0x9213f), s (0x92146),
  control (0x9215a).
  (b) THE `s` ARM DOES NOT END THE LINE. At 0x51a4e the token `s` is
  compared; on a match (0x51a64 is the not-match exit) 0x51a6a scans
  the sequence NAME with " %[^ ,]%*[ ,]" (0x92148) through 0x57d30,
  0x51a7b-0x51a92 resolves that name through the record table reached
  from ds:0xcef40 +0x398, then its [obj+0x16] vtable +0x4, with the
  record-id counter ds:0xceff8 as the second argument, and 0x51a9a
  reads the frame with "%d," (0x92156) through 0x49920. 0x51aa9
  allocates the row node (0x18 bytes) and 0x51ac1 calls the row ctor
  0x515e0 - the same ctor the ordinary row lines use from the
  state-body reader 0x51eb0 at 0x51f54; its class word is 0xa2638.
  0x51ac9-0x51af7 appends the node to the state's row vector at
  [st+0x2e], growing it through 0x21e80.
  (c) THE ROW RECORD AND THE TWO DIFFERENT CTOR ARGUMENTS. The ctor
  zeroes [node+0x8]/[0xc]/[0x14] and sets [node+0x10] to 1 (its own
  default threshold), then 0x51660 reads the units itself with "%hi"
  (0x92115) from that same cursor - so the number AFTER the name is
  the row's units - multiplies by the caller's factor and divides by
  0x3e8 (0x51679, 0x5168d). The frame paths follow: 0x51692 branches
  on the sign, a negative frame sets [node+0x14] (0x51696) and stores
  the magnitude at [node+0xc] (0x516a3-0x516a8), a positive one
  stores it minus one (0x516d2) - PR-107's 1-based, negative-means-
  mirrored mapping is this port's copy of that pair - and the record
  the field named goes to [node+0x8] on every path (0x5169e, 0x516cf,
  and for an authored frame 0 the record comes from 0x44110 at
  0x516af-0x516c2). The ordinary fill passes the state's [st+0xe]
  time_scale (0x51f37-0x51f3e, the word the `time_scale` arm stores
  at 0x519c3); the `s` arm passes the CONSTANT 0x3e8 (0x51ab7). So an
  `s`-led row keeps its authored units. That is observable in exactly
  three shipped states: LONA.05's T_TELEPORT1, T_TELEPORT1_2 and
  T_TELEPORT2, `time_scale=600` with 37 `s`-led rows between them.
  [node+0x8] is the sequence record the field named: a row may choose
  the art its frames come from, while the state's own `seq=` line
  names only the default. 0x516d5 then walks the rest of the line
  through the directive chain 0x45df0 like any other row, which is why
  the `GEN`/`Wait`/`F` tails of these lines parse with the rules the
  port already has.
  (d) THE POPULATION, RE-MEASURED. A scan that reproduces the 18617
  row lines the older records quote EXACTLY, run over the same 777
  extracted texts: 206 of them are `s`-led, in 26 files and 36
  states, in two written forms - `s name 1,300` (164) and
  `s name,1,200` (42, the comma the engine's %*[ ,] eats) - so the
  shipped row count is 18823, not 18617. No `s`-led line carries an
  M tail, so PR-59's 285 stands. The lists the port was short: one
  A_FALL_DOWN row plus five A_TO_BOR rows in each of ZARIA.01,
  ZARIA.02, their LEWPL twins, TUNGA.11 and TUNGA2.12; KADMAR.07's
  0_0 (A_FALL_DOWN, A_LISC_END), its six ninjas' A_DEAD (5 each) and
  its three SCHODY A_RUN; KARA.07's A_PUT_BOMB (27); LONA.05's
  A_WSP_LIN_DOWN2 (5) and T_TELEPORT trio (37); ENA.03's A_BORING4
  (24); and seven SADES.06 objects' A_DEAD and A_RUN (42).
  (e) THE MODEL. ll_mov_row_line is now the ONE row test, and it
  returns the frame and the units too: ll_mov_parse calls it, rewrites
  the line to what follows the `s` field and parses the rest with the
  unchanged rules - the 100-unit floor, the tails, the `Wait` capture.
  The sequence record is counted as ll_mov_st.seq_switch, totalled per
  object and reported by the object census with the shipped 206 named
  in the wording; ll_mov_fr.no_scale carries the ctor difference. The
  end-level injector of PR-199 counts rows through the same function,
  so its <state>:<row> addressing cannot drift from the parser's.
  (f) WHY A PLAY FIXTURE MOVED. ZARIA.01's A_FALL_DOWN has THREE
  authored rows and the unread one is the FIRST, so every row index
  and the state's own `A_FALL_DOWN(3)=!AC_ONAIR` token were one row
  off. The PR-278 ladder-descend leg re-pins to the authored chain:
  the fall ENTERS on `s idle 1,300` - frame 1 at tick 251 - the three
  rows close in 1+1+3 iterations, the list ENDS at 253,
  `A_DRAP(1)=AC_BREAK_NEXT` takes him out at 254, `A_LOOKDOWN(1)=
  K_DOWN` (FWD,DOWN held since 223) follows at 255, and the ground
  comes at 217,652 at 264: feet 652 plus the 30 px look_dn art
  contact = 682, the .plt main-ground line at that x. The old pins -
  251 frame 8, 270 pos 214,651 - are superseded. Nothing else moved:
  verify-all with the data staged is 71 (ok), the same count as
  before.
  (g) RED FIRST, AND THE MUTATIONS. The data-free leg is LEG S of
  --play-selftest, built from ZARIA.01's own [A_FALL_DOWN] text:
  three rows, seq_switch == 1, the frame 1 and units 300 of the
  `s` row and its GEN K_GEN1 tail, the `7,0` row's 100-unit floor and
  its WAIT K_NEVER capture, the `8,300,F 0,100` landing row, and
  ll_mov_row_start(3) resolving to that third row - plus a
  time_scale=600 block shaped like LONA.05's (300 scaled to 180 for
  the ordinary row, 300 kept for the `s` row) and the negatives: an
  uppercase S is not the field, a nameless `s` line is not a row.
  Against the parser as it was, LEG S is RED at the row count. Seven
  mutations, every one caught: M1 the old test (8 failures, first at
  the row count), M2 the row taken with the `s` prefix left in place
  (8), M3 the field name matched case-insensitively (1, the negative
  leg), M4 the row read but the switch not counted (2), M5 the count
  raised once per block row instead of per line (1), M6 the `s` row
  scaled by the block time_scale (1), M7 no_scale never set (1).
  (h) THE NAMED DIFFERENCES, ALL WITH ZERO SHIPPED INSTANCES. An `s`
  line with no name before its comma: in the engine the name scan
  fails, %*[ ,] still consumes the separator, "%d," reads the frame
  and the record slot keeps the caller's value, so a row IS appended;
  this parser calls it not-a-row. Its mirror: %[^ ,] ends a name only
  at a space or a comma in the engine and this parser ends it at a
  tab as well, and the engine's %*[ ,] would consume a tab that this
  parser leaves. Both are unreachable in the shipped 206 lines.
OPENS: the sequence record at [node+0x8] and the draw path that reads
  it - OI-120; what 0x44110 returns for an authored frame 0, the one
  row path that resolves a record WITHOUT the `s` field; whether the
  record table at 0x51a7b-0x51a95 hands back
  the SAME record a block's `seq=` line named - "idle" is both
  A_FALL_DOWN's row sequence and the idle state's own art - which
  decides whether a row can share art with a state at all; the
  nameless-`s` row and the tab rules of (h); the growth law of the
  row vector at 0x21e80 beyond the append at 0x51ade; and OI-111's
  `Wait` tail, still unconsulted by the player's row admit, which is
  why `7,0,WAIT K_NEVER` holds nothing in this port today.
CLOSES: nothing. It restores the authored row lists of 36 states and
  with them the row numbers their own transition tokens name -
  ZARIA.01's A_FALL_DOWN(3) among them - which is the precondition
  for the surface-link raiser step that follows it.
CORRECTS: PR-278's ladder-descend note, whose fall stayed inside
  A_FALL_DOWN to tick 270 on a two-row list; the population quoted as
  18617 shipped frame lines in ported/ll_play.c and in PR-110,

## PR-332 - THE ROW STEP HAS TWO PATHS AND THE EMPTY ANSWER TAKES THE CLOCK
## COMPARE: A `Wait` CLAUSE MATCHES OR THE STEP RETURNS WITHOUT ADMITTING,
## AND K_ANY / K_NEVER ARE MASKS WHOSE MEANING IS THE MODE BYTE'S
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the branch structure of the engine's row step 0x521f0, the
  empty test 0x495b0 it runs on the row node's answer, and the two
  special names in the clause resolver 0x48000. It settles the question
  OI-111 opened - which of the two paths a row with a `Wait` tail takes
  - and it is the reading that ported/ll_play.c's player row clock
  (section 7 of player_iterate) and PR-287's object-side gate
  ll_mov_row_gate in ll_level.c both have to answer before the
  row-driven states of HANDOFF section 8 T5's exit thread can be
  trusted. No code changed here; this record is the ground the next
  step ports.

  0x52229, 0x5222c, 0x5222f, 0x52233, 0x52235, 0x52238, 0x5223c,

  0x522bc, 0x522c1, 0x522de, 0x522e2, 0x522e6, 0x522eb, 0x522ed,
