  0x5232b, 0x5232d, 0x52334, 0x52336, 0x52338, 0x5233b, 0x52341,
  0x52347, 0x5234a, 0x52354, 0x520c0, 0x495b0, 0x495bd, 0x495c7,
  0x495ce, 0x495d5, 0x49580, 0x47e40, 0x47e4b, 0x47e5b, 0x47e63,
  0x47edc, 0x47f42, 0x47fb2, 0x47fd8, 0x48000, 0x48010, 0x48020,
  0x48029, 0x48032, 0x48037, 0x4803d, 0x48048, 0x4804f, 0x48056,
  0x48066, 0x4806f, 0x48075, 0x4807d, 0x49543, 0x45970, 0x45981,
  0x45986, 0x4598f, 0x749a0, 0x76a69, 0x919ca, 0x919ec, 0x919f5,
  0x919fb, 0x91a06, 0x2e, 0x44, 0x95, 0xa1, 0xa0, 0xa4, 0x60,
  0x6c, 0x8, 0xc, 0x10, 0x18, 0x2001f8, 0x60
NAMES: TEventSet::match, ll_mov_row_gate, K_ANY, K_NEVER, AC_K_ANY,
  AC_K_NEVER, AC_TIME, K_GEN1, K_UP, K_DOWN, WAIT, LL_GOP_ANY,
  ll_mov_fr, gsig_id, gop, player_iterate, OI-111, OI-112, F6, T5
CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. The port step this
  grounds is named in OPENS; the reading is load-bearing for it, so it
  is written to the register in the same commit (OI-111).
HOOKS: none - no code, so nothing to hook.
MEASURED: (a) THE QUESTION IS DECIDED BY THREE INSTRUCTIONS. The row
  step 0x521f0 zeroes [obj+0x95] at 0x52217, takes the row node at
  [ebp+0x2e][[ebp+0x4]*4] (0x52221-0x5222c), calls its test slot
  +0x8 with edx = a 12-byte scratch set (0x52235), then calls 0x495b0
  on that set (0x5223c). 0x495b0 walks the three DATA dwords: any one
  non-zero jumps 0x495ce and returns 0; all three zero leaves eax at 12
  (0x495bd-0x495d5). Back at 0x52241: `test eax,eax / sete al / and
  eax,0xff / je 0x522fc`. The `sete` is the whole point: sete AL
  writes 1 exactly when the flags say EQUAL, i.e. when 0x495b0
  returned 0, and `and eax,0xff` then makes ZF the test of that byte
  - so `je` fires when 0x495b0 returned NON-ZERO, which is the EMPTY
  set. The clause-LESS row is the one that reaches 0x522fc. PR-218
  wrote this the other way round in OI-111's notes and PR-219
  repeated it there.
  (b) THE CLAUSE-LESS PATH, 0x522fc-0x52351, IS THE CLOCK PATH. It
  runs the node's execute slot +0xc (0x52303), OR-s the returned set
  into the caller's set through 0x49580 (0x5230c), calls the class verb
  [edx+0xa0] (0x52317), then compares the node's authored threshold
  [ebx+0x10] against the object's clock [obj+0xa1]: `cmp eax,ebx / jge
  0x52354` at 0x52320-0x5232b, so the row admits only when the
  threshold is BELOW the clock, and the budget handed on is the
  difference - `sub ebx,eax` at 0x52334 - passed in edx to the record
  verb [esi+0x18] (0x52338; esi = [ebp+0x44], the row-record class -
  PR-219 named 0x520c0 as that verb, the one that writes [obj+0xa1]
  from the budget). Then the class verb [edx+0xa4] (0x52341) and
  [obj+0x95] = 1 (0x5234a): that flag is the step's admit report, and
  it is the only writer of it in this body.
  (c) THE CLAUSE PATH, 0x52251-0x522fa, HAS NO CLOCK IN IT. It copies
  the caller's EventSet - 12 data bytes by `rep movs` and the MODE byte
  from [set+0xc] (0x52255-0x52278) - then the object's own [obj+0x60]
  with its mode from [obj+0x6c] (0x52279-0x522a6), merges the two with
  0x49580 (0x522bc), and calls TEventSet::match 0x47e40 at 0x522e6
  with eax = the node's answer and edx = that union. 0x47e4b reads the
  MODE byte from [eax+0xc] - the CLAUSE's own mode, the byte the clause
  parser wrote from the `!`/`*`/`|` prefix (PR-218) - and jumps the
  table at 0x47e30: mode 0 subset 0x47e63, 1 shares-nothing 0x47edc, 2
  identical 0x47fb2, 3 shares-anything 0x47f42, above 3 the error arm
  0x47fd8 whose string is 0x919ca, the source of the method's name. A
  NO answer takes `je 0x52354` at 0x522ed and leaves the whole step: no
  execute slot, no clock compare, no budget, no [obj+0x95]. A YES
  answer takes `xor ebx,ebx` at 0x522f8 and `jmp 0x52338` - the row
  runs, with a ZERO budget, and the threshold compare at 0x52329 is
  never reached. That is PR-287's unmodelled half, byte-exact: a gated
  row ignores its threshold.
  (d) THE NODE'S ANSWER IS ITS CLAUSE. 0x45970 copies 12 bytes from
  [node+0x8] plus the mode byte at [node+0x8+0xc] (0x45981-0x4598f)
  and never calls the operand, so the answer is empty exactly when the
  clause carries no bits. On the shipped texts that happens once, the
  tokenless `Wait ;` (PR-218's census), and it means "no gate".
  (e) THE TWO SPECIAL NAMES ARE BIT MASKS; THE MODE BYTE IS THE
  MEANING. The resolver 0x48000 compares the token through 0x76a69
  against 0x919ec AC_K_ANY and 0x919f5 K_ANY (0x48010-0x48027) and on
  a hit zeroes the set with 0x749a0 then OR-s 0x2001f8 into DATA DWORD
  1 (0x48037-0x48048); against 0x919fb AC_K_NEVER and 0x91a06 K_NEVER
  (0x4804f-0x4806d) and on a hit OR-s 0x60 into DATA BYTE 4
  (0x4806f-0x4807d). Both return 1 through 0x49543, and both leave a
  NON-EMPTY set, so both take the clause path of (c) - a `Wait` with
  either name is never the plain path. PR-263's masks and their
  attribution stand; what is new is what they are. In this port's
  verified bit indexes 0x2001f8 in dword 1 is bits 35,36,37,38,39,40 -
  K_BKWD, K_FWD, K_UP, K_DOWN, K_FIRE, K_ALT - plus bit 53, and 0x60
  in byte 4 is bits 37 and 38 = K_UP and K_DOWN together. Read with
  the plain subset arm, K_ANY means all six arrows at once and
  K_NEVER means UP and DOWN held together: both, in play, never -
  which is why an author writes `WAIT K_NEVER` to park a state. Read
  with the `|` arm, K_ANY is simply "an arrow is held", and with `!`,
  K_NEVER is "neither arrow". So the name does not decide whether the
  row admits: the clause's mode byte does, and the port's
  LL_GOP_ANY-style reading of these two names as always/never is a
  shortcut, not the engine's rule.
  (f) THE BLAST RADIUS, COUNTED. Over the 777 extracted .MOV texts,
  using PR-330's row-line test: 203 row lines carry a `WAIT` tail, in
  124 of the files. By operand: K_NEVER 115, K_GEN1 24, AC_DUP 19,
  AC_TIME 15, `!K_UP` 7, `!K_DOWN` 7, `!AC_ENEMY_ATC` 7, K_GEN2 2,
  AC_START 2, `K_NEVER ;` 2, AC_BECZKA 1, AC_BUTLA 1, K_BKWD 1. The
  K_NEVER rows are NOT written as zero-threshold stops: their second
  field is 200 in 26 of them, 1000 in 18, 1500 in 15, 0 in 33, 500 and
  100 in 6 each, 300 in 4, 5000 in 3, 400 in 2, 4 in 1, 10000 in 1 -
  the author is writing a hold, and under (c) the hold is indefinite:
  the row never admits and the list never moves. 170 of the 203 carry
  a non-zero threshold, which is exactly the set where PR-287's
  threshold-skip gap and a faithful clock path differ. And none of it
  reaches the LION today: ll_play.c section 7 compares the threshold
  with `row_t` and never calls ll_mov_row_gate, so all 203 run
  ungated for the player.

  18,40;80,40`, `1 -80,45;-18,45`, `1 -80,45;-18,45`. Placed: the

  surface, under nothing - and the palms' seats are 838..900 at
  y 475, 885..947 at y 380 and 930..992 at y 320, a rising chain

  (c) THE TABLE GRAMMAR, 0x45120, BYTE FOR BYTE: "%d" (0x9182d)
  reads N; the allocation at 0x45149-0x4515a is (N+1)*0xd + 4
  bytes - N+1 records of 13, the 13-byte record of PR-312's
  0x45400, x at +0, y at +4, flag byte at +0xc; the loop at
  0x4517e runs while a counter sits at or below N, i.e. N+1 times,
  each record parsed "%d,%d" (0x91836/0x91839) and after EACH
  record ONE character read with " %c" (0x91830), which decides
  that record's flag byte: ';' (0x3b) stores flag 1 and continues
  (0x451a6-0x451be), '#' (0x23) stores flag 2 and ends
  (0x451cf-0x451e0), any other character stores flag 0 and ends.
  So `1 7,45;40,45 -6300,-1350` is exactly TWO records - (307,633)
  flagged 1, (340,633) flagged 0 - and the leading number is the
  record count minus one, the same "count = points - 1" fact
  PR-311 measured for .PLT lines, now with its reader named. The
  trailing `-6300,-1350` is NOT consumed by 0x45120 (the character
  after `40,45` is '-', which closes the loop with flag 0) nor by
  any other reader found here: it stays counted data, in OPENS.
  0x3dd60, the other 0x45120 caller, is another family's version:
  it stores the table at [obj+0xee], copies the FIRST record into
  [obj+0xfa]/[obj+0x100], and looks for an optional ` F = %d,
  %d \n` tail (0x91446) into [obj+0x11a]/[obj+0x11e], zeroing
  both when the match count is not exactly 2 (0x3ddbb-0x3ddd8):
  that tail appears ZERO times in the shipped containers (scan of
  ETAPY and ANIMACJE for `F = n,n` and `T = n,n`: none), so no
  shipped object carries it.
  (d) HOW A SEAT BECOMES SOMEONE'S GROUND, END TO END. 0x1e970,
  the +0x78 entry of the table 0x96d1c (PR-311's), is setup plus
  one call: eax = [kat+0xa5], ebx = a pointer to the predicted
  pair, ecx = mode 2, call 0x45320; then the empty signal
  composition (0x749a0, n=0xc, [ans+0xc]=0, the PR-296 mode) and
  return - it raises NO signal, exactly as PR-311 read. The part
  never read is what 0x45320 does first: it refreshes the
  requester's presented point (0x541f0 with a temporary of class
  0x98278, 0x45340), adds the requester's PENDING DELTA
  [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] to it (0x45349-0x4536b - the predicted
  position of PR-275's lift law), and calls 0x45400 with that
  pair. 0x45400 runs the query on the point's record list: the
  FIRST record's flag must not exceed the mode (0x4540f-0x45419 -
  the "first-entry flag vs the mode" of PR-312; mode 2 accepts
  flags 0, 1 and 2); 0x45380 finds the segment whose x span
  brackets the passed position (0x45397-0x453bd, the walk over
  13-byte records, 0x453d2 the same pair plus 0x455a0); then the
  REQUESTER's own class +0x6c verb is called (0x45439 - the
  anchor-point verb family of PR-329, 0x23a10 `add eax,0x89` for
  the lion) and 0x455a0 interpolates the segment line AT THAT
  POINT (0x4545e-0x45468) and again at the list position
  (0x45491). If the requester is not already attached to this same
  point ([actor+0xa9], 0x45471-0x4547f) a positive clearance is
  rejected; the closest non-positive gap wins over any previous
  candidate (0x4549a) and the winner is written into the REQUESTER
  as the triple PR-312 named: [actor+0xe6] = the point object
  (0x454a2), [actor+0xea] = the signed clearance (0x454a8),
  [actor+0xe2] = that record's flag byte (0x454ba). That is the
  whole "the surface may come from an ask" sentence, now read
  through: an animated platform is candidate ground for every actor
  whose state asks its class, and the rider moves by the law
  PR-312 already read at 0x54250/0x54827 - pos += [obj+0xca],
  [obj+0xce] and the [obj+0xea] snap. The seven ZARIA.01 states
  that name KATAPULT (PR-311's list) therefore receive the seat
  segment as a surface with the object's pending delta as the
  carry term: the mechanism the first chasm's crossing needs.
  (e) THE LADDER/LINA ANSWERS ARE SWITCHED ON THE LADDER'S OWN
  STATE. 0x3f1c0 (DRABINKA's +0x78, PR-147) and 0x3f390 (LINA's)
  agree instruction for instruction through everything read: first
  the requester's askable probe (class +0x3c, PR-329; refusal
  composes the inert answer, 0x3f1d1/0x3f3a1); then a switch on
  [obj+0x5c], the LADDER's own current state index - not the
  asker's. State 1, the unrolling A_UP of PR-325: the requester's
  rectangle getter (+0x4c) and the contact-point walk 0x44ec0
  against [obj+0xa5] (PR-243's gate seen from the asked side),
  and on TRUE a write to its OWN set: byte +2 of [[obj+0x64]]
  |= 0x40 - bit 22, AC_LINA_CATCH in the PR-69 numbering
  (0x3f203/0x3f3d3). State 2, A_DOWN, "the only state that
  answers the lion" (PR-325): first the requester's PRESENTED
  POINT (class +0x68, PR-329) is tested against the object at
  [obj+0xc5] (0x3f222-0x3f230); TRUE raises AC_EDGE, bit 8, into
  the answer (0x3f24d) - the authored raiser of the AC_EDGE that
  `A_PODCIAG(1)=AC_EDGE,K_UP` needs, raised from the LADDER's
  state exactly as PR-271 measured in play. FALSE falls to the
  band arm: [obj+0xb1..0xbd] (the entry's own rectangle, paragraph
  (a)) into a temporary of class 0x98274 - the same temporary
  family as 0x4a050's in PR-329 - with the point selector 0x46
  (LINA: 0x32, 0x3f448), and a hit runs the P3+ tail (0x3f2a4):
  the requester's +0x8 verb, then the answer carries
  AC_DRAB|AC_DRAB_CATCH - or dh,0x10 and or bh,0x4, bits 12 and
  10, the PR-271 pair - merged through 0x49580 and copied as the
  12-byte answer (0x3f313-0x3f331: three dwords plus the +0xc
  mode byte, the TEventSet of PR-332). What is NOT in this answer:
  no surface triple travels on it - the ladder answer raises
  signals only. PR-282's hunt for "the writer that moves the rider
  up the column" therefore does not end inside 0x3f1c0: the only
  position-moving ask channel in the image is the (d) chain.
  (f) WHAT THIS SETTLES FOR THE PORT. The LINA scope the port
  pinned as a leg (ladder_class's L3 class-scope case, PR-270:
  DRABINKA 1, LINA 0, "the K-prefixed variants stay unanswered")
  is now answered as DATA: LINA owns an answer verb of the same
  shape, 0x3f390, with the same state switch, and ZARIA.01's two
  ropes author the three fields that verb consumes - so a LINA can
  raise AC_EDGE, AC_DRAB and AC_DRAB_CATCH at its own band, and
  the rope at 525,525 with rectangle 546,555;554,645 stands INSIDE
  the first chasm's x span (408..624), with the canopy line
  `5 98,514;288,520;379,503;453,504;539,536;589,566` over it: the
  video's "up the ladder, mid-canopy east" route has a second,
  authored version through a rope the port refuses to answer. The
  ANIPL2 seat lines are not ground in the port at all (ll_level
  counts the four lines as "polyline data (moving ground: needs
  the AC_* signal bus)") - paragraphs (b)-(d) name the three
  pieces to port: the table parse with its flag bytes and the
  0x45200 translation, the ask verb's predicted-position insert,
  and the triple write. And the port's two-block A_UP/A_DOWN model
  (ladder_answer_core) now has its engine switch named: the arms
  are chosen by the ladder's own [obj+0x5c], which the port's
  obj_transition already runs for drab.mov.
  (g) THE FOUR SHIPPED NEGATIVES, COUNTED. The '#' flag-2
  separator appears in no shipped entry text (scan of ETAPY for
  ';' in entry lines: none); the ` F = n,n` tail appears nowhere
  (both containers); a trailing pair after a table line appears
  exactly once in the whole shipped set - the KATAPULT's
  -6300,-1350 - unread by any found consumer; and the animated-
  platform set itself: ZARIA.01's four entries are the only
  seat-line tables in the fixture's levels that any lion state
  names. These bound the port step: flags 0/1 and the two-point
  segment can be implemented without inventing anything, and the
  trailing pair stays counted, unacted data.
OPENS: what consumes `-6300,-1350` after 0x45120 leaves the rest
  pointer at it - and whether the pad moves at all: kat.mov authors
  A_RUN `1,0,WAIT K_GEN1` then nine 300-unit rows with NO motion
  word, so the cat's motion is that pair, or the .SEQ art frames
  through the frame-step verb 0x53df0 (which copies the position
  to the [obj+0x89] anchor and runs the .MOV step), or nothing -
  read the 0x1e560/0x1e638 tails; 0x45200's dx,dy source at
  0x1e521-0x1e52a (is the table stored absolute by the placement,
  or kept relative and placed at query time through the +0x6c
  provider?); the point class 0x98278's +0x6c verb 0x54910 and
  +0xb0 verb 0x41180; the exact derivation of the [obj+0xc5] box
  from the bare pair (0x3f159-0x3f175: the -0x50 side and the
  equal-dword corners) and the point selectors 0x46 vs 0x32 (70 /
  50 - which authored point each names); LINA's 0x3f426-0x3f54a
  tail, including the 0x3f4ac arm PR-244 named for AC_LINA bit 21,
  and the object at [obj+0xc5] with its +0x8 probe verb; the
  semantics of the record flag byte inside queries beyond the
  first-entry mode compare (0x45417) - PR-312's "a kind-2 surface
  is ignored while [obj+0xc6] < 0x58c" against flags 0/1/2; the
  remaining 0x45120 callers (0x288d5 inside the WSPRECT answer
  0x287a0 - a box class building a table at runtime - and
  0x3efe0), and the other 0x3dd60 families (0x2783c, 0x27d18,
  0x34477, 0x346a6) including whether the platformy= .PLT lines
  reach 0x45120 too (PR-279's "one surface-table object per line"
  says yes, unverified here); and the K-prefixed climbable
  variants KLINA/KDRABINA, whose answer verbs stay unanchored.
CLOSES: nothing. It grounds the OI-072 port half (the parse + ask
  + triple chain of (b)-(d)) and the LINA scope of the climb chain
  ((f)), and narrows PR-282's lift hunt to one answer: the ladder
  answer moves nothing, so the (d) chain is the only moving
  ask-surface in the image.
CORRECTS: PR-311's "each entry's polyline points are RELATIVE to
  the placement point" - the table is parsed INTO the object's own
  point [obj+0xa5] and translated by 0x45200 at parse time (the
  dx,dy source stays in OPENS), not left relative; PR-311's "it
  registers the asker in its contact list and raises NO signal" -
  the no-signal half stands, but what 0x45320 does with the asker
  is write the surface triple into it (the (d) chain), and the
  platform's physics then acts on the asker's position through the
  attach law, not through a list; and the port's own load-log
  framing of the ANIPL2 lines as "moving ground: needs the AC_*
  signal bus" - they are the object's OWN surface tables and no
  signal bus is involved in their query at all.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no red
  leg is owed and no suite run; the last full no-Windows suite run
  is PR-333's, rc=0 with 71 green verdict lines.

## PR-335 - THE ENTRY'S OWN SURFACE TABLE IS A GRAMMAR, NOT NOISE: THE
## SEPARATOR IS THE PRECEDING RECORD'S FLAG BYTE, THE COUNT ALONE ENDS THE
## LOOP, AND 0x45200 AT 0x1e52a MAKES EVERY RECORD ABSOLUTE WITH ITS OBJECT
```
KIND: port
SUBSYSTEM: place_seat_table in ported/ll_level.c and the fields it

CODE: yes: one new reader (place_seat_table, 85 lines, 112 with its
  comment), four new lvl_obj fields plus OBJ_MAXSEAT 24, six new
  obj_stats counters, one new hook in the continuation loop, one new
  load-report line, the reworded polyline-noise line, one new
  selftest leg (L13, 11 cases plus the ordering test), and two new

HOOKS: ./ll_level --mov-selftest runs L13; make verify-level's
  authored-scene leg greps TUNGA.11's seat-table report line
  (36 lines, 87 records) in /tmp/opencode/lv_tick8.log; every
  level's load log prints its own seat counts.
MEASURED: (a) THE LOOP, BYTE FOR BYTE - 0x45120 is not the grammar
  PR-334 recorded. `%d` (0x9182d) writes the count at [point+8]
  (0x4512c-0x4513b); count 0 jumps to the epilogue, so NO table is
  allocated (0x45141-0x45143); otherwise (N+1)*0xd+4 bytes are
  allocated (0x45149-0x4515a) and record 0's pair is read first
  (0x45169). The loop at 0x4517e runs EXACTLY N times and each pass
  reads one ` %c` (0x91830) and then one `%d,%d` pair: the character
  is the flag byte of the record that came BEFORE it - ';' 0x3b
  stores 1 (0x451a6), '#' 0x23 stores 2 (0x451d4), anything else
  stores 0 (0x451db) - and control then joins the SAME store-and-
  continue tail (0x451cf → 0x451dd → 0x451ad), so NO separator ends
  the table: only `cmp ebp,[point+8]; jg` at 0x451c9-0x451cb does.
  The last record therefore has no flag byte written at all, and the
  allocation's +4 bytes and initial contents stay unread. After the
  loop 0x451e2 asks the stream for one literal ';' (the format at
  0x91834 through 0x498f0), which is why the shipped `N x,y;..;`
  lines end clean and why ZARIA.01's `1 7,45;40,45 -6300,-1350`
  leaves its trailing pair where it is: the count says one pair
  after the first, and the literal ';' does not match a '-'. The
  parse is a stream walk, not a pointer walk: 0x49920/0x498d0 work
  on a stream object (0x498d4 reads [obj+1], 0x498d9 calls its
  vtable slot 0), which is why every call site passes the same
  register.
  (b) THE TABLE IS ABSOLUTE FROM LOAD, AND IT MOVES. The record verb
  calls 0x45200 right after the parse with edx = [obj+0] and
  ebx = [obj+4] (0x1e521-0x1e52a) - the placement itself, which
  closes PR-334's open question about that pair's source - and
  0x45217-0x4521a adds that pair to EVERY record, count+1 of them
  (the loop at 0x45225 runs while edx <= [point+8]). So the seat
  lines are stored exactly like the ladder's contact points
  (PR-246's law), not kept relative. The same verb is also the
  runtime step: 0x1e5c0 reads the current state record's field +4
  (0x1e5da-0x1e5e0), takes +1 when it is below 7 and -1 otherwise,
  and calls 0x45200(point, 0, ±1) at 0x1e5f6 - the platform's seat
  walks one pixel a tick vertically, and 0x1e585-0x1e596 shows the
  same verb family asking its own surface (the state field compared
  with 0xd, then 0x45320 with mode 2).
  (c) WHAT THE SHIPPED DATA HOLDS. FIRST THROUGH THIS READER: 147
  table lines in 15 .des files of 9 levels; 309 records stored
  absolute; 1 line with text after its records; 0 over the cap, 0
  stale counts, 0 zero-count entry continuations. Per level:
  ENA2 PLAT.DES 25/50, KADMAR.07 4 files 1/2 each, KADMAR2
  PLAT1.DES 4/8, KARA.07 ANIPL2.DES 7/14, LONA.05 ANIPL2 32/64 +
  ANIPL22 5/10 + ANIPL3 11/22, TUNGA.11 ANIPL1 36/87, TUNGA2.12
  ZWIERZ 6/12 + ANIM 11/22, ZARIA.01 ANIPL2 4/8, ZARIA.02 ANIPL2
  2/4. Those lines were noise before this PR: the same load runs
  counted them as polyline lines at HEAD and count them now -
  ZARIA.01 4 → 0, TUNGA.11 44 → 8, LONA.05 41 → 4, ENA2 37 → 12,
  TUNGA2.12 35 → 18. THEN WITH A RAW SCANNER, over all 103 dumped
  .des members and sorted by the line that stands IN FRONT of it:
  338 lines have this shape. 154 follow an entry line - this reader
  takes 147 and the other 7 hang off entries authored at 0,0 that
  PR-93 does not instantiate (ENA2 PLAT.DES's six EBECZKA barrels,
  TUNGA2.12 ZWIERZ.DES's GORYL); 150 continue another table line
  and 3 start right after a bare count line, so no record verb
  owns them (KADMAR2 ANI1's `76` then 76 `0 x,y;` rows, TUNGA2.12
  PLATF.DES's `66`, SADES.06 PLATF.DES's `8`); 23 follow a
  per-entry property line - `bounds=` (KARA.07 ANIPL2, 7),

  pair FEWER than their count asks for (count + 1): LONA.05 ANI3's

  is TUNGA.11 ANIPL1's `3 0,0;30,0;63,-1;135,10;`, 4 records.
  Separators in that text: ';' 467, '!' 11 (all of them LONA.05

  the engine owns and no shipped object uses.
  (d) ZARIA.01, MEASURED. The four ANIPL2 entries are read: the
  KATAPULT pad is the segment (307,633)-(340,633), and the PALMA
  seats are (838,475)-(900,475), (885,380)-(947,380) and
  (930,320)-(992,320) - a rising chain whose top
  ends 28 px short of the level's authored exit x = 1020, so the
  chain reaches the exit column only if the seat also MOVES while
  the lion stands on it, which is what (b)'s (0,±1) step is for.
  (e) THE LEGS AND THEIR MUTATIONS. L13 holds eleven cases: ten

  authored positions (the three ZARIA.01 seats above, ZARIA.02's

  Where something is a fixture rather than shipped data, the case
  says so - the zero-count line's placement (that block hangs off a
  count line, so it belongs to no entry) and the third case of the
  ordering test. That test is the order of the four continuation
  grammars: `1 33,-3` and `1 0,200` are ZARIA.01 ANI2's DRABINKA
  and LINA lists and must reach place_points, never the table

  count of 0 author one record; not consuming the literal ';' of

  (f) THE NEGATIVES, COUNTED. No play behaviour changed: no surface

OPENS: whether a property line cuts a record at all - 23 shipped
  table lines sit behind `bounds=`/`koniec=`/`R=`/`frame=` words,

  port reads a continuation only while such lines run on directly:

  asker's presented point, adds [actor+0xca]/[+0xce] and calls

  flag byte's meaning inside the query (0x45417's first-record mode

  tokens use it; and whether a seat's own object position ([obj+0])

  placement only at load; the runtime calls pass (0,±1), so a
  horizontally moving platform must move its records some other way
  - read 0x1e638/0x1e6ce/0x1e733/0x1e798/0x1e803/0x1e896).
CLOSES: nothing. It lands the parse half of OI-072 and narrows that

  F6c exit leg of HANDOFF section 8 T5 needs; and it closes
  PR-334's open question about 0x45200's dx,dy source.
CORRECTS: PR-334's reading of 0x45120, in three parts. (i) "';'
  stores flag 1 and continues, '#' stores flag 2 and ends, any other
  character stores flag 0 and ends" - nothing ends the loop; the
  count does (0x451c9). So `1 -5,0!67,0` is a two-record table with
  flag 0 on the first record, not a one-record table with a trailing
  pair. (ii) the flag byte belongs to the record the separator
  FOLLOWS, and the final record carries no flag at all - PR-334
  wrote the KATAPULT pad as "(307,633) flagged 1, (340,633) flagged
  0", which is wrong twice over. (iii) the trailing pair survives
  because the count is 1 and 0x451e2's literal ';' does not match
  it, not because the loop stopped early. It also corrects the
  geometry PR-334 put in the HANDOFF F6 paragraph: no PALMA seat
  "spans the 64 px exit hole" - measured, the seats are
  838..900/475, 885..947/380 and 930..992/320, and the top one
  stops 28 px short of the exit column at x 1020. And the port's
  own load-log phrase for these lines, "moving ground: needs the
  AC_* signal bus", is replaced: they are the object's own surface
  tables and no signal bus is involved.

HOOKS: none. Every claim below is machine code, the full-image

MEASURED: (a) THE TWO SEAT ASK VERBS RAISE NOTHING. 0x1e970 is six
  instructions of setup - `mov [esp],edx`, `mov edx,ebx` (the
  requester), `mov ebx,0x2` (the mode), `add eax,0xa5`,
  `xor ecx,ecx`, `call 0x45320` - and then the empty answer:
  `xor edx,eax`, `mov ebx,0xc`, `mov BYTE PTR [ans+0xc],0`,
  `call 0x749a0` (0x1e98a-0x1e99a): the PR-332 TEventSet with no
  bit set. 0x1e570 ends the same way at 0x1e59b-0x1e5ab. A seat
  answer carries NO signal; its whole output is the triple of
  paragraph (c). 0x1e570's only test is on the state record:
  `ebx = [[obj+0x50] + [obj+0x5c]*4]`, `mov ebx,[ebx+4]`,
  `cmp ebx,0xd`, `jge` skips the ask (0x1e577-0x1e588). [[rec]+4]
  is that state's ROW CURSOR, the same field the `( N )` of a
  transition writes (PR-157/PR-181): the seat answers only while
  its state has run fewer than 13 rows.
  (b) WHAT 0x45320 PUTS ON THE TABLE. eax = the seat list
  [obj+0xa5], edx = the requester, ebx = the mode; the callee pops
  one stack slot (`ret 0x4`, 0x454c6) that the caller pushes at
  0x45348. First 0x541f0 with a three-dword block whose third
  dword is the point class 0x98278: 0x541f0 writes [edx] = [obj+0]
  and [edx+4] = [obj+4] - the requester's OWN position, not a
  stored presented point - and then, when [obj+0xb6] bit 2 is clear
  and its class +0xbc verb answers 0 and bit 1 is clear, runs the
  layer path +0x48 -> +0x50 -> [[+0x33]+0x4] (0x54209-0x5423a),
  the same unmodelled transform PR-329 named. Then
  0x45349-0x4536b adds [requester+0xca]/[+0xce] to that pair - the
  integer step of the velocity register, PR-99's /100 output - and
  hands 0x45400 the pair twice: as a pointer, `lea ebx,[esp+0x4]`,
  and again through the caller's own slot, which 0x45400 reads at
  0x4546d as `mov edx,[esp+0x18]` (the callee frame puts that
  offset exactly on the caller's second pair dword).
  (c) 0x45400, EVERY TEST IN ORDER, ITS ONLY CALL SITE IN THE IMAGE
  (0x4536f). 0x4540f-0x45419 loads BYTE [rec[0]+0xc], `and 0xff`,
  `cmp eax,ecx`, `jg` -> answer nothing: the mode gate reads the
  FIRST record's flag byte only, never the candidate segment's;
  mode 2 accepts 0, 1 and 2. 0x45380 (called 0x45423) is the x
  bracket: count 0 -> nothing; pos.x < rec[0].x -> nothing;
  pos.x > rec[count].x -> nothing; else the first k in 1..count
  with rec[k].x >= pos.x, returned as k - a table whose first x
  exceeds its last can never bracket, and a one-record table is
  never a segment. 0x45434-0x45439 calls [[requester+8]+0x6c], the
  REQUESTER's anchor verb (0x23a10 `add eax,0x89` for the lion,
  PR-329); the class +0x14 verb 0x53df0 is what fills that block:
  `esi = obj+0x89; [esi] = [obj]; [esi+4] = [obj+4]` plus the same
  layer path - the anchor IS a copy of the object's own position.
  0x455a0 is the line evaluator, and its arithmetic is exact:
  `(pos.x-p0.x)*(p1.y-p0.y)/(p1.x-p0.x)` with `sar edx,0x1f` +
  `idiv` as the truncating-divide pair, then `+ p0.y - pos.y` -
  the segment's y at pos.x minus pos.y, a signed clearance,
  negative when the segment is ABOVE the point (y grows downward).
  It runs TWICE: 0x45468 on the ANCHOR, 0x45491 on the passed PAIR.
  The first result is a gate only; the second is the answer. The
  gate, 0x45477-0x4547f: `eax = clearance_at_anchor - pair.y`;
  skipped when [requester+0xa9] is this very point object;
  otherwise negative -> answer nothing. Then 0x45496 rejects a
  clearance POSITIVE at the pair and 0x4549a rejects anything
  GREATER than the stored [requester+0xea] - so among the surfaces
  at or above the predicted position the one FARTHEST above wins,
  not the closest. 0x454a2-0x454ba write [requester+0xe6] = the
  point object, [requester+0xea] = that clearance, [requester+0xe2]
  = rec[k-1]'s flag byte. The consumer PR-312 named,
  0x54804-0x5482d, adds [obj+0xca] to x and [obj+0xce]+[obj+0xea]
  to y and zeroes +0xea/+0xca/+0xce: since the clearance was taken
  at the predicted position, pos.y + dy + clearance = seg_y, so the
  law lands the POSITION POINT exactly on the seat line.
  (d) THAT GATE CANNOT PASS AT SHIPPED COORDINATES. 0x53df0 makes
  anchor.y = pos.y and the pair is pos.y + [obj+0xce], so the test
  is `seg_y_at(pos.x) >= 2*pos.y + [obj+0xce]` - a y delta
  compared against an absolute world y. Measured on ZARIA.01's four
  shipped seats, a new attach needs pos.y <= 316 for the KATAPULT
  pad at y 633, <= 237 for the PALMA at 475, <= 190 for 380, <=
  160 for 320; the lion on the west ground sits at pos.y 622-654
  (the ground is y 680-684, the shape-bottom contact is 30-58 px,
  PR-97). So 0x45400 rejects the lion at every position that level
  can put him in. And the exemption closes on itself: over the full
  instruction index the ONLY writer of [actor+0xe6] is 0x454a2,
  inside 0x45400; [actor+0xa9] is written from +0xe6 at
  0x5478e/0x547bc, cleared at 0x547f0/0x54e6a/0x1f8e9, and written
  from anything else at exactly one place - 0x54624, the verb
  0x54560's case `[arg+4] == 0x1b`, whose payload dword [arg+8] IS
  the surface object it stores: 0x5460e first calls the held
  surface's +0x4 (detach), stores [arg+8], and if non-null calls
  its +0x0 (attach). 0x54560 is a standard slot - 87 class tables
  hold it at +0x88, KATAPULT's 0x96d1c among them - and it is
  reached through the message dispatch 0x53480, which calls
  [class+0x88] when [class+0x84] finds no handler for the message
  NAME (0x5348d-0x534ab). Who sets `[arg+4] = 0x1b` is not in the
  image: the only memory stores of 0x1b are 0x4a1fd, which writes
  it to `[ebp+8]` as a PAYLOAD with `[ebp+4] = 0` before posting a
  named message (eax = 0xcf1a8, call 0x5b8f0), and 0x54ec8, which
  builds the block {0, 0x1b, 0, 0} for the class +0x10 verb - a
  third opcode namespace, the same slot 0x1e5c0's {0, 1, 0, +-1}
  block uses. The `mov edx,0x1b` at 0x1ea47/0x1ead1 is the SIGNAL
  poster 0x52b10, another namespace again (27 = AC_BUTLA, 13 =
  AC_DUP_CD). So either that message arrives from a poster this
  pass did not find, or the seat-ask chain is dead in the shipped
  set.
  (e) THE BRACKET LAW OVER THE SHIPPED TABLES: 153 lines of the
  dumped .des set follow an entry line and match 0x45120's grammar
  EXACTLY - count, one pair, then count passes of one separator
  character and one pair - and EVERY one of the 153 is x-ascending,
  so 0x45380's endpoint gate never fails and no shipped table is a
  single record. First-record flag byte: 142 are flag 1 (a ';'
  follows record 0), 11 are flag 0, none is flag 2: over all 153
  lines the separator characters are 157 ';' and 11 '!' and no '#'
  at all, so the '#' branch at 0x451d4 is dead in the shipped set
  and the 11 '!' lines - all of them LONA.05 ANIPL3's
  `1 -5,0!67,0` - take the "any other character" branch at 0x451db
  and store 0, which is what PR-335's reader does. The literal ';'
  that 0x451e2 asks for is present on 59 of the 153 lines and
  absent from 93; its
  return value is never tested (0x451e8 is followed only by
  `add esp,8`), so an absent terminator costs nothing and leaves
  the stream on that character. Per entry token: MOVEPLAT 48, KRA1
  21, CEBRZYK 11, TMPLAT 10, TWINDA 10, KATPLAT 8, KRA2 8, EBECZKA
  6, KGARNEK 5, PTAKPLAT 5, KRA0 3, PALMA 3, PIASEK 2, KWINDA 2,
  and CAMEL, ZOLW, faraon, winda, schody, mach_a, ZAPADNIA, GEJZER,
  KATAPULT, BRANCH, TREE one each. This counts the GRAMMAR in all
  103 members; PR-335's 147 is what this port's reader reaches, and
  the difference is the property-line cut and the 0,0 entries it
  already named.
  (f) THE TRAILING PAIR IS READ DATA. 0x1e630, 0x45120's third
  caller, is 0x45120 on [obj+0xa5] (0x1e640), then 0x45200 with the
  object's own coordinates (0x1e64c), then `lea eax,[obj+0xb1]`,
  `call 0x4a0b0` (0x1e651-0x1e659) - the pair reader, "%d,%d"
  (0x91d0f) then the optional literal " , " (0x91d15) - storing
  into [obj+0xb1]/[obj+0xb5]. 0x45120 leaves the stream exactly
  there: 0x498f0's failed literal match consumes nothing. Of all
  153 lines exactly ONE carries such text, ZARIA.01 ANIPL2's
  `1 7,45;40,45 -6300,-1350`, so that pair is -6300,-1350, i.e.
  -63 and -13.5 px per iteration in the 1/100 scale of PR-99's
  velocity register. Which class reads it for KATAPULT is OPENS (1).
  (g) THE SEAT'S OWN MOVE STEP, AND THE ROW CURSOR THAT DRIVES IT.
  0x1e5c0: `eax = [[obj+0x50] + [obj+0x5c]*4]`, `eax = [eax+4]`,
  `cmp eax,7` -> esi = +1 below 7 and -1 at or above
  (0x1e5ca-0x1e5e9); then 0x45200([obj+0xa5], edx = 0, ebx = +-1)
  (0x1e5ee-0x1e5f8) shifts EVERY record of the seat table by
  (0,+-1); then when [obj+0xb1] is non-null, [[obj+0xb1]+8]+0x10
  runs with the four-dword block {0, 1, 0, +-1} (0x1e5fd-0x1e624),
  the same block shape 0x1e4e0 builds for the class +0x4 verb of
  0x98278 - the element is moved by the same delta as its own
  surface. Measured over the dumped .mov texts of the 22 of the 25
  tokens of paragraph (e) that have a .mov in that set - a row
  being a line that starts with an integer
  (negative row numbers count: ZARIA.01 PALMA PALML is numbered
  -1..-14) and a comma: ENA2 MOVEPLAT's A_RUN states are 28 rows
  (7 of +1 then 21 of -1, ask off from row 13) and WINDA2's 33
  rows (7 of +1, 26 of -1); TUNGA.11 MOVEPLAT's ED000001..7 pair
  A_MOVE_DN and A_MOVE_UP with 5 rows each, which never reach 7,
  so BOTH move +1 and the authored up/down distinction cannot come
  from this gate; ZARIA.01 KATAPULT's only state A_RUN is 10 rows
  BY_TIME (7 of +1, then 3 of -1, its ask stays on all cycle) and
  ZARIA.01 PALMA's PALM and PALML are both 14-row A_RUN BY_TIME
  (7 and 7, ask off from row 13). And over those 22 tokens' 290
  shipped states, not one carries the SOLID flag in its `flags=`
  line - so PR-92's solid push-out never puts the lion on one of
  these objects either. That is the third independent reason the
  F6c crossing cannot run through a path the port already has: the
  seat objects are not SOLID, the ask chain's own gate rejects the
  lion at shipped coordinates, and KATAPULT and PALMA's shipped
  class tables hold no seat verb.
  (h) THE SEAT VERBS DO HAVE A CLASS FAMILY - AND NO SHIPPED
  OBJECT IS BUILT FROM IT. The installer chain PR-328 used does
  name the two seat objects: 0x1fb32 compares the token at 0x90738
  ('KATAPULT'), allocates 0xc5 bytes (0x1fb42 -> 0x5c320), runs
  the base ctor 0x531f0, builds the embedded point object at
  [obj+0xa5] with 0x44fe0, zeroes [obj+0xb1]/[obj+0xb5], stores
  0x98278 at [obj+0xb9], then [obj+8] = 0x96d1c (0x1fb83),
  [obj+0xa5] = 0x96cf8 and [obj+0xc] = 0x96cf0; 0x1fc08 does the
  same for 'PALMA' (0x9074a) with size 0xb5, [obj+8] = 0x96c38
  (0x1fc3b) and [obj+0xa5] = 0x96c14. But 0x96d1c's
  +0x18/+0x78/+0xa4 are 0x23ba0 / 0x20230 / 0x53d80 and 0x96c38's
  are 0x1edb0 / 0x52570 / 0x20280: neither of the two shipped
  classes answers a seat ask. The seat verbs live in three tables
  of their own, read slot by slot - 0x95c38 has +0x18 0x1e510,
  +0x78 0x1e570, +0xa4 0x1e5c0; 0x95d1c has +0x18 0x1e630,
  +0x78 0x1e970, +0xa4 0x1e690; 0x95ddc has +0x78 0x1ea90. So
  PR-334's SLOT map holds - +0x78 is the ask, the slot 0x4b5b7
  calls with the requester in ebx - only its TABLE was wrong.
  Those three carry a family signature shared with 20 tables that
  ARE installed by immediate (0x96cdc, 0x9907c, 0x9c168 ...
  0xa1498): +0x4 0x23ea0, +0x8 0x23e00, +0x10 0x53770, +0x84
  0x23a90, +0x88 0x534c0, +0x8c 0x23a60; and 0x534c0 is no event
  verb, it allocates 0x48 and calls 0x51770. Immediately before
  0x95c38, at 0x95c1c-0x95c34, the image lays out one row of the
  surface family itself: 0x45250, 0x452d0, 0x453d0, 0x45320,
  0x45400, 0x45120. And nothing points at any of it: no dword of
  the image holds 0x95c38, 0x95d1c or 0x95ddc, no .text
  instruction loads any address of that 0x95a00-0x96000 blob as
  an immediate (the imm table filtered to prov='code' stops at
  0x95b49), the blob holds no printable byte at all, and the only
  code naming it is the guarded pair at 0x74980/0x74bb2, passing
  0x95c20 and 0x95c40 to 0x77bdc - which calls 0x7be36 and, if
  that answers 0, 0x7b8f1: the static-object init pattern, not a
  class install. Two shipped objects are built from tables with no
  seat verb, and the tables with the seat verbs are built by
  nothing the image shows.

  tables and how they get installed) and OI-123 (the poster of
  the 0x1b attach message), narrows OI-072 to exactly those two

  seat move step of 0x1e5c0 is read end to end and can be ported.

CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moved is the
  shape of F6c: the port now knows which shipped object types can

HOOKS: none. Every claim is machine code (leodb dis), the immediate
  index (imm), the call index (xref), a raw four-byte scan of
  build/leo/leo.img, or PR-335's dump of the 103 shipped .des
  members under /tmp/opencode/pr335/des.
MEASURED: (a) THE READER AND THE HEADER IT FILLS. 0x3dd60 starts
  `lea esi,[eax+0xee]` (0x3dd6a) and calls 0x45120 on that address,
  so the surface table of these objects hangs off an inline header at
  [obj+0xee], not off the seat family's point at [obj+0xa5]. The
  header's layout comes out of 0x45120 itself: 0x45136 scans the
  format at 0x9182d, `%d`, into [hdr+8] - the COUNT; 0x45143 returns
  when it is 0; 0x4514a-0x4515a sizes (count+1)*13 + 4 bytes and
  allocates through 0x76a64 and 0x76bb7; 0x45166 stores the block at
  [hdr+4]; 0x4a0b0 reads the first pair and the loop 0x45177-0x45198
  reads one separator with the format at 0x91830, ` %c`, then one
  pair at [hdr+4] + 0xd*i for i = 1..count. So [hdr+4] is the record
  block and [hdr+8] the count, records are 13 bytes with x at +0 and
  y at +4, and there are N+1 of them: PR-335's grammar, now with the
  fields it writes. 0x3dd60 then reloads [[obj+0xee]+4] (0x3dd7d)
  and copies rec[0].x and rec[0].y into [obj+0xfa] and [obj+0xfe]
  (0x3dd91-0x3dda4): the FIRST RECORD becomes the object's own
  ANCHOR PAIR. Last, 0x3ddad-0x3ddbb push [obj+0x11e], [obj+0x11a],
  the string at 0x91446 and the cursor to 0x498f0, and 0x3ddc3-0x3ddd8
  zero [obj+0x11a]/[obj+0x11e] unless exactly 2 items were read. The
  string at 0x91446 is ` F = %d, %d \n` (its bytes are 20 46 20 3d
  ... 0a 00); `F =` occurs in NO member of the shipped .des set -
  zero lines in 103 - and `f =` in none either, so on shipped data
  that clause ALWAYS takes the zero branch. (The ` f = ` variant has
  its own reader at 0x3e770, 0x49920 with the format 0x914a6 and
  0x4a0b0 into [obj+0x122]; it is a different function from the
  0x3e680 that precedes it, which ends at 0x3e76a and never calls
  0x3dd60.)
  (b) THE MOVE VERB IS A MESSAGE, NOT A ROW CURSOR. 0x3dcb0's first
  test is `cmp DWORD PTR [edx+0x4],0x1` (0x3dcbc) - the message
  block's opcode word must be 1 - and then `add eax,0xee` with
  edx = [arg+8] and ebx = [arg+0xc] to 0x45200 (0x3dcc2-0x3dccd).
  0x45200 is the translation: ebx = [hdr+8] the count (0x45209),
  eax = [hdr+4] the record block (0x45214), and per record
  `add DWORD PTR [ebx+eax],esi` and `add DWORD PTR [ebx+eax+0x4],
  edi` with ebx stepping 0xd (0x45217-0x45227) - the WHOLE surface
  moves by the message's pair. Then, if [obj+0x112] is non-null -
  the ELEMENT attached to this surface - it builds {0, 1, [arg+8],
  [arg+0xc]} on the stack and calls that element's class +0x10
  (0x3dcd2-0x3dd02), and finally tail-calls the standard event verb
  0x54560 (0x3dd06). This is the live twin of the seat move step of
  PR-336: a delta carried by a message, applied to the object's own
  table and to its element, with no row cursor in sight.
  (c) THE ASK AND THE ANCHOR READ THE SAME FIELD. 0x3df00 skips when
  the asked object IS the asker (0x3df0d); otherwise it first calls
  the asked object's own predicate at class slot +0xd8 with the
  asker in edx (0x3df16), and only when that answers non-null does
  it call 0x45320 with eax = [asked+0xee], ebx = 2 and ecx = 0
  (0x3df20-0x3df2f) - the query entry of PR-275 and PR-336, now with
  a live caller; the other path goes to 0x552e0 (0x3df3b). Its
  companion 0x3ddf0 calls 0x55070, lays {rec[0].x, rec[0].y,
  0x98278} at esp+0x18 out of the same table (0x3de04-0x3de23),
  calls the object's anchor verb [[obj+8]+0x6c] (0x3de2c), builds
  the difference between that answer and rec[0] through the 0x98278
  verb +4 (0x3de58, 0x3de8d), stores it at [obj+0x106]/[obj+0x10a]
  (0x3de9c-0x3dea1), re-places the whole table by that delta with
  0x45200 (0x3dea4-0x3deb2), and posts signal 1 to the element
  [obj+0x112] through the poster 0x52b10 with ebx = [obj+0x106] and
  ecx = [obj+0x10a] (0x3deb7-0x3ded8).
  (d) WHICH SHIPPED TYPES CARRY THOSE VERBS. The factories name an
  object with `mov edx,<name>` plus call 0x76a69 (the compare chain
  of e.g. 0x1f870, whose branches are delimited by those compares);
  this census indexes every all-caps name string in the object-name
  block (334 names, 335 compare sites) and, for each branch up to
  the next compare in the same function, reads the `mov DWORD PTR
  [...],0x9xxxx` stores and keeps the classes that hold 0x3dcb0,
  0x3dd60, 0x3ddf0 or 0x3df00 at any slot of +0x00..+0x300. 61
  branches qualify; the class pointer goes either to the object's own
  class fields as a two-view pair (PERLOPL stores 0x98078 at
  [eax+0x8] and 0x98070 at [eax+0xc]) or to three sub-object fields
  (PLATF, WINDA, KGARNEK and MOVEPLAT each store 0x9957c, 0x99558
  and 0x99550 at [eax-0xfe], [eax-0x18] and [eax-0xfa]). The
  seat-line types and what their own branch stores: 'MOVEPLAT'
  0x4e035 -> 0x99550/0x99558/0x9957c (move, anchor, ask); 'PLATF'
  0x2917e and 'WINDA' 0x2bc4b and 'KGARNEK' 0x34f87 -> the same
  three; 'KRA0' 0x3875f -> 0x9e944/0x9e94c/0x9e970 (all four);
  'KRA1' 0x387f5 -> 0x9eb6c/0x9eb74/0x9eb98; 'KRA2' 0x3888b ->
  0x9ec84/0x9ec8c; 'KWINDA' 0x34ead -> 0x9d790/0x9d798/0x9d7bc
  (all four); 'KBLOK' 0x34f43 -> 0x9df44/0x9df3c; 'LINA' 0x4e81d
  and 'DRABINKA' 0x1f8ac -> 0x97f50; 'GRABOBJL1' 0x385ff ->
  0x9e824/0x9e82c; 'PIASEK' is NOT one of them - the branch that
  stores 0x9a074/0x9a07c is
  'KOLUMNA' at 0x29729, and 'KATPLAT' 0x4e222 stores none (the
  classes at 0x4e3e2/0x4e3ec belong to 'ZWIERZ', those at
  0x4e684/0x4e68e to 'SURPRISE'). The 61, read off that run:
  A_SQUAT, BAL_RAN, BICZRECT, BRECT, CIUCHCIA, DRABINKA, FLAGA,
  FOKA, GLAZ, GPTAK_RA, GRABOBJL1, GRABOBJL2, KALAMARN, KBLOK,

  KMIOTLA, KOLUMNA, KONIK, KPAJECZ, KRA0, KRA1, KRA2, KRAB,
  KRABY, KROPLA, KROPLAS, KTRASA, KWINDA, LINA, LISC, MOVEPLAT,
  OLEJ, OSMIORNI, PERLOPL, PILAGEN, PILARYB, PLATF, POCISK2,
  RBLOK, ROZGW, SCHODY3, SCHODY4, SEP_RAN, SKALA, SKALA_A,
  SKJUMP, SURPRISE, TAB_KOLO, TAB_KOT, TABLICZKALONA, WINDA,
  WODOSPAD2, WSPRECT, WULKAN, ZWIERZ.
  (e) AND NEITHER ZARIA.01 SEAT OBJECT IS ONE OF THEM. The
  'KATAPULT' branch at 0x1fb32 and the 'PALMA' branch at 0x1fc08 of
  the factory at 0x1f870 store 0x96d1c/0x96cf8/0x96cf0 at
  [eax-0xa9]/[eax-0xc]/[eax-0xa5] (0x1fb83, 0x1fb8d, 0x1fb94) and
  0x96c38/0x96c14/0x96c0c at [eax-0x9d]/[eax]/[eax-0x99] (0x1fc3b,
  0x1fc45, 0x1fc4b), the same six again at 0x20996-0x207ff;
  scanning those six over +0x00..+0x300 finds no reader, no move,
  no anchor and no ask - the only entry they share with the
  surface census is 0x3e680, which gates on [obj+0x5c] == 1, calls
  [[x+8]+0x3c] and 0x52eb0, reads a string at [obj+0xfe] through
  0x76bcc and multiplies at 0x3e6e6: no surface access. So the
  ANIPL2 lines this port parses for ZARIA.01 - the one KATAPULT pad
  and the three PALMA spans of PR-335 - belong to two object types
  whose shipped classes never read a surface table.
  (f) THE CROSS-CHECK AGAINST THE SHIPPED DATA. Counting, in the
  103-member .des dump, the object header lines `NAME,anim,mov,x,y`
  that are followed by a counted pair line: 161 objects over 24
  tokens - MOVEPLAT 48, KRA1 21, CEBRZYK 11, TMPLAT 10, TWINDA 10,
  KATPLAT 8, KRA2 8, LINA 7, EBECZKA 6, KGARNEK 5, PTAKPLAT 5,
  DRABINKA 4, KRA0 3, PALMA 3, PIASEK 2, KWINDA 2, and CAMEL, ZOLW,
  ZAPADNIA, GEJZER, GORYL, KATAPULT, BRANCH, TREE one each. All 24
  have a factory compare site (named above), so each can be matched
  against paragraph (d): 98 of the 161 belong to types that DO carry
  the verbs (MOVEPLAT, KRA1, KRA2, LINA, KGARNEK, DRABINKA, KRA0,
  KWINDA) and 63 to types that carry none (CEBRZYK, TMPLAT, TWINDA,
  KATPLAT, EBECZKA, PTAKPLAT, PALMA, PIASEK and the eight single
  ones). ZARIA.01 is entirely in the second group.
OPENS: five gaps. One, a new row OI-124: what carries the lion
  across ZARIA.01's first chasm now that the seat-line objects of that
  level are measured to hold no surface verb - the port's walk
  (2 px a tick) and jump
  (measured vertical) cannot, and the surface machinery does not
  reach those two objects. Two: which message posts opcode 1 to the
  verbs of paragraph (b), and what [obj+0x112] is - the element
  moved by the same delta and signalled with 1 by 0x3ddf0. Three: why
  the ` F = %d, %d \n` clause exists when no shipped .des member
  contains those characters: another data set, or the engine's own
  writer. Four, NOT MEASURED HERE: whether the 0x287a0/0x288e0/
  0x3efe0/0x380d0 family and the 0x1exxx seat family of PR-336 are
  installed in any shipped branch - the census of paragraph (d) was
  run with only the four 0x3dxx verbs in its verb set, so it says
  nothing about those. Five: the three tables 0x95c38/0x95d1c/0x95ddc
  are still named by nothing (OI-122).
CLOSES: nothing. It answers OI-122's first question for the surface
  machinery as a whole - the entry points exist, and the census names

CORRECTS: PR-336's OI-122 framing that the surface machinery is
  unreachable because its tables are unnamed: the machinery has TWO
  verb families, and the one that is installed is 0x3dd60 / 0x3dcb0 /

GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no red

CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What this changes is
  which object types a future F6c leg may be written against, and it
  reopens the seat chain PR-337 closed.
HOOKS: none. Every claim is machine code (leodb dis), the call index
  (xref), the immediate index (imm), the string index (str), the aligned
  dword index (dword), or the build parameters of the index itself
  (tools/re/leodb.py, the meta table).
MEASURED: (a) THE CONVENTION THIS IMAGE MUST BE READ AT. tools/re/
  leodb.py runs objdump with `--adjust-vma=0x10000`; its meta table
  carries `text 0x10000 0x82b51`; the dword rows are built as
  (0x10000 + off, ...), the str rows as (0x10000 + m.start(), ...), and
  its `hex` subcommand reads data[va - 0x10000:]. So VA = file offset +
  0x10000 for the whole image, code included, and a 0xf000 base is wrong
  by one page. Inside the image: 0x1fb32 is `mov edx,0x90738` +
  `call 0x76a69`, and the str row for the text 'KATAPULT' sits at VA
  0x90738, i.e. at file 0x80738 - the compare immediates are VA in this
  same convention, so every other immediate the same branch writes is
  too.
  (b) WHAT THE WRONG BASE COST. 0x95d1c - 0xf000 = 0x86d1c =
  0x96d1c - 0x10000: the bytes PR-336 read as the "unnamed" table
  0x95d1c are the bytes the 'KATAPULT' branch stores at 0x1fb83 as
  0x96d1c, and the same for 0x95c38/0x96c38 (0x95c38 - 0xf000 =
  0x86c38 = 0x96c38 - 0x10000). Read at the base the installer uses,
  those views resolve the seat verbs at exactly the slots PR-336
  described: 0x96c38 +0x18 = 0x1e510, +0x78 = 0x1e570, +0xa4 =
  0x1e5c0, +0xfc = 0x1e630; 0x96d1c +0x18 = 0x1e630, +0x78 = 0x1e970,
  +0xa4 = 0x1e690. The aligned dword index gives each of those verbs
  exactly one slot: 0x1e510 at 0x96c50, 0x1e570 at 0x96cb0, 0x1e630 at
  0x96d34, 0x1e970 at 0x96d94. That also says why "which class table
  holds verb V" has no answer: 0x96d1c = 0x96c38 + 0xe4, so the class
  block is one contiguous array of code pointers and each type's stored
  class pointer is a different INDEX into it. The question that does
  have an answer is "which stored view resolves V, at which slot" -
  which is the census of paragraph (f).
  (c) THE TABLE IS AN OBJECT WITH ITS OWN CLASS. The KATAPULT branch
  allocates 0xc5 bytes (0x1fb42 `mov eax,0xc5`, 0x1fb47 `call
  0x5c320`), then 0x1fb56 `call 0x531f0`, 0x1fb5b `add eax,0xa5`,
  0x1fb60 `call 0x44fe0` - and 0x44fe0 is three stores: [hdr+4] = 0,
  [hdr+8] = 0, [hdr] = 0xa0cc0. So the surface table hangs off an
  inline header at [obj+0xa5] whose record block is [hdr+4] and whose
  count is [hdr+8] (PR-335's fields, now with their constructor), and
  its class is 0xa0cc0. The installer then overrides it with the
  per-type view: 0x1fb8d stores 0x96cf8 at [eax-0xc] with eax =
  obj + 0xb1, i.e. [obj+0xa5] (0x1fb6a did `add eax,0xb1`), and the
  PALMA branch stores 0x96c14 the same way at 0x1fc45. 0xa0cc0's verbs
  are +0x0 0x45230, +0x4 0x39d00, +0x8 0x45250, +0xc 0x452d0,
  +0x10 0x44f90, +0x14 0x453d0, +0x18 0x45320, +0x1c 0x45400,
  +0x20 0x45120; and 0x96c14, 0x96c0c, 0x96cf8, 0x96cf0 carry the same
  layout with per-type entries at +0x0/+0x4/+0x10 (0x96c14 = +0x8
  0x45250, +0xc 0x452d0, +0x14 0x453d0, +0x18 0x45320, +0x1c 0x45400,
  +0x20 0x45120). PR-335's parser and PR-336's query are therefore
  METHODS OF THE TABLE (its +0x20 and +0x18), not free functions, and
  the allocation PR-335 read at 0x4514a - (count+1)*0xd + 4 - is
  repeated inside the class at 0x45012 (`imul eax,edx,0xd`, `add
  eax,0x4`, ebx = 0xa0c64, then 0x76a64 and 0x76bb7).
  (d) EXACTLY FIVE READERS AND SIX ASKERS, OVER THREE HOMES. The call
  index gives 0x45120 five callers: 0x1e51c and 0x1e640 (inside the
  seat verbs 0x1e510 and 0x1e630, both `lea/add eax,0xa5` - the header
  at [obj+0xa5]), 0x288d5 (inside the two-instruction verb 0x288d0,
  `add eax,0xee; call 0x45120; ret`), 0x3dd72 (inside PR-337's 0x3dd60,
  [obj+0xee]) and 0x3efe9 (inside 0x3efe0, `add eax,0x44` - a THIRD
  home). 0x45320 has six: 0x1e596 (0x1e570, which first gates on the
  state record's row cursor [[rec]+4] < 13, 0x1e585), 0x1e985 (0x1e970,
  no gate), 0x2890d (0x288e0, after the class +0xd8 predicate, on
  [obj+0xee]), 0x38102 (0x380d0, after +0x3c and a gate that the
  ASKER's [obj+0x5c] is 31 or 32, 0x380e9-0x380f4, on [obj+0x44]),
  0x3df2f (PR-337's 0x3df00, on [asked+0xee]) and 0x3f028 (0x3f010,
  which requires ebx == [obj+0x3c] first, on [obj+0x44]). All six pass
  ebx = 2 and ecx = 0. 0x45200 has ten: 0x1e52a, 0x1e64c (the two seat
  readers placing the table at [obj]/[obj+4]), 0x1e5f8, 0x1e6ce,
  0x1e733, 0x1e798, 0x1e803, 0x1e896 (the seat family's runtime
  members), and PR-337's 0x3dccd and 0x3deb2.
  (e) THE FOURTH SHAPE IS NOT A TABLE. 0x28880 opens with the same
  message gate as 0x3dcb0 - `mov ebx,[edx+4]; cmp ebx,1` (0x28885) -
  and then reads [obj+0x3c], [obj+0x40], [obj+0x44], [obj+0x48], adds
  the message's [arg+8] to the first and third and its [arg+0xc] to the
  second and fourth (0x288a2-0x288b2) and stores them back: that is
  PR-328's authored rectangle, absolute at [obj+0x3c], moved by the
  same opcode-1 message protocol. A surface table and a rectangle share
  a move mechanism and nothing else; 0x3f010's ask gate (paragraph (d))
  tests `ebx == [obj+0x3c]` on the same field.
  (f) THE CORRECTED INSTALL CENSUS. Methods matter here: the old
  census scanned a fixed +0x00..+0x300 window over every table-
  looking base and used a 0xf000 base, and both mistakes inflate
  the answer. The corrected script takes the set of class views
  that shipped factory branches actually store - a factory branch
  being the code between one `mov edx,<name>` + `call 0x76a69`

  verbs only inside those. It finds 334 object-name strings and
  327 compare sites; the branches store 298 distinct class views;
  65 of the 327 branches, over 59 tokens, resolve at least one of
  the fifteen verbs. Per verb, how many of the 298 stored views
  resolve it: 0x3dcb0 201, 0x3ddf0 192, 0x3df00 147, 0x3dd60 109,
  0x288d0 11, 0x28880 9, 0x288e0 9, 0x3f010 10, 0x1e630 10,
  0x1e970 8, and 7 each for 0x1e510, 0x1e570 and 0x1e5c0; 0x380d0
  6. THE [obj+0xa5] SEAT FAMILY IS RARE AND EXPLICIT: only four
  tokens resolve it - KAMIEN (0x96a88 at +0x1c8/+0x228/+0x254/
  +0x2ac), KILOF_PL (0x96b88 at +0xc8/+0x128/+0x154/+0x1ac/
  +0x20c), PALMA (0x96c38 at +0x18/+0x78/+0xa4/+0xfc/+0x15c, the
  full set including the per-tick move 0x1e5c0) and KATAPULT
  (0x96d1c at +0x18/+0x78, reader and ungated ask only). The
  [obj+0x44] home is one-sided: 0x3efe0 is resolved by NO stored
  view, while 0x3f010's ask is installed by ten (KKULA 0x9daf8
  +0x17c, KPAJECZ 0x9da40 +0x234, KTRASA 0x9dbfc +0x78, TUNTRAS
  0x9f7b4 +0x78) - so a [obj+0x44] header is asked but never read
  from data. The rectangle pair is installed where PR-328 said:
  0x28880 on nine views (CIUCHCIA 0x99e64 +0x19c, BICZRECT
  0x99f64 +0x9c, WSPRECT 0x99ff0 +0x10) and 0x288d0/0x288e0 on
  eleven/nine (PIASEK, SCHODY4, BRECT, LISC), and the gated
  [obj+0x3c] ask 0x380d0 on six (SKJUMP 0x9ed18 +0x298, FLAGA
  0x9edd0 +0x1e0, TABLICZKALONA 0x9ee88 +0x128).
  (g) THE DATA CROSS, DONE AGAIN. Counting object headers
  `NAME,anim,mov,x,y` whose next data line is a record line, over
  the 103 dumped .DES members: 160 objects over 23 tokens
  (MOVEPLAT 48, KRA1 21, CEBRZYK 11, TMPLAT 10, TWINDA 10,
  KATPLAT 8, KRA2 8, LINA 7, EBECZKA 6, KGARNEK 5, PTAKPLAT 5,

OPENS: four gaps. One, what kind of object carries a surface table at

## PR-339 - THE SEAT ROW-CLOCK IS RUN BY THE ROW ADMIT AND THE STATE
## CHANGE, NOT BY A TICK, AND ITS SIGN IS THE ROW THRESHOLD: EVERY SHIPPED
## SEAT ROW MOVES THE TABLE DOWN 1 PX, AND KATAPULT HAS NO ROW-CLOCK AT ALL
```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the seat surface-table motion of OI-072/OI-124 - who runs the
  class +0xa4 verb, what decides how far a surface table moves, and what
  the shipped .MOV row thresholds make that. Read-only: no port code moves.
ADDRESSES: 0x1e5c0, 0x1e5c8, 0x1e5d4, 0x1e5da, 0x1e5dd, 0x1e5e2, 0x1e5e9,
  0x1e5ee, 0x1e5f8, 0x1e5fd, 0x1e605, 0x1e624, 0x1e690, 0x1e69e, 0x1e6a7,
  0x1e6aa, 0x1e6ad, 0x1e6b0, 0x1e6b6, 0x1e670, 0x1e6be, 0x1e723, 0x1e788,
  0x1e7f3, 0x1e886, 0x1e95d, 0x45200, 0x45209, 0x45214, 0x45217, 0x4521a,
  0x45225, 0x520c0, 0x52320, 0x52323, 0x52329, 0x52334, 0x52338, 0x52341,
  0x5234a, 0x52354, 0x535a0, 0x535aa, 0x535b0, 0x535b2, 0x535db, 0x535e1,
  0x535ed, 0x96a88, 0x96b88, 0x96c14, 0x96c38, 0x96cf8, 0x96d1c, 0xa0cc0,
  0xcef40, 0x394, 0xa1, 0x5c, 0x50, 0xa5, 0xbd, 0xc1, 0x10, 0xa4, 0x154,
  0x254, 0x18
NAMES: 0x1e5c0, 0x1e690, 0x45200, 0x520c0, 0x52320, 0x535a0, ROW CLOCK,
  ROW THRESHOLD, FEED ACCUMULATOR, STATE TYPE, SURFACE TABLE, TABLE MOVE,
  KATAPULT, PALMA, KAMIEN, KILOF_PL, KAT.MOV, PALM.MOV, PALML.MOV,
  A_RUN, OI-072, OI-124, OI-125, F6
CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What this changes is
  what an F6 seat leg would have to model - a 1 px per-row-admit descent
  and per-state-jump offsets, not a per-tick climb.
HOOKS: none. Every claim is machine code (leodb dis), the instruction
  index (insn, for the count of +0xa4 call sites), the call index (xref),
  the data bytes at the class views and the jump table, or the port's own
  .MOV parser run over the shipped ANIMACJE container.
MEASURED: (a) THE +0xa4 VERB HAS EXACTLY TWO RUNNERS. 0x1e5c0 and
  0x1e690 carry no call edge at all (the xref index returns nothing for
  either), so they are reached only as the object class's +0xa4 method.
  One instruction in the image calls that slot from a class-bearing
  register, `call DWORD PTR [edx+0xa4]` at 0x52341 and
  `call DWORD PTR [edi+0xa4]` at 0x535db, and both are inside named
  machinery the port already models. 0x52320-0x5235c is the row-admit
  epilogue of 0x520c0: `mov eax,[ebx+0x10]` is the CURRENT ROW'S
  THRESHOLD, `mov ebx,[edx+0xa1]` is the feed accumulator, `cmp eax,ebx;
  jge 0x52354` is the PR-115 one-row law, and the +0xa4 call sits on the
  ADMITTED branch right after the row handler at [[rec+0x44]+0x18], with
  `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x95],1` after it. 0x535a0 is the state applier the
  port already knows from PR-172:
  `mov edi,[eax+0x5c]` the current state index, `cmp esi,edi; je 0x53602`
  no change, no call, and on the changed path 0x535db calls +0xa4 before
  the new record's ENTER at [[rec+0x44]+0x1c] (0x535e1-
  0x535ea) and the state-word write `mov [ecx+0x5c],esi` (0x535ed). So a
  seat's surface moves once per admitted row and once per state change -
  never "every tick".
  (b) THE SIGN IS THE ROW THRESHOLD, NOT THE ROW POSITION. 0x1e5c0:
  0x1e5c8 reads [obj+0x5c], 0x1e5d4-0x1e5da indexes the state record
  through [obj+0x50], 0x1e5da `mov eax,[eax+0x4]` is that record's
  record-object pointer (the same chained deref 0x1e570 of PR-334 uses at
  +0x4), and the value
  compared at 0x1e5dd is the word at [[state record]+0x10], the same
  threshold the row admit reads at 0x52320, and `cmp eax,0x7` has two
  arms, `mov esi,1` (0x1e5e2) and `mov esi,-1` (0x1e5e9). esi is then
  handed to the table move in its y argument: 0x1e5ee
  `lea eax,[ecx+0xa5]`, 0x1e5f6 `mov ebx,esi`, 0x1e5f8 `call 0x45200`;
  and 0x45200 is the record loop
  0x45214-0x45227, which adds edx to each record's x at [rec+0] and ebx
  to its y at [rec+4], for [hdr+8] records at stride 0xd from [hdr+4]
  (0x45209 reads the count, 0x45225 the loop bound). The threshold word
  is the same one the row admit compares with [obj+0xa1] in paragraph
  (a), so the seat's direction per row is authored: threshold >= 7 moves
  the table 1 px DOWN, threshold < 7 moves it 1 px UP. The second half of
  0x1e5c0, 0x1e5fd-0x1e624, is skipped unless [obj+0xb1] is non-null,
  and the KATAPULT installer zeroes that field (0x1fb7d).
  (c) WHICH SEAT CLASSES CARRY A ROW-CLOCK AT +0xa4. Read at the views
  the installers store (the corrected convention of PR-338): 0x96c38,
  PALMA's own class stored at [obj+8], holds 0x1e5c0 at +0xa4. 0x96d1c,
  KATAPULT's class, holds 0x1e690 - not a row-clock but a state-type
  dispatcher: 0x1e6a7 reads the state record's +0x4 word, 0x1e6aa/0x1e6ad
  subtract 3 and compare 4, `ja` skips everything, and the jump table at
  0x1e670 reads 0x1e6be, 0x1e723, 0x1e788, 0x1e7f3, 0x1e886. Each of
  those moves the table by a FIXED offset through 0x45200 on
  [obj+0xa5]: (dx,dy) = (+13,+5), (+13,+6), (+13,+10), (+3,+10) and
  (-42,-42). Then, gated on [obj+0xbd] (0x1e6d3) or [obj+0xc1]
  (0x1e808, 0x1e89b), it runs [[obj+0xbd or 0xc1]+8]+0x10 with the block
  {0, 1, dxdy} built at [esp+0x10] - the same protocol as 0x1e5c0's
  half, on different fields. The word [rec+0x4] is not observable in the
  shipped data for KATAPULT, whose only state is the single A_RUN of
  KAT.MOV. The two other seat types PR-338 named hold 0x1e5c0 at
  +0x254 (KAMIEN's 0x96a88) and at +0x154 (KILOF_PL's 0x96b88) - other
  slots, so their row-clock is not the +0xa4 one. The three sub-object
  views - 0x96c14, 0x96cf8 and the table class 0xa0cc0 - hold no verb at
  +0xa4 at all (0x96c14 and 0x96cf8 hold 0x531b0; 0xa0cc0's own extent
  ends long before +0xa4).
  (d) THE CENSUS OF THE AUTHORED THRESHOLDS, THROUGH THE PORT'S OWN
  PARSER. /tmp/opencode/pr339_rowclock.c opens the shipped ANIMACJE
  container with ported/llrs.c and parses every .MOV member with
  ported/ll_play.c's ll_mov_parse - the same walk tools/endlevel_census.c
  has used since PR-199 - and counts st->fr[].thresh, the value the
  engine puts at [rec+0x10]. Over the whole install: 777 members, 2317
  states with rows, 18823 rows. Thresholds range 1..40000; 1509 rows are
  below 7 (the 1 px UP branch) and 17314 are at or above 7 (the DOWN
  branch). Per state the net of one pass over its rows: 2167 states net
  DOWN, 149 net UP, 1 exactly balanced; 2164 states move down on every
  row and 117 up on every row. ZARIA.01 is at the down-only extreme:
  KAT.MOV's A_RUN is 10 rows all >= 7, PALM.MOV and PALML.MOV are 14
  rows each all >= 7, so each admitted row lowers those objects' surface
  tables by exactly 1 px and each state change adds the fixed offsets of
  paragraph (c). That voids PR-336 paragraph (g)'s reading, which turned
  the ORDER of the rows into the sign and reported "7 of +1 then 3 of
  -1" for KATAPULT and "7 and 7" for PALMA: there is no oscillation in
  any shipped seat text, and no seat rises.
OPENS: OI-125, named by this record: the state-change surface jumps -
  five authored (dx,dy) offsets behind one dispatcher, gated by
  [obj+0xbd] and [obj+0xc1], two fields no PR has read. Also: the state
  record's +0x4 type word, which selects that dispatcher's branch, is not
  observable in the shipped data for KATAPULT (one state, one A_RUN), so
  which of the five offsets ZARIA.01's catapult actually takes is open.
  And what a descending table does to an attached actor: the ask chain of
  PR-336 answers through [obj+0x89]/[obj+0xa9] and nothing in the image
  re-attaches a standing actor when its table moves - the 0x1b message
  poster of OI-123 is still the gate.
CLOSES: PR-338 OPENS item three, the row-clock question of PR-336, for

```

  0x96cf8, 0x96d1c, 0xcef40, 0x394, 0xba8, 0xbb0, 0xbb4, 0xbb8, 0xbbc,
  0xbc0, 0xbc4, 0xbc8, 0xbd, 0xc1, 0xc2, 0x66, 0x64, 0xb5, 0xc5, 0x4,
  0x18, 0x94
NAMES: [obj+0xbd], [obj+0xc1], [obj+0xc2], [obj+0x66], ID BLOCK,
  GAME OBJECT ANCHOR, SINGLETON, KATAPULT, PALMA, KAMIEN, KILOF_PL,
  0x22e30, 0x22dd0, 0x22de0, 0x22dfa, 0x20964, 0x20940, 0x1dfd9, 0x44350,
  0x52c70, 0x53a30, 0x96574, OI-123, OI-125, F6
CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moves is what an
  F6 seat leg would have to carry: an id, not a pointer, in [obj+0xbd].
HOOKS: none. Every claim is machine code (leodb dis), the instruction
  index (insn), the store-immediate index (loadimm), the global-reference
  search over the instruction index, or the data bytes at the class views.
MEASURED: (a) WHERE THE FIELDS LIVE. 0x1e690's body tests
  [obj+0xbd] before its element call (0x1e6d3, 0x1e738, 0x1e79d) and
  [obj+0xc1] (0x1e808, 0x1e89b), and writes them at 0x1e7e0 and 0x1e957.
  KATAPULT is allocated 0xc5 bytes (0x1fb42) and PALMA 0xb5 (0x1fc18), so
  [obj+0xbd] and [obj+0xc1] are inside KATAPULT's object and past PALMA's
  end: with the +0xa4 verb itself different for the two types (PR-339),
  the element half belongs to the catapult alone.
  (b) THE GETTERS RETURN A GLOBAL. 0x22e30 is `mov eax,ds:0xcebb8; ret`
  and 0x22dd0 is `mov eax,ds:0xcebc0; ret`. Slot positions, read at the
  ten seat and seat sub-object views the installers store (the full list
  is in the GATE file): 0x22e30 sits at +0xc of the KATAPULT class view
  0x96d1c, +0x30 of 0x96cf8 and +0x38 of 0x96cf0, at +0xf0 of the PALMA
  class view 0x96c38, +0x114 of 0x96c14 and +0x11c of 0x96c0c, and at
  +0x2a0/+0x2a8 of the KAMIEN pair 0x96a88/0x96a80 and +0x1a0/+0x1a8 of
  the KILOF_PL pair 0x96b88/0x96b80. 0x22dd0 sits at +0xcc of 0x96d1c,
  +0xf0/+0xf8 of 0x96cf8/0x96cf0, +0x1b0/+0x1d4/+0x1dc of the PALMA
  trio and +0x260/+0x268 of the KILOF_PL pair - seven of the ten, not
  the KAMIEN pair. The only writers of those two globals are 0x1e001 and
  0x1e015.
  (c) THE GLOBALS ARE COUNTER VALUES, NOT POINTERS. 0x1dfd9-0x1e029 is
  the static-init pattern PR-336 names: eight stores to the consecutive
  globals 0xceba8, 0xcebb0, 0xcebb4, 0xcebb8, 0xcebbc, 0xcebc0, 0xcebc4
  and 0xcebc8, each the result of `call 0x44350`, and 0x44350 is four
  instructions - `mov eax,ds:0xa90ac; lea edx,[eax+1]; mov
  ds:0xa90ac,edx; ret`. So that block hands out successive small
  integers, and what a seat object keeps at [obj+0xbd] through the
  getters is one of those ids: the element a seat manages is selected by
  id, not by pointer.
  (d) THE SETTERS AND THE FLAG BYTES. 0x20964 is `mov DWORD PTR
  [ebx+0xbd],edx` where ebx = [eax-0xa5] is the object (0x20958), eight
  bytes after `or BYTE PTR [eax-0x3f],0x40` (0x20955) - the flag byte at
  [obj+0xc2]. Its sibling 0x20940 `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x18],0; sub
  eax,0xa5; ret` is stored in eight of the ten views - +0x4 of 0x96cf8,
  +0xc of 0x96cf0, +0xc4/+0xdc/+0xe8 of the PALMA trio, +0x174/+0x17c of
  the KILOF_PL pair and +0x268/+0x270 of the KAMIEN pair - but NEITHER
  0x20964 nor 0x22dfa, 0x22e18 appears in any stored view: they are
  reached through a view this census does not hold, or by direct call.
  0x22dfa is the other setter: `or BYTE PTR [edx+0x2],0x40` at 0x22df6
  with edx = [eax+0x64] (the object's flag word at [obj+0x66]) and then
  `mov [eax+0xbd],ebx` with ebx = the edx argument. The clearer 0x22de0
  `mov [eax+0xbd],0` is stored at +0xb4 of 0x96d1c, +0xd8/+0xe0 of
  0x96cf8/0x96cf0, +0x198/+0x1bc/+0x1c4 of the PALMA trio and +0x248/
  +0x250 of the KILOF_PL pair. And 0x22e18 does `call 0x52c70` (eax,
  edx = the object) followed by `mov [edx+0xbd],0` and `mov
  [edx+0xc1],0` at 0x22e22.
  (e) THE OBJECT BEING MANAGED IS A GAME SINGLETON. 0x1e6e0 loads the
  anchor 0xcef40, 0x1e6ef reads [anchor+0x394], 0x1e6fc reads its +0x8
  and 0x1e713 calls [[that]+0x10] with the block {0, 1, dx, dy} built at
  [esp+0x10] - so the element the seat moves is a singleton reached
  through the same game-object anchor 0x45230 reads at 0x4523c (PR-338),
  and [obj+0xbd] only decides WHETHER that call happens. The sub-object's
  own +0x10 verb 0x208e0 shows the same shape from the other side: it
  tests bit 2 of its argument (0x208eb) and for that branch names the
  class 0x96574 through 0x74bc0/0x74be0, else it calls the table class's
  0x44f90 after `add eax,0xa5` (0x20909-0x2090e) and then 0x53a30 (which
  at 0x53a58-0x53a6b installs 0xa2498/0xa2490 at [x+8]/[x+0xc] and calls
  the +0x94 verb - one +0x94 call site in the image).
OPENS: OI-125's remaining half, restated with the new facts: what value
  is handed to the set-element verbs 0x20964 and 0x22dfa, who calls them
  and who calls the clearer 0x22e18, what 0x52c70 does, what the class
  0x96574 named at 0x208f0 is, and what [obj+0xc2] bit 7 and [obj+0x66]
  bit 6 mean. Also open, and now the thing that decides whether a seat
  moves at all: the state record's +0x4 word that 0x1e690's dispatcher
  compares (3..7) and that 0x1e570 gates at < 13 - the record's control
  word is at +0x12 (0x543af reads it and masks 7, PR-147's mode table),
  so +0x4 is a different field and no PR has named it.
CLOSES: nothing. It answers OI-125's element-field question in part: the
  fields are real, only KATAPULT-sized, and hold an id from a static
  counter block, while the managed object is a singleton.
CORRECTS: PR-339's OI-125 wording that [obj+0xbd]/[obj+0xc1] carry the
  element: the fields hold an id from the counter block of paragraph (c)
  and the element itself is the singleton read of paragraph (e).
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no red leg

## PR-341 - THE SEAT VERBS SWITCH ON THE STATE RECORD'S ROW CURSOR, NOT ON
## THE ROW THRESHOLD: PR-339 MISREAD ONE DEREF, THE PALMA CYCLE IS BALANCED

```

SUBSYSTEM: the seat surface-table motion of OI-072/OI-124/OI-125 - what
  0x1e5c0 and 0x1e690 actually switch on, what one cycle of the shipped

  0x1e5dd, 0x1e5e0, 0x1e5e2, 0x1e5e9, 0x1e5ee, 0x1e5f4, 0x1e5f6, 0x1e5f8,

  0x1e944, 0x1e952, 0x1e957, 0x1e95d, 0x1e570, 0x1e579, 0x1e57c, 0x1e57f,
  0x1e582, 0x1e585, 0x1e588, 0x1e58f, 0x1e596, 0x1e970, 0x1e979, 0x1e985,
  0x521f0, 0x52311, 0x52317, 0x52320, 0x52323, 0x52329, 0x5232b, 0x52331,
  0x52338, 0x5233b, 0x52341, 0x5234a, 0x520c0, 0x52135, 0x52158, 0x52195,
  0x521b9, 0x521c1, 0x521c5, 0x521d4, 0x521d7, 0x535a0, 0x535b4, 0x535b6,
  0x535b9, 0x535bc, 0x535bf, 0x535db, 0x535e1, 0x535e7, 0x535ea, 0x535ed,
  0x53602, 0x53609, 0x5360c, 0x5360f, 0x53612, 0x53616, 0x52b10, 0x45200,
  0x45320, 0x5c, 0x50, 0xa4, 0xa5, 0x4, 0x8, 0x10, 0x12, 0x2e, 0x44, 0x95,
  0x9d, 0xa1, 0xb1, 0xb5, 0xc1, 0x18, 0x1c, 0x20, 0x78, 0xd, 0x7, 0x3
NAMES: ROW CURSOR, STATE RECORD, TABLE SHIFT, KATAPULT, PALMA, KAT.MOV,
  PALM.MOV, PALML.MOV, A_RUN, 0x1e5c0, 0x1e690, 0x1e570, 0x1e970, 0x53616,
  0x521c5, 0x521d7, 0x52341, 0x535db, 0x45200, o-fi, OI-072, OI-124,
  OI-125, F6
CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moves is the law
  an F6 seat leg would carry: a shift keyed to the row index, and a
  catapult cycle that closes.
HOOKS: none. Every claim is machine code (leodb dis over the four bodies),
  the data bytes of the jump table at 0x1e670, or the port's own .MOV
  parser run over the shipped ANIMACJE container.
MEASURED: (a) 0x1e5c0 HAS FOUR LOADS AND NO FIFTH. 0x1e5c8 `mov ecx,eax`
  keeps the object; 0x1e5ca `mov eax,[eax+0x5c]` is its state index;
  0x1e5cd `lea edx,[eax*4]`; 0x1e5d4 `mov eax,[ecx+0x50]` is the state
  array; 0x1e5d7 `mov eax,[edx+eax*1]` is the state record; 0x1e5da `mov
  eax,[eax+0x4]` is a word in THAT record; 0x1e5dd `cmp eax,0x7` with
  `jge 0x1e5e9` to `mov esi,-1` and below to `mov esi,1` at 0x1e5e2. Then
  0x1e5ee `lea eax,[ecx+0xa5]`, 0x1e5f4 `mov ebx,esi`, 0x1e5f6 `xor
  edx,edx`, 0x1e5f8 `call 0x45200` - x zero, y the sign, the record loop
  of PR-338 adding edx to [rec+0] and ebx to [rec+4]. There is no other
  load in the body. PR-339 paragraph (b) said 0x1e5da yields a "record-
  object pointer" and that the compared word sits "at [[state record]+0x10]
  - the same threshold the row admit reads at 0x52320". There is no such
  second deref, and 0x52320 `mov eax,[ebx+0x10]` is a load through the ROW
  entry in another body: the threshold and this word are different fields.
  (b) THE WORD IS THE ROW CURSOR - THE PORT ALREADY RUNS IT AS o-fi. The
  applier 0x535a0 addresses the same record with the same pair of
  instructions: 0x53602 `lea esi,[edi*4]`, 0x53609 `mov eax,[eax+0x50]`,
  0x5360c `mov eax,[esi+eax*1]` - and then treats +4 as a row number:
  0x5360f `mov esi,[eax+0x4]`, 0x53612 `cmp esi,edx`, 0x53616 `mov
  [eax+0x4],edx`, which is PR-172's "write the transition's authored start
  row". The walk keeps it: 0x521b9 `mov ecx,[esi+0x4]`, 0x521bc-0x521bd
  compare against the row count minus one at [[rec+0x2e]+8], and at the
  last row 0x521c1 `or BYTE PTR [ebp+0x0],4` plus 0x521c5 `mov
  [esi+0x4],0`, elsewhere 0x521d4 `lea edi,[ecx+1]` and 0x521d7 `mov
  [esi+0x4],edi`. esi is that record: 0x52158 tests its control byte at
  +0x12 (PR-147's mode bits) and 0x52195 takes its row list at +0x2e
  (PR-162 F1b). So the sign of a seat's table shift is the ROW POSITION,
  as PR-336 paragraph (g) had it; 0x1e570 reads it the same way
  (0x1e579-0x1e582) and `cmp ebx,0xd` at 0x1e585: PALMA's ask runs the
  table query 0x45320 on [obj+0xa5] only while the cursor is below 13,
  while KATAPULT's ask 0x1e970 runs it with no gate at all (0x1e979 `mov
  ebx,2`, 0x1e985 `call 0x45320`).
  (c) WHEN THE VERB RUNS AND WHAT CURSOR IT SEES. The step 0x521f0 ends
  its admitted path like this: 0x52311-0x52317 the owner's +0xa0 verb,
  0x52320-0x5232b the row threshold against the feed accumulator [obj+0xa1]
  and `jge 0x52354` for a step that admits nothing, then 0x52331 `mov
  esi,[ebp+0x44]` with 0x52338 `call [esi+0x18]` for the row handler, then
  0x5233b `mov eax,[ebp+0x0]` - the record's owner field, which is the
  +0xa4 verb's eax - and 0x52341 `call [edx+0xa4]`, then 0x5234a `mov
  [eax+0x95],1`. So the shift happens in the same step as the admit, after
  the row handler. The cursor step of paragraph (b) is in the other body
  0x520c0-0x521e1, which PR-324 reads as running BEFORE the step: whether
  the verb sees the admitted row's index or the next one is not settled by
  these bytes, and it cannot be, from one cycle's arithmetic - a cycle
  walks the cursor through 0..n-1 exactly once either way. At the state
  change the second runner 0x535db runs while the object is still in the
  OLD state: 0x535b4-0x535b9 index the old record for its +0x20 verb,
  0x535db is the +0xa4 call, the new record's ENTER is 0x535e1-0x535ea and
  the state word is written after it at 0x535ed. That call therefore uses
  the OLD state's cursor.
  (d) THE ARITHMETIC OF ONE CYCLE, MEASURED THROUGH THE PORT'S PARSER.
  For a state whose list admits its rows in order, one cycle shifts the
  table by min(n,7) minus max(0,n-7) in y, y growing down, where n is the
  number of rows. Over the shipped install - 777 members, 2317 states with
  rows, 18823 rows - 1890 states come out screen-DOWN, all of them with 13
  rows or fewer; 366 come out screen-UP, all with 15 rows or more, the
  worst -83 px; and exactly 61 states balance at zero, which are exactly
  the 61 states with 14 rows. No state's in-cycle descent exceeds 7 px,
  because only cursors 0..6 add. ZARIA.01: PALM.MOV and PALML.MOV are
  both 14-row A_RUN states, so each of that level's four PALMA objects
  lowers its surface table by 1 px for seven admits and raises it back for
  seven - net zero, never a carry - and KAT.MOV's A_RUN is a 10-row
  state. PR-339's census counted row THRESHOLDS instead, and its "every
  shipped seat row moves the table down 1 px" is void: thresholds at or
  above 7 have no bearing on this shift.
  (e) THE KATAPULT DISPATCHER SWITCHES ON THE SAME CURSOR AND ITS JUMPS
  CLOSE. 0x1e690's head is the identical chain - 0x1e69e, 0x1e6a1,
  0x1e6a4, then 0x1e6a7 `mov eax,[eax+0x4]` - and 0x1e6aa `sub eax,3`,
  0x1e6ad `cmp eax,4`, ja to 0x1e95d, so it acts only for cursor 3, 4, 5,
  6 or 7, through the jump table at 0x1e670 whose five entries are 0x1e6be,
  0x1e723, 0x1e788, 0x1e7f3, 0x1e886. Each moves the table by a fixed
  amount through 0x45200 and then, if its element field is set, runs the
  element: cursor 3 0x1e6c3/0x1e6be (+13,+5); cursor 4 (+13,+6); cursor 5
  (+13,+10); cursor 6 0x1e7f3/0x1e7f8 (+3,+10), which also writes 1 into
  [obj+0xc1] at 0x1e7e0 with ecx = 1 from 0x1e7af; cursor 7 0x1e886, `mov
  edx,0xffffffd6` and `mov ebx,0xffffffe1` = (-42,-31) - PR-339's fifth
  offset "(-42,-42)" misreads that second immediate - and its tail
  0x1e93e-0x1e957 reads [obj+0xb5] and [obj+0xb1], calls 0x52b10 with
  edx=2 and ebp=0, and writes 0 to [obj+0xc1]. The five offsets sum to
  exactly (0,0): KAT.MOV's ten rows carry the cursor through 3..7 once per
  cycle, so the catapult's table is displaced by up to (+42,+31) between
  the cursor-6 admit and the cursor-7 admit and is put back exactly where
  the author put it. Note the shape of that tail: [obj+0xb1..0xbd] is
  where PR-246 stores the AUTHORED RECTANGLE x0,y0,x1,y1, so the fields
  OI-125 asks about may be rectangle words on these objects rather than
  only the id of PR-340's counter block.
OPENS: the phase of paragraph (c) - which cursor value the admitted row
  pairs with, which fixes the order of a cycle but no net; rows skipped by
  a GOTOREL cursor jump of PR-324, which change which values a cycle
  visits and are not in the census arithmetic; the element calls those five
  arms make, with the block values each one passes; whether [obj+0xbd] and
  [obj+0xc1] are rectangle words or PR-340 counter ids on the same object,
  and what 0x52b10 does with the pair it is handed; and the standing gate
  OI-123, the poster of the 0x1b message that would attach a requester to
  a surface - with a seat table that returns to its authored place every
  cycle, no seat can carry the lion to the ZARIA.01 exit anyway.
CLOSES: PR-339 OPENS item two, which of the five offsets ZARIA.01s
  catapult takes: all five, in jump-table order, once per 10-row cycle,
  with a net of zero - the word that selects them is the row cursor, which
  the port already runs as o-fi. It also settles OI-125s question of
  whether the seat has an authored motion: it does, and its size is 1 px a
  row against a 14-row list and a closed five-jump path for the catapult.
CORRECTS: PR-339 - paragraph (a) is unchanged, but paragraph (b)s sign
  source is the row cursor at [[state record]+0x4], not the row threshold
  at [[row]+0x10]; paragraph (d) and the title measure and claim the wrong

  observable" is wrong, the word is the row count the shipped texts do

  closed by paragraph (e). PR-336 paragraph (g) stands: its 7-of-+1-then-3-
  of--1 and 7-and-7 counts were the cursor values. OI-124, OI-125 and
  HANDOFF section 8 T5 F6 lose PR-339s sentence that a seat descends 1 px
  per admitted row.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no red leg
  and no mutation run. Reproducible: /tmp/opencode/pr341_cursor.c and its
  output /tmp/opencode/pr341_cursor.out are the cycle arithmetic of

```
