CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moves is the
  question F6 has to ask next: not who posts the attach, but what the
  thing it posts is, and which shipped level reaches it.
HOOKS: none - this reads the image only. It does bear on three things
  the port already models: o->sig and the AC_* live-set mask (PR-218,
  PR-262), the standing-surface triple [actor+0xe6]/[+0xe2]/[+0xea]
  (PR-336) and the seat ask verbs 0x1e570/0x1e970 (PR-336, PR-341).
  None of them is changed here.
MEASURED: (a) THE MECHANISM, WHICH THE PORT HAS NO MODEL OF. The verb
  is class slot +0x10; KAMIEN's view 0x96a88 holds the base 0x54560
  there. Messages are QUEUED, never called: 0x52b10(eax = the object,
  edx = the value, ebx and ecx = two payload words) walks the list at
  [obj+0x10] to its tail (0x52b13-0x52b20), allocates one 0x10-byte
  node (0x52b22 -> the allocator 0x5c320, eax = 0x10) and writes
  node[0] = 0, node[4] = the value, node[8] = ebx, node[12] = ecx
  (0x52b30-0x52b3c), then links it (0x52b3f). The drain 0x52b50 is
  the only reader: it takes [obj+0x10], calls [[obj class]+0x10] with
  eax = the object and edx = the node (0x52b67), releases the node
  (0x52b72 -> 0x5c370) and repeats. 0x52b80 is the step that runs it:
  drain, then [[class]+0x14], then if [obj+0x28] is not zero,
  [[class]+0x0] with edx = 2. Its six callers include the object walk
  0x4ba90, which walks the twelve list heads at [ebp+0x0..0x2c] with
  the count at [x+0x44] and the link at [x+0x34], and for every entry
  whose [[class]+0x60] answers nonzero calls 0x52b80 (0x4bae4-0x4baed).
  Over the 176 class views the ctor pattern names, 0x52b10 is the only
  writer of those nodes: no other instruction in the image stores
  through a [reg+0x10] that is an object field.
  (b) THE BASE HANDLER IS A VALUE TABLE. 0x54569 reads the value at
  [node+4] and branches: 2 sets [obj+0xc2] and [obj+0xc6] to node[8]
  and node[12] (0x54590); 3 or's 4 into [obj+0xb6] (0x545c6); 4 or's
  8 (0x545d2); 6 sets [obj+0x6d] from node[8] when that is nonzero and
  [obj+0x71] from node[12] (0x545de); 8 zeroes the two words at
  [obj+0xc2]/[obj+0xc6] (0x545f4); 0xd ADDS node[8] and node[12] to
  them (0x545a7); 0x1b is the attachment (0x5460e, paragraph c); every
  other value goes to 0x53770 (0x5463a, 0x54652, 0x54675, 0x5468d).
  Two words OI-125 asks about as flag bits - 0x20964 writes
  `or BYTE PTR [obj+0xc2],0x40` - are written here as whole dwords by
  values 2, 8 and 0xd, so that pair has both an owner-flag meaning and
  a message-payload meaning.
  (c) 0x1b IS AN ATTACH AND ITS PAYLOAD IS NOT AN OBJECT POINTER. At
  0x5460e: if [obj+0xa9] is nonzero, esi = [[obj+0xa9]], eax =
  [obj+0xa9], edx = the object, and [[obj+0xa9]]+4 is called (0x5461e)
  - the detach notice. Then [obj+0xa9] := node[8] (0x54621-0x54624),
  and if that is nonzero, ecx = [[obj+0xa9]] and the code AT ecx is
  called with edx = the object (0x54632) - the attach notice. So the
  payload's first word is a table of two code pointers, +0 attach and
  +4 detach, and the field written is [obj+0xa9]: PR-336's "[obj+0x89]"
  in OI-124 and OI-072 is the wrong offset, and [obj+0x89] is the
  position snapshot of PR-159, a different field.
  (d) THE TWENTY DIRECT CALLS OF 0x54560 ARE NOT POSTERS. Every one is
  a fall-through from a local handler or a wrapper thunk: 0x24830
  handles value 0x10 and 0x24843 forwards the rest, 0x24f40 handles
  0x13, 0x3d8f1 handles 5, 0x3e5b4 handles 0x1c, 0x50e4f is the lion
  chain of paragraph (f), and 0x2f466, 0x2f5b6, 0x3b6b6, 0x3c226 are
  the shape `push ebx; push ecx; mov ebx,eax; mov ecx,edx; call
  0x54560`, a forward that keeps the object and the node in the
  callee-saved pair. The 0x1b value reaches the base only through a
  queue, which is what paragraph (a) is for.
  (e) WHICH CLASSES REACH THE ATTACH. At slot +0x10, 81 of the 176
  ctor-pattern views hold 0x54560, 16 hold 0x53770, 10 hold 0x52bb0,
  one holds 0x40ca0, and five hold 0x50d60 - 0x98f34 TLewEna2,
  0x9b4d4 TLewKadmar2, 0x9f540 TLewJunction, 0xa0624 and 0xa2218, the
  per-level lion classes PR-303 enumerated. PALMA's 0x96c38,
  KATAPULT's 0x96d1c and SPLYW's 0x96ddc hold 0x53770 and STRUMIEN's
  0x96e94 holds 0x52bb0. 0x53770 answers value 0x10 only when
  node[8] is the constant 0x8138764 (0x537b, 0x53780) and otherwise
  calls 0x52bb0 (0x537dd). 0x52bb0's own table takes node[4] again:
  1 moves the object - [[obj]] += node[8], [[obj+4]] += node[12] -
  and then calls [[obj+8]]+0x54 (0x52bc6-0x52bdd); 0xe writes
  [obj+0x30] := node[8] (0x52bef); 0x21 writes [obj+0x28] := 1
  (0x52be4); everything else, 0x1b included, is RETURNED UNHANDLED
  (0x52bc2). So no seat object and no SPLYW or STRUMIEN takes the
  attach at all: 0x1b is dropped by their own handlers before any
  chain. ZARIA's own lion is not reachable either - TLewZariaB 0x97a98
  holds 0x1e130 at +0x10 and 0x1e130 is not among the twenty chains.
  (f) THE LION'S HANDLER FORWARDS IT. 0x50d60, the +0x10 verb of the
  five classes above, first drops value 1 whenever [obj+0x126] is
  nonzero (0x50d6e-0x50d7f); otherwise `sub edx,9; cmp edx,0xc; ja
  0x50e4f` and the jump table at 0x50d20 for values 9..0x15. Values
  0xc, 0xd, 0xe, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14 all go to 0x50e4f, the
  chain to 0x54560, and 0x1b is above the table's range, so it takes
  that chain and reaches 0x5460e.
  (g) THE POSTER CENSUS, WHICH VOIDS OI-123'S CENTRAL CLAIM. All 66
  call sites of 0x52b10 are in /tmp/opencode/pr343_posters.py with
  its output in pr343_posters.out; each reads back the value in edx
  and the two payload words. By value: 1 x7, 2 x5, 5 x7, 8 x5, 11 x1,
  12 x1, 13 x4, 15 x5, 16 x1, 17 x1, 18 x2, 20 x1, 21 x4, 25 x11,
  27 x5, 29 x1, 30 x1, 33 x1, and 2 sites whose value is a register.
  Five post 0x1b: 0x1ea52 is the ask verb of SPLYW (the view 0x96ddc
  at +0x78), payload 0; 0x1eadc is the ask verb of STRUMIEN (0x96e94
  +0x78), payload 0, reached when [[class]+0xc] equals the global
  ds:0xceba4 and 0x52eb0 answers nonzero; 0x36533 is the +0xe0 verb of
  the lion class 0x9f170, payload 0, node[12] = [[esi]+0x50] as the
  state list; 0x45d28 is a method stored only at the data slot
  0xa11d0, whose view the ctor pattern does not name, and it posts to
  the object at [edi] rather than to itself, payload 0; and 0x2c252 is
  the +0x90 verb of TLewKadmar2 - the only one of the five that
  carries a payload at all. /tmp/opencode/pr343_names.py maps the
  views back to the factory name branches, and it is that script that
  answers SPLYW and STRUMIEN.
  (h) THE ONE ATTACH, AND ITS GATE. 0x2c1c0 is a lion verb. It runs
  only when the lion already holds something - it reads [obj+0xa9] at
  0x2c1cd and leaves if it is zero - and only in the lion's state
  index 1 (the compare on [obj+0x5c] at 0x2c1db), and only with a
  state-flag bit set at [obj+0x64]: bit 0x20 takes the scanner
  0x4b6d0, bit 0x40 takes 0x4b760. Those two are the same scan with
  opposite signs. Both walk the array at [0xcef40+0x74],
  [0xcef40+0x80] entries at stride 0xc, and for each entry call that
  ENTRY'S OWN code block at +0x14 (0x4b7ad, 0x4b71d) with the id the
  requester's class verb +0x6c returned as its argument (0x4b7a3,
  0x4b713); 0x4b760 keeps only scores above 0 and under the running
  best, from a start of 0x7fffffff (0x4b7b0-0x4b7c7), and 0x4b6d0
  keeps only scores below 0 and over the running best, from a start of
  0x80000001 (0x4b720-0x4b737); both write the ENTRY ADDRESS to the
  caller's out-parameter. The caller then requires the score to be
  usable - above -5 after 0x4b6d0 (0x2c209) and below 5 after
  0x4b760 (0x2c230) - and posts value 1 with zero as node[8] and the
  score as node[12], which paragraph (e) shows is a MOVE of the
  object by (0, score), and only then posts 0x1b with the entry as
  node[8] (0x2c245-0x2c252). This is consistent with the ask side:
  0x45400 reads the held surface of the requester at 0x45471 (`mov
  ebx, DWORD PTR [edi+0xa9]`) and at 0x45479 waives its own
  negative-clearance rejection exactly when the surface being asked
  about IS the held one (0x4547d `jl 0x454c0` is skipped by
  `cmp esi,ebx; je 0x45481`).
OPENS: what those entries are - the code block at [entry] with +0 the
  attach notice, +4 the detach notice and +0x14 the scorer, and the
  anchor's table at [0xcef40+0x74] with its count at +0x80: no name
  branch installs it and nothing in the port reads it, so it is OI-127;
  the class whose only stored verb 0x45970 sits at the data slot
  0xa11d0, which the ctor pattern does not name, and who calls it;
  whether any shipped level other than KADMAR II reaches the attach at
  all, since 0x2c252 is installed by one class only and ZARIA's own
  lion 0x97a98 forwards nothing to the base; the state-flag bit of
  0x2c1ec and the state index 1 that gate it; the first test of
  0x45400, at 0x4540c, which is NOT a position test - it compares
  [[surface table]+4]+0xc, that is the FIRST RECORD'S FLAG BYTE of
  PR-335, against the ask's mode dword, and both shipped seat ask
  verbs pass 0, so the ZARIA.01 tables whose first separator is ';'
  (flag 1) fail there before any bracket or clearance is evaluated:
  that needs its own measurement over the shipped tables; and whether
  [obj+0x10] queues are per-object lists the .MOV or .DES author at
  all, since the only writer found is 0x52b10.
CLOSES: the question OI-123 asks, as written: who posts the message
  whose value word is 0x1b. Five sites do, all through 0x52b10, and
  this record names each one with the class that installs the verb
  running it. It also settles the mechanism half - the queue at
  [obj+0x10], the drain 0x52b50, the class verb +0x10 - and that
  0x52b10 is the only writer of those nodes. It does not close OI-123
  as a whole: the attach still has no reach in ZARIA.01, because no
  seat class dispatches 0x1b and ZARIA's lion does not forward it, so
  F6 and OI-124 stay open, and the payload type is OI-127.
CORRECTS: PR-336 in two of its words, not in its read: OI-123's
  paragraph that row writes, saying nobody writes that opcode, and
  OI-124's and OI-072's naming of the held-surface anchor as

GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no red

CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moves is the
  shape of the gate an F6 leg would have to satisfy, and one field's
  type.
HOOKS: the seat ask verbs 0x1e570/0x1e970 (PR-336, PR-341) and the
  record grammar the port copied from 0x45120/0x4a0b0 into
  place_seat_table (PR-335) - neither is changed; no port behaviour
  moves. The port's own seat tables are built from the .MOV text, so
  the handle slots measured here are not modelled and none of this
  changes a port answer.
MEASURED: (a) THE SIX ASKERS AND THEIR MODE. 0x45320 has exactly six
  callers and all six set the same registers: eax = a surface HANDLE,
  edx = the requester, ecx = 0, and EBX = 2. The seat pair: 0x1e58a
  `mov ebx,2; add eax,0xa5` and 0x1e979 `mov ebx,2; add eax,0xa5`,
  both behind the cursor test of PR-341, the first also gated at
  0x1e585 `cmp ebx,0xd; jge`. The other four: 0x288fe is reached only
  when the class +0xd8 verb answers nonzero at 0x288f4, and passes
  &[edi+0xee]; 0x380f6 passes &[edi+0x44] and only when [obj+0x5c] is
  0x1f or 0x20 (0x380e9-0x380f4), two of the state indices of PR-336;
  0x3df20 passes &[esi+0xee] behind the same +0xd8 verb; 0x3f01e
  passes &[eax+0x44] only when the caller equals [eax+0x3c], the
  rectangle word of PR-328 - and 0x3efe9 shows that class parsing its
  own table with 0x45120 at &[eax+0x44]. So mode 2 is not a seat
  peculiarity: no asker in the image passes anything else.
  (b) WHAT A SURFACE IS. The handle is a three-word block: +4 is the
  record array, +8 is the count. 0x45120(eax = the handle, edx = the
  text) is what fills it: it scans the header with the format at
  0x9182d, which is the literal "%d %c ;" - a count, one character, a
  semicolon - writing the count at [handle+8] (0x4512c, 0x4513b),
  then allocates (count+1)*0xd + 4 bytes (0x45149-0x45152) and stores
  the array at [handle+4] (0x45166) before filling the rows through
  0x4a0b0, PR-335's line parser. A seat's handle is EMBEDDED in the
  object at obj+0xa5, so its record array is [obj+0xa9] and its count
  is [obj+0xad]: the ladder's constructor 0x1f8ac initialises exactly
  that triple - 0x1f8de writes [obj+0xa5] = 0, 0x1f8e9 writes
  [obj+0xa9] = 0, 0x1f8f9 writes [obj+0xad] - and 0x2b6a0, 0x4a621
  and 0x4a63f clear the same fields. The other handle homes are the
  rectangle class's embedded one at obj+0x44 and the pointer at
  [obj+0xee]. That is the type OI-127 asked for: the value the 0x1b
  attach stores at [obj+0xa9] (0x54624) is a HANDLE OF THIS SAME SHAPE,
  because the waiver 0x45479 `cmp esi,ebx` compares it against esi,
  which is 0x45400's own first argument - a handle - and 0x54618 and
  0x5462e read [handle+0] as a CODE TABLE and call its +4 and +0 with
  edx = the object, which is the same first word 0x4b7ad uses when it
  calls `[[entry]+0x14]` on the provider entries. So a surface handle
  is {code table, record array, count}: PR-343's "the payload's first
  word is a table of two code pointers" is right about the use and
  incomplete about the shape, and OI-127's conflict between the two
  readings of [obj+0xa9] is dissolved - there is one type.
  (c) THE QUERY AND THE MODE. 0x45320 keeps the handle in edi and the
  requester in esi, builds {0, 0, 0x98278} on the stack and fills it
  with 0x541f0 (0x45340), the position block of PR-336, which also
  tests [obj+0xb6] bits 1 and 2 and calls the class +0xbc verb
  (0x54200, 0x54218). It then adds the velocity words [obj+0xca] and
  [obj+0xce] to that point (0x45349-0x45363) - the ask is aimed where
  the requester is MOVING, not where it stands - and calls 0x45400
  with eax = the handle, edx = the requester, ecx = ebx = the mode
  (0x45359 `mov ecx,ebx`, 0x4536f), the mode being the caller's ebx,
  not its ecx as PR-343's OPENS paragraph said.
  (d) THE FIRST GATE CANNOT FIRE. 0x4540c `mov eax,[eax+4]` takes the
  record array, 0x4540f `mov al,BYTE PTR [eax+0xc]` and 0x45412 read
  the FLAG BYTE OF RECORD 0, and 0x45417 `cmp eax,ecx; jg 0x454c0`
  rejects when that flag exceeds the mode. But 0x45120 is the only
  writer of that byte and its three branches are 1 for ';' (0x451a6),
  2 for '#' (0x451d4) and 0 otherwise (0x451db); with the mode fixed
  at 2 by paragraph (a) the compare can never go the wrong way. The
  flag filter is INERT in the shipped game: no shipped table is
  rejected before the bracket test, and PR-343's claim that the
  ZARIA.01 tables whose first separator is ';' fail there is void.
  (e) THE GATES THAT DO FIRE, IN ORDER. 0x4541f calls 0x45380 with the
  handle and the aimed point. It returns 0 if [handle+8] is zero
  (0x4538c), if x < record 0's x (0x45393 `cmp edx,[eax]; jl`), or if
  x > record count's x (0x45397 `imul edx,[ecx+8],0xd`, 0x4539f);
  otherwise it walks the table from index 1 (0x453a3-0x453bb) and
  returns the SMALLEST SEGMENT INDEX i with x <= record i's x - not a
  boolean, a bracket. 0x45400 rejects only on 0 (0x4542c) and turns i
  into the record PAIR: 0x4543c `imul ebx,edx,0xd` and 0x45440
  `imul edx,edx,0xd` after `dec edx`, both added to [handle+4] -
  record i and record i-1. 0x453d0 is the same pair used the plain
  way - call 0x45380, interpolate records i and i-1 with 0x455a0, and
  return 0x7fffffff when the point is outside the table (0x453f5).
  The requester's class verb +0x6c is called at 0x45439 and its
  result is passed as 0x455a0's second argument
  (0x45462): the pair of 0x455a0 calls (0x45468, 0x45491) is
  PR-336's segment interpolation, asked at the requester's own +0x6c
  value, and the first result has the aimed point's y subtracted
  (0x4546d reads 0x45320's block, 0x45477 `sub eax,edx`). The
  rejections are 0x4547d `test eax,eax; jl 0x454c0` - a negative
  clearance, which is what PR-336 measured at ZARIA.01's coordinates -
  skipped only when 0x45479 `cmp esi,ebx` finds the handle to be the
  requester's own attached one, ebx = [requester+0xa9] read at 0x45471;
  then 0x45496 `test eax,eax; jg` and 0x4549a `cmp eax,[requester
  +0xea]; jg` reject a worse clearance than the incumbent. The winner
  is stored as PR-336 said - [requester+0xe6] = the handle, [+0xea] =
  the clearance, and [+0xe2] = the winning record's flag byte, read at
  0x454b1, which is the only place that byte is ever USED - so with
  mode 2 the flag byte carries no selection meaning anywhere and
  [actor+0xe2] is information, not a gate.
  (f) THE HANDLE'S CODE TABLE, AND WHO HAS ONE. That first word is a
  four-method table and it is in the image: 0x96c28 = {0x453d0,
  0x45320, 0x45400, 0x45120} - height-at-x, the query, the query core,
  the parser - and it sits SIXTEEN BYTES BEFORE PALMA's class view
  0x96c38; 0x96d0c is the same quartet sixteen bytes before KATAPULT's
  0x96d1c. Counting aligned dwords whose value is 0x453d0 gives 38 of
  these tables, all in the class-view region 0x96c28-0xa2044, which is
  the census of the classes that own a queryable surface. No
  instruction names any of those 38 addresses, so they are installed by
  the template copy of PR-294 rather than by a store, and that is the
  remaining OI-127 question. It also renames what PR-343 called the
  attach and detach NOTICES: they are methods of this table. The
  detach half 0x5461e calls the old surface's +4, which is the query
  0x45320, so detaching re-runs the standing-surface query for the
  object; the attach half 0x54632 calls the new surface's +0, which
  all 38 tables hold as 0x453d0, the height probe - and it passes the
  OBJECT as the position block, which works because 0x45380 reads the
  point as [edx] and the object's x is at [obj+0] (PR-159).
OPENS: what the class verb +0x6c returns, since it is the x at which
  the segment is interpolated - no port model has it, and the two seat
  verbs run it on the lion; who calls 0x453d0, the plain "ground
  height at my x" entry that returns 0x7fffffff outside the table, and
  whether the physics tail of PR-336 uses that instead of 0x45400;
  whether a .des built by a different tool ever passes a mode below 2,
  since the bound comes from 0x45120's three writers and not from the
  data; and the provider entries of OI-127, whose +0 code table is now
  known to be the same first word as a seat handle's - what installs
  those entries and who their +0 and +4 methods are.
CLOSES: the open item PR-343 opened about the flag-byte gate at
  0x4540c - answered from 0x45120's value range and the askers' mode,
  so the census of the shipped tables it asked for is not needed; the
  first half of OI-127, the shape of a 0x1b payload, which is a
  surface handle {four-method table, record array, count} and not a
  surface object; and the census of who owns a queryable surface - 38
  of those handle tables, PALMA's at 0x96c28 and KATAPULT's at
  0x96d0c. It does not close OI-072, OI-123 or OI-124: with the flag
  filter inert the ZARIA.01 chain still ends at the bracket and
  clearance law PR-336 measured and at a waiver that needs an attach
  this level never posts.
CORRECTS: PR-343 twice. Its OPENS paragraph says the two seat ask
  verbs pass the mode 0 and that ZARIA.01's tables fail the flag test
  before any bracket or clearance: they pass 2, in the ebx of the call
  rather than its ecx, and 0x45120 never writes a flag above 2, so
  that test never rejects. Its paragraph (h) calls the 0x1b payload
  "a table of two code pointers": it is a surface handle, and its
  first word is the code table that a seat's own handle at obj+0xa5
  also begins with. And PR-336's "surface object" for that argument is
  a handle, not an object: 0x45400 never reads a vtable of the surface.
  PR-336's bracket law, its clearance arithmetic, its winner triple and
  its measured rejection all stand.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no red
  leg and no mutation run. Reproducible: the six asker sites are the
  leodb callers list of 0x45320 with their `mov ebx,2` quoted at 0x1e58a,
  0x1e979, 0x288fe, 0x380f6, 0x3df20 and 0x3f01e; the flag bound is
  0x45120's branches 0x451a6/0x451d4/0x451db and its header format is
  the string at 0x9182d; the query body is dumped in
  /tmp/opencode/pr344_45400.txt.

CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moves is what
  F6 has to assume about a standing lion.
HOOKS: the query and its waiver 0x45320/0x45479 (PR-336, PR-344), the
  seat ask verbs at 0x1e560 and 0x1e970 (PR-336, PR-341), the state
  list [obj+0x50]/[obj+0x5c] of PR-336 and the applier of PR-341 -
  none of them changed here, and no port behaviour moves.
MEASURED: (a) THE VERB AND ITS CENSUS. Class slot +0xAC is the
  ground-contact verb. 0x546a0 is installed there in 118 of the
  class-view tables the ctor pattern names, and every class this ladder
  cares about that can stand on something has it: TLewZaria 0x96960,
  TLewZariaB 0x97a98, TLewKadmar2 0x9b4d4 and KAMIEN 0x96a88 all hold
  0x546a0 at +0xAC. The seat classes hold NOTHING: PALMA 0x96c38,
  KATAPULT 0x96d1c, SPLYW 0x96ddc and the ladder DRABINKA 0x97cdc hold
  0x23930, which is a bare `ret`, and STRUMIEN 0x96e94 holds 0x52a00.
  A seat never maintains a standing surface for itself; only the things
  that stand on one do. Two call sites run it: 0x523f0, which calls
  [obj+0x44]'s +0x8 and +0xc and then the class +0xAC at 0x52416, and
  0x535e0, which is the state applier's tail - it writes the new state
  index to [obj+0x5c] at 0x535ed and calls +0xAC at 0x535f7, so
  changing state re-runs ground contact immediately.
  (b) ITS GUARDS. 0x546a0 returns at once when [obj+0xb6] bit 2 is set
  (0x546ac). It then reads the state record of PR-336 - eax =
  [[obj+0x50] + [obj+0x5c]*4] at 0x546b9-0x546bf - takes the dword at
  [state+0x12] and branches on its bits: 0x4000 takes the provider
  scan 0x4b600 of OI-127 with ecx = 0 (0x546c5, 0x546d5, 0x546d7) and
  a second arg of &esp+0x20; 0x100 runs three scan-and-apply pairs
  0x4b600 with ecx = 2, 0x4b430 and 0x4b7f0, each followed by 0x49580
  (0x54706-0x54754). The block between 0x546de and 0x54700 is not
  read here and stays open.
  (c) THE TAIL IS THE MAINTAINER, AND IT IS THE OTHER WRITER OF
  [obj+0xa9]. 0x54759: if the query result [obj+0xe6] is zero, go to
  the leave branch 0x547d7. Otherwise compare the kept surface
  [obj+0xa9] with the fresh answer. They are equal: do nothing
  (0x547c8). [obj+0xa9] was zero: set bit 0x10 of the flag byte at
  [edi], copy the answer into it (0x5478e), call the NEW surface's +0
  method - the height probe 0x453d0 - with the object as the position
  block (0x54794-0x54798), then call the object's own class verb +0xb4
  (0x5479a-0x5479f). They differ: call the OLD surface's +4 method -
  the query 0x45320 - first (0x547af-0x547b3), then copy the new
  answer in (0x547bc) and call its +0 (0x547c2-0x547c6). So the
  attachment slot of PR-343 and OI-127 is not a message-only field:
  it tracks the standing query every step, by the same +0 and +4
  method pair, and the 0x1b message is the scripted twin of this tail.
  Afterwards 0x547c8 sets bit 0x20 of [edi+1] whenever the winning
  record's flag byte [obj+0xe2] is non-zero.
  (d) THE EJECTION LAW. The leave branch 0x547d7 is taken from the top
  of the tail (0x54760) when there is no answer, and also when
  [obj+0xe2] == 2 - a '#' record, the flag 2 of PR-335 and PR-344 -
  AND [obj+0xc6] >= 0x58c (0x54766, 0x5476f): standing on a '#'
  surface is time-limited to 1420 of the [obj+0xc6] counter, which is
  one of the two words the message values 2, 8 and 0xd write (PR-343).
  The branch calls the kept surface's +4 method (0x547e1-0x547e8),
  zeroes [obj+0xa9] (0x547f0) and calls the class verb +0xb8
  (0x547eb-0x547fa).
  (e) THE LAND AND LEAVE VERBS. +0xB4 is land and +0xB8 is leave: the
  lions' pair is 0x238b0 and 0x23880, KAMIEN's the same, PALMA's
  0x1e560 and 0x208d0, KATAPULT's 0x22de0 and 0x20a40, the ladder's
  0x23290 and 0x20230. PALMA's +0xB4 is the seat ask verb of PR-341 -
  so a seat's ask is the thing that runs when something of that class
  lands, not a per-tick poll. The only other dispatcher of that pair
  is 0x45cb1(eax = a surface handle, edx = the object): it calls
  0x457e0 and then dispatches on [handle+8], the record COUNT, to
  +0xB4 when the table has records and to +0xB8 when it does not
  (0x45cc6, 0x45cd4). 0x45c80 is the same shape onto +0xc0 and +0xc4.
  Nothing in the image names 0x45cb1 or 0x45c80 by call or pointer.
OPENS: the unread block 0x546de-0x54700, and what the three
  scan-and-apply pairs 0x4b600/0x49580, 0x4b430/0x49580 and
  0x4b7f0/0x49580 give the object - those are the provider tables of

  calls 0x523f0, the other caller of +0xAC, and what [obj+0x44] is

  ask; and 0x45cb1, unreachable in the image, which is either dead or

CLOSES: the part of OI-123 and OI-124 that said the attachment slot is
  reached only through the 0x1b message - it is maintained by the

## PR-348 - THE GROUND HEIGHT IS A SLOPE, NOT A LOOKUP: 0x455a0 IS
## `(x - A.x) * (B.y - A.y) / (B.x - A.x) + A.y - point.y`, A
## CLEARANCE WITH TRUNCATING SIGNED DIVISION AND NO ZERO GUARD, AND
## THE CLASS VERB +0x6c HANDS IT THE POINT, NOT A NUMBER
```

SUBSYSTEM: F6's seat chain and OI-124's crossing arithmetic - the

  0x91840, 0xd, 0x4, 0x8, 0x10, 0x6c, 0x31, 0x7fffffff
NAMES: segment sampler, slope, clearance, height probe, bracket,
  segment index, sample point, truncation, signed division,
  OI-072, OI-123, OI-124, F6, pr348_455a0.txt
CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moves is the
  arithmetic a crossing leg would have to reproduce.
HOOKS: the query 0x45320/0x45400 and its winner triple (PR-336,
  PR-344), the height probe 0x453d0 installed at +0 of every surface
  handle table (PR-344, PR-346), the seat tables the port parses with
  place_seat_table (PR-335). No port behaviour moves.
MEASURED: (a) THE SAMPLER. 0x455a0(eax = A, ebx = a POINT POINTER,
  edx = B) takes two records A and B of a seat table - each 0xd
  dwords, x at +0, y at +4 - and returns how far the segment A-B is
  BELOW the sample point at that point's own x. The instructions:
  0x455aa `mov edx,[edx+4]; sub edx,[ecx+4]` is B.y - A.y; 0x455ad
  `mov edi,[ecx]` is A.x; 0x455b1 `mov edx,[ebx]` reads the SAMPLE
  POINT from [ebx], so ebx is a pointer to {x, y}, not a number;
  0x455b3 `sub edx,edi` is x - A.x; 0x455b5 `imul edx,esi` is that
  times B.y - A.y; 0x455bc-0x455c1 take B.x - A.x - esi = [B] - edi;
  0x455be-0x455c3 sign-extend with `sar edx,31` and divide with
  `idiv esi`, so the quotient is TRUNCATED TOWARD ZERO with the sign
  of the dividend; 0x455c5 `mov edx,[ecx+4]` is A.y and 0x455c8
  `mov ecx,[ebx+4]` is the sample point's OWN y, added and subtracted
  at 0x455cb/0x455cd. So the result is
  `(x - A.x) * (B.y - A.y) / (B.x - A.x) + A.y - (*ebx).y`, which is
  `ground(x) - point.y`: the clearance, in the engine's down-positive
  y. There is no test for B.x == A.x: a vertical segment makes this
  fault, and nothing on the path checks it.
  (b) THE PROBE IS THE SAME CALL WITH THE OBJECT AS THE POINT.
  0x453d0(eax = the surface handle, edx = the object) calls 0x45380
  for the segment index, returns 0x7fffffff when the point is outside
  the table (0x453f5), and otherwise forms the pair with 0x453df
  `imul edx,eax,0xd` and 0x453e3 `imul eax,eax,0xd` after `dec eax`,
  adds the record base [handle+4] at 0x453e6-0x453eb, and calls the
  sampler with ebx = the object (0x453d4 `mov ebx,edx`) - valid
  because the object's x and y are at [obj+0] and [obj+4] (PR-159),
  the same shape the sampler reads. This is the method every surface
  handle table installs at +0 (PR-344, PR-346), and 0x54632 calls it
  on attach (PR-345).
  (c) THE QUERY USES IT TWICE AND ITS SIGN DECIDES. 0x4543c-0x45458
  build the same pair from the bracket index: [handle+4] + i*0xd and
  + (i-1)*0xd; 0x45462 puts the requester's class verb +0x6c result
  into ebx, and since the sampler dereferences ebx twice - [ebx] for
  x and [ebx+4] for y - THAT VERB RETURNS THE POINT TO SAMPLE, which
  is what PR-344 left open. The first call at 0x45468 then has a
  value loaded at 0x4546d from [esp+0x18] and subtracted at 0x45477;
  by the frames that slot is the dword the caller pushed at 0x45348,
  the asker's own ecx as 0x541f0 left it, and what that is remains
  open. A negative result is the rejection at 0x4547d, waived only
  for the held surface (0x45479). The second call at 0x45491, with
  the pair reversed at 0x4548d/0x4548f, is rejected when it is
  positive (0x45496) or worse than the incumbent [requester+0xea]
  (0x4549a), and the accepted value is what is stored at [+0xea]
  (0x454a8).
  (d) WHY THAT IS THE CROSSING LAW. A seat's table moves by the row
  cursor of PR-342, so its x and y per record move with it; the
  clearance the lion gets is a slope evaluated at the sample point's
  x and compared against that point's own y, and the sign of
  `(x - A.x) * (B.y - A.y) / (B.x - A.x) + A.y - point.y` is what
  decides whether the ask answers. Any ZARIA.01 crossing leg has to
  reproduce this expression, including the truncation: the division is
  not rounded and the sign comes from the dividend, so an off-by-one
  in the quotient changes a rejection.
OPENS: the records' other dwords - +8 and the 0xd-stride tail, which
  0x45622 compares as ranges ([eax+4]/[eax+8]/[eax+0x10] against
  [ebx+0xc]) and which PR-335 parsed but did not use; whether a
  shipped seat table can produce B.x == A.x, which would fault in the
  sampler; what the class verb +0x6c actually RETURNS as that point -
  the object itself, its rider, or a per-frame block - for the lion
  and for PALMA; and the two record-line shapes 0x455e2 parses with
  the extra 0x49920 fields at 0x9183d and 0x91840, a second grammar
  beside 0x4a0b0's.
CLOSES: PR-344's first open item, the type of the class verb +0x6c's
  result - it is the sample point pointer, read as [ebx] and [ebx+4];
  and it gives OI-124 the exact arithmetic of the clearance the seat
  chain grants, which PR-336 measured only as a rejected number. The
  crossing itself is still unmeasured.
CORRECTS: PR-344's OPENS wording, which asked what +0x6c "returns,
  since it is the x at which the segment is interpolated" - it is not
  an x but a pointer to {x, y}. PR-344's bracket law, its gate order
  and its winner triple stand; PR-336's measured rejection stands and
  is now reproducible as an expression.

  views: TLewZaria 0x96960, TLewZariaB 0x97a98 and TLewKadmar2
  0x9b4d4 - every lion this ladder names - and KAMIEN 0x96a88, PALMA

  written by the anchor's snapshot pass, not by the object's own
  motion, so at the moment of the ask the engine compares the seat's

  point for the incumbent test, and the waiver of 0x45479 keyed to

CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moves is what
  a crossing leg may assume.
HOOKS: the query and its sampler (PR-336, PR-344, PR-348), the
  ground-contact tail that keeps [obj+0xa9] (PR-345), the class verbs
  +0x48, +0x50 and +0x33 the land verb of PR-345 also used. No port
  behaviour moves.
MEASURED: (a) THE BLOCK AND WHO FILLS IT. 0x45320 builds three dwords
  on its own frame - 0, 0 and the code table 0x98278 (0x4532c-
  0x45338) - and hands it to 0x541f0, which overwrites block[0] with
  [obj+0] and block[1] with [obj+4], the LIVE position (0x541f6-
  0x541fd), then tests [obj+0xb6] bit 2 (0x54200) and otherwise calls
  the class verb +0xbc with edx still = the block (0x54209-0x5420e).
  Read by how 0x45320 uses it afterwards, block[0] is the live x,
  block[1] becomes the AIMED x (0x4536b) and block[2] the aimed y, and
  ebx = &block[1] (0x4535f) is exactly the {x, y} pair the sampler
  reads. The +0xbc verb is not a coordinate for the classes this
  ladder uses: for every
  lion class and for KAMIEN it is 0x23870, `cmp DWORD PTR [eax+0xa9],
  0x0; setne al`, a predicate that says "I already hold a surface"
  (0x23870-0x541f0's 0x54214 then skips the rest), and the answer it
  returns is used only to branch. The chain that could write the third
  dword is the one at 0x54221-0x5423a: the class verbs +0x48 and +0x50
  and the script method at [[obj+0x48 result]+0x33]+4, the same three
  the land verb 0x238b0 of PR-345 calls. STRUMIEN's +0xbc is 0x23a00,
  `mov eax,[eax+0x54]; ret`, one instruction. PALMA's 0x20870 is a
  different shape again: it saves the block pointer in ecx (0x20872),
  moves `this` back 0xc to reach its own base (0x20874 `sub eax,0xc`),
  and tests bit 2 of the low byte of block[0] - the live x, so that
  test is on the position (0x20879 `test cl,0x4`); when that bit
  is clear it calls 0x44f90 with edx=1 on `this+0xa5` (0x20897 `add
  eax,0xa5`, 0x2089c) - PALMA's own embedded handle - and then
  0x53a30 on the same field (0x208ab). So that verb reads the block as
  a flag word and answers with a handle: a handle accessor, not a y.
  (b) THE AIM. 0x45320 then sets ebp = block[0] + [obj+0xca] - the
  live x plus the x-velocity - writes that into block[1] (0x4536b) and
  adds [obj+0xce] to block[2] (0x45357-0x45363), and passes ebx =
  &block[1] (0x4535f). The sampler reads [ebx] and [ebx+4] (PR-348),
  so the ask is aimed at {x + vx, block[2] + vy}: the x is the live x
  plus the velocity, and the y is whatever the controller chain left
  in block[2] plus the y-velocity - or, if that chain did not run,
  the code table 0x98278 plus the y-velocity, a number no coordinate
  can compete with. The branch order makes this exact: the chain runs
  unless bit 2 of [obj+0xb6] is set (0x54200) AND the +0xbc verb
  answers non-zero, and for the lions and KAMIEN that verb is
  "[obj+0xa9] != 0" - so the chain runs exactly when the object holds
  no surface, and a holder keeps the table value as its aimed y.
  (c) THE FIRST TEST IS THE RAW CLEARANCE: THE SUBTRAHEND IS ZERO.
  0x45400's first sampler call at 0x45468 is followed by a load at
  0x4546d of [esp+0x18] and a subtraction at 0x45477. Reading the
  frame: 0x45400-0x45403 pushes esi, edi, ebp and takes 8 local bytes,
  so [esp+0x18] is the first argument pushed by its caller - the dword
  0x45320 pushed at 0x45348, which is 0x45320's own ecx, and 0x541f0
  does not disturb it (0x541f1 pushes ecx, 0x5423f pops it back). The
  convention this family uses is `this` in eax with the other argument
  in edx - 0x45320 passes (eax,edx) to 0x541f0 unchanged (0x4533e-
  0x4533f) and to 0x45400 as (eax=this handle, edx=requester,
  ebx=mode, ecx=its own ecx), which is also how PR-344 read the flag
  gate at 0x45417, where ecx is the mode. So the subtrahend at 0x45477
  is 0x45320's ecx, and every one of the six askers zeroes it on the
  way to the call: 0x1e594, 0x1e983, 0x2890b, 0x38100, 0x3df2d,
  0x3f026 are all `xor ecx,ecx` one instruction before `call 0x45320`.
  The test at 0x4547d `jl` is therefore the bare clearance. Note that
  this is the mode=0x45320 supplies, not the mode in ebx: a caller
  that reaches 0x45400 directly, as the handle-table slot +8 does
  (PR-346), would put its own ecx in that slot.
  (d) THE TWO CALLS USE THE TWO POINTS AND THE SAME SLOPE, SO THE
  ACCEPTED SET IS ZERO CLEARANCE. The first call at 0x45468 has
  eax = [esp+0x4] and edx = [esp] - the pair record i and record i-1
  built at 0x4543c-0x4545e - and ebx = the class verb +0x6c result
  (0x45462), which PR-349 showed is the SNAPSHOT point at obj+0x89.
  The second call at 0x45491 is built at 0x45481-0x4548f from the same
  bracket index with the pair reversed, and its ebx = ebp is the
  AIMED block (0x4540a), the same point the bracket test at 0x4541f
  used. Algebraically the two expressions are negatives of each other:
  with A = record i, B = record i-1 and t = (x-A.x)/(B.x-A.x), the
  first is (1-t)(B.y-A.y) + A.y - p.y and the reversed second is
  -t(A.y-B.y) + B.y - q.y, and their difference is
  (B.y-A.y)(1-t-t') with t' = (x-B.x)/(A.x-B.x) = 1-t, i.e. zero - so
  both calls measure ONE clearance, in opposite signs, each off the
  other by at most 1 because `idiv` truncates toward zero. The gates
  then read: reject if the first is negative (0x4547d) unless the
  queried handle is the one already held (0x45479, 0x4547b); reject if
  the second is positive (0x45498) or worse than the incumbent
  [requester+0xea] (0x4549a). A surface the requester is NOT holding
  is therefore accepted only where the AIMED point lies on the slope
  to within the division's truncation; a surface it IS holding skips
  that first gate and is accepted at any non-positive clearance
  measured at its SNAPSHOT point.
  (e) WHY THAT IS THE CARRYING LAW. The held surface is the last
  answer the standing path accepted (PR-345, 0x5478e/0x547bc). So a
  seat's table can hold the lion at a depth, which is what a moving
  seat needs to carry it - but only after some earlier frame's ask
  landed on that same table at exact contact. That is the first link
  F6 needs, and it is a measurement of the level, not of the law: the
  question is whether any ZARIA.01 position puts the lion's aim on a
  seat's slope at zero clearance while that seat's cursor is running.
OPENS: what the controller chain (+0x48, +0x50 and the [obj+0x33]
  script method) writes into block[2] and with what - that is the
  lion's aimed y and it is unread; what [obj+0xea] holds before the
  first accepted ask, since the "worse than the incumbent" test needs
  its initial value; how far the snapshot at [obj+0x89] lags the live
  position (PR-349's open half); and PALMA's +0xbc answering with its
  own handle at obj+0xa5, which suggests a seat asks about itself.
CLOSES: PR-348's open item about 0x4546d's subtrahend - it is zero,
  because all six askers reach 0x45320 with ecx cleared (0x1e594,
  0x1e983, 0x2890b, 0x38100, 0x3df2d, 0x3f026) - and the shape of the
  acceptance law OI-124 needs: first contact must land the AIMED point
  on the slope to within the truncation, and after that the held
  surface re-accepts itself at any non-positive clearance at the
  snapshot. The crossing itself is still unmeasured and is now a leg,
  not a read.
CORRECTS: PR-349's paragraph (b), which attached the class verb
  +0x6c's point to the REJECTING call and the aimed block to the
  second call and the incumbent test: the registers are the other way
  round. The first call at 0x45468 runs with ebx = the +0x6c result
  (0x45462) - the snapshot - and the second at 0x45491 runs with
  ebx = ebp, the caller's aimed block (0x4540a, 0x4548b); the bracket
  test at 0x4541f uses that aimed point too. The measurement point
  PR-349 identified - obj+0x89 for the lions, KAMIEN, PALMA, KATAPULT
  and SPLYW - is right; the call it feeds is not. PR-344's reading of
  the flag gate's mode register (ebx at 0x45417) and PR-348's
  expression stand.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no red
  leg and no mutation run. Reproducible: 0x541f0 is dumped in
  /tmp/opencode/pr350_541f0.txt and the +0bc verbs in

  /tmp/opencode/pr344_45400.txt; the substitution is written out at

  accessor the land verb used (PR-345). The result is kept in ecx

  chain runs directly. Clear, 0x5420e calls +0xbc and a non-zero
  answer skips it (0x54214-0x54216); a zero answer then tests bit 1 of
  [obj+0xb6] (0x54218) and skips the chain if it is set. Of the 186
  views, 155 carry 0x23870 - `cmp DWORD PTR [eax+0xa9],0x0; setne al`
  - so for them the chain runs exactly when no surface is held and bit
  1 is clear. The exceptions: 0x23ea0 in 12 views (it writes [eax] and
  [eax+4], a different argument convention - not a predicate as used
  here), 0x23850 in 11 (writes [eax] and [eax+4] then calls +0x54),
  and one view each of 0x20870 (0x96c38, PR-350's PALMA/seat verb),
  0x20a00 (0x96d1c, its KATAPULT twin, which likewise `sub eax,0xc`
  then tests bit 2 of the block's first dword and calls 0x53a30 at
  0x20a27), 0x2cc90, 0x2cdd0, 0x354e0, 0x38d10, 0x4f450, 0x4f820.
  (e) THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE AIM. 0x45320 reads the aimed x BEFORE
  the chain (0x45345 ebp = block[0], +[obj+0xca] at 0x45355, stored at
  0x4536b), so the x is unaffected; but the block's y-component,
  [esp+0x8], is left at the seeded 0x98278 - the dump table's code
  pointer, which is not a coordinate - unless a +0xbc verb writes it,
  and the lions', KAMIEN's and every other predicate view's +0xbc does
  not. So for the classes this ladder uses, the aimed point the second
  sampler call and the incumbent comparison use is
  {live_x + [obj+0xca], 0x98278 + [obj+0xce]}: the second test at
  0x45498 (`jg`) is never taken and 0x4549a only compares which
  candidate is nearer, while real acceptance comes from the first test
  at the snapshot point (PR-349's +0x6c = 0x23a10, universal per
  paragraph (a)) and from the held-surface waiver. The chain does
  write block[0] = ±1, after the aimed x has been taken, and if the
  chain is skipped block[0] stays at the live x.
OPENS: what the word at [record+0x24 row +0x14] is, whose zero makes
  0x53e40 answer +1, and what [record+0x12] bit 3 and [obj+0x6d]
  gate - that is the state-active test whose sign becomes the aimed y;
  why 0x53e40 writes block[0] and not block[2], and whether the
  callers that reach 0x45400 directly (the handle-table slot +8,
  PR-346) pass a real block; what the 31 non-predicate +0xbc verbs
  write when they do run, in particular 0x2cc90/0x2cdd0/0x354e0/
  0x38d10/0x4f450/0x4f820, unread; and the last call 0x5423a, which
  for these classes reaches only a dump verb - whether some script
  table installs a different +4 that fills the block.
CLOSES: PR-350's first open item. Nothing in the class chain ever
  supplies a y coordinate: the chain is two accessors that do not
  touch the block and one state-active predicate that stores ±1 at its
  head, and the block's y stays the seeded code pointer for the lions,
  KAMIEN and every seat in ZARIA.01. That fixes the inputs a crossing
  leg has to use - the aimed point's y is not a prediction of the
  lion's next y, so the second gate does no spatial filtering and the
  accept/reject decision is the first test at the snapshot plus the
  held-surface waiver.
CORRECTS: PR-350's paragraph (a), which said the chain "could write
  the third dword" and that the y of the aim is "the controller
  chain's output plus the y-velocity": 0x53e40 writes through edx at
  [edx] = block[0], not the third dword, and for the 155 predicate
  views the chain does not run at all when a surface is held - so the
  aimed y is the seeded 0x98278 + [obj+0xce], not a chain output.
  PR-350's symmetry argument, its zero subtrahend and PR-349's
  measurement point stand.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok); no code, so no red

## PR-352 - THE STANDING QUERY ANSWERS ONE ROW OF A COLUMN, NOT A BAND:
## 0x45380's BRACKET ENDS BEFORE ITS LAST RECORD, THE TWO 0x455a0 CALLS
## BOUND THE SNAPSHOT ROW AND THE AIM ROW APART, AND NO STEP OF
## ZARIA.01'S SEAT CHAIN SATISFIES THEM
```
KIND: port
SUBSYSTEM: F6's standing query, OI-124 - the port's first model of the
  surface ask itself (0x45380's bracket, the flag gate at 0x4540c,
  0x45400's two clearance tests and the incumbent at [obj+0xea]), and
  the leg that drives ZARIA.01's four ANIPL2 seat tables through it.
ADDRESSES: 0x45380, 0x45388, 0x4538c, 0x45393, 0x453a3, 0x453b3,
  0x453b8, 0x453bd, 0x453c4, 0x4540c, 0x45417, 0x45419, 0x4542c,
  0x4542e, 0x45462, 0x45468, 0x4546d, 0x45471, 0x45477, 0x45479,
  0x4547d, 0x4548b, 0x4548d, 0x4548f, 0x45491, 0x45496, 0x45498,
  0x4549a, 0x454a0, 0x454a2, 0x454a8, 0x454b1, 0x454ba, 0x455a0,
  0x455be, 0x455c3, 0x451a6, 0x451db, 0x1e570, 0x1e594, 0x1e970,
  0x1e983, 0x550a0, 0x550aa, 0x96c38, 0x96d1c, 0x8, 0x4, 0xc, 0x89,
  0x8d, 0xa9, 0xe2, 0xe6, 0xea, 0x6c
NAMES: seat_bracket, seat_slope, seat_rec_flag, seat_ask_core,
  surface_ask_selftest, L15, MOV SELFTEST, STANDING QUERY, BRACKET,
  CLEARANCE, SURFACE TABLE, ZARIA.01, ANIPL2, PALMA, KATAPULT,
  PALM.MOV, PALML.MOV, KAT.MOV, A_RUN, OI-124, OI-128, F6,
  pr352_run.log, pr352_build.log
CODE: yes: ported/ll_level.c only - seat_bracket, seat_slope,
  seat_rec_flag and seat_ask_core, the new leg L15
  surface_ask_selftest appended to the --mov-selftest chain, and that
  chain's description string. No new hook, no return code, no Makefile
  or tool change. Nothing in the port's own step calls the model yet.
HOOKS: obj_advance and L14's obj_seat_shift, which L15 uses to move the
  authored tables through a whole row-list cycle, and place_seat_table
  of PR-335, which parses the four authored ANIPL2 lines. The legs
  need no game data.
MEASURED: (a) THE BRACKET 0x45380 IS NOT A RANGE TEST. It answers 0
  when the count at [handle+8] is zero (0x45388), when x is below the
  FIRST record's x (0x45393 `jl` - the only end the function tests),
  or when the scan runs past the count (0x4538c); the scan starts at
  index 1 and 0x453b8 is `jg`, so the first record whose x is GREATER
  than x ends it and that index is the upper member of the pair. The
  leg measures the consequence: a two-record table authored
  18,40;80,40 at 820,435 answers x 838..899 and NOTHING at x 900 -
  the right end of a surface is outside it.
  (b) THE FLAG GATE READS ONE BYTE OF ONE RECORD. 0x4540c-0x45417
  takes the byte at [record 0]+0xc (PR-335's separator grammar) and
  rejects when it exceeds the mode; the leg answers a mode-2 ask on a
  table whose SECOND record carries 2, because record 0's byte is 0 -
  the authored `;` belongs to the pair that FOLLOWS it (PR-344) - and
  no shipped asker passes a mode below that byte (all six pass 2).
  (c) THE TWO CLEARANCE TESTS BOUND TWO DIFFERENT ROWS. c1 is 0x455a0
  with the bracket's own order (record i as A, i-1 as B) at the
  position snapshot [obj+0x89] of PR-349 (0x45462, 0x45468), and
  0x4547d rejects a negative one; the only exemption is 0x45479, which
  compares the handle being asked with [obj+0xa9] (0x45471) - the
  surface the requester already holds, never a new one. c2 is the same
  call with the pair REVERSED (0x4548d, 0x4548f) at the caller's aimed
  block (0x45491): 0x45498 `jg` rejects a positive value, and 0x4549a
  `cmp eax,[edi+0xea]` with 0x454a0 `jg` rejects a value ABOVE the
  incumbent, so 0x454a2/0x454a8 store the MOST NEGATIVE c2 - among
  answerable tables the HIGHEST surface wins. The leg measures that in
  both ask orders.
  (d) THE ACCEPT WINDOW OF A COLUMN IS L2..L1, AND THAT IS NOT A BAND.
  Writing L1 for the line value the first form computes and L2 for the
  second's: 0x4547d needs the requester's row y <= L1 and 0x45498
  needs his aim y >= L2. Both forms interpolate the same line, but
  0x455be `sar edx,31` / 0x455c3 `idiv` truncates toward zero, so L1
  and L2 are the true value or the whole pixel beside it, and the
  answerable rows of that column - taking aim and snapshot at one
  point - are exactly L2..L1, which the sign of the slope can make
  empty, one row, or two. Measured on a 1:2 slope: at x 33 of
  (0,100)-(100,50) the true line is 83.5, L1 = 83 and L2 = 84, and NO
  row of that column answers at all; at x 33 of the mirror
  (0,50)-(100,100) it is 66.5, L1 = 67 and L2 = 66, so y 66 AND y 67
  both answer, with clearances 0 and -1; at x 32 the interpolation is
  exact and only y 84 answers. A floor division or a rounding one
  breaks all three cases, and the leg is the witness. For a LEVEL
  table, which is what every authored seat table is, L1 = L2 = the
  top, so the standing query is exact-contact-only by construction.
  (e) THE FOUR AUTHORED TABLES, UNDER THEIR OWN MOTION. Parsing the
  ANIPL2 lines and running each object's row list to its cycle end
  (L14's path): PALMA at 820,435 stands at x 838..900 y 475 and its
  cycle keeps it at x 838..900 with its top over y 475..482; PALMA at
  965,335 at x 885..947 y 380, cycle x 885..947, top y 380..387;
  PALMA at 1010,275 at x 930..992 y 320, top y 320..327; KATAPULT at
  300,588 at x 307..340 y 633, cycle x 307..382, top y 633..664.
  Every sampled row pair of all four carries the SAME y in both
  records, so paragraph (d) applies exactly. A step from one such
  table to another therefore needs a point inside both brackets with
  the second table's top at the requester's own row: the pairs' top
  bands are 88, 148, 151, 53, 246 and 306 px apart and two of the six
  x spans never overlap, so 0x45400 carries NO step of ZARIA.01's
  authored chain. Only the 0x45479 waiver reaches a surface above the
  requester at all, and it covers one table: the one at [obj+0xa9].
OPENS: what [obj+0xea] holds for a requester before its first accepted
  ask - 0x454a8 is the only writer of a computed value and 0x550a0,
  0x550aa and 0x5481b zero it, and the leg assumes that 0; whether
  0x455a0 is ever asked with B.x == A.x, where `idiv` would fault and
  no guard exists (PR-348's open item, and no shipped table of the
  four has it); what the port should DO with an answer - the winner
  triple [obj+0xe6]/[obj+0xe2]/[obj+0xea] and the class +0xB4 land
  verb of OI-128, which for PALMA is the seat ask verb itself; and
  whether any asker passes a mode other than 2, none having been
  found.
CLOSES: the measuring half of OI-124. Every input of the standing query
  is now in port code, ZARIA.01's four tables have been driven through
  it over their full cycles, and the answer to the question PR-350
  left is no: the standing query is not the carrier of that crossing,
  and no choice of requester position makes it one.
CORRECTS: PR-350's wording that the two sampler calls "measure ONE
  clearance with the pair reversed". They measure the same line but NOT
  the same value: their truncations differ by up to one pixel, which is
  what makes a column answer zero, one or two rows (paragraph (d)), and
  the two gates apply at different points and therefore bound different
  rows. PR-350's assignment of the points, PR-349's snapshot verb and
  PR-344's flag-gate reading stand; PR-336's "keep-the-smaller" rule
  for [obj+0xea] is confirmed and pinned to its instruction pair.
GATE: make 0 warnings; verify-all fixtures rc=0 71 (ok); the same
  suite with DATA=/tmp/opencode/nope HD=/tmp/opencode/nope, and
  verify-docs plus verify-index rc=0. L15 runs inside
  verify-level's `./ll_level --mov-selftest` and prints the numbers of

GATE-FIXTURE-FREE: rc=0 13 (ok) + 23 named - PR-335's shape (13 and

## PR-353 - THE LAND AND LEAVE VERBS +0xB4/+0xB8 ARE ONE SCRIPT DISPATCH

```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: F6's landing half and OI-128's first item - the class verbs

  notice-table family at 0xa0f28 that holds the standing path's second

ADDRESSES: 0x23880, 0x23885, 0x2388c, 0x23893, 0x23896, 0x23899, 0x2389c,

NAMES: land verb, leave verb, script dispatch, current script object,
  notice table, method table family, embedded record, standing query,
  land/leave dispatcher, pr353_census.py, pr353_census.txt,
  pr353_notices.py, pr353_notices.txt, pr353_bodies.py, pr353_bodies.txt,

CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What moves is where
  F6 has to look for a landing effect: it is script code, not engine
  code, for every class the ladder uses.
HOOKS: PR-345's ground-contact verb 0x546a0, which calls the +0xB4 /
  +0xB8 pair when the standing query's answer changes; PR-351's current-
  script accessor at [obj+8]+0x48 and the script object's +0x33 table,
  which the aim chain reaches at 0x5422e/0x5423a; PR-343's message
  poster 0x52b10 and the 0x1b attach; PR-344's embedded handle at
  [obj+0xa5] and the `sub eax,0xc` shape its +0xbc verb used.
MEASURED: (a) THE PAIR IS ONE PAIR. Taking the views the way PR-351 took
  them - a view is a block whose +0x48 slot is the current-script
  accessor 0x23aa0 - there are 186 of them, and 155 install the SAME
  land/leave pair, +0xB4 = 0x238b0 and +0xB8 = 0x23880; the other 31
  install per-class pairs, 31 distinct pairs, and their +0xbc is never
  0x23870. The two sets are IDENTICAL: the views with the script pair
  are exactly the 155 PR-351 found gating the aim chain with the held-
  surface predicate 0x23870 (script /tmp/opencode/pr353_census.py; it
  prints both sets and their equality). So the shipped game ships one
  landing behaviour for everything that asks the standing query, and a
  private one for the 31 that do not - PALMA 0x96c38 at 0x1e560/0x208d0,
  KATAPULT 0x96d1c at 0x22de0/0x20a40, SPLYW 0x96ddc at 0x20ab0/0x20a70
  and the ladder 0x97cdc at 0x23290/0x20230 among them.
  (b) WHAT THE COMMON PAIR DOES - IT IS NOT ENGINE BEHAVIOUR AT ALL.
  0x238b0 and 0x23880 are the same eight instructions and differ only in
  the slot they call: `mov edx,eax` keeps the requester in edx;
  0x238b5/0x23885 `test BYTE PTR [eax+0xb6],0x1` / `jne` skips the whole
  verb when that bit is set; otherwise ebx = [obj+8] (the class view) and
  0x238c3/0x23893 `call DWORD PTR [ebx+0x48]` runs PR-351's accessor
  0x23aa0, eax = its result, and 0x238c6/0x23896 `mov ecx,[eax+0x33]`
  takes the SAME table the aim chain takes at 0x5422e; ebx is then
  loaded with [obj+0x6d] (0x238c9/0x23899) and the verb is
  `call DWORD PTR [ecx+0x4]` for land (0x238cc) or
  `call DWORD PTR [ecx+0x8]` for leave (0x2389c). So for 155 of the 186
  classes - every lion class, KAMIEN and the rest - landing on a surface
  and leaving one are methods of the object's CURRENT SCRIPT OBJECT, at
  slots +4 and +8 of its +0x33 table, called with [obj+0x6d] as the
  argument, and they do not run while [obj+0xb6] bit 0 is set. The
  engine's own land/leave code is a dispatcher: nothing in it raises,
  lowers, carries or releases anything.
  (c) THE 31 PRIVATE PAIRS ARE THE EMBEDDED-RECORD SHAPE. Byte census
  over the first 48 bytes of each (/tmp/opencode/pr353_pair_shapes.py,
  which prints these counts and the two field writes; pr353_bodies.py
  prints the bodies themselves): 29 of the 31 contain
  the step-back `sub eax,0xc` and 29 the test of bit 2 of the argument
  (`test reg,0x4`); in 25 of them one verb carries BOTH, and its shape
  is `push ebx/ecx; mov ecx,edx; sub eax,0xc; mov ebx,eax; test cl,0x4`
  - the object's embedded record stepped back to the containing object
  and a branch on bit 2 of the caller's argument, exactly the shape
  PALMA's +0xbc verb 0x20870 used (PR-350). Two of the extremes show
  what the pair is for when it is not a dispatcher: PALMA's land verb
  0x1e560 is `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0xb1],0; ret` and its leave verb
  0x208d0 is `mov eax,ds:0xcebb8; ret`, a load of a global object
  pointer; KATAPULT's land verb 0x22de0 is `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0xbd],0;
  ret`. Those are one-word state resets, not motion.
  (d) THE SECOND DISPATCHER AND THE ONE DATA SLOT THAT NAMES IT. 0x45cb0
  is: push ebx/ecx, ecx = eax (the surface handle), ebx = edx, `call
  0x457e0`, then 0x45cbb `cmp DWORD PTR [ecx+8],0` - the record COUNT of
  PR-335's grammar - and it calls the requester's +0xB4 at 0x45cc6 when
  the count is non-zero and its +0xB8 at 0x45cd4 when it is zero, both
  through [[edx]+8]. 0x457e0 walks [x] to the object the handle names and
  calls [[that]+4]. No instruction names 0x45cb0 - no xref row has it as
  a destination and no immediate operand carries it - and no dword in the
  image holds 0x45cb1 at all. Exactly ONE dword names 0x45cb0: the data
  slot 0xa10ac, which is slot +4 of the record headed 0xa10a8 - the same
  block the constructors store at [obj+4] as 0xa10a8 (0x46584, 0x465db,
  0x4756b, 0x4791c; 0x46ac1 stores 0xa1060 the same way, and 0xa1000,
  0xa1030 and 0xa10a8 give 14 such sites in the imm table). That block is
  a run of six-dword records at stride 0x18 - /tmp/opencode/pr353_notices.py
  finds 25 of them from 0xa0f28 to 0xa11e8, each {a method at +0, a
  notice verb at +4, 0x45800, 0x45870, 0x458e0, a method at +0x14}, and
  the +4 verbs are all distinct: 0x45750, 0x459b0, 0x459d0 ... 0x45cb0,
  0x45ce0, 0x45d10.
  In the SAME family, the record headed 0xa1060 carries the verb 0x45d10
  at slot +4, and 0x45d10 posts the ATTACH message 0x1b at 0x45d28 to
  the object at [[arg]] and then posts value 1 (0x45d3a) with
  [x+0xc]/[x+8]; the record headed 0xa1078 carries 0x45ce0, which posts
  value 1 the same way at 0x45cfd. So the attach of PR-343 and
  PR-347, the message that is the only writer of the attachment apart
  from the standing query itself, and the land-or-leave decision itself
  are records of one installed table.
  (e) WHAT THAT LEAVES FOR F6. A landing lion runs script code (b); the
  seat classes' own pair only clears a field (c); the standing path's
  second dispatcher only tells the requester that it is on or off a
  surface (d). No engine code moves anything at landing, so the
  crossing of ZARIA.01's first chasm is either a scripted chain reached
  through the script object's +0x33 table, or the 0x1b attach path of
  this table family, or the .plt ground of T6 - which is what OI-124
  now points at.
OPENS: what the script object's +0x33 table is and who fills it - the
  same slot the aim chain reaches, and now the landing and leaving
  methods too; what [obj+0x6d] is, the value handed to those methods,

  without the step-back shape (0x1e560/0x208d0, 0x22de0/0x20a40,

CLOSES: OI-128's first named item - the bodies of the land and leave

CORRECTS: PR-343's fourth 0x1b poster, "0x45d28 is a method stored only
  at the data slot 0xa11d0". 0x45d28 is not a method entry but the call
  instruction inside the method 0x45d10, and 0x45d10 sits at 0xa1064,

  0x54f90, 0x54fe0 and 0x55020 are one body with different tests:
  0x54f40 and 0x54f90 ask [view+0xBC] first (0x54f4a, 0x54f9a) and skip
  when it answers nonzero, and all four then test bits of [obj+0xB6];
  when the test allows it they run the current script object's +0x33
  slot +4 (the land
  method, the call at 0x54f78 in 0x54f40 and 0x55054 in 0x55020) or
  slot +8 (the leave method, 0x54fc8 in 0x54f90 and 0x5500b in
  0x54fe0), each time through PR-351's
  [view+0x48] accessor and [view+0x50] aim pair, and then they write
  the byte: 0x54f40 sets bit 0x01 at 0x54f7b, 0x54f90 clears it at
  0x54fcb, 0x54fe0 sets 0x03 at 0x5500e after calling the LEAVE method,
  and 0x55020 calls the LAND method only when bits 0x01 and 0x02 are
  both set and then clears both with `and 0xfc` at 0x55057. So bit 0x01
  is the script's own "I am standing" state, maintained by the runner
  the `lock`/`ground_on` verbs call, and bit 0x02 is the extra flag the
  `2` variants add: `lock2`/`unlock2` build the 0xa10c0 node, whose verb
  runs 0x54fe0 to put the object out of the standing state and 0x55020
  to put it back. Bit 0x20 is the one `atc_on`/`atc_off` write and the
  one the 0x52660 thunk clears (`and [eax+0xb6],0xdf` at 0x5266c, after
  running 0x54f90 on the object at [obj]) - that thunk sits at state-
  table slots +0xf8 to +0x1e8 of 16 views (0x97bc0, 0x98cc4, 0x9916c,
  0x9a778, 0x9b4d4, 0x9f298 among them, found by pr354_views.py).
  (e) THE GATE THE RUNNERS ASK, AND THE BIT THE SCRIPT WRITES. 0x54f40
  and 0x54f90 ask [view+0xBC] first and skip the script method when it
  answers nonzero; for the views that carry the script-dispatch pair that
  slot is 0x23870, `cmp [obj+0xa9],0; setne` - PR-351's held-surface
  answer, the same field the standing query keeps. The bit predicate of
  this byte is a DIFFERENT slot: 0x23860, `mov eax,[obj+0xb6]; shl
  eax,0x1a; shr eax,0x1f` - bit 0x20 - and the mtable census in
  /tmp/opencode/pr354_views.py finds it at slot +0x40 of 116 of the 189
  class tables, always with 0x23850 at +0x04 and 0x23870 at +0xBC. That
  slot is asked at 0x550cf and 0x55262, in verbs of their own (0x550c0
  combines it with [view+0x70] and two calls of 0x52d30 and answers a
  signed comparison), so bit 0x20 - the bit `atc_on`/`atc_off` write and
  the bit 0x546a0's tail sets (PR-345) and the 0x52660 thunk clears -
  gates those, not the land and leave runners.
  (f) WHAT THE LANDING ARGUMENT IS. The land/leave pair passes
  [obj+0x6d] to the script methods (PR-353). The verbs that write that
  field are ldir's 0x459f0 - `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x6d],0xffffffff` at
  0x459fa - and rdir's 0x45a10, which is PR-320's read and PR-321's
  modelled pair; so the script's land and leave methods are called with
  the object's facing direction, which the level script sets with
  `ldir`/`rdir`.
OPENS: what the script object's +0x33 table is and who fills it, now

- WHY. The owner asked to load the ledger into a database so a search
  is cheap at every step. The index already answers "which records
  mention key X" (PR-197's docs/RE_INDEX.md), but it is a flat page:
  it returns PR numbers, not jump-to-line ranges, and it cannot do
  free-text plus kind/supersession filters in one step. This PR adds
  that query layer WITHOUT replacing the pinned index and WITHOUT
  becoming a second source of truth. The one property that makes it
  safe is the one PR-197 argued for: ONE parser. re_db.py imports
  doc_census and re_index and reuses their regexes and their
  real-heading record boundary; it defines no new vocabulary. A second
  parser is the PR-55 "twins that both look right but drift" failure.

- WHAT SHIPPED. (1) tools/re_db.py: reads NEXT_STEPS.md through
  re_index.records() and doc_census's record boundary, and emits a
  SQLite file build/journal.db (gitignored, like build/*.raw) with a
  records table (pr, kind, start/end lines), an FTS5 table over record
  text, and addr/field/name/oi/corrections/pr_cites link tables. The
  field block itself supplies the columns (KIND/SUBSYSTEM/CORRECTS are
  already structured). (2) tools/jq.py: a query CLI that rebuilds the
  DB first if NEXT_STEPS.md is newer (it can never answer from a stale
  index), auto-routes a bare token (0x->addr, [->field, OI->oi,
  PR->show, else free-text), and prints one line per hit -
  `PR-nn [kind]  NEXT_STEPS.md:START-END` - so the reader opens that
  slice instead of the 49k-line file. (3) The journal-db Makefile leg,
  called from verify-docs, so the search layer is regenerated whenever
  the docs structure is checked. (4) .gitignore: build/journal.db.

- IT SHARES THE PARSER, AND THAT IS MEASURED. Both tools read the
  whole tree. re_index reports 339 records; re_db parses 339 records
  (340 with this one) from the SAME boundary, and reuses doc_census's
  ADDR_RE/FIELD_RE/NAME_RE/DES_RE verbatim. The DB is never cmp-pinned
  (it is untracked), so the guarantee is not byte-identity but this:
  every record the index sees, re_db sees, because it calls re_index
  and doc_census. The DB is a derived artifact and a client of jq.py
  is a client of that - nothing here can read a different ledger than
  `make verify-docs` and `make verify-index` do.

- THE OI-102 CLOSURE, MEASURED. OI-102 (PR-197 OPENS) said the
  index's correction pointers "stay prose-co-occurrence until records
  carry a CORRECTS: line the generator can read," and noted records
  HAVE carried CORRECTS: lines since PR-198 but "the generator upgrade
  never happened." On this tree re_index flags correction pointers on
  71 address entries by matching an address and a correction word on
  one physical line - sparse, direction-agnostic. The structured
  CORRECTS: field the records actually write encodes 147 correction
  edges across the 340 records. re_db parses that field into a
  corrections table and jq.py `corr PR-nn` walks it: it shows both
  that PR-350 corrects PR-349 and that PR-351 and PR-352 correct
  PR-350. The generator now reads the field, exactly what OI-102
  asked for, so OI-102 flips CLOSED in this same commit. re_index is
  left unchanged: the field-graph is an addition beside it, not a
  rewrite of its prose heuristic.

- CONTROLS (data-free, /tmp/opencode/pr355_control.py, no fixtures,
  no window; a synthetic two-record ledger). C1: re_db parses 2 records
  and reads the correction edge (10 -> PR-9) straight from the
  CORRECTS: field. C2: an address shared by the two records is linked
  to BOTH, so the mention graph is queryable. Mutation 1: rewrite the
  field to CORRECTS: none and the edge disappears. Mutation 2: break
  the field name (CORRECT:) and no edge is read - the parser follows
  the exact field name, not a stem, exactly as P4 requires. The two
  mutations are the red-check: the count moves only when the field
  does.

- WHAT IT IS NOT. Not the source of truth: docs/RE_INDEX.md stays the
  pinned, git-diffable human index; journal.db is a disposable build
  product and re-indexing is unchanged. No vector/embedding store:
  the ledger's whole discipline is exact tokens and citations, and FTS5
  plus the structured fields match that; an embedding model would add a
  dependency and fuzzy recall that contradicts "name the evidence or
  stop." jq.py `corr` reads only the structured CORRECTS: field, not
  prose retractions that were never marked - the same honest limit
  OI-102 named, now resolved for marked claims only. The kind and
  supersession filters cover records >= PR-196 only, because earlier
  records predate the field block (P4's TEMPLATE_FROM); that is the
  correct behavior, not a bug.

- WHY. PR-355 built the search layer but declared indexes only on the
  four vocabulary tables (addr/field/name/oi). Checking the generated
  DB with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN showed jq.py's other hot paths were full
  table SCANs: the correction graph (`corr PR-nn` walking corrections by
  `pr` and by `corrects`), resolving a PR number to its Read range
  (`show`, `records WHERE pr=?`), and the PR-citation walk
  (`pr_cites`). The tables are small (340 records, 147 correction
  edges) so those scans were sub-millisecond and correct - but a layer
  meant to be queried at every step should seek, not scan, and the
  schema was simply unfinished.

- WHAT SHIPPED. re_db.py's create_schema gains eight indexes on top of
  the four that already exist: ix_corr_out on corrections(pr) and
  ix_corr_in on corrections(corrects) (the `corr` graph both ways);
  ix_rec_pr on records(pr) (`show` resolving a PR to its line range);
  ix_cite / ix_cite_pr on pr_cites(cited) and pr_cites(pr); and
  ix_addr_rid / ix_field_rid / ix_name_rid on the mention tables' rid
  so the mention->record join and a per-record lookup seek instead of
  scan. The FTS5 index (record_fts) was already a real inverted index;
  nothing there changed. Twelve explicit indexes total now.

- CONTROL + MUTATION (data-free, /tmp/opencode/pr356_index_control.py;
  it reads only the GENERATED build/journal.db, no fixtures and no
  window). It runs EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on all six hot paths and asserts
  each names its index - ix_addr, ix_corr_out, ix_corr_in, ix_rec_pr,
  ix_cite_pr, and the FTS VIRTUAL TABLE INDEX - and that none falls
  back to SCAN of the driving table. MUTATION: copying the DB and
  dropping ix_corr_in makes `corr PR-350` reverse the plan to
  `SCAN corrections`, so the assertion has teeth (it fails when an
  index is missing). This is the red-check for a schema change: the
  plan is the observable, and it moves only with the index.

- WHAT IS UNCHANGED. The query results are byte-identical - an index
  changes the plan, never the answer - so the PR-355 numbers in its
  record (340 records, 147 correction edges, the 71-vs-147 contrast)
  all still hold. The layer is still a client of the ledger, never a
  source of truth: docs/RE_INDEX.md and P4 are untouched, the DB stays
  gitignored, and jq.py's readers are unchanged. README now documents
  the layer (it was undocumented before): a make-target line in the
  verify legend and a "Searching the ledger" subsection that states it
  is a tool, not a document, so it is not part of the P5 closed set.

CODE: no: nothing in ported/ or the Makefile moved. What changes is the
  meaning of PR-353's and PR-354's dispatch: there is no script method
  at the end of that chain, and the port's own .SEQ reader already
  parses the four words the pair uses.
HOOKS: PR-255, which named 0xa0c08 ("the frame records' shared method
  block") and ported its slot +0 verb as live_box - this pass reads the
  two verbs next to it; PR-353's +0xB4/+0xB8 pair and PR-354's four
  runners, which all end at these two methods; PR-351's [view+0x48]
  accessor 0x23aa0, followed to the end this time; PR-350's ask block
  0x541f0 and its "unmodelled transform", now named; PR-308's +0xB0
  provider 0x544d0 and its "the caller's buffer gets [obj+0x00] and
  [obj+0x04] - the live position"; PR-316's +0x54 frame-step verb and
  the [obj+0x89] pair; PR-321's modelled ldir/rdir, which is the sign
  the pair reads; and the port's own .SEQ grammar in ported/ll_seq.h,
  which already lists FUN_00043e70, FUN_00041ef0, FUN_00041f60, the
  f0/f2/f4/f6 words and the 0x7fff sentinel.
MEASURED: (a) THE +0x33 WORD HAS ONE WRITER AND ONE VALUE. Over the
  whole instruction index the only place that stores a dword at +0x33 is
  0x41f4d, `mov DWORD PTR [ebx+0x33],0xa0c08` (the /tmp/opencode/
  pr357_33chain.py query is `select ... from insn where ops like
  '%+0x33]'`, 42 sites read it, none writes it except this one). It is
  the last field of a 0x37-byte record - 0x33 + 4 = 0x37 - allocated at
  0x43f59 `mov eax,0x37; call 0x5c320` inside 0x43e70, and 0x43f69
  calls 0x41ef0 on it with the stream reader in edx. That is the .SEQ
  element record, exactly as ported/ll_seq.h describes it ("the game
  loads a whole .SEQ record payload ... FUN_00043e70 + FUN_0005c6b0,
  then parses `count` elements (FUN_00041ef0 -> FUN_00041f60 ...)"),
  so the table is 0xa0c08, the block PR-255 named, and its eleven
  entries run 0xa0c08 = 0x42930 (the live box), 0x42980, 0x429d0,
  0x42a20, 0x421f0, 0x42230, 0x422f0, 0x423c0, 0x42480, 0x42210,
  0x442f0, with 0 at 0xa0c34.
  (b) THE ANCHOR WORDS ARE READ STRAIGHT OUT OF THE .SEQ BLOB. The
  element initializer 0x41ef0 stamps the sentinels - `mov WORD PTR
  [eax],0x7fff` at 0x41ef3, the same at +0x4 (0x41ef8) and +0x8
  (0x41f01) - zeroes from +0x15 up, zeroes [x+0x2f] at 0x41f44,
  installs the table at 0x41f4d, and calls the reader 0x41f60. That
  reader takes w0 into a stack temp (0x41f7c, which is the word its own
  later tests mask with 0x4, 0x3, 0x8, 0x2, 0x1), reads the shape-frame
  words through 0x41d40 at [x+0x15], then `mov edx,ecx` at 0x41f96 and
  the stream verb `call [edi+0x1c]` at 0x41f9d read 2 bytes into [x+0]
  = f0; the same call with edx = ecx+0x2 (0x41fa3), +0x4 (0x41fb9) and
  +0x6 (0x41fd0) fills f2, f4 and f6, and under w0&4 it continues at
  +0x8 (0x41fec) and +0xa (0x42002). Then 0x42015: with w0&3 it reads
  the shape margins through 0x41da0 and calls 0x420b0, ELSE it derives
  the box from the anchors right there - [x+0xc] = -(f0 or 0) at
  0x42030-0x42040, [x+0xe] = -(f2 or 0) at 0x42044-0x4205c,
  [x+0x10] = (b19*0x50 + b15) at 0x42058-0x42072, [x+0x12] = b17 at
  0x42076, and [x+0x14] = w0&8 at 0x4207e-0x42083. So the DRAW anchor
  the port already applies (ll_seq_anchor_origin, "x -= f0, y -= f2,
  BOTH skipped when f0 holds the 0x7fff ctor sentinel") and the box
  fields come from the same four words as the landing shift.
  (c) THE PAIR, INSTRUCTION BY INSTRUCTION. 0x42980 (slot +4, the LAND
  method) is: `movsx ecx,WORD PTR [eax]` / `cmp ecx,0x7fff` /
  `je 0x429c1` - an element whose f0 is the sentinel moves nothing -
  then esi = f2 - f6 and `sub DWORD PTR [edx+4],esi`, then by the sign
  of ebx (0x429a0 `test ebx,ebx` / `jle`): eax = f0 - f4 applied as
  `sub DWORD PTR [edx],eax` when ebx > 0 and as `add` of the same
  value when ebx <= 0. 0x429d0 (slot +8, the LEAVE method) is the same
  eight instructions with add and sub exchanged: `add DWORD PTR
  [ecx+4],esi` at 0x429ec, `add DWORD PTR [edx],eax` at 0x429fb for a
  positive facing, `sub ebp,eax` at 0x42a0d for the other. eax = the
  element, edx = the position
  pair, ebx = the facing sign. Read together: landing translates the
  position by (f4 - f0, f6 - f2) - the vector from the element's first
  anchor to its second - with the X leg negated when the facing is not
  positive, and leaving translates it back. Nothing else is touched: no
  flag, no counter, no velocity.
  (d) WHO RUNS THE TWO METHODS - A TEN-SITE LIST, NOT A SCRIPT. The
  /tmp/opencode/pr357_33chain.py census walks every `mov <reg>,[base
  +0x33]` to the first call through that register: 42 sites read the
  word; five reach slot +4 - 0x238c6 in 0x238b0 (the class +0xB4 verb
  of PR-353's 155 views), 0x53e2b in 0x53df0 (the +0x54 frame-step verb
  PR-316 named, at [0x97cdc+0x54] among others), 0x5422e in 0x541f0
  (PR-350's ask block), 0x54f6a in 0x54f40 and 0x55046 in 0x55020
  (PR-354's `ground_on`/`lock` and `unlock2` runners) - and five reach
  slot +8 - 0x2389c in 0x23880 (the class +0xB8 verb), 0x3c38a in
  0x3c330 (a private verb, at +0x78 of one table 0xa0524 only), 0x5452e
  in 0x544d0 (PR-308's +0xB0 point provider), 0x54fc8 in 0x54f90 and
  0x54ffd in 0x54fe0 (the OFF and `lock2` runners). The other slots of
  the same block: +0xc is a second reader like 0x41f60 but calling
  0x42800 for the shape frame (3 sites), +0x10 has 12 sites (ten of
  them 0x446d2-0x448a7 inside one function), +0x14 has 9 (0x5ece7,
  0x5f08b, 0x60a10 and others), +0x1c and +0x28 one each, and slot +0
  is read at 0x5350b, which is PR-255's live-box builder 0x534e0. The
  pair is never reached from the level-script builder: it is engine
  code.
  (e) THE ARGUMENT IS EITHER THE LIVE POSITION OR A COPY OF IT. 0x238b0
  passes `mov edx,eax` (the object) at 0x238b3, and 0x54f40/0x54f90/
  0x54fe0/0x55020 pass the object too - so for the class verbs and the
  script commands the shift lands on [obj+0x00]/[obj+0x04], which
  PR-308 established is the live position (0x544f6-0x54500 copies
  exactly that pair into the caller's buffer). 0x53df0 first copies the
  pair: `mov eax,[edx]` / `mov [esi],eax` and the same at +4, with esi
  = `lea esi,[edx+0x89]` (0x53dfa-0x53e0d), then asks [view+0x48] and
  calls slot +4 with edx = &[obj+0x89] - the [obj+0x89] pair PR-316
  saw as the v-channel copy. 0x541f0 and 0x3c330 pass a block on their
  own frame, and 0x3c38d sets ebx = 1 there, i.e. an always-right-facing
  query. So the same method both moves the object and offsets a
  position a test is about to use.
  (f) THE SIGN ARGUMENT, CONFIRMED AS THE AUTHORED FACING. 0x238b0 and
  0x23880 load it as `mov ebx,DWORD PTR [edx+0x6d]` (0x238c9, 0x23899)
  - the word `rdir` sets to 1 and `ldir` to -1, PR-316 and PR-320 -
  while 0x54f40, 0x54f90, 0x54fe0, 0x55020, 0x541f0, 0x544d0 and
  0x53df0 ask the class +0x50 verb instead (0x53e40 in the lion's
  table, PR-255's mirror-bit answer, -1 when [element+0x14] is set and
  [obj+0x6d] == -1). Both forms are used only as `test ebx,ebx`, so the
  pair cares only about the sign, exactly like the box verb 0x42930's
  `test ecx,ecx`. The /tmp/opencode/pr357_slots.py census confirms the
  table-side framing: 0x238b0 and 0x23880 sit at +0xB4/+0xB8 of 116 of
  the 189 constructor-proven class tables, 0x53db0 at +0x94 of 140 and
  0x53e40 at +0x50 of 140.
OPENS: whether any SHIPPED element carries a second anchor at all - the
  measurement is the same one ll_seq_anchor_origin already needs: over
  every .SEQ payload, how many elements have f0 != 0x7fff and
  (f4,f6) != (f0,f2), and which kinds (the seat and animal elements are

CLOSES: PR-350's OPENS - "what the controller chain (+0x48, +0x50 and

CORRECTS: PR-353 and PR-354, both from the same week: they call the
  holder of +0x33 "the current script object" and say the land and leave

- WHY. The layer was field-tested by a second session working a real
  thread (it used `jq free "+0x33"` to reach PR-255/PR-308; that
  read landed as PR-357). Its report named two sharp edges. Both were
  checked against the generated DB before changing anything.

- THE OI GAP (a real inconsistency I introduced). `re_db` fed
  `oi_refs` from ONLY the OPENS:/CLOSES: fields. But records name OI
  ids in prose far more often: measured 51 distinct OI ids appear in
  record bodies (the bodies include the fields, so they subsume them)
  against 29 ids in the structured fields, 361 prose mentions in all.
  OI-128 specifically: 6 records name it, only 2 in OPENS/CLOSES, so
  `jq oi` reported 2 of 6 - while the same tool indexes
  addresses/names/fields from body text. That double standard was the
  bug. The fix mirrors how those other vocabularies already work: a new
  `oi_mentions(pr,rid,oi)` table filled from `dc.OI_MEN_RE.findall(body)`
  - the SAME regex `make verify-docs` P6 uses to resolve OI citations,
  so there is still one definition of "a mention" - with ix_oi_men, and
  the `oi` verb now reports prose mentions plus the structured
  opens/closes graph, marking which is which.

- A THIRD, UNREPORTED BUG, found while checking the above. `oi_refs.oi`
  stores the bare number (`128`), but `v_oi` matched the raw arg
  (`OI-128`) as a string, so `jq oi OI-128` returned 0 - it missed even
  the 2 structured rows (only `jq oi 128` hit them). `v_oi` now strips
  the id to digits and compares by integer, so OI-128, OI-128 and 128
  all resolve. OI-128 now returns its full 6 records.

- THE SHORT-HEX EDGE (correct behaviour, misleading answer). The split
  is right and shared with the pinned index: `doc_census.ADDR_RE` is
  `0x[0-9a-fA-F]{4,6}`, so `0x33`/`0x8` are not address keys - only
  the bracket form `[obj+0x33]` is a field token. I did NOT change
  ADDR_RE (it would silently move RE_INDEX and the P1/P3 counts - the
  "never change acceptance to make a leg pass" rule). The defect was
  only that `jq addr 0x33` answered a question that cannot exist with a

  that found the thread - `field [obj+0x33]` is only 2 records), and an
  explicit `jq addr <short>` prints a hint pointing to free/field.

  paths seek not scan); dropping an index still flips a plan back to
  SCAN, so it has teeth.

  layer keeps reading through the shared parser, so it still cannot see
  a different ledger than the index and `make verify-docs` do. Results
  for every other verb are byte-identical; docs/RE_INDEX.md and P4 are
  untouched; build/journal.db stays a gitignored client, never a source
  of truth. README's "Searching the ledger" note now states the OI
  prose door and the short-hex split so a user hits them knowingly.

  (b) THE SENTINEL, ONE METHOD AT A TIME. land alone and leave alone are

  immediately: the position goes to (-32667,100), i.e. an unguarded
  0x7fff is read as an anchor 32767 px to the left.
  (c) THE STEP AND ITS EXACT INVERSE, THREE FACINGS. Over element 1
  (f2-f6 = 12, f0-f4 = -20): facing +1 -> (120,88), facing -1 ->
  (80,88), facing 0 -> (80,88), because 0x429a0 is `test ebx,ebx`/`jle`
  and ZERO takes the left-hand branch. Leaving with the same facing
  returns (100,100) in all three. Landing facing right and leaving facing
  LEFT ends at (140,100): the y leg cancels, the x leg does not, because
  the engine passes the sign fresh at every call ([obj+0x6d] in
  0x238b0/0x23880, the +0x50 verb in the other six sites, PR-357
  paragraph (f)) and never remembers it. The leg prints that pair as a
  number rather than leaving it as an implication.

  table (838,463)-(900,463) - the same two records L15 measures on
  ZARIA.01's lower PALMA, moved 12 px up so the case is a clean
  off-by-12. Asked from (890,475): refused, seat_slope gives 463-475 =
  -12 at 0x45477 and the 0x45479 waiver covers only [obj+0xa9]. Land
  through element 2, whose second anchor is 12 px above its first with
  the same x: the point becomes (890,463) and the SAME law answers
  (c1 = c2 = 0, the incumbent test at 0x454a0 accepts 0). Leave: back to
  (890,475) and refused again. Then the mirrored leg: the same landing
  through element 1 facing right ends at (910,463) - past the table's

  landing step decides WHICH surface the standing query can see at all:
  the element's second anchor is a placement offset for the object, not a
  drawing detail.
