  per polyline of the same class family that 37 object classes own at
  [obj+0xee]; 0x45380 brackets a query x in it (no answer when x is
  outside the first or last record) and 0x453d0 hands out the two

  (e) THE LIVE TABLE. tools/golden_surface_read.py against the PR-390
  disk-D rig at icount shift 8, ZARIA.01 started from the chapter map by

  (f) THE IMAGE ADDRESSING, CHECKED BECAUSE THE TWO RULES IN THE REPO
  LOOK ALIKE. `build/leo/leo.img` is flat from 0x10000 (build/leo/leo.json
  `"image": ["0x10000","0xd76d0"]`), so its file offset is VA - 0x10000;
  "VA - 0xf000" is the rule for the raw LEO.EXE text sweep. The two
  differ by 0x1000, and a string read under the wrong one still returns
  plausible text: image offset 0x9182d - 0xf000 spells "its.is" where the
  VA 0x9182d holds "%d". Every string address in this block was read at
  VA - 0x10000, and the string addresses the earlier records name
  (0x9182d "%d", 0x91830 " %c", 0x91834 ";", 0x91d0f "%d,%d") re-read
  correctly under that rule, so PR-334/371/389/390 need no correction
  here. PR-338's CLOSED OI-124 row is the earlier instance of the mistake.
```

- WHY. OI-128 and the F6 thread ask what the lion stands on, and PR-390
  followed a handle into an anonymous 45-element array. This says what
  that array is: the authored ground file, byte for byte, with the
  separator after each point carried into a per-point byte. The port
  already measures its own actors against the level's line list
  (`ll_plt_first_below`), so the geometry law is not what was missing -
  what was missing is that the engine keeps the authoring separator
  (0/1/2) as data, and the only ground line ZARIA.01's lion ever stands
  on is one of the seven that carry 0 there.

- WHAT SURPRISED ME. That a separator character survives into runtime as
  a flag at all, and that the byte 0x45258 tests belongs to the FIRST
  point of the line, not to a lookup result: for line 0 the author's
  choice of '!' over ';' is what that test reads. And that the last
  point of all 45 lines keeps an uninitialized byte, in a structure the
  engine otherwise fills completely.

MEASURED: (a) WHO RUNS THE QUERY. 0x546a0 is stored at +0xAC of 155 class
  tables (155 of 155 stores are 4-aligned; the authored lion tables all
  carry it: 0x96874 -> 0x96920, 0x9a134, 0x9ad48, 0x9e740, and
  TLewZaria 0x96960 -> 0x96a0c). It opens by testing [obj+0xB6] bit 0x02
  (0x546ac) and jumps to 0x54804 when set - the `lock2` flag skips the
  whole query but still runs the position carry of (g).
  (b) THE MODE AND WHERE IT COMES FROM. eax = [[obj+0x50]+[obj+0x5c]*4]
  and the dword read at [[eax]+0x12] (0x546b9-0x546c2), tested a byte at a
  time - OI-078 already names that word as the current state's control
  word and its two bits as the mode selectors; what is added here is the
  instruction-level shape of the three cases and what each one calls. Bit
  0x4000 of that word (`test ah,0x40`, 0x546c5) runs
  0x4b600 with ecx = 0 (0x546c5 falls through to 0x546d3); if the bit is
  clear, bit 0x0100 runs 0x4b600 with ecx = 2 (0x54706 -> 0x5470b); with
  stands. Those two bits are not unnamed: the `.MOV` parser ORs them from
  the tokens `CHECK_BASE_LN` (0x4000) and `CHECK_LN` (0x0100) at
  0x51b0d-0x51e07 (PR-99's table, in tools/re/mov_channels.py), so the
  engine's own authoring vocabulary calls the ground query a base-line
  check or a line check, and the mode says which one was asked for. Read
  to the end, the two branches differ ONLY in the mode argument and the
  stack buffers: bit 0x4000 runs 0x4b600 at 0x546d7 into [esp+0x20],
  0x4b430 at 0x546f0 into [esp+0x30] and 0x4b7f0 at 0x5474b into
  [esp+0x40]; bit 0x0100 runs 0x4b600 at 0x54719 into [esp], 0x4b430 at
  0x54732 into [esp+0x50] and the same 0x4b7f0 into [esp+0x10]; and
  every one of those six calls is followed by 0x49580 with eax = the
  caller's blob, ebx = the object and edx = the result - that is how the
  answer triple reaches the signal set. Both query calls take the world
  pointer from the global ds:0xcef40 - the slot the rig reads as the
  world anchor, 0x16c000 + 0xcef40 = 0x23af40. 0x4b600 has exactly two
  call sites, 0x546d7 and 0x54719.
  (c) WHAT 0x4b600 DOES, the read that row named as next. 0x4b616 sets
  ecx = the class view 0x98278 and 0x4b62c calls the aim filler 0x541f0,
  which leaves a point pair at [esp]/[esp+4]; 0x4b638-0x4b64b ADD the
  previous step's clamp delta [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] to that point;
  0x4b64f-0x4b669, when a surface is held, call the held element's clamp
  verb `[class+0x8]` = 0x45250 with ecx = 2 and that point; and
  0x4b66c-0x4b6a8 walk the level's ground table: count = [[world]+0x80]
  (skip when <= 0), eax = [world+0x74] + i*0xc, push the threshold 0, and
  `call [element class + 0x1c]` = 0x45400 with ecx = the mode, ebx = the
  point, edx = the object (the `push 0` shifts the stack, so the saved
  mode is read at [esp+0x14] and the point at [esp+0x4] after it). The
  stride is 0xc and the bound is [world+0x80], so in ZARIA.01 every
  ground query calls 0x45400 once per polyline of ZARIA_A.PLT, 45 times,
  over exactly the array PR-391 read.
  (d) THE CANDIDATE LAW, 0x45400 - one direct call site, 0x4536f inside
  the contact-list verb 0x45320; everything else reaches it through
  +0x1c. 0x4540c reads the byte at [record 0 + 0xc] and 0x45417
  `cmp eax,ecx; jg 0x454c0` returns when it is above the mode: the same
  comparison the clamp verb makes at 0x45258. A flag-0 line ('!') answers
  every mode; a flag-1 line (';') answers only mode >= 1; a flag-2 line
  ('#') only mode 2 - and no '#' is authored anywhere (PR-391), so the
  shipped separator choice IS the query filter. Then 0x45423 asks 0x45380
  for the first record index i at or past the query x (0 -> return);
  0x45439 calls the asker's own +0x6c verb (eax = the object, edx = the
  record index) and its result is the point for the FIRST clearance - in
  186 of the 186 class views that verb is 0x23a10, `add eax,0x89; ret`
  (PR-351's census), so what the ask samples first is the CLAMP SAMPLE
  PAIR [obj+0x89]/[obj+0x8d] that 0x45250 writes at 0x4526a-0x452c4, and
  the 0x4b669 call above may have filled it a few instructions earlier in
  the SAME query. 0x455a0 computes the clearance, and read instruction by
  instruction it is exactly A.y + idiv((qx-A.x) * (B.y-A.y), B.x-A.x) -
  qy, the line's y at the query x minus the query y (0x455a3-0x455cd, the
  divide at 0x455c3; eax = A, edx = B, ebx = the point). 0x4546d-0x4547f:
  if this element is NOT the one at [obj+0xa9] (0x45479 `cmp esi,ebx` and
  0x4547b `je 0x45481` skip the test for the held one) and that first
  clearance minus the pushed threshold is negative, the candidate is
  refused. Then 0x45481-0x45491 computes it a second time through the same
  0x455a0 against the SAME record pair - both calls put array + (i-1)*13
  in eax and array + i*13 in edx; the first builds them across the stack
  slots at 0x45443-0x45464, the second in registers at 0x45481-0x4548f -
  and only ebx differs, 0x4548b `mov ebx,ebp` restoring the point the
  CALLER passed, saved at 0x4540a. So the two calls measure one segment
  at TWO points: the snapshot pair for the first gate, the caller's point
  for everything that is kept. It is the second value that is tested and
  stored: any clearance above 0 is refused (0x45496) and any clearance
  above the current best [obj+0xea] is refused (0x4549a), so a candidate
  must sit at or below the caller's point and beat the incumbent. The
  winner is stored at 0x454a2-0x454ba:
  [obj+0xe6] = the element, [obj+0xea] = the clearance, and [obj+0xe2] =
  the flag byte of the record at index i-1, read as `[ecx+array+0xc]`.
  (e) THE CLAMP, 0x45250, the same mode gate at 0x45258. If the query x
  is left of record 0 (0x4526a), write record 0's x,y into
  [obj+0x89]/[obj+0x8d] and the offsets into [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce];
  otherwise take the LAST record, addressed as array + [element+8] * 13
  (0x45293-0x45297: PR-391's record count, times the 13-byte record
  stride), and if the query x is right of it (0x4529f) write that
  endpoint and the offsets. For an x between the endpoints nothing is
  written. 0x4b600 calls it with mode 2, so for the held surface the gate
  never fires. The offsets are read by 0x4b638 BEFORE that call, which
  means a mode-2 query sees the clamp the mode-0 query of the same +0xAC
  verb just made, and the carry of (g) then applies and clears them.
  (f) THE ANSWER IS BRANCHED ON, at 0x54759-0x547d5, and the branches are
  the signals of PR-313. No answer ([obj+0xe6] = 0): run the held
  element's +0x4 verb, clear [obj+0xa9], run the object's class +0xB8
  (PR-353's leave verb), and set signal byte 2 bit 0x4 = AC_ONAIR
  (0x54800). Answer flag 2 and [obj+0xc6] >= 0x58c: the same detach path
  (0x5476f `jge`) - [obj+0xc6] is the signed v_y and 0x58c its terminal
  value, so a flag-2 line lets go at terminal fall. Nothing held: set
  signal byte 0 bit 0x10 (AC_DUP), attach [obj+0xa9] = the answer, call
  the element's +0 verb, then call the object's class +0xB4, PR-353's
  land verb (0x54785-0x5479f). A DIFFERENT surface held: run the old
  element's +0x4, re-attach, run the new element's +0, with no signal at
  all (0x547a7-0x547c6). And 0x547c8: if the answer flag is not 0, set
  signal byte 1 bit 0x20 (AC_DUP_CD) - every step. What that means for
  ZARIA.01, counted from the authored file at this record's reading: the
  byte the mode gate 0x45417 tests is the separator of each line's FIRST
  point, and it is 0 on 7 of the 45 ground lines (lines 0, 5, 10, 11, 12,
  14 and 44 - line 0 is `1 -50,680!408,684;`, the west ground under the
  spawn, line 44 `1 -100,1500!3000,1500;`, the world floor) and 1 on the
  other 38. So a mode-0 query (bit 0x4000) can only be answered by those 7
  lines, and any answer found on one of the other 38 raises AC_DUP_CD. The
  byte 0x454ba actually stores is the same field of the bracket's LEFT
  record, so which of the two an answer carries depends on the segment the
  query point falls in.
  (g) THE CARRY MOVES THE BODY - the shape OI-078 states in words, here
  instruction by instruction. 0x54804 reads [obj+0xce], [obj+0xea],
  [obj+0xca] and the live position, zeroes [obj+0xea] (0x5481b) and writes
  [obj+0x00] = x + [obj+0xca], [obj+0x04] = y + [obj+0xce] + [obj+0xea]
  (0x54825-0x5482d), then clears the two clamp words with a
  self-subtraction, `sub [obj+0xca],[obj+0xca]` and the same at +0xce
  (0x54830-0x5484a). So one ground query contributes, once and only once,
  the clamp offset plus this frame's clearance to the position - not the
  .SEQ anchor pair of OI-129 - and it runs even when the query itself was
  skipped by the lock2 bit. The other reset sites 0x54e1a/0x54e98/0x550a0
  clear the answer triple.
  (h) WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE PORT. The port asks its own level lines
  (`ll_plt_first_below`), so the geometry is covered; what was not
  modelled is the FILTER: the same polyline is a different surface
  depending on the query mode, and the authored ';' or '!' after each
  point is what decides that, plus the AC_DUP_CD side effect that follows
  it.
  (i) WHAT I TRIED TO MEASURE AND DID NOT GET. Two live sessions on the
  PR-391 disk-D rig with the extended tracer (the new fields sample
  cleanly: `answer_flag`, `answer_surface`, `answer_gap`, `clamp_dx`,
  `clamp_dy` appear in every trace row). Neither session reached a
  playable ZARIA.01: the level boundary appeared at t=304 s with
  [world+0x74] = 0, and the census then found no TLewZaria object - the
  first session's fallback traced five objects of the KAMIEN class (their
  answer triple stayed 0 and their clamp delta stayed 0 over 3,368
  samples each at 20 Hz), the second found two objects of the lion-family
  table 0x96874 that never moved (4,747 samples, one distinct position). The
  baseline filter was the reason the player was missed in the first
  session - the menu already holds a lion, so "new class words since the
  menu" hides it - which is what the code change in this record fixes;
  the second session shows the fix works for the census (0x96874 objects
  were found) but that run still had no moving player. The live half of
  (d)'s exact-zero question stays open.
  (j) THE SHIPPED DATA BEHIND THOSE TWO BITS. Re-extracted the `.MOV`
  members of the HD ANIMACJE tree with the existing
  `tools/re/llrs_extract_mov.c` (777 members into /tmp/opencode/mov, then
  a line census over their `control=` lists) and counted the two token
  names PR-99 ties to those bits: CHECK_BASE_LN = 0x4000 appears on 8
  `control=` lines in 8 members - KADMAR.07, LONA.05, TUNGA.11, TUNGA2.12
  and the two `LEW.*` members of each of ZARIA.01 and ZARIA.02 - while
  CHECK_LN = 0x0100 appears on 340 lines in 101 members. 2 members name
  both and 670 of 777 name neither, so for most shipped object state text
  the ground query never runs at all. The 8/8 for CHECK_BASE_LN matches an
  earlier token census of another record (NEXT_STEPS line 2157), which is
  a second measurement of the same thing. So the mode-2 path (0x0100) is
  the common one, the mode-0 path is rare and sits in level-exit scripts
  of five levels including ZARIA.01 - which is the other half of why that
  level's 7 '!' lines matter.
```

- WHY. PR-391 made the level's ground table readable, and the ledger row
  for the ground signals had been carrying "the kind byte, the mode
  argument and the per-point flag byte are the unmodelled half" since
  PR-313. Reading 0x4b600 - the row's own named next read - collapses
  that whole sentence into one comparison that appears twice, and it names
  the thing the ask is filtering on.

- WHAT SURPRISED ME. That the author's choice of ';' or '!' after a point
  is a runtime query filter rather than an authoring comment, and that the
  engine's own answer keeps the byte of the record it chose so it can
  raise a signal every step from it. Also that the position carry at
  0x54825 is a sum of the clamp delta and the ask's clearance: the ground
  query moves the body directly, every frame.

CODE: yes: ported/ll_level.c only. seat_ask_core now takes A = record i-1
  and B = record i for BOTH clearances, the order 0x45443-0x45464 and
  0x45481-0x4548f build, and changes only the sampled point; seat_slope's

GATE-FIXTURE-FREE: rc=0 15 (ok) + 21 named
  Counts are the house verdict pattern of HANDOFF section 2 on
  /tmp/opencode/pr393b_verify_fixtures.log and pr393b_verify_nofixtures.log

  too: `docs structure: ... hold (ok)` and `index: docs/RE_INDEX.md

  description string this record rewrites. An earlier pair against the same

  for the change itself is pr393_test_first.log and pr393_after_fix.log,
  quoted in MEASURED (c).
MEASURED: (a) THE PAIR, INSTRUCTION BY INSTRUCTION. 0x4543c-0x4545e is
  the compiler's own dance for the first 0x455a0 call: ebx = i*13, edx =
  (i-1)*13, then base, then base + i*13, then ebx = base + (i-1)*13,
  edx = [esp+0x4] = base + i*13, [esp+0x4] = ebx, ebx = eax (the +0x6c
  result) and eax = [esp+0x4]. So eax = base + (i-1)*13 and edx = base +
  i*13. 0x45481-0x4548f does the same in registers: imul edx,ecx,0xd,
  dec ecx, imul ecx,ecx,0xd, eax = [esi+4], ebx = ebp, add edx,eax,
  add eax,ecx. 0x455a0 reads eax as A and edx as B (0x455a3-0x455c1:
  ecx = A, B.y - A.y, then (point.x - A.x), then B.x - A.x, idiv at
  0x455c3, then + A.y - point.y). Nothing reverses. Only ebx changes:
  0x45462 puts the class verb +0x6c result there - 0x23a10, `add
  eax,0x89; ret`, the clamp sample pair - and 0x4548b puts the caller's
  point.
  (b) THE HAND-RE-DERIVATION, ONE COLUMN AT A TIME. Rising span
  (0,50)-(100,100) at x 33: 50 + trunc(33*50/100) = 50 + 16 = 66, so the
  column answers y 66 and nothing else; PR-352 had 66 AND 67. Falling
  span (0,100)-(100,50) at x 33: 100 + trunc(-1650/100) = 100 - 16 = 84,
  because `idiv` truncates toward zero and -16.5 becomes -16; PR-352 had
  that column EMPTY (its L1 was 83, its L2 84). Same span at x 99:
  100 + trunc(-4950/100) = 100 - 49 = 51; PR-352 had 50. At x 32 the
  value is exact (100 - 16 = 84) and unchanged. Two new rows pin the two
  POINTS now that the value is one: snapshot on the line with the aim one
  row under it answers with the incumbent -1, and the same pair the other
  way round is refused by 0x4547d, which is the only gate that reads the
  snapshot.
  (c) THE TEST BITES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. With the re-derived table in and
  the code unchanged, `./ll_level --mov-selftest` returns rc=1 and names
  exactly the four discriminating rows (rising y 67 answered with -1 where
  0 is wanted, the point-pair mirror, x 33 of the falling span, x 99 of
  it) - /tmp/opencode/pr393_test_first.log. With the pair order fixed it
  returns rc=0 with no FAILED line (pr393_after_fix.log). As a mutation
  check, reversing ONLY the second call again fails 8 of the L15 rows.
  (d) WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, AND WHY THE MEASURED HALF STILL HOLDS. Every
  sampled row pair of ZARIA.01's four ANIPL2 seat tables carries the same
  y in both records, so B.y - A.y is 0, the division is exact in either
  order, and the leg's measured envelopes are identical: x 838..900,
  885..947, 930..992 and 307..382 with tops y 475..482, 380..387,
  320..327 and 633..664. The top bands stay 53..306 px apart, so
  0x45400 still carries no step of the authored chain - the answer
  PR-352 measured is unaffected by its own arithmetic slip.
  (e) The chain's description string, printed by verify-level, now states
  the law as one value at two points instead of "the pair reversed ...
  L2..L1". The string is not pinned by any grep; the leg passes on rc.
```

- WHY. PR-392 read the bytes and named `seat_ask_core` as carrying the
  wrong reading into port code. A model that is wrong about which pair it
  measures is wrong about which rows a column accepts, and the L15 leg was
  asserting those rows. Re-pin it while the correction is fresh, and let
  the hand arithmetic - not a re-recording - set the pins.

- WHAT SURPRISED ME. That PR-352's headline conclusion was right while
  its arithmetic was wrong: one row per column falls out of the corrected
  reading directly, and the "sometimes empty, sometimes two" band it
  measured was an artifact of the invented reversal. And that the
  truncation direction is load-bearing in the visible direction: on a
  falling line `idiv` puts the engine's surface one pixel ABOVE the real
  one, so a floor division in the port would have accepted a row the
  engine refuses.

MEASURED: (a) THE FULL LADDER, AGAIN. 0x546c2 reads the state control
  word at state+0x12 and tests it twice: `test ah,0x40` (bit 0x4000) at
  0x546c5 and `test ah,0x1` (bit 0x0100) at 0x54706. Bit 0x4000 runs
  0x4b600 with ecx = 0 into [esp+0x20] (0x546d7), 0x4b430 into
  [esp+0x30] (0x546f0), then falls through 0x54704 to the SHARED tail
  0x54746-0x54754, which runs 0x4b7f0 into [esp+0x40] and merges. Bit
  0x0100 runs 0x4b600 with ecx = 2 into [esp] (0x54719), 0x4b430 into
  [esp+0x50] (0x54732), and its `jmp 0x54742` loads [esp+0x10] into the
  tail instead - so with that bit the ceiling registry is asked with a
  buffer the caller filled earlier, not with a fresh one. With neither
  bit, 0x54709 jumps past all of it to 0x54759. Each of the six query
  calls is followed by 0x49580, which is exactly `for k in 0..2:
  [eax+4k] |= [edx+4k]` over three dwords (0x49586 `lea ecx,[eax+0xc]`,
  0x49590 `or edi,ebx`): the answer is OR-ed into the caller's signal
  set, not stored.
  (b) 0x4b430 AND THE 0x14-BYTE ENTRY, RE-READ FROM THE BYTES.
  0x4b439 saves the caller's point at [esp+0x14]; 0x4b441-0x4b455 build
  a 20-byte request block on the stack: [0] = [4] = [8] = [0xc] = 0 and
  [0x10] = 0x98274. 0x4b45b calls 0x534e0 with eax = the entry from the
  walk and edx = that block, and 0x534e0 fills the block's first four
  dwords from the entry's getters (see (d)). 0x4b462-0x4b48c then shift
  the block in place: [0] += [obj+0xca], [8] += [obj+0xca],
  [4] += [obj+0xce], [0xc] += [obj+0xce] - the same clamp-delta pair
  the position carry uses, added to BOTH x fields and both extent fields.
  The walk is 0x4b494-0x4b4bc: count = [[world]+0x7c] (skip when <= 0),
  eax = [world+0x70] + i*0x14, edx = the requester, and a direct
  `call 0x45620` - there is no verb through the entry here. 0x45620
  (ecx = edx = the requester throughout) tests the ENTRY as a vertical
  barrier: reject unless [entry+4] is in [block+0]..[block+8] (0x45629,
  0x45631) and [entry+8] in [block+4]..[block+4+block+0xc] (0x45640,
  0x45651); then 0x4565c-0x45676 choose the nearer edge -
  ([block+0]-[entry+4]) >= ([entry+8]-[block+0]) pushes to
  [block+8]+1, else to [block+0]-1 - and 0x45677-0x45686 take
  |[block+4] - that target| and refuse it when <= 1; otherwise
  0x45688-0x45690 ADD the signed distance to [requester+0xca], the
  X-delta the carry at 0x54825 applies, and return 1. On 1, 0x4b4d6
  clears the block's flag byte at 0x4b4e3/0x4b4cb, 0x749a0 zeroes the
  12-byte result head, and 0x4b4ec `or BYTE [result],0x1` sets signal
  bit 0 = AC_BLOK. 0x4b7f0 is the same shape over [world+0x78] with
  count [world+0x84], asking through `[[entry+0x10]+0x4]` (0x4b823,
  0x4b828), and its raise is 0x4b844 `or BYTE [result+3],0x2` =
  AC_UP_DUP; that is index 25 of the port's verified table, byte 0 bit
  1, so the result block's own layout is what those two writes agree
  on: bit 0 for the block answer, bit 1 for the ceiling answer, in the
  first dword.
  (c) THE FILE WORDS ARE COPIED, NOT CONVERTED. 0x4cf94/0x4cfc7 are the
  `blokady` and `sufity` arms of the levels-file parser (the compare is
  0x76d20 against 0x91e2c/0x91e38, and a line matching no key ends at
  0x4d423 with the string "Bledny wpis w pliku levels: %s" at 0x91ee5),
  and the block loader is 0x4db50: it
  reads one line, parses it with the scanset format at 0x91f24 into a
  stack row (0x4db8e), allocates count*0x14 through 0x76a64, stores the
  array at [anchor+0x70] (0x4dbc6) and per record calls 0x455e0, which
  copies FOUR dwords from the parsed row into the record and then parses
  two more numbers out of the same line into a side buffer. So the
  record's [0x00], [0x04], [0x08] are the file's three numbers verbatim
  and [0xc] is the unparsed remainder - and 0x45620 uses [0x08] as the
  RIGHT EDGE, x0 <= wall.x <= x1. Measured on the HD ETAPY container
  (sha be5d8b92, 10 `.BLK` members; the CD-stage ETAPY holds none, the
  same split PR-391 measured for `.PLT`): ZARIA.01/ZAR.BLK is 76 bytes,
  /tmp/opencode/pr394_zar.blk, `6` then `0,0,700`, `2240,0,700`,
  `1299,341,118`, `1462,244,28`, `1540,194,27`, `1620,0,200` with CRLF
  endings. Under the engine's own reading those last two numbers are
  absolute right edges, so the second wall spans x 2240..2940 - outside
  the 0..2240 world - which is either an authoring convention the
  loader completes somewhere else or a name for these numbers that
  PR-314/PR-313 had wrong. Named open. 0x5da60 is not the supplier: it
  only copies the group heads [anchor+0x14..0x20] into the registry
  mirrors [0x6c..0x78] when they are null (0x5daa8 stores the same zero
  it has just tested).
  (d) 0x534e0 AND THE GETTER CENSUS. 0x534e0 writes four dwords into
  the block: `call [class+0x68]` then [[that]+0] (0x534e9-0x534ee),
  the same call again then +4 (0x534f5-0x534fb), `call [class+0x48]`
  (0x53503), then [[state]+0x33] (0x5350b) and `call [class+0x50]`
  (0x53510), then `call [[0x33 result]]`. The +0x48 getter 0x23aa0
  indexes state = [[obj+0x50] + [obj+0x5c]*4], so the two extent words
  come from the state block. The +0x50 getter 0x53e40 is the row
  accessor: it re-reads that same state, takes [[state]+0x2e] (0x53e55)
  as an index into the .SEQ table it gets from [[state]]+0x4, and
  returns that row, or -1 when the row's +0x14 is 0 (0x53e63). So
  "position and extents" for this engine means the current STATE block's
  fields [0x75] and [0x76] (the +0x68 getter 0x23a50 is `lea
  edx,[eax+0x75]; call 0x534e0` on top of 0x23900 = `add eax,0xd6`,
  giving [state+0x75] = the animation block's x, [state+0x76] = its y)
  and the current .SEQ row. The census, `python3 tools/re/leodb.py
  slots 0x6c 0x68` over the 158 ctor-proven class tables: slot +0x6c is
  0x23a10 in 140, 0x23b50 in 17, 0x23b80 in 1; slot +0x68 is 0x23900
  in 116, 0x23b60 in 41, 0x23b90 in 1. Widening to PR-351's own method
  (every view in 0x96000..0xa7000 reached from its +0x48 slot) gives
  two clean families and no mixture: 186 views with +0x48 = 0x23aa0,
  +0x50 = 0x53e40, +0x68 = 0x23900, +0x6c = 0x23a10 - PR-351's and
  PR-392's reading, confirmed - and 33 views with +0x48 = 0x23be0
  (`mov eax,0xcf004`), +0x50 = 0x23bc0 (`mov eax,1`), +0x68 = 0x23b60
  (`ret`) and +0x6c = 0x23b50 (`ret`, the object itself), the STRUMIEN
  family, 0x96e94 first among them. For those 33 the aim chain's state
  block is the data-segment block at 0xcf004, which is all zeroes in
  the image, and their sample point is the object's own x at [obj+0].
  0x23b60's `ret` means the +0x68 result is the object, so the "x"
  0x534e0 stores is [obj+0] - the position, not an animation extent.
  0x23b80/0x23b90 (4 tables for +0x68, 1 for +0x6c, e.g. 0xa0774) are
  the setter/getter pair on [obj+0x2c], the clamp output of 0x23b70.
  (e) THE TWO SHARED VIEWS, AND WHY 0x98274 IS NOT AN ELEMENT CLASS.
  0x98274 = {0x23e30, 0x23ed0, 0x23ea0, ...} is the view of the
  request block itself: 0x23e30 reads a record as x0 at +0x0, y at
  +0x4, x1 at +0xc (0x23e3b-0x23e4f, |x1-x0|/2 + x0 = its centre),
  writes 0x98278 at [out+8] (0x23e67) and then calls
  [[out+8]+0x4] = 0x23ea0, which stores that centre as {x, y} - the
  12-byte surface descriptor of 0x4b600's element array. 0x98278 =
  {0x23ed0, 0x23ea0, 0x23e00} is that descriptor's view, and 0x443b2
  fills arrays of 12-byte records {0, 0, 0x98278} (0x443ce), which is
  the shape 0x4b600 walks: `call [[entry+8]+0x1c]` (0x4b697) reads the
  view at [entry+8], not at [entry+0]. That settles the sentence in
  OI-127 about an entry's first word being a code table: for these two
  registries the table 0x4b600 dispatches through is the SECOND dword
  and it is the shared surface-descriptor view. 0x23ed0, the +4 slot,
  tests the mode byte's bits 0x4 and 0x2 and calls 0x96858's table or
  0x5c370 - the second read named in OI-127's tail, not chased here.
```

- WHY. PR-392 corrected the sampler of the ground query and left its two
  siblings unread. A ground model that ignores the block query cannot
  tell a pushed lion from a landed one, and the push is written into the
  same [obj+0xca] the carry applies - so the port needs the block law
  before it can claim anything about sideward motion. Reading it also
  tests the getter story PR-351 built for the aim: if that story is
  wrong for 33 of the game's classes, it is wrong in a way that matters
  for water.

- WHAT SURPRISED ME. That the engine never converts the `.BLK` third
  number: the loader copies it and the test treats it as an absolute
  right edge, so a wall authored as `2240,0,700` spans 2240..2940,
  outside the world - the "length" reading was ours, not the engine's.
  And that the sample getter is not one function: 33 class views hold
  `ret` there, so their sample point is their own position, and their
  whole state block is a single global buffer at 0xcf004 that the image
  leaves zero.

MEASURED: (a) THE RECORD IS PARSED, NOT COPIED. 0x455e0 (eax = the
  record, edx = the token cursor): 0x455e2-0x455e9 set ecx = rec+0x10,
  eax = rec+4 and call 0x4a0b0, which at 0x4a0b1 takes ebx = rec+8 and
  at 0x4a0bc calls the engine's scanner 0x49920 with the format "%d,%d"
  (0x91d0f) - the row's first pair lands in rec+4 and rec+8 - then
  probes its separator string " , " (0x91d15) through 0x498f0 (0x4a0c4).
  Back in 0x455e0, 0x455f2-0x455f8 scan "%d" (0x9183d) into rec+0x10
  and 0x45600-0x45606 probe a bare "," (0x91840) and drop the answer.
  rec+0 and rec+0xc are written by nothing: the array comes from a
  zeroed allocation at 0x4dbb9 (ecx = 0 into 0x76a64, count*0x14+4
  bytes). So a record is a VERTICAL WALL at x = rec+4 running from y =
  rec+8 down by rec+0x10 - and ZAR.BLK's six rows are exactly the
  world's edges x 0 and x 2240 over the full 700 px plus four
  stone-corridor walls at 1299/341+118, 1462/244+28, 1540/194+27 and
  1620/0+200, the very corridor OI-065 asks about.
  (b) THE FILE IS A TOKEN STREAM. 0x4db50 (esi = the level anchor):
  0x4db59/0x4db77 put the table pointer 0x961fc at cursor+9 and
  0x4db72-0x4db7b build the cursor at 0x49820 with a 0x400-byte buffer
  and read the whole file ONCE; 0x4db80-0x4db8e scan the header count
  straight into [world+0x7c] with the format "%d" (0x91f24); a zero
  count skips the allocation (0x4db9b); 0x4dbcf-0x4dbe4 then run the
  record scan once per record - eax = [world+0x70] + i*0x14, edx = that
  SAME cursor, the loop gated by `cmp ecx,[world+0x7c]; jl` at 0x4dbe2 -
  and 0x4dbe6 destroys the cursor. Lines mean nothing: after the one
  read the count is authoritative in both directions - extra numbers are
  never read and a short file leaves the remaining records at their
  allocated zero, which is what the pins "2 + a missing triple gives
  0,0,0" and "1 + a fourth number ignores it" pin. What separates
  numbers is exactly what those scans carry: "%d,%d" with its " , "
  argument and the trailing "," probe; the port treats commas, spaces,
  tabs and newlines as separators everywhere.
  (c) THE TEST, GATE BY GATE (0x45620: eax = record, ebx = the request
  block, ecx = edx = the requester). x: 0x45629/0x4562b (`jl`) and
  0x45631/0x45634 (`jg`) leave unless bx0 <= rec.x <= bx1 - the gate is
  on the WALL's face, so a body strictly inside the world never meets an
  edge wall; a wall exactly at an edge passes the gate and is then
  always refused at 0x45683 (see (f)). y: 0x45640 first tests `rec.y >
  block+0xc` and looks at the height only when it is true
  (0x45644/0x45647); 0x45651 tests `rec.y < block+4` and likewise
  (0x45655/0x45658) - both ends of the wall's range past the same end
  of the requester's is the ONLY refusal, so it is an OVERLAP of the
  two ranges, and it handles a negative authored length as the same
  interval upside down. Side: 0x45666/0x45668 compute bx1 - rec.x and
  rec.x - bx0, 0x4566a compares with `jge` at 0x4566c - the TIE takes
  [block+8]+1 (0x45673/0x45676), else [block+0]-1 (0x4566e): the
  target is the REQUESTER'S OWN EDGE plus one, never a face of the
  wall, because the engine is resolving an overlap, not aiming at it.
  Push: 0x4567a d = rec.x - target; 0x4567e-0x45681 is the cdq/xor/sub
  absolute value; 0x45683/0x45686 refuse |d| <= 1, which is exactly the
  already-flush case, and on a refusal [obj+0xca] is NEVER written;
  0x45688-0x45690 ADD d, signed, to [obj+0xca] - the same field the
  carry at 0x54825 applies - so the requester's near or far edge lands
  at the wall's x minus/plus one. A blockade TELEPORTS a body out of an
  overlapped wall; it never stops it.
  (d) THE WALK STOPS AT THE FIRST ANSWER. 0x4b4af `test eax,eax` and
  0x4b4b1 `jne 0x4b4d6`: the loop over [world+0x70] leaves as soon as
  one 0x45620 call returns 1, and 0x4b4ec raises AC_BLOK once. A body
  spanning BOTH edge walls gets ONE push, from the FIRST row in file
  order - the second wall, which would have answered the other way, is
  never asked. Pinned: ZAR.BLK's six walls, asked by a body at x
  -10..2250, answer index 0 with dx +11, and a body only the last row
  reaches answers index 5.
  (e) THE CENSUS. All ten `.BLK` members of the HD ETAPY (dumped to
  /tmp/opencode/pr395_blk/, table in /tmp/opencode/pr395_census.txt):
  ENA 2, ENA2 9, KADMAR 3, KADMAR2 49, KARA 11, LONA 6, RAN 4, TUNGA 2,
  ZAR 6, ZARIA_B 2 - 94 records, and EVERY file carries exactly
  1+3*count integers: no leftovers, no short rows, all CRLF. The walls
  span each whole world in every file - the minimum authored x is in
  {-1, 0, 2, 3} (RAN.BLK's first row is `-1,0,450`, a wall one px
  OUTSIDE the left edge, so x values are not clamped to the world) and
  the maximum reaches 1597..28880, the level's right edge; most authors
  put long walls at those edges FIRST (ENA, RAN, TUNGA, ZAR, ZARIA_B,
  KADMAR, ENA2's 1200-px wall at row 1), but LONA buries its edge
  walls at rows 3 and 5 and KADMAR2 - the biggest registry - has no
  long edge wall at all, its leftmost being a 198-px stub at y 1400
  for a vertically scrolling level. File order is not position order,
  which is exactly what the first-answer walk of (d) depends on. No
  authored length is negative or zero (min 8, KADMAR2), so the
  inverted-range pins are the law, not the data. The largest header is
  49, so LL_BLK_MAX 64 has room.
  (f) THE PINS BITE - AND WHERE THEY CANNOT. A mutation harness
  (pr395_mut4.log, pr395_mutate.py over pr395_mut_main.c) rebuilds
  ll_play.c 14 times with one law broken each: the 1-px flush rule off,
  each x-gate end exclusive, each y-gate end exclusive, the y test made
  a point test or a containment test, the side test turning 1 px early,
  the two sides swapped, the push sign flipped, the walk summing every
  record, the walk reversed, a short file truncating instead of
  zero-padding, a missing number defaulted to -1. `./ll_level
  --play-selftest` FAILS on 12 of them, naming 1-16 checks each. The
  two survivors are the x gate's two end strictnesses, and an
  exhaustive check (pr395_equiv.c, output pr395_equiv.txt) proves no pin
  could catch them: over 997,953,125 record/requester cases the
  exclusive-end variants differ NOWHERE from the inclusive ones, because
  every one of the 59,078,825 cases where rec.x sits exactly on a
  requester x edge is refused by the |d| <= 1 rule - a record at the
  edge is always flush. The inclusiveness of that gate is not
  observable behaviour of 0x45620; the port follows the bytes (jl at
  0x4562b, jg at 0x45631) either way.
```

- WHY. PR-394 read the query and stopped at an unresolved record shape -
  one whose authored data ("2240,0,700 spans past the world edge") did not
  fit its own reading - and the port's .blk header comments had already
  started repeating that reading. The registry is named in the plan
  (HANDOFF section 8, OI-065 and the OI-078 note), so the shape had to be
  settled before anything could be modelled: one more pass over
  0x4db50/0x455e0/0x4a0b0 with the formats read out of the image resolved
  it, and a data-free leg is the cheap place to pin the law while it is
  fresh.

- WHAT SURPRISED ME. That the two obvious half-pixels are unfalsifiable:
  making either end of the x gate exclusive changes NOTHING across
  997,953,125 cases, because the |d| <= 1 rule already refuses every
  record sitting exactly on a requester edge - so a test suite can never
  confirm that part of the law, and only the bytes (jl at 0x4562b, jg at
  0x45631) record it. And that the shipped registries disagree with each
  other about everything except the grammar: RAN.BLK authors an edge
  wall at x -1, outside the world; LONA buries its edge walls at rows
  3 and 5; KADMAR2's 49 walls contain no long edge wall at all - and
  still every file carries exactly 1+3*count integers. The ZAR.BLK
  "puzzle" PR-394 recorded was never in the engine at all, only in one
  wrong read of its formats.

  malloc chain 0x5c320 -> 0x7521f -> 0x78ce0), and 0x76bb7 -> 0x76b24 is
  what builds an array: 0x76b35 writes the COUNT at [mem], 0x76b74 chooses
  the generic path (the class's first byte is not 4) and 0x76b96 calls
  0x76ab0, which runs the class's CONSTRUCTOR over count elements at the
  class's own element size; 0x76b24 then returns mem+4, and that is the
  pointer the registry stores. For `.BLK` that constructor is 0x4fb70 -
  the field at C+1 of the class record 0xa14c0 - and it writes the method
  table 0xa2178 at rec+0x0 and the view 0x98278 at rec+0xc while zeroing
  +0x4, +0x8 and +0x10; for `.SUF` it is 0x4fbd0 of the class 0xa14d8,
  which zeroes +0, +4 and +0xc and stores the view at +8 and the table
  0xa218c at +0x10. So PR-395's "rec+0 and rec+0xc are never read by
  0x45620" and its whole record/query law stand; what was wrong is that
  the two words are NOT zero and the array is not calloc'd. PR-394's and
  PR-313's account is untouched.

MEASURED: (a) THE CLASS RECORD, AND WHERE A RECORD'S TABLE COMES FROM.
  PR-395 left the question open - the .SUF loader 0x4da90 calls
  `[[rec+0x10]]` for a record whose +0x10 nothing in the loader writes.
  It is the record's CONSTRUCTOR. This binary keeps a class record's
  fields one byte in: at 0xa14d8 the bytes read as C+1 = 0x4fbd0 (the
  constructor), C+5 = 0x74bac (the destructor), C+9 = 0x4fba0, C+0xd =
  0x14 (the ELEMENT SIZE), and 0x76ab0 is the routine that uses them -
  0x76ac9/0x76ad3 read [class+1] and [class+0xd], 0x76ad9 calls the
  constructor on each element and 0x76ae3 steps by that size. 0x4fb70
  (.BLK) and 0x4fbd0 (.SUF) are those two constructors, and they are
  where every constant in a record comes from: 0x4fbd0 writes 0 at +0, +4
  and +0xc, the shared view 0x98278 at +8 and the method table 0xa218c at
  +0x10; 0x4fb70 writes 0 at +4, +8 and +0x10, the view at +0xc and the
  table 0xa2178 at +0x0. The allocation itself is not a zeroing one:
  0x4db9f-0x4daf5 computes count*0x14+4, 0x4dafd calls 0x76a64 (a malloc
  wrapper: it jumps to 0x5c320, then 0x7521f, then 0x78ce0) and 0x4db02
  calls 0x76bb7, which pushes 1 as the count-to-construct and calls
  0x76b24; 0x76b35 stores the file's count at [mem], 0x76b74/0x76b83
  take the generic constructor path and 0x76b96 runs 0x76ab0 over the
  array, and 0x76b24 RETURNS mem+4 - the address of record 0 - which
  0x4db0f stores at [world+0x78] and 0x4dbc6 at [world+0x70]. 
  (b) THE ROW IS PARSED BY THE SAME SCANNER AS A WALL. 0x4db12-0x4db2e
  loop: `mov eax,[esi+0x78]; add eax,ecx` with ecx stepping 0x14,
  `mov edi,[eax+0x10]`, `mov edx,esp` (the same cursor the header was
  scanned from) and `call [edi]` - once per record, count times. [[rec+
  0x10]] is 0xa218c[0] = 0x454d0: 0x454d6/0x454d9 hand the record to
  0x4a0b0, which at 0x4a0bc scans "%d,%d" (0x91d0f) into entry+0 and
  entry+4 and at 0x4a0c4 probes its separator argument " , " (0x91d15)
  through 0x498f0; 0x454de-0x454e5 then scan "%d" (0x91836) into
  entry+0xc and 0x454ed-0x454f3 probe " , " (0x91839) and drop the
  answer. A record is therefore a HORIZONTAL LINE from entry+0 along +x
  for entry+0xc px at y = entry+4 - the .SUF pair of the .BLK wall, with
  the same three words in a different order and the same formats. The
  header count is the "%d" at 0x91f21 (as .BLK's is 0x91f24 and .PLT's
  0x4dc00 uses 0x91f27), the read is the same 0x400-byte single pass
  0x4dabb with the same scanset 0x961fc, a count of 0 allocates nothing
  (0x4dadf), and the loop runs count times whatever the file holds. 
  (c) THE QUERY IS GIVEN THE BODY, NOT A BOX. 0x4b7f0 (eax = the world,
  ebx = the body, edx = the result block) walks [world+0x78] for
  [world+0x84] records at stride 0x14 and calls `[[entry+0x10]+4]` =
  0xa218c[4] = 0x45500. 0x45500 (eax = the record, edx = the body):
  0x45516 calls the BODY's class slot +0x68 - the same getter 0x534e0
  wraps for 0x4b430, whose box fields the blockade walk then shifts by
  [obj+0xca] and [obj+0xce] (0x4b46d-0x4b48a) - and keeps only [esi+4],
  the box's near y; 0x4552f calls slot +0xb0 with the argument block
  {0, 0, the view 0x98278} and 0x4553c-0x4554f ADD [obj+0xca] and
  [obj+0xce] to what it wrote, giving the anchor the body would have
  after the pending move. Those two slots are ALREADY NAMED - this row
  adds the count, and says what the three numbers therefore are. 0x23900
  is `add eax,0xd6` / `ret`, which PR-305 read and called "the
  presented point"; counted here, 176 distinct class views are stored at
  [obj+8] (502 constructor sites), 118 of them answer +0x68 with
  0x23900 and 118 answer +0xb0 with 0x544f0, and 42 more answer +0x68
  with 0x23C60 - `ret`, identity, so for those classes the box IS the
  object and its near y is the position field. 0x4552f is one of the
  three ask-side callers PR-308 found (0x2b881, 0x2b900, 0x4552f), all
  three pre-seeding the buffer as {0, 0, 0x98278}, and 0x544f0 opens by
  copying [obj+0] and [obj+4] - the LIVE position - into it; its tail,
  0x54500-0x5453a, is an attachment path for a body flagged attached at
  [obj+0xb6] (class slots +0xbc, +0x48, +0x50 and the table at
  [that+0x33]), which PR-396 did not follow. So the three values
  0x45500 compares have DIFFERENT PROVIDERS: `ax`,`ay` are the live
  position plus the pending delta, while `top` is [obj+0xda] - the
  STORED presented point, which PR-306 and PR-307 showed is written
  only by the class's +0x1c verb 0x54e00 on a layer notify/select. That
  is what the asymmetry noted below really is: not a quirk of this
  query but live-versus-stored. It is also why the port keeps all three
  as parameters - it states 0x45500's arithmetic and takes no position
  on which of the two a caller should pass. Then, in order:
  `cmp entry+0, ax / jl` (0x45555)
  and `cmp entry+0 + entry+0xc, ax / jl` (0x45562) - the anchor's x must
  lie on the line, BOTH ends inclusive; `cmp [esi+4], entry+4 / jl`
  (0x4556c) - the body's top must be at or below the line, so a line
  that is not above the body is not a ceiling; and `sub` + `test / jle`
  (0x45576/0x4557a) - entry.y - anchor_y must be >= 1, so a body whose
  anchor is already on or under the line is left alone. On an answer
  0x45582-0x45584 do `[obj+0xce] += entry.y - anchor_y`, which lands the
  anchor exactly ON the line; on a miss nothing is written. There is no
  distance-of-1 exemption as 0x45683 has for a wall: a ceiling moves a
  body by 1 px as happily as by 300. Note the engine's own asymmetry,
  kept in the port: the top comes from the getter with NO delta added,
  the anchor WITH it. 
  (d) THE WALK, AND WHERE IT RUNS. 0x4b806-0x4b818: a count <= 0 skips
  everything (0x4b808), the count is RE-READ from [world+0x84] at every
  step (0x4b80d), and 0x4b82d `test eax,eax / je 0x4b80c` moves to the
  next record only while the answer is no - the first record that answers
  leaves the walk. Its tail clears the caller's result block the same way
  the blockade walk's does (0x4b83b/0x4b83f call 0x749a0 with ebx = 0xc
  and edx = 0) and 0x4b844 raises `or BYTE [result+3],0x2` - bit 1 of
  byte 3 of the same first dword whose bit 0 AC_BLOK uses (0x4b4ec), the
  flag PR-394 named AC_UP_DUP. The call sites settle the ORDER inside the
  physics step: 0x546f0 and 0x54732 are the two blockade walks and 0x5474b
  is this one, reached from both branches (0x54704 `jmp 0x54746`), with
  eax = the world global [0xcef40] and ebx = the body in both cases, and
  both results merged through the same 0x49580 tail. So in one step the
  engine asks the walls first and the ceilings last. 
  (e) THE CENSUS - AND WHAT THE KEY ACTUALLY NAMES. A level asks for a
  registry with its `sufity=` line, and the provider is a member of THAT
  LEVEL'S OWN CONTAINER SLOT - the sub-member shape PR-392 measured for
  `platformy=`, which PR-396 did not re-read in the loader. All 52
  `.DES` members of the CD-stage LEVELDES container (the same 13 level
  descriptors in four language slots ENG, GER, POL, POL.ORG) carry
  exactly one such line; the HD ETAPY's own 103 `.DES` members carry
  none. What they name, and what is shipped: 4 `kadmar.suf` ->
  KADMAR.07/KADMAR.SUF, 15 bytes, `1` then `0,0,3000`; 4 `ran.suf` ->
  RAN.01/RAN.SUF, 17 bytes, `1` then `20,100,28800`; 4 `kara.suf` ->
  KARA.07/KARA.SUF, 37 bytes, `3` then `0,0,1600`, `125,290,10`,
  `1535,40,10`; 12 `sufity.des` -> the ENA.03, SADES.06 and TUNGA2.12
  members named SUFITY.DES, 14 bytes `1 / 0,20,6720`, 76 bytes
  `6 / 0,185,1000 / 47,997,241 / 495,1384,178 / 41,1817,53 /
  55,2621,272 / 0,0,1000` and 48 bytes `4 / 0,613,358 / 0,740,358 /
  0,-40,2600 / 0,235,233`; and 28 `none.des` -> the NONE.DES member of
  KADMAR2, JUNCTION, LONA.05, ENA2, ZARIA.01, ZARIA.02 and TUNGA.11,
  whose whole content is the token `0`. So EVERY provider named by a
  shipped descriptor is shipped, and the seven `none` levels are
  authored EMPTY REGISTRIES, not missing files - PR-396's own first
  reading of this paragraph held that neither `none.des` nor
  `sufity.des` exists as a member of any shipped container, and that is
  corrected here. The
  shipped total is therefore 13 registries, 6 of them with records, the
  largest header 6 (SADES.06) - which is what LL_SUF_MAX 8 is sized
  against. Negative y is authored (TUNGA2.12's `0,-40,2600`, above the
  y 0 that four other files use as the map's top line), every file
  carries exactly 1+3*count integers, CRLF, no leftovers and no short
  rows, and no `.SUF`, `SUFITY.DES` or `NONE.DES` member exists in the
  ANIMACJE, SOUND or CD-stage ETAPY containers (all of it in
  /tmp/opencode/pr396_suf_des.txt). For the OI-078 climb this is now a
  DIRECT answer rather than an absence: ZARIA.01 and ZARIA.02 each ship
  a NONE.DES holding `0`, so 0x4b808 skips the walk entirely and no
  ceiling can be hit on that climb.
  (f) THE PINS BITE - AND WHERE THEY CANNOT. The leg is data-free:
  `./ll_level --play-selftest` runs 53 new CHECKs and passes (rc=0,
  pr396_playst6.log). Five of the six non-empty shipped registries supply
  its bytes - KADMAR.SUF's one line, RAN.SUF's one, KARA.SUF's three,
  SADES.06's six and TUNGA2.12's four with its negative y - beside a
  NONE.DES `0`, the interval algebra, and the port cap. A mutation
  harness (/tmp/opencode/pr396_mutate.py, which rebuilds ll_play.c
  against a standalone driver pr396_playst.c) breaks one law at a time:
  the x gate's lower bound made strict, its upper bound widened, the
  whole x gate dropped, the top test made strict, the top test dropped,
  the d test made strict, the d test dropped, the dy sign flipped, dy
  made absolute, the header cap off by one, the cap widened by one, the
  row keeping y as its length, the record's x and y swapped, the row
  reading two numbers instead of three, the walk taking the LAST answer,
  and the walk skipping record 0. The selftest FAILS on 15 of the 16
  (pr396_mut1.log). The survivor is `*dy = d < 0 ? -d : d`, and no pin
  can catch it: 0x4557a's `test / jle` already established d >= 1, so the
  absolute value of that value is the same number - an equivalent mutant,
  not a gap. Two gaps the first run found and closed are the cap
  boundary (8 accepted, 9 refused, and now a widened cap refused too) and
  the FIELD ORDER of the record, which only the swap mutant pins.
  SADES.06 is what makes the first-answer law bite on real bytes: at ax
  500, ay 1300, top 1400 rows 0 and 5 span the x but neither can answer,
  row 2 answers with dy 84, and the nearer line of a later row is never
  asked.
```

- WHY. PR-395 closed the wall registry and named its own ceiling half as
  the next unread thing - "0x4b7f0 asks through [[entry+0x10]+0x4], a
  different builder, unread" - and OI-127's PR-394 paragraph had already
  said the two 0x14 registries are "a different shape again". The shape
  turned out to be the missing piece of a mechanism, not a second data
  layout: this binary gives every record its own method table through its
  class's constructor, whose fields sit at C+1/C+5/C+9/C+0xd. That single
  fact answered the .SUF record, the .SUF query, and PR-395's open calloc
  question in one pass - and it says the port's own record comments were
  wrong about where the zeroes come from, which is fixed here rather than
  left to drift. The census also moved twice while this row was written,
  and both moves are recorded here rather than quietly fixed: the first
  reading said ten of the thirteen `sufity=` names point at a file nobody
  ships, and the measurement says the opposite - every named provider is
  shipped, as a `.SUF`, a `SUFITY.DES` or a `NONE.DES` member of the
  level's own slot, and the ten are authored zeros. A row that ends with
  "the shipped data says no" has to be sure the data was looked for
  properly, and here it was not the first time.

  consumes it, and here that is 0x76b24 - which is why this row started

- WHY. Two of PR-396's OPENS items and one sentence of its reasoning were
  about the structure that row had just leaned on: what the field at class+9
  of the two registry classes does, and whether the two views 0x98274 and
  0x98278 are records or tables. The answers reach past the two registries.
  The class's first byte is a real switch in the engine's own array builder,
  and it switches the ARGUMENT a constructor receives, not whether one runs;
  the guard the builder registers is where a class's copy verb is kept, and
  that verb touches no field of the record, which closes the last doubt
  about where a registry record's numbers come from. The negative test also
  matters as method: the byte pattern PR-396 used to guess at 0x98274
  matches 344 places in that region, so it was never evidence, and the three
  addresses it was meant to explain are tables after all.

- WHY. PR-397 had found a switch in the engine's own array builder and
  could not say who used either side of it, and it had found an argument
  passed to every constructor and could not say what it was for. Those were
  the two live questions its record carried, and both are answered here in
  the same direction: nothing takes the second path and nothing reads the
  argument. That is worth having, because it turns three separate
  observations - PR-395's .BLK records, PR-396's .SUF records, PR-391's
  provider array - into one mechanism that the port can implement once. It
  also puts names on the .PLT containers and their records, which OI-129
  had only described as bytes, and it is a reminder about method: three of
  this row's own passes were wrong about a count as small as forty, each
  time because the instrument, not the engine, decided where a function
  began.

MEASURED: (a) THE BAND, FOUND BY SIGNATURE, NOT BY A TABLE LIST. The five
  verbs of the attachment family sit in five CONSECUTIVE slots, so the
  five dwords 0x544f0, 0x238b0, 0x23880, 0x23870, 0x54fe0 in order are a
  signature for the table that carries them. It occurs 155 times, at bases
  0x96874 through 0xa6520 (pr399_band.py). In all 155: +0x44 = 0x23920,
  +0x48 = 0x23aa0, +0x50 = 0x53e40, +0x98 = 0x23a50, +0xbc = 0x23870,
  +0xc0 = 0x54fe0, +0xc4 = 0x55020. Two more slots split the set: +0x8c =
  the self key getter 0x54910 in 140 and +0xcc = 0x549f0 in the same 140,
  +0xa8 = 0x54860 in 99. The gap between consecutive bases is not one
  number (0xe0 x21, 0xec x14, 0x110 x13, 0x1b8 x11, ...), so these tables
  differ in length. This also says why a table list is the wrong way to
  ask the question: attributing the same dwords to the re DB's `mtable`
  entries and their declared lengths puts only 116 of the 155 at +0xb0,
  because several declared regions contain more than one band
  (pr399_slots.py). The content signature is the reliable name.
  (b) THE SIX BODIES. Five of the six share one chain, called C below:
  `mov edx,[obj+8]`, `call [edx+0x48]` = the current element, `mov
  edi,[element+0x33]` = the ELEMENT'S method table (PR-357's 0xa0c08),
  `call [edx+0x50]` = the sign, then `call [edi+0x4]` or `[edi+0x8]` with
  eax = the element, edx = the object, ebx = the sign.
    +0xbc 0x23870: `cmp DWORD [obj+0xa9],0; setne al` - the held-surface
      boolean, one instruction, no chain.
    +0xb4 0x238b0: runs C and the +0x4 verb unless mask 0x01 of
      [obj+0xb6] is set, and passes ebx = [obj+0x6d] (0x238c9) instead of
      the sign. Writes no flag.
    +0xb8 0x23880: the same with the +0x8 verb (0x2389c). Writes no flag.
    +0xc0 0x54fe0: if mask 0x01 is CLEAR, C and the +0x8 verb; then
      ALWAYS `or BYTE [obj+0xb6],0x3` (0x5500e) - it sets both lock bits
      even when it skipped the chain.
    +0xc4 0x55020: if mask 0x01 is set AND mask 0x02 is set, C and the
      +0x4 verb; then ALWAYS `and BYTE [obj+0xb6],0xfc` (0x55057).
    +0xb0 0x544f0: PR-308's point provider. Its tail, to the instruction:
      it copies [obj+0] and [obj+4] into the asker's buffer first and
      unconditionally; then mask 0x02 set skips the tail (0x54500,
      0x54507); otherwise it calls +0xbc, and the chain runs iff the
      boolean is nonzero OR mask 0x01 is set (0x54514-0x5451f); the chain
      it runs is C with the +0x8 verb at 0x5453a. So the gate is
      `!bit0x02 && (held || bit0x01)` - the exact opposite polarity of
      the aim-chain gate of 0x541f0 (PR-355's `bit0x02 || (!held &&
      !bit0x01)`), because the provider is asked by whoever wants the
      point and 0x541f0 is asked by whoever wants the shift.
  The two functions that are NOT slots - 0x54f40 and 0x54f90 - are the
  single-bit pair: 0x54f40 calls +0xbc and skips if the object holds a
  surface or mask 0x01 is set, else runs C with the +0x4 verb, then
  `or BYTE [obj+0xb6],0x1` (0x54f7b); 0x54f90 runs C with the +0x8 verb
  only when the object holds NO surface and mask 0x01 IS set, then
  `and BYTE [obj+0xb6],0xfe` (0x54fcb). Neither appears as a dword in any
  table (pr399_slots.txt: 0 occurrences), and their only call edges are
  through the thunks of (d).
  (c) THE BIT MAP, EVERY SITE RE-READ FROM AN ALIGNED SLICE. 44 sites
  mention +0xb6 outside a stack slot; all 44 are real instructions when
  re-read from a slice that starts at the enclosing function entry
  (pr399_bits.py). Setting, each with exactly one site: mask 0x01 at
  0x54f7b, mask 0x03 at 0x5500e, mask 0x04 at 0x545c6, mask 0x08 at
  0x545d2 - the last two inside the control-message dispatcher 0x54560 of
  PR-171 and PR-343. Clearing, one site each: 0xfe at 0x54fcb, 0xfc at
  0x55057, 0xdf at 0x5266c. The only computed write is 0x45c45,
  `or DWORD [obj+0xb6],ebx` with ebx = (edx&1)<<5, i.e. bit 0x20 and
  nothing else. Testing: mask 0x01 at 11 sites, mask 0x02 at 8, mask 0x10
  at 2 (0x54964, 0x54bd6) and no literal setter for 0x10 anywhere. So
  mask 0x02 is never SET on its own - the one instruction that sets it
  also sets 0x01 - but it CAN stand alone, because 0x54fcb clears 0x01 and
  leaves it; PR-355's "bits 0x03" test case and its lone-0x02 case are
  both reachable, and this is the map that says so.
  (d) THE THUNKS: NOT DEAD, AND THEY ARE THE ONLY LIVE WAY IN. Five thunks
  at 0x45c00, 0x45c20, 0x45c50, 0x45c80, 0x45cb0 all open the same way -
  `push ebx; push ecx; mov ecx,eax; mov ebx,edx; call 0x457e0` (PR-101's
  node chain walk) - and then test `cmp DWORD [ecx+8],0`, the surface
  record count PR-362 named:
    0x45cb0 nonzero -> `call [class+0xb4]`, zero -> `call [class+0xb8]`;
    0x45c80 nonzero -> `call [class+0xc0]`, zero -> `call [class+0xc4]`;
    0x45c50 nonzero -> `call 0x54f40`, zero -> `call 0x54f90`;
    0x45c20 clears mask 0x20 and re-writes it as (edx&1)<<5 (0x45c36,
      0x45c45);
    0x45c00 asks the object's class for +0x30 then +0x2c (0x45c13,
      0x45c19).
  Their entry addresses were first written one byte low (0x45c1f,
  0x45c4e, 0x45c7f, 0x45caf) because a `dis` slice that starts inside a
  function drifts; the byte pattern `ret`, padding, `53 51` puts them at
  the addresses above (pr399_thunktable.txt). Each of the five is named
  exactly once in the image, by field +0x04 of a row of PR-101's

  (row 17), 0xa10ac -> 0x45cb0 (row 16), and a sixth, 0xa107c -> 0x45ce0

  (e) WHAT THAT LEAVES LIVE. The slot +0xc0 has exactly one call site,
  0x45c96, and +0xc4 exactly one, 0x45ca4, both inside 0x45c80; +0xb4 has
  two, 0x45cc6 (in 0x45cb0) and 0x5479f (the ground-contact verb), and

  0x5040c, in the state-reset path that zeroes [obj+0x11a]/[obj+0x11e]
  and [obj+0xb5] and writes 0x64 to [obj+0xad], and 0x52665, a teardown
  thunk that calls 0x54f90 on [[obj]] and then clears mask 0x20 at

  are reachable only through node-class rows 17 and 16, and two (0x54f40

```

- WHY. Three rows of this ledger have described the same six slots as if
  they were six separate discoveries - PR-308 read the point provider,
  PR-353 the land/leave pair, PR-350 the boolean, and the two lock verbs
  had never been named at all. Reading them as one band is what made the
  last two findable in one pass, and it is also the only way to say
  honestly how many classes carry the contract: a table list gives 116 and
  a content signature gives 155. Two of this row's findings change what a
  later row may assume. PR-362's "the split is only in slot +0x54" was the
  reason the standing-query question looked like one mechanism with two
  settings; it is not - the 31 classes with the ungated writer have no
  attachment band at all, so any law about lock bits is a law about the
  lion family and its 124 tables. And the pair-keyed dispatchers this row
  started out calling dead code are the node-class rows' +0x04 verbs,
  which OI-128 had been told were unnamed for eleven PRs: what was wrong
  was an address one byte out of place. Both corrections are cheap to
  carry and expensive to have missed, and both came from the same habit -
  check the address against the bytes before believing anything about the
  thing that owns it.

CORRECTS: PR-345, PR-362 and PR-399, three sentences about the same
  four dispatchers. (1) OI-128's PR-345 paragraph and the PR-345 record
  say the dispatcher is
  keyed "on the surface's record count at [handle+8]". The subject of
  that test is the NODE, not a surface: the verb is entered with eax =
  the node, its prologue keeps edx (the second argument) and tests `cmp
  DWORD PTR [ecx+0x8],0` with ecx = the node (0x45c8b, 0x45cbb, 0x45c5b)
  - the same field the +0x10 channel query adds into an output. (2) The
  same row in OI-128 and PR-399 say these thunks "choose between" a pair
  and that the object action runs "only when it is non-zero": both arms
  act on the object, the branch only picks which member of the pair runs
  (0x45cb0: +0xb4 at 0x45cc6 else +0xb8 at 0x45cd4; 0x45c80: +0xc0 else
  +0xc4; 0x45c50: 0x54f40 else 0x54f90). (3) PR-399's paragraph calls
  0x45c20 "the mirror of bit 0x20" as if it branched; it does not test
  anything - it clears bit 0x20 of [[arg]+0xb6] and re-or's it from
  ([node+0x8]&1)<<5. What those six verbs DO to the object, as PR-399
  described it, is unchanged; the owner and the meaning of the branch
  value are what change.
MEASURED: (a) THE SHAPE. 30 rows at 0xa0f28, stride 0x18, carry 25
  distinct +0x04 verbs (six rows share 0x457e0). Decoded from each verb's
  own address (pr400_visitshape.py, pr400_nodeverbs.txt), 23 of the 25
  open the same way: save the second argument, then `call 0x457e0`, then
  exactly one type-specific action. The two exceptions ARE the walk:
  0x457e0 is `mov ebx,[eax]; test ebx,ebx; je ret; mov eax,ebx; mov
  ebx,[ebx+4]; call [ebx+4]` - visit the next link's +0x04 with that link
  in eax, and stop at a null link - and 0x45750 is the variant that
  first writes through the level record (PR-101) and then walks. So a
  visit is a right fold: the chain is walked to its end before the first
  action runs, and the LAST node's action happens first. (PR-399 named the
  six surface verbs; this row reads the other 18.)
  (b) SLOT-ONLY DISPATCH. A raw scan of every rel32 call and jump in the
  image finds ZERO direct edges into the 24 per-type verbs, and 23 direct
  edges into 0x457e0, all of them inside those verbs (0x459b3, 0x459d3,
  0x459f3, 0x45a13, 0x45a37, 0x45a53, 0x45a74, 0x45a93, 0x45ab7,
  0x45ae3, 0x45b06, 0x45b28, 0x45b58, 0x45b96, 0x45bb3, 0x45bd3,
  0x45c06, 0x45c26, 0x45c56, 0x45c86, 0x45cb6, 0x45ce7, 0x45d18). The
  verb is reachable only as `[row+4]`, which is why PR-399's "nothing
  calls it" reading of the same code was half right.
  (c) THE ACTION, PER ROW. After the walk, 12 verbs make no call at all
  and write one constant to one object field - 0x459b0 is `mov eax,[ebx];
  mov ebx,[eax+0x99]; neg ebx; mov [eax+0x99],ebx`, which NEGATES
  [[arg]+0x99]; 0x459f0 writes -1 and 0x45a10 writes 1 to [[arg]+0x6d].
  Seven call a known helper on [[arg]]: 0x52b10 (PR-137's 16-byte
  per-object queue node) from 0x45a70, from 0x45ce0 with edx=1 and from
  0x45d10 twice; 0x52c80 from 0x45ab0, 0x45b20, 0x45b50; 0x52cc0 from
  0x45ae0, 0x45b00; 0x52d00 from 0x45bb0; 0x53670 (the facing flip of
  PR-160) from 0x459d0; 0x52070 (the word setter of PR-105) from 0x45a50
  with eax = edx itself; 0x1cc10 from 0x45a90. Four run the OBJECT's
  class verbs: 0x45bd0 `call [class+0x30]` then `[class+0x1c]` then
  writes 0 to [[arg]+0x20]; 0x45c00 `[class+0x30]` then `[class+0x2c]`;
  0x45b90 `[class+0x30]` then `[class+0x0c]`; 0x45cb0, 0x45c80, 0x45c50
  and 0x45c20 are the four pair dispatchers of (d). One more, 0x45a30,
  visits a second object's +0x04 through `[esi+4]`.
  (d) THE PAIR DISPATCHERS AND THEIR BRANCH VALUE. Four verbs end the
  same way: they walk, then test the NODE's own field at +8 (`cmp DWORD
  PTR [ecx+0x8],0` with ecx = the node, at 0x45c8b, 0x45cbb, 0x45c5b),
  and BOTH arms call the object - non-zero takes the first verb of a
  pair, zero takes its partner. 0x45cb0 runs `[class+0xb4]` (0x45cc6) or
  `[class+0xb8]` (0x45cd4); 0x45c80 runs `[class+0xc0]` (0x45c96) or
  `[class+0xc4]` (0x45ca4); 0x45c50 runs 0x54f40 (0x45c63) or 0x54f90
  (0x45c6d), which are not table slots; 0x45c20 does not branch at all -
  it clears bit 0x20 of [[arg]+0xb6] and re-or's it from
  ([node+0x8]&1)<<5 (0x45c36-0x45c45). So PR-399's "chooses between the
  pair" is right but incomplete: the pair is not gated, one of its two
  members always runs, and what decides which is the value the node
  itself carries - the same field the +0x10 channel query 0x45dc0 adds
  into an output (`add [out],[node+8]`). 0x45c00 is the odd one of the
  six: it reads [node+0xc] and [node+0x8] but runs its two class verbs
  unconditionally.
  (e) WHO INSTALLS A ROW. Every one of the 30 rows is named by code that
  writes it at [x+4]: between two and nine sites each, all in
  0x45750-0x47d50 (0xa0f28 by 0x45ea1, 0x46db5, 0x46dc5 and one more;
  0xa1078 by 0x46a42, 0x46aa5, 0x47641, 0x478b2; 0xa1180 by 0x462bb,
  0x4717b, 0x47b3c; the full list in pr400_rowctors.txt, 30 of 30 rows
  named). Those are the per-kind builders PR-101 noticed, and they are
  the way back from a row to the authored thing it stands for.

- WHY. PR-399 ended with a question it could not answer - if the only way
  into the object's attach, detach, land and leave code is a class slot
  that nobody calls, is that code alive at all? This row answers it from
  the callee side and the answer is a shape, not a call graph: the slot is
  a visit verb, every node type implements it the same three steps, and
  the walk makes a chain of them fold from the tail. That matters beyond
  the attachment question. It says an authored list of these nodes applies
  its LAST entry first, which is the kind of detail that decides whether a
  ported sequence matches the original. It moves a value - the node's own
  +8 word - where four rows put a surface handle, and it shows that the
  land/leave and lock pairs are never gated: one member of the pair
  always runs, so "not attached" is not "nothing happens", it is the
  other verb of the pair. And it hands the next row a concrete way back
  from a class row to the authored directive it models: the two to nine
  builder sites that install it.

- WHY. PR-400 closed with a shape and no way into it, and the obvious
  guess - that some code holds a node in a register and calls through its
  +0x04 - is false in this image. The engine never keeps a node in a
  register across a boundary: it keeps a POSITION. Both entry points are
  index operations, one against a record's own row array and two against
  a global slot that the image fills with exactly one static row. That
  answers the question this line of work has been circling since PR-399 -
  how authored clause nodes reach the object's land/lock verbs - without
  needing a clause-walker: the row-advance visits the row, the row's own
  verb is the bare walk, and the walk reaches each clause's verb. It also
  retires a nine-year-old loose end, PR-101's item (4): the mysterious
  0x98278-indirect call inside the row-advance is a base delete, so the
  row-advance frees what it visited.

  or one of exactly three: 0xa9ab8 -> 0x74be8, 0xa9ab0+0xc -> 0x74bec,

  0xc8, 1, then those three pointers, i.e. a count, an index and a

- WHY. PR-401 found three `call [reg+4]` sites selected by index and
  assumed all three were node-class visits, which made the 0xcf518 slot
  look like a second family of clause rows. It is not: 0xa9ab8 is the
  base-implementation table of an invoke-by-descriptor helper, and its
  three entries are arithmetic thunks - one of them is the textbook
  virtual-this computation. Reading the block turns a false lead into a
  real mechanism: the engine calls methods through a DESCRIPTOR whose
  first word is a calling-convention kind, with twelve cases, two entry
  points that take the receiver from a global current object, and a
  message path that names itself ("undefined constructor or destructor
  called!"). That is worth recording before it is mistaken for game
  semantics again - and the 0x96140 blocks show the descriptors are
  authored data, which is the thread a later row should pull.

- WHY. Three rows in a row reached for a game-side meaning for the same
  bytes. PR-401 read 0xa9ab8 as a class row, PR-402 read 0x96140 as a
  table of call descriptors, and both were wrong in the same direction -
  they were reading the engine's own C++ runtime. The tell is a shape
  that appears twice with nothing in common between the two classes:
  `test dl,0x4` -> the free pair, else swap the vtable to the base
  record, run the base destructor, and for `dl&2` free. Once that is
  seen, the 481-copy field, the 257 code sites and the base thunk at
  0xcf518 all fall into place as construction and destruction of the
  engine's own objects, and the game-side claim they were supporting
  shrinks to the honest size: exactly ONE node-class visit, 0x520e1.
  The lesson is cheap to carry: before naming an unknown block by the
  game model, check whether it is the runtime's.

- WHY. PR-400 and PR-401 built a clean story - the row-advance visits the
  node at the current row - and it rested on one instruction sequence
  read once. This row went to the other side of the same field, found
  141 sites that write it, and they all write a CLASS TABLE from a
  generated family whose three shared verbs do exactly the thing the
  story needed done: index an element array by a cursor and call through
  the element's class. Either those 140 tables are the element classes
  and the array reading is wrong, or the field is overloaded and the
  code-generation family belongs to a different owner. Both options are
  interesting and neither is established, so the honest output is the
  correction plus the census - and a much better next question: the 140
  generated tables are the largest single family of class tables in the
  image, 4.5 times the size of the node-class run PR-101 counted, and
  nobody has said what they are for.

  slots are the 25 verbs PR-400 named: row 0 is 0x46d70, 0x459b0,

  pr405_thunk.txt)

  mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x2e],0xa09f0; mov eax,[eax+0x2a]; xor edx,edx;

  edx,edx; call 0x21670; pop ebx; ret` - the class table is installed
  last, as a destructor does, then the pointer at +0x2a is released by
  the 0x74bc0/0x74be0 pair of PR-403, then the base subobject at +0x1e
  is destructed by 0x57a00 and the block freed by 0x21670. 0x3fb30 is
  the matching base constructor: it allocates, `lea ebx,[eax+0x1e]`,
  `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x16],0xffffffff` (the cursor), and runs the
  0x96200/0x961fc engine pair at that subobject. The allocation in
  front of each of the 141 stores is `mov eax,N; call 0x5c320` with
  N = 0x32 in 135 sites, 0x36, 0x3e in two each, and 0x46 in one; two
  sites allocate differently. And four sites call THROUGH that field
  without indexing it: 0x3fc84, 0x3fc98 and 0x3fca9 do
  `mov ebx,[ecx+0x2e]; ...; call DWORD PTR [ebx+0x10]`, and 0x215d8
  does `mov ebx,[eax+0x2e]; mov edx,2; call DWORD PTR [ebx]`. (pr405_
  2e.txt, pr405_alloc.txt)
  (c) THE THUNK AT +0x04 OF THE GENERATED TABLES. Reading each of the
  140 tables' first seven slots and decoding the first instruction of
  each target: slot +0x00 is a plain function in all 140 (a ctor, e.g.
  0xa3054's 0x61f00), and slot +0x04 is a two-instruction thunk
  `call <f>; ret` in 136 of them, where f is the very next slot, +0x08
  (0xa3054 has 0x61de0 = `call 0x3fdf0; ret`, and 0x3fdf0 is its own
  +0x08). So for this family a call through [table+0x04] runs the
  method at [table+0x08] - the mirror of PR-400's discovery that the
  node classes' +0x04 verbs are the interesting ones. (pr405_thunk.txt)
  (d) THE THIRD FIELD, [obj+0x44]. 42 immediate sites store a class
  table at `DWORD PTR [reg+0x44]` - 17 of the 18 distinct values there
  are class tables, e.g. `mov DWORD PTR [eax+0x44],0x97c9c` at 0x1e119
  and 0x23115, and 0xa25d4 at 0x524cf and 0x52508. That is how the
  record classes of PR-401 are attached, and the record code calls
  through that field: 0x52331-0x52338 is `mov esi,[ebp+0x44]; mov
  eax,ebp; call DWORD PTR [esi+0x18]` - the row-advance at +0x18 of
  that table. The field is not itself a vptr in the same sense: of the
  14 tables, 9 hold data addresses or small integers at their +0x44
  (0x23ea0, 0x12a00, 0xbf00, 0x2a00, 0x44b80, 0x3). (pr405_vptr.txt)

- WHY. PR-404 ended by doubting its own finding, and the doubt came from
  assuming a class table can only live in one place per object. It does
  not: this engine keeps three different table fields at three different
  offsets, and once all three are on the table PR-400's and PR-401's
  reading survives intact - `[[T]+cursor*4]+4` names the +0x04 verb
  whenever T is the table, which is the case for the node classes whose
  tables sit at [node+0x04]. What is genuinely unresolved is narrower
  and much more useful: whether the 140 generated state classes and the
  14 record classes are one object (the field layouts fit: cursor at
  +0x16, table at +0x2e, table at +0x44, and the cursor the row-advance
  uses is at +0x04 of a 0x48+-byte object), because if they are, the
  "node list" the row cursor walks is a vtable and the row index is a
  slot number.

- WHY. This is the thread PR-400 left, ten rows back: "which authored
  directive is each row?" turned out to be the wrong question for the
  node classes, but the right one for the record classes - and here is
  the answer for those: the record class is selected by the state name
  string, and there are exactly sixteen of them, one per authored state
  shape that carries a clause ladder. That gives the port a checkable
  claim it never had - a state name maps to one of 16 record classes,
  and the class determines the row step, the row-advance and the
  clause-match verbs, which is the shape PR-111 and PR-163 modelled
  from behaviour alone.

- WHY. Eleven rows have described the row-advance from the outside; this
  is the first that says what the cursor IS. It is set once, at state
  entry, to count-minus-one, and the row-advance then walks it - so
  authored clause rows run last-to-first unless something else resets
  it, and that single sentence is testable against the port, which
  walks its ladder forward. The second useful fact is cheaper: a record
  class differs from another record class in exactly two slots, +0x08
  and +0x1c, so the port's "state" object and the engine's are much
  closer than the sixteen tables suggested - the state is a pair of
  hooks plus a name, not a subclass of anything large.

MEASURED: (a) HOW THE CHAIN PAIRS. The pattern is `mov edx,<keyword>;
  mov eax,[ebp-0x20]; call 0x76a69; test eax,eax; jne <next keyword>;
  or BYTE PTR [esi+0x12],<mask>; jmp 0x51dc3`. The `jne` on NO match
  jumps to the NEXT keyword's string load, and the OR on a match is at
  the bottom of that block - so the mask printed just after a keyword
  literal belongs to THAT keyword, and the keyword string that appears
  immediately above an OR belongs to the NEXT one. A walk that prints
  each OR with the last literal loaded therefore shifts every name by
  one; that is how PR-408's second reading fooled me. Pairing them the
  other way gives BY_X 0x1 at 0x51b6f, BY_Y 0x2 at 0x51b89, BY_TIME
  0x3 at 0x51ba3, BY_TX 0x4 at 0x51bbd, BY_TY 0x8 at 0x51bd7,
  FRAME_REV 0x10 at 0x51bf1, SEQ_REV_X 0x20 at 0x51c0b, CHECK_ZW 0x40
  at 0x51c25, CHECK_ANI 0x80 at 0x51c3f, CHECK_ALL 0x1c0 at 0x51c73,
  SOLID2 0x20400 at 0x51d5f, SEMI_SOLID 0x40400 at 0x51d79. Note
  CHECK_ZW is compared first (0x51c14, mask 0x40) and CHECK_ANI second
  (0x51c2e, mask 0x80). (b) THE MODE FIELD. 0x543a2 is the row-clock
  feed: `mov eax,[obj+0x5c]; mov edx,[obj+0x50]; mov eax,[edx+eax*4];
  mov eax,[eax+0x12]; and eax,0x7; cmp eax,4; ja 0x5443f; jmp
  [eax*4+0x54380]`. The table 0x54380 = 0x543c6, 0x543dc, 0x543fb,
  0x543f2, 0x5441b: the first two arms add |[obj+0xca]| and |[obj+
  0xce]| to the row clock [obj+0xa1]; the third adds [world+0x388] per
  iteration; the fourth requires [obj+0xba] non-zero first and the
  fifth requires [obj+0xbe] non-zero first, both then adding the same
  [world+0x388]. With the table of (a) the mode field reads cleanly:
  bits 0..2, 1 = BY_X, 2 = BY_Y, 3 = BY_TIME, 4 = BY_TX, and BY_TY's
  0x8 is outside the mask, so `and eax,7` maps it to 0 - the slot no
  keyword produces, whose arm adds |[obj+0xca]|. (c) THE FIELD IS CLEAN,
  AND BY_TY DOES NOT REACH IT. No flag keyword writes bits 0..2:
  CHECK_ZW is 0x40, CHECK_ANI 0x80, CHECK_ALL 0x1c0, SEQ_REV_Y 0x40 -
  all at bit 5 or above - so the mode is set by the BY_* keyword alone
  and cannot be corrupted by the rest of the line. But BY_TY's 0x08 is
  bit 3, OUTSIDE `and eax,0x7`: an authored `control=BY_TY` on its own
  produces the word 0x08, which masks to mode 0 and takes the first arm
  of the dispatcher, adding |[obj+0xca]| - the BY_X behaviour. The arm
  that guards on [obj+0xbe], which is the one PR-108 read as the
  vertical feed, is reached only by a word whose bits 0..2 are 4, and
  the only keyword that writes that is BY_TX.

  field is written only by the BY_* keywords happens to be right, but
  for the wrong reason.
MEASURED: (a) THE PAIRING RULE, SETTLED. The chain is `mov edx,
  <keyword>; mov eax,[ebp-0x20]; call 0x76a69; test eax,eax;` then
  either `je`/`jne`. 0x76a69 upper-cases both operands and returns
  `[a]-[b]` of the first differing byte (0x76a92-0x76aa9), so ZERO
  means equal and the branch to the OR is the MATCH arm; the keyword
  that matches is the literal loaded at the TOP of that block. The one
  exception is BY_X: its compare at 0x51b49 uses `je 0x51dc3` (0x51b58,
  the only wide je in the chain) and its match arm performs NO write -
  BY_X is the value the word already has, because 0x51b2e zeroes
  [rec+0x12] first. (b) THE FULL TABLE. [rec+0x12] byte: BY_Y 0x01
  (0x51b6f), BY_TIME 0x02 (0x51b89), BY_TX 0x03 (0x51ba3), BY_TY 0x04
  (0x51bbd), FRAME_REV 0x08 (0x51bd7), SEQ_REV_X 0x10 (0x51bf1),
  SEQ_REV_Y 0x20 (0x51c0b), CHECK_ANI 0x40 (0x51c3f), CHECK_ZW 0x80
  (0x51c25). [rec+0x13] byte: CHECK_LN 0x01 (0x51c59), CHECK_LEW 0x02
  (0x51c8f), SOLID 0x04 (0x51cc3), CH_DIR 0x08 (0x51cdd), INV_V 0x10
  (0x51cf7), DANGER 0x20 (0x51d11), CHECK_ALL_PLANE 0x80 (0x51d2b).
  [rec+0x14] byte: ANTI_SOLID 0x01 (0x51d45), ANTI_POCISK 0x08
  (0x51d93). WORD/DWORD macros: CHECK_ALL ORs the WORD 0x1c0 (0x51c73)
  = CHECK_ANI | CHECK_ZW | CHECK_LN; SOLID2 ORs the DWORD 0x20400
  (0x51d5f) = SOLID | CHECK_ZW | bit 17; SEMI_SOLID 0x40400 (0x51d79)
  = SOLID | CHECK_ZW | bit 14. The separators are `,` OR `|` (0x51dd8

  token prints the engine's own message `Bledny control %s w pliku %s.`
  (0x9223b, used at 0x51dac) when the log pointer 0xa92d4 is set. (c)
  THE MODE FIELD IS CLEAN, AND THE CENSUS PROVES IT. With
   BY_TY = 0x04 the modes are 1, 2, 3, 4 and no flag keyword writes
   bits 0..2: CHECK_ANI 0x40 and up all start at bit 6, and CHECK_ALL's

   control= lines reproduces the published numbers exactly - mode 2

   not one line produces a word whose bits 0..2 fall outside 0..4.

   and 20 comma lines, and every token in it matches a keyword, so the
   engine's error path never fires on shipped data.

- WHY. Three rows of me reading one compare chain produced three
  different tables, and this row settles it by reading the comparison
  helper itself rather than guessing the branch convention. That removes
  the finding I announced last row - there is no keyword-versus-dispatch
  crossing, the author's BY_TX and BY_TY do line up with the
  [obj+0xba]/[obj+0xbe] guarded arms - and leaves two things worth
  keeping. First, the row-cursor mirror of PR-407 is switched by
  SEQ_REV_X against SEQ_REV_Y, which is the reading of those names that
  matches what the code does, and both are rare on shipped data (7 and
  22 states). Second, the control fields are three bytes wide, not one,
  and nine keywords write the second and third of them; the port's
  single LL_CTRL_* word cannot represent ANTI_SOLID, ANTI_POCISK,
  CHECK_BASE_LN or CHECK_ALL_PLANE the way the engine does. The honest
  output of this row is mostly a retraction, and the journal needs it
  there, because the wrong tables are already in OI-111 and in two
  commit messages.

- WHY. PR-407 left the row cursor's upper bound unexplained: something
  wrote a "count" into +0x36 and a "sibling" into +0x32 and neither had a
  source. This row says where they come from - an interval, looked up by
  value, in a table that is seeded from the executable's own .data - and
  with it the shape of the thing the port has no analogue for: the port
  takes a state's row count from the number of authored row lines and
  never derives one from a range, so the engine's "this walk belongs to an
  x-interval, and its ends are marked ten units in from each boundary" is
  unmodelled. That is worth recording before any further row-cursor work,
  because the mirror branch of 0x52360 counts down from exactly this
  value.

                                                            [rec+0x12]
      C = ([obj+0x99] == -1)

  the answers with -1 and +1; 0x73438-0x73459 is the same pair. So the
  +0x70 verb answers whether a coordinate is near one end of the
  object's segment, in ten-unit steps, with -1 for false and 1 for true -
  which is why the row-advance can test it with `cmp eax,-1`: that is
  "NOT at a boundary".

  depends on dir.

  requires -1. It then XORs the two operands (0x523b8) and writes
  count - edx - 1 if non-zero (0x523bc-0x523c5) else edx (0x523cb).

  again at 0x53883, and read as a plain value by the mode dispatcher's

  "this state has been running for at least one row" flag whose setter is
  not found.
