- WHY. PR-101 already wrote this expression down - the port's own
  comment at ll_play.c:763-775 names the two guards and the
  `[obj+0x99] == -1` third operand and records the mirror as unmodelled.
  What this row adds is what the operands ARE. The first is PR-411's
  segment predicate: the same vtable slot, called one instruction after a
  `+0xa` / `-0xa` compare against the two ends of the object's interval at
  0x730d3 and 0x73438, answers -1 or +1. The second is the walk
  direction itself: [obj+0x71] is only ever set to 1 or -1, in the block
  that also sets the horizontal and vertical speed accumulators. So the
  authored SEQ_REV flag means "reverse at the end of my segment, when I am
  facing back along it", not "walk backwards", and the port - which
  counts these tokens as known gaps and walks forward - has a named
  condition set it could now reproduce. The opposite test sense at state
  entry (jge there, cmp -1 in the row path) is recorded as found, not as
  explained; it is either a bug in the original or a hint that the entry
  call answers something else, and the OPENS line says so.

- WHY. PR-411 was the first row to name this mechanism and it got three
  of its four structural facts wrong, which matters because PR-412 then
  built on it: the segment predicate is keyed on the container's FIRST
  dword and gated on its SECOND being within ten of an anchor value, so
  the "segment" an object walks is selected by a two-coordinate test, not
  by an index the object carries. With the seeding also corrected - the
  ranges, their high ends and their anchor indices are all compiled-in
  data in the executable, not level data and not computed - the open
  question becomes the honest one: whose coordinates are those, and why
  the anchors step by 96. That is a question the shipped level files can
  answer, not more disassembly.

- WHY. Four rows in a row used these tables as if their shape were known
  (PR-404 counted 140 of them; PR-411 to PR-413 called a verb out of
  one) and nobody had read one. The shape is small and decisive: a state
  class is four authored-shaped verbs plus three identical base
  functions, and the base functions all revolve around one child index at
  [obj+0x16]. For the port that is the boundary between what a state
  class can do and what the engine does for every state: anything the
  port models per state belongs to those four slots, and the shared trio
  means the engine's per-state behaviour is normally a delegation to the
  object's child, which is the thing the port's state records have no
  equivalent of.

  could not say what the shared ones did, and called [obj+0x16] a child
  index. It is not a child: it is a cursor, and the state-class object

  per-state instance, created on demand by calling that state's own
  +0x18 verb. That is the boundary PR-414 was looking for stated
  exactly: for every authored state the engine keeps a list of items and,
  per item, one object that only that state's +0x18 factory knows how to
  make. The port has item lists but no per-item instance layer, so any
  future difference in how often per-row setup runs has a named mechanism
  behind it, and the pure-virtual table at 0xa09f0 says the base class
  was never instantiated in the original either.

- WHY. Five rows have described the segment lookup as if it were general
  machinery; it has exactly one real user, one function, the same
  function that owns the row cursor and the row direction law of
  PR-412. That makes the mechanism's role definite: the interval table
  selects which of 17 authored x-ranges an object is inside, once per
  state verb, using its container's two coordinate dwords, and the answer
  is cached in the object at [obj+0x3a] or [obj+0x42]. For the port that
  is a concrete missing concept - it has no notion of an authored level
  being cut into ranges with anchor values - and the fact that the table
  is seeded once from the executable's own data, not from any level file,
  says those ranges belong to the engine, not to the content.

- WHY. This is the first row to read the neighbourhood of the interval
  table instead of the table, and the neighbourhood is not scratch: the
  engine keeps a chain of live scene objects at 0xcedf0/+0x288 and a
  seven-slot registry at 0xcedf4 in the same BSS block as the 17
  authored intervals. Two consequences worth having on the record. First,
  a wrong name is fixed before it spreads: PR-411 and PR-416 both called
  0xcedf0 a segment count, and it is a list head - the guard `if
  (0xcedf0 == 0) return` in the permute function of PR-416 is simply
  "no objects registered". Second, the round-and-carry accumulator pair
  0xced10/0xced14 is a pattern the port already implements per object for
  the BY_X fractional-pixel carry, but here it is one global sum over all
  objects whose type field is 0x22 or 0x23 - a level-wide quantity the
  port has no equivalent of.

- WHY. Four rows reached the same object without naming it: PR-413 and
  PR-416 read its first two dwords as the segment lookup's key and probe,
  PR-417 pushed and popped it on a chain, PR-414 found the table installed
  at its +0xc. Here it has a class: 24 method slots, three of them
  overridden per derived class, register and unregister at +0x20 and
  +0x08. That is also the place where the port's model thins out - the
  port's scene objects carry no class tables, no registry slot index and
  no chain link, so anything in the engine that iterates "all registered
  objects of this kind" (which is what the chain implies) has no port
  counterpart at all. And PR-414's "overlapping views of one table" was
  wrong in a way that mattered: the second field is the BASE table, which
  is exactly what makes the shifted first field make sense.

  re-implementation drift apart silently - a key the engine reads and the
  port ignores is a behaviour gap with no symptom until some level uses
  it. Two of those 64 also show the cost of not having the vocabulary:
  narty_param's four values are hundredths, which is only visible from
  the `/100.0` in its scanner, and JumpCoef1000's name says the same
  thing about a jump coefficient. Neither key appears in the unpacked
  shipped levels, so today they are inert - but a port that does not
  know them cannot report that honestly.

## PR-420 - THE `(x)` ROW ARGUMENT OF AN AUTHORED TRANSITION LINE IS NOT
## A NAME: THE PARSER HAS NO x CASE, AND A NON-NUMERIC ARGUMENT BECOMES 0

```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the row argument of an authored transition line - the exact
  parse of `A_FOLLOW(x)=K_GEN2`, the three helpers it uses, what each
  shape of argument yields, the corpus counts of the argument forms, and
  what the states that use `x` look like
ADDRESSES: 0x51e07, 0x51e12, 0x51e17, 0x51e1f, 0x51e22, 0x51e27, 0x51e2a,
  0x51e2f, 0x51e36, 0x51e3b, 0x51e3e, 0x51e43, 0x51e4d, 0x51e54, 0x52360,
  0x52381, 0x523cb, 0x57d30, 0x57d44, 0x57db0, 0x57dbb, 0x57dc3, 0x57fd0,
  0x74cc8, 0x76fa3, 0x76fc4, 0x76fd3, 0x76ff0, 0x76fff, 0x9225c, 0x92310,
  0xa9510, 0xa68b4, 0xa25d4, 0x11, 0x04, 0x7d, 0x1f4
NAMES: row argument, transition line parse, non-numeric argument, atoi
  skip, ctype class table, authored x, row start, pr420_rowargs.txt,
  OI-016, OI-111, OI-128
CODE: no: no file under ported/ or tools/ changes. The port's behaviour
  for this case is already what the engine's is - see WHY.
HOOKS: none - no leg and no fixture moves.
OPENS: WHAT THE AUTHORS MEANT BY x - 44 of the 777 unpacked .MOV files
    use it, always as the whole argument, and the states that carry it are
    dominated by control=BY_TIME and FRAME_REV, so it reads as "start at
    the beginning", but no comment or code supports a different intent;
    whether any packed level outside the unpacked corpus uses another
    non-numeric argument, since the parse would silently turn it into 0
    too; WHAT THE 125-ENTRY TABLE AT 0xa9510 IS, copied by 0x57d30 into a
    0x1f4-byte scratch buffer - it is the token grammar this parser
    works from, and it has not been read; and whether the 0x76fa3 helper
    is shared with other parsers, which would make every one of them
    equally tolerant of a non-numeric value.
CLOSES: PR-411's OPENS item WHETHER THE AUTHORED PARENTHESISED ROW
  ARGUMENT IS THE ENGINE'S INTERVAL LOOKUP. It is not: the transition
  parser never calls anything near 0x37150, and the argument never reaches
  a numeric table - it is converted by sscanf/atoi at parse time and
  stored as a small integer.
CORRECTS: PR-107's note in the port, at ported/ll_play.c:483-518, which
  says an "absent or non-numeric" token stores -1: only an ABSENT or
  EMPTY group stores -1.
  A PRESENT but non-numeric argument such as x stores 0, because
  0x51e36 is reached only when the %ld scan succeeded and the value it
  calls is an atoi-style scanner, not a strict one. The port's outcome for
  `x` is unchanged - it treats it as -1 and starts at row 0, and the
  engine's 0 also means row 0 - so this corrects the description, not the
  model.
MEASURED: (a) THE GRAMMAR OF ONE TRANSITION LINE. 0x51e12 loads ecx =
  0x9225c, whose bytes are ` ( %[^) ] %*[)] = `, with edx = 1, and calls
  0x57d30, which copies a 125-entry table from 0xa9510 into a 0x1f4-byte
  stack buffer and matches the line against it. Exactly ONE capture group
  exists - the left-hand state name - and everything inside parentheses
  is matched by `%*[)]`, i.e. skipped. So the name is what the parser
  resolves (0x51e4d: `call 0x49610` with the name in ecx); the argument
  is handled separately: 0x51e27 calls 0x57db0, which pushes the format
  0x92310 = `%ld` and calls the scanner 0x74cc8, returning 1 only if a
  long was read. (pr420_rowargs)
  (b) THE THREE OUTCOMES. Empty or missing group: 0x57db0 returns 0, so
  0x51e3e stores -1. A numeric group: 0x51e36 calls 0x57fd0 = `call
  0x76fa3`, and 0x51e3b decrements - the authored 1-based number becomes
  a 0-based row. A NON-NUMERIC group: 0x57db0 also returns 1, because
  0x76fa3 is not strict - it first SKIPS letters (0x76fa6: while ctype
  [c+1] AND 0x2, i.e. alnum, advance), then takes an optional sign, then
  accumulates digits (0x76ff0: `ebx = ebx*10 + c`, minus 0x30), and
  returns 0 when no digit was ever seen - and note that the two tests
  disagree, so a mixed token such as `x2` fails the %ld scan yet still
  yields 2 from this one. `x` therefore becomes 0, and the
  row-setter at state entry, 0x52360, writes rec+0x04 = 0 (its only
  refusal is a negative argument, `test edx,edx; jl` at 0x52381).
  (c) THE CORPUS. Across the 777 unpacked .MOV files the parenthesised
  argument is `(1)` 2415 times, `(x)` 208 times, and other small numbers
  a few dozen each - so `x` is 8 percent of the uses, in 44 distinct
  files. It is always the whole argument: no form such as `A_WAIT(x,2)`
  occurs. The .MOV files that contain it carry control lines dominated by
  `control=BY_TIME|FRAME_REV|CHECK_ALL...`.
  (d) THE ctype TABLE. 0xa68b4 is a 256-entry class table indexed by
  character: bit 0 space (0x20), bit 3 alphanumerics, bit 5 digits
  (0x30-0x39). The classes 0x2 and 0x20 are what 0x76fa3 tests, and no
  bit 4 (punctuation) class exists in the table's used range.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok);
  The diff is NEXT_STEPS.md, docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md and the generated
  docs/RE_INDEX.md only - nothing under ported/, tools/, the Makefile or
  .github - so the light profile of section 2 rule 4 applies. Evidence:
  /tmp/opencode/pr420_docs.log (tools/re_index.py, then
  `make verify-docs verify-index`, rc=0, index byte-identical) and
  /tmp/opencode/pr420_rowargs.txt (the argument-form census over the 777
  unpacked .MOV files in /tmp/opencode/mov, and the three parse
  outcomes). 0x51e07, 0x57db0, 0x57fd0 and 0x76fa3 were decoded from
  their own entry addresses, and the scan format and grammar literals
  were read as bytes at 0x9225c and 0x92310 from build/leo/leo.img.
```

- WHY. PR-411 left "is the authored `(x)` the engine's interval lookup?"
  as an open question, and PR-412 then made `x` sound like it might mean
  "my current position". It does not: the transition parser has no case
  for the letter at all, and an argument it cannot read as a number
  becomes 0 through an atoi that first throws away letters. Two things
  follow. The port's model choice is vindicated - its "(x) means start at
  the top" is what the engine does - but its comment states the wrong
  reason, and that comment is quoted by future readers, so the difference
  between "absent means -1" and "non-numeric means 0" is now written down
  correctly. And the authored habit is measurable: 208 uses in 44 files,
  always alone, in states whose control word is usually BY_TIME - that is
  content evidence, not code, and it belongs on the record.

- WHY. PR-418 established that this class family exists and that a
  variant overrides three methods, but not how many variants there are or
  what they vary. Twelve, and what they vary is a 20-byte class-data
  block plus a getter - the behaviour is inherited wholesale. That is the
  cheapest possible extension mechanism, and it is the opposite of what
  the port does: the port branches on an authored object NAME (ll_level.c
  1555-1556, `strcasecmp(leaf,"PALMA")` and `"KATAPULT"`), while the
  engine encodes the same variety as compiled variants selected at
  construction time. Also new: these constructors double as destructors
  chosen by a mode bit, so "how many scene objects exist and when are
  they freed" is a question about a flag, not about a call site - which
  matters for anything in the port that tries to match object lifetime.

- WHY. This is the first row that reads the compiler's own class
  metadata rather than following it. The payoff is a census of the engine
  as a program: 503 classes, 187 of them without a constructor, sizes
  from 8 to 7085 bytes, and the largest concentration at 50 bytes. For
  this project the two cross-checks matter most: the 0x60-byte state
  record of PR-406 and the field map of the scene object of PR-418 are
  now confirmed by the sizes the executable itself carries, so any future
  claim about a field beyond +0x288 on that object or +0x60 on a state
  record is refutable from one dword. It also gives every later row a
  cheap way to identify an unknown object - find its descriptor and read
  its size and constructor triple.

- WHY. The port's object model has always branched on authored names
  because that is what the data contains; this row proves the engine
  does exactly the same, mechanically: names come off the level
  description line, case is folded, and 160+ compiled branches pick
  size plus constructor. The practical payoff is a completion measure
  with a denominator - the 178 ETAPY leaders, each of which the port
  must map to a behaviour - and three named identities that turn
  abstract rows into things: the scene-object class is a penguin,
  the 0x120 class family is fish, and the third-largest class is a
  gorilla. It also opens the second, larger vocabulary (`AC_*`) whose
  owner file and parser have not been placed - the next known
  unknown.

  journal had no place where such a name meant anything. It does -

  AC_BREAK_NEXT is the engine's own "finish this animation and
  advance" behaviour, not level content. That makes the built-in
  list a first-class part of the state model the port implements,
  and its file-frequency ranking says exactly which ones a faithful
  port needs first: AC_BREAK_NEXT, AC_TIME and AC_ENEMY_ATC lead the

  coverage result after PR-425: authored action names are a subset
  of compiled ones, with 9 spare built-ins as slack.

  transition lines - its body carries a compiled command program,
  and the engine tokenises it once at load into fixed 12-byte items.
  The vocabulary is small enough to port wholesale (34 verbs, and
  the corpus uses ~20 of them), and the two error strings hand the
  class a name, TEventSet, which future rows can anchor. The
  frequency census orders the work: GEN, MOVE, lock, end_level and
  goto are the verbs a faithful port needs; zero_v/zero_t/Wait are
  engine-only slack, exactly like the 9 unused built-ins of
  PR-426.

  verb. The shared families are also data: one run stub behind
  several verbs means the engine itself merged those behaviours
  behind a parameter (lock/unlock/ground_on/ground_off share

  the run stubs named, reading them in file-frequency order
  (MOVE 0x475f0, end_level 0x476b0, goto 0x47710, then the
  0x47460 family) is the direct next step toward a state machine
  the port can execute instead of merely display.

- WHY. PR-428 mapped names to handlers and expected one behaviour
  per verb; the real structure is smaller and stranger - the verbs
  are argument-marshalling classes, and the behaviour always lives
  in three fixed methods of whatever object the command points at.
  That is the engine's command pattern, and it says the port should
  not implement 34 verb functions either: it needs one command
  object with three message calls, plus per-verb argument parsing
  and cloning. It also explains the shared records PR-428 flagged:
  lock/unlock/ground_on/ground_off share a record because the record
  only fixes the argument shape - the distinction must be carried
  elsewhere, and finding that carrier (most likely the subject or a
  parameter word) is the next concrete question on this path.

- WHY. This closes the command path from authored text to run-time:
  a state body is parsed into a chain of small per-verb objects that
  only marshal arguments, each pointing at a nested subject, and the
  row walker drives everything by calling record slots +0x08 and
  +0x0c per item with a scratch buffer that predicates then read.
  The port can mirror exactly this shape - one abstract command with
  clone/delete-by-record, per-verb argument fields, and two hooks
  the state machine calls - instead of inventing its own. The one
  unproven link, that the items walked at 0x52229 ARE those
  compiled commands, is now the single sharpest open question here,
  and the predicate pair 0x495b0/0x47e40 is where the row-condition
  semantics of PR-412 will actually live.

- WHY. The command pattern now has its missing verb: three slots
  forward, one executes, one clones - and execution is "chain
  first, then act", so a script runs in authored order with each
  effect landing on the owner's actor member in a handful of
  instructions per verb. That is directly portable: the port's
  state machine needs an actor with fields at these offsets (the
  direction word at +0x6d and the atc flag byte at +0xb6 are
  concrete new targets for the physics-side work), and verbs like
  ldir/rdir/rev are already fully understood. The paired-constant
  finding also settles the engine's design question from PR-428:
  near-identical commands are one code path plus a data flag, and
  a faithful port should model commands as (opcode record, flag,
  parsed pair), not as text-specific routines.

- WHY. This is where the script layer meets the physics layer the
  port has been rebuilding: the engine's own authoritative actor
  state is now visible at concrete offsets - a locked flag whose
  set/clear conditions exactly match the port's AC_/lock semantics,
  a direction word with one sign-flip accessor, a move-event queue
  in front of motion, and a control bit (CH_DIR, authored in 556
  states per PR-410's census) that gates whether the authored
  chdir command does anything. Each one is testable against the
  port: ll_play already models locked state and facing; wiring the
  direction field and a queued-move model is now unblocked work.
  The corrected control-bit census also upgrades the method:
  bit-test searches must include the load-then-test-dh form, which
  is how CH_DIR hid from PR-410 and how FRAME_REV may still hide.

- WHY. The per-frame contract of the engine's scene objects is now
  legible and tiny: drain queued events into a virtual handler,
  tick through a second virtual, self-free when a flag says so.
  That is exactly the shape ported/ll_play.c's step loop has been
  approximating, and it says a faithful port needs one per-class
  event virtual rather than inline special-case handling, plus the
  self-free flag at object+0x28. The 18-type census also gives a
  concrete work queue for the physics line: reading the base
  implementations of table slots +0x10 and +0x14 will name the
  event semantics (type 1 = the MOVE pair this line started from),
  and those two bodies are the closest engine-side description of
  the step the port still has to match.

- WHY. The engine's event model is now legible end to end: one
  shared baseline vocabulary every object understands, overridden
  per class through the same slot. For the port that means the
  event enum has a common core - store/add a pair, set two
  control bits, clear a pair, set direction, attach, raise a
  signal, move relatively, request deletion - and per-class arms
  on top. Two direct port hooks follow: the signal raise ends in
  a row re-resolution through the 0x49580 merge into [obj+0x60],
  exactly the flag vector PR-435's tick core consults, so the
  port's signal handling and row selection are one pipeline; and
  the MOVE arm shows authored motion is DELTA-based through the
  same position words the pos verb sets, which is what the port's
  step loop must consume.

- WHY. This is the engine's per-frame contract in one line of
  code, and it is exactly what ported/ll_play.c has been
  approximating: fold the object's own flags and the current row's
  conditions into one 12-byte flag vector at [obj+0x60], select
  parameters from the row chosen by the cursor, apply motion
  through the +0x54 pair of calls, then the draw slot +0x28. The
  21-byte sequence-condition entries with target words at +0x0d
  and +0x11 match the authored row language the port already
  parses, so the port's row structs and the engine's row objects
  can now be aligned field by field. The F/T/G row-type letters
  from 0x92281 also name the row classes the parser at 0x52590
  builds - direct input for naming the port's row kinds.

  [row+0x5c], both clamped to 0x82 = 130 (0x525f2-0x52610); the

  and sets [obj+0x58] = 100 (0x4456a-0x44590) before further

  [table+0xa4] with the flags; take the row at [[obj+0x50]+
  edx*4], call its slot +0x20 with the flags, set [obj+0x5c] =
  edx, and finish with virtual [table+0xac]. The equal branch at
  0x53602 follows the [row+0x04] link and updates it. (pr440_rows)

```

- WHY. The authored row language and the engine's row objects are
  now joined: the same parser family that reads a state header
  (PR-410) builds rows, dispatching on the F/T/G letters the port
  already sees in .MOV files, and the row cursor is plain state -
  zeroed when an object is constructed from the state file,
  switched only through the tick's own arm. The cursor and count
  fields [obj+0x58]/[obj+0x5c] are even capped by the ctor at
  130, matching authored-row bounds. For the port this means row
  switching needs no new machinery: keep the index, call the old
  row's exit and the new row's entry through one pair of slots,
  exactly as the switch arm does.

- WHY. The engine's match set has three sources - raised signals,
  held keys, and the intent word - and the port had the first two.
  Shipping the third is what lets a future non-key intent (the
  contact chain, PR-149's arm) become expressible at all. The
  regression is the honest part of this record: the first reading
  of PR-438's builder said "velocity signs"; the ZARIA.01 climb
  chain answered in one run, mid-draft, and the bytes re-read
  under that correction say intent. One PR therefore moves both
  the ledger (PR-224's row closes) and the reading (PR-438's WHY
  is corrected) - and no authored leg moved, which is the check
  that the corrected half is the one the original ran.

  refresh and 0x54eb0's identity stitch them: authored tracking

  becomes a turn. Closing +0x34 and +0x68 also retires the last
  two slots PR-439 left unread on the object's base surface, so
  the next PR can take the row-control keyword chain itself.

  but only ever from the parser's side; this is the consumer
  side, and it is where the table becomes behavior: which bit
  feeds the row clock, which bit lets a scene query vote into
  the flag vector, which pair makes a stone bounce, and which
  bit no one reads at all (CHECK_LN - the port has carried its
  BEHAVIOR for 400 PRs without its consumer ever mattering, and
  this row says that is not an accident). The two PR-410
  negatives that were too strong are fixed where they were said.

  reading arithmetic rather than hopeful, and the port already
  models the receiving half.

  explicit consumes.

  objects at all - they create PR-100's state records. Every A_*
  arm is exactly `mov eax,0x60; call 0x5c320; call 0x524e0;
  mov [rec+0x44],TABLE`: 0x524e0 is the state-record
  constructor (it runs 0x51700 and installs the DEFAULT method
  table 0xa25d4 at [rec+0x44]), and the arm then OVERWRITES that
  field with a per-word row table. So there is one record class
  and the authored action word is selected purely by its method
  table - which is the mechanism the journal already relied on
  for PR-166's control-word verbs, now shown for the A_* words.
  It also settles the sharing question raised in PR-470: sharing
  a table is normal and means "the same behaviour" - A_LOOKDOWN
  and A_SQUAT both take 0x9a894; A_JUMP and A_JUMP_S both take
  0xa2ed4; and PR-135's atc_on/atc_off both take 0xa10f0, with
  lock/lock2/unlock/unlock2/ground_on/ground_off all taking
  0xa10d8. And TLewKadmar2's class arm builds an EXTRA record
  through the same 0x524e0 with the row table 0x9b5f4 - the
  lion's own death-row - while BAL_RAN and TLewRan share
  0x9d590 at field +0x26.

  call 0x76a69; jne next; mov eax,0x60; call 0x5c320; mov
  edx,esi; call 0x524e0; mov [eax+0x44],0x9a8cc` - the source
  string 0x9090d is "A_LOOKUP". (c) THE CONTROL-WORD GROUP: 15
  arms at 0x45e85-0x46bc7 install 8-21-byte records' method

- WHY. The action words looked like a second class vocabulary.
  They are not: they are rows of one record class, differing
  only in the method table written into the same field. That
  makes the engine's authoring model uniform - classes, plan
  rows and action rows are all "a record plus a table installed
  by a name comparison" - and it gives the next read a short
  list: nine A_DEAD row tables.

    0x61000-0x74700 band reads [x+0x16] 60+ times but those
    objects are not 0x1e bytes, so the descriptor's reader is
    elsewhere; the sub-objects of the composite dtor (0x44930,
    0x449d0, 0x44a10, 0x44a40, 0x456e0 through 0x21490/0x214d0)
    - three parts at strides 8, 8 and 0x1b inside a 0x43-byte
    object; and the vector's other verbs (0x97654's entries past
    +0x28).
CLOSES: PR-467's OPENS "what 0x21880 allocates, versus the
  0x1e-byte block allocated right after it in the same factory":
  0x21880 is the element-VECTOR constructor - it calls the
  generic object ctor 0x228d0 with the vector tag (ebx=1,
  edx=0xa), installs the vector's method table 0x97654 at
  [v+0x10] and a word count at [v+0x14], and the factory then
  allocates the 0x1e-byte element (0x43fdf is its ctor) and
  push_backs it: `count=[v+0x8]; [v+0x0]+count*4 = element;
  ++count`, with the empty case routed through the shared
  growth helper 0x22780. The vector's verb +0x28 is the
  DESTROY verb of the descriptor - 0x218a5 calls
  `[[x+0x33]+0x28]` with edx=2, and 0xa0c08+0x28 = 0x442f0.
  It also closes PR-467's "the 14 entries at +0x00..+0x34 of
  block A": they are not business methods but the delete and
  destructor family - 0x44270/0x44280/0x44260/0x442d0/0x442e0
  are bare `ret` stubs, 0x442a0/0x442b0/0x44290/0x442c0 are
  `ret 4` stubs, and the non-stubs (0x44210, 0x442e0, 0x441b0,
  0x442f0) all have the same shape: `test dl,0x4; delete with
  type tag` or the array form (`lea ebx,[eax+0x2b]`, sub 8/8/
  0x1b through 0x21490/0x214d0, then `test dl,2; free`), i.e.
  scalar dtor, vector dtor and composite dtor variants with tags
  0xa0b94/0xa0ba8/0xa0bbc.

  map": the arithmetic about the two views and the box entry
  stands, but the block's contents are overwhelmingly destructor
  and delete variants, so calling it a "method block" overstates
  it - it is the type descriptor of the element, and the only
  behaviour entries are the dtor family plus the two stub bands.
MEASURED: (a) THE FACTORY, verbatim at 0x43fb0: vector from
  0x21880, `mov [element+0x16],0xa0bd0`, `mov eax,0x1e; call
  0x5c320; call 0x43df0`, then the push shown in CLOSES. (b)

  evidence file; 14 of them are `ret`/`ret 4` stubs, 4 are
  delete/dtor variants, 7 are the draw/box band shared with the
  frame view. (c) THE COMPOSITE DTOR at 0x442f0: three
  sub-object destructors at [obj+0x2b], -0x8, -0x8, -0x1b and
  the conditional free - so the object it destructs is 0x43

  type, consistent with the frame descriptor being the tail

```

- WHY. The element was the one object in the engine whose type
  the journal had described only by pointers into it. Reading
  its descriptor entry by entry shows what it actually is: a
  small object in a growable vector, with a default draw (a bare
  `ret`) and a full set of destructor variants. That also fixes
  the language of PR-467 - the block is a type descriptor.

- WHY. The port ticks objects in one flat pass. The original
  gates every object through a virtual getter first, and drains
  its message queue before the physics update, then pumps if the
  latch is on. That ordering is observable - a message sent in
  frame N is consumed by the same frame's update - and the
  [obj+0x2c] gate is why whole classes of authored objects never
  move.

- WHY. The port's level run ends on its own conditions. The
  original ends on three: the hero's pause word, the manager's
  second word, and the run flag - the last written only by
  level start, menu completion, and an exhausted life counter.
  Recording the codes and the flag's three writers makes the
  quit path portable and it retires a wrong reading of
  [mgr+0x3a0] as an effect switch.

  (kind) and +8 == 0x8138764; on a match it takes the payload
  byte at +0xc as an event code, builds a 3-dword bitmap with
  bit (code % 0x20) of word (code / 0x20) set and ORs it into
  [obj+0x60..+0x68] through 0x49580; a kind-0x10 message
  WITHOUT the tag is dropped silently, any other kind
  tail-calls the next default 0x52bb0. The tag immediate
  occurs at exactly 7 code sites: 6 senders (0x2882d, 0x2c5e1,
  0x2c613, 0x2c653, 0x2c99a, 0x3eacf) and the one compare
  0x53780

  kind, marker, code} at +0/+4/+8/+0xc, the same node shape

  direct senders build at 0x28849. It also names the delivery
  trio: broadcast 0x4bc40 over the level, queue-push 0x52b10
  to one object, and direct verb call through the relative
  picker 0x55760 ([[parent+0x40][i]] with count [parent+0x3c],

  cl/0x20 (shr 5 then idiv 0x20 for the remainder), set 1 <<

  0x52b10` followed by storing 1 at [obj+0x571]; 0x2883f/
  0x3eadb build the 4-word stack payload and call [rel+0x10].

```

- WHY. The event bits at [obj+0x60] are how authored triggers
  gate level behaviour (PR-478's bit-7 test), and the port has
  no counterpart for this message bus. The marker makes one
  verb slot carry two protocols, and the six observed codes
  show the intended use: relay to parent, queue to the hero
  singleton, broadcast to all objects, and fan-out to sibling
  children.

  -1; no case folding). The record at [X+0x30] is the
  level-plan script chain - PR-190 F3 / PR-191 F2 established
  its alphabet is 'A','B','L','T' either case (TOUPPER
  0x76e98), and the interpreter 0x4af10 is exactly the
  settings object's method of PR-487 (its body ends with the
  error print 'Bledny opis poziomu - plany', 0x91d2a at

  0x8c settings object (tables 0xa0c5c, tools/crown, PR-487)
  iff the plan contains 'B' (0x42), or contains no 'b'
  (0x62). A plan that uses lowercase 'b' without any 'B' is
  the author's opt-out and leaves [X+0x38c] = 0; 'B' forces
  the object; no B/b at all builds it by default.

  would crash where the engine does not; the engine's real
  contract is "notify thunks tolerate a null belt by writing
  dead scratch" - and the three field pairs at +0x58..+0x6c
  are new settings-object fields for the journal.

  manager), 0xcf054, 0xcf058, 0xcf05c, 0xcf060 (0x51572-
  0x51595) - the five cf05x are built back-to-back with NO
  intervening setup, so they are plain base-built objects;
  debug print descriptors 0xa2198/0xa21ac/0xa21c0 guard the

  called by both ctors - is the owning-array loop: while
  [L+8] elements, call [[L+0x10]+4](elem, edx=4) then

## PR-504 - THE LIGHT FAMILY'S INTERNALS: 8-BYTE PAIR SLOTS,
## THREE OPS TABLES WHERE THE CTOR TABLE IS THE VERB TABLE
## SHIFTED BY ONE SLOT

```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: PR-503's OPENS "what the array elements are".
  The light container family has THREE code-installed ops
  tables (all with zero data-segment stores): 0x9b4b4 =
  [ctor 0x2d7d0, dtor-verb 0x2d8f0, ...], 0x9b4bc =
  [0x2d8f0, ...] and 0x9b4c4 = [0x2da90, 0x2dd20, 0x2dc50,
  0x2dc10, ...]. They are ONE table viewed at successive
  slots: 0x9b4b4 = 0x9b4bc shifted one slot, 0x9b4c4 = two
  - the ctor-path installs put the vptr at the ctor's own
  slot, post-construction installs land on the verb slots
  (0x2d7f7 -> 0x9b4b4, 0x2d90b/0x2d938/0x2d9a3 -> 0x9b4bc,
  0x2daab/0x2dad8 -> 0x9b4c4). THE ELEMENTS ARE NOT
  OBJECTS: the build routine 0x2dad2 allocates count*8
  bytes (0x76a64) and copies PAIRS of dwords from the
  source array - an element = 8-byte (dword, dword) slot;
  the reset verb 0x2da30 walks them calling
  [[L+0x10]+4](self, pair[0], pair[1]) per slot (the
  PR-30x protocol form), while 0x2d8a0 passes the single
  first field. VERB GETTERS of the family: 0x2dc90 =
  `mov eax,ds:0xcec84` (the frame counter global),
  0x2dca0 = `mov eax,ds:0xcec98`, and verb 0x2dd20 runs a
  SECOND startup-singleton block: 10 consecutive `call
  0x44350; mov ds:0xcec98..0xcecb4+` stores. 0x2dc50 calls
  the PR-106 base ctor 0x500b0, sets [obj+0x12a]=-1,
  [obj+0x12e]=1 and installs the TLewKadmar2 pair
  ([obj+8]=0x9b4d4, [obj+0xc]=0x9b4cc - PR-303's named
  table). 0x2dc10 starts `sub eax,0xc` - a contained-part
  dtor whose object sits at +0xc in its owner. In the level
  classes only the LIGHT MANAGER getter (0x2b4c0 at table
  slot +0xc) is exported; the frame/0xcec98 getters belong
  to the inner ops tables only.

## PR-505 - LIGHT ATTACHMENTS ARE BUILT EMPTY AT CONSTRUCTION:
## THE 0x2d820 HELPER ALLOCATES THE LIGHT BASE AND THE CLASS
## SIZES FIX THE +0xa9 ATTACHMENT IN THE ALLOCATION CENSUS

```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: PR-504's OPENS "which code fills a source pair
  array". Answer: NOTHING at construction time. The 8 call
  sites of the light-base ctor 0x2d7d0 pass edx=0 (e.g.
  0x2cac4 `xor edx,edx`), and the helper 0x2d820 - called
  8 times from the KADMAR2 families 0x2ba90/0x2ca80 - is:
  push ecx; mov ecx,ebx; xor ebx,ebx; call 0x2d990 (alloc
  empty light base) -> [L+0x10]=0x9b4b4 -> `mov WORD PTR
  [eax+0x14],cx`: the light base starts with an EMPTY pair
  array (PR-504) plus one WORD parameter from the stack
  argument at [light+0x14]. So pairs are registered only at
  RUNTIME by the protocol verbs (0x2da30 walks slots as
  (pair0,pair1) through [[L+0x10]+4]) - the source arrays
  are built while the level plays, not while classes
  construct. The construction sites also settle the class
  allocation sizes (0x5c320 sizes, PR-191 census form):
  SWIATLO/LEW_SWT objects = 0xbf bytes, OBJ_SWT = 0xc3,
  PODMUCH = 0x575 (1397 bytes - a large embedded payload,
  consistent with a pumped-light emitter), and the pattern
  `mov eax,<size>; call 0x5c320; call 0x531f0 (base chain);
  add eax,0xa9; <edx flag>; call 0x2d820/0x2d7d0` shows
  the light base lives INSIDE the object allocation at
  +0xa9, total size = class size (0xbf = 0xa9 + 0x16 -> the
  light base is exactly 0x16=22 bytes: array ptr, count,
  capacity, ops block ptr, and the +0x14 word). The
  0x2d820 sites sit right after the manager-getter print
  branches (0x2cb40/0x2cc3f), i.e. in the same ctor arms.

  parsers 0x4dc00/0x4db50 - siblings of the 0x4db00 group -
  all called ONLY from the level settings/frame-loop

  0x91f27), then ' %[^,\r\n] , ' per entry, and record
  verb+0 = the PR-104 FACTORY 0x4df10 fed the name string
  (0x4dcc0 reads the name via the PR-2xx settings scanner
  and calls 0x4df10 directly). So lights - like the journal's
  PLANT/GRABOBJ/ANITAB sections - are INSTANTIATED FROM
  NAME LISTS in the level settings file; allocation is
  `n*3*4+4` bytes (0x76a64) with defaults 0xa14c0/0xa0c78.

  member of the engine's SHARED THUNK BLOCK (0x23a10 =
  `add eax,0x89; ret` - the +0x89 sub-object locator seen
  in the same census): 0x238e0 = `if [obj+0x5c]==2 return
  0; else return [[obj+8]+8](obj)` - an IS-ACTIVE check
  delegating to the object's own ops verb +8. A_LOOKUP's
  per-light call is therefore a liveness/busy probe, not a
  registration: light REGISTRATION is msg-code 0x1b (the
  PR-508 setter), completing the light model: build (ctor)
  -> register (msg 0x1b) -> query (A_LOOKUP loops) ->
  draw (camera math). (3) The 0x5da60 level-object cleaner
  zeroes such list fields in groups of four ([+0x5c..0x68],
  [+0x6c..0x78], [+0x7c..0x80]).

## PR-511 - THE PLAN-STAGE FUNCTION 0x4b1d0: UP TO 3 PLAN
## ENTRIES, PER-STAGE TARGET COUNTS, AND THE STAGE COUNT
## PUSHED TO EVERY STAGE RECORD VIA VERB +0x5c

```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: PR-510's OPENS "exact stage-loop bounds in
  0x4b1d0". 0x4b1d0 (called ONLY from the settings/frame-
  loop function 0x4c8a0) walks the PLAN ENTRY TABLE at
  [level+0x30] - 4-byte entry handles, HARD-BOUNDED AT 3
  (0x4b20e `cmp ebx,0x3; jge done`): the engine supports
  at most THREE plan chains per level. Per entry: [e+0x44]
  = stage count (dword), [e+0x58] = stage-record list
  base; the inner walk (0x4b23d) counts 'A' chars (0x4b250
  `cmp dl,0x41; inc eax`) up to a per-stage target (loop
  runs WHILE the 'A-count < ebp = stage index+1 - a
  POSITIONAL check, the 'A' at stage n gates stage n), and
  tallies 0x7c '|' separators into ecx. Then for EVERY
  stage record in the chain (0x4b27f: rec=[e+0x58]+i*4,
  then rec=[rec+0x34] linked list) it calls verb +0x5c
  (eax=record, edx=ecx=the stage count) - each stage-
  trigger record is TOLD how many stages its plan has.
  Finally (0x4b2ba) it enumerates the '|'-positions of the
  chain via the PR-494 scanner loop: 0x57dd0 find, then
  0x57e70(eax=chain, edx=position) per hit until -1 -
  segment iteration (split or per-segment callback, 0x57e70
  body unread). Lengths use `repnz scasb` (strlen, 0x4b1e8)
  - so [level+0x30] elements ARE string-bearing plan
  objects, confirming PR-495's chain reading. This also
  answers PR-501's stage question mechanically: 'T|TALA|
  ATAB' = 2 separators = 3 stages, each with its own 'A'
  positional gate and record chain.

- WHY. Two open items asked whether the port's physics model is
  the engine's. For the integrator the answer is now yes, with
  the live word: the player's own registers ramp by the authored
  add and settle at the authored equilibrium, and the position is
  that register truncated. That kills the "where does +20 halve"
  question and opens the real one, which is the CADENCE: the same
  run admits the same accumulator at 5.5, 10 and 20.5 a second,
  so no px/s claim built on a fixed 20 Hz is safe, and the walk's
  travel is bounded by its step cadence, not by F/T. And the row
  list, not the impulse, is what holds a flight - the authored
  data says so twice (a self-restarting list, and a state that
  enters one row past the I row and never fires it), which is
  exactly the port's one-shot gap. What the crossing arithmetic
  of OI-124 now needs is one named state measured end to end, and
  that is OI-130: the object keeps a record pointer while the
  engine names states through another table, so the resolver had
  to be built before the claim could be made.

SUBSYSTEM: pr516i's four A_JUMP entries - the state-entry semantics

  in the code and withdrew. (1) THE TRY, AND WHY IT FELL. PR-518's
  gate-on path deadlocks a BY_X state entered at v=0: its row feed
  reads the word the last physics pass left, so with that word 0 it
  never admits and never runs the pass that would fill it - the
  PR-110/PR-114 A_PUSH leg (F=1000,T=40, one row `1,1000`) cannot
  build any velocity. Wiring "entering a state is an admit" changed
  the shape of the red (gate off 0 FAILED unchanged; gate on 94,

  the PR-259 BY_TY climb picking up 7) but it is NOT what the engine
  does, so the code is reverted here and only the measurement stays.
  (2) WHAT THE ENTRY SAMPLES SAY. Four entries into A_JUMP (380.31,
  384.61, 389.12, 397.18 s, all from A_DOSTAL): at the entry sample
  accum_a1 is 0 - the transition zeroes it, the rule PR-110 took from
  obj_transition and the port keeps - and it STAYS 0 for 4 to 8
  samples (0.08-0.16 s) before the first +100 feed appears; gate_95
  is 1 at the entry and stays 1 through that hold, so the one-shot
  I/F pull is ARMED at the entry and NOT fired there; v_raw_x carries
  across the transition untouched (1, 2, -12, 1), while v_raw_y is 0
  at every entry although the state before one of them held 250
  (389.10) - on this entry the y word is cleared and the x word is
  kept; the position does not move. (3) THE PULL AND THE PHYSICS ARE
  ONE STEP. The first sample with a flight y register already shows
  the dragged value: the authored I pair is (150,-1200) and the first
  observed v_raw_y is -1145, exactly -1200 dragged once by the
  T2=1/G=0,55 law. So the admit that takes the I row runs the pull
  and the physics pass together. That had been read as "the register
  is mid-decay at the entry, so the entry step carries physics" - it
  is not: it is the first sample AFTER the row's admit. Corrected at
  OI-015. (4) THE DEADLOCK STAYS OPEN, AND THE TRACE CANNOT CLOSE IT.
  Because the x word carries across an entry (paragraph 2), the
  engine's mode-0 feed is never 0 in these four cases; but a walk
  entered from a true stop - a spawn, or a lion whose x register
  reached the sign-cross 0 - has no feed and no admit under the
  literal reading. The live game's walk entries all carry a non-zero
  x register, so this capture cannot answer: it needs a spawn-plus-
  first-key capture, or RE of 0x543a0's mode-0 arm and whoever writes
  [obj+0xca] on a transition.

## PR-522 - THE COLD-START IS AN ENTRY REGISTER-SEED, NOT AN ADMIT, AND IT
## ONLY MOVES A WALK AT s=20: AT THE PORT'S s=10 THE SEEDED REGISTER IS 81
## (< 100), SO v//100 FEEDS 0 AND THE WALK NEVER ADMITS - CLOSING OI-015'S
## COLD-START AND BINDING IT TO OI-011

```
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the row-admit cold start (a BY_X state entered at a
  standstill) and what its entry step does to the velocity register and
  the row accumulator. PR-519 left this open ("the cold-start feed ...
  stays open"); this is the capture read it asked for, over
  /tmp/opencode/pr516i.jsonl (player 0x524400, 50 Hz). (1) WHAT A COLD
  START IS. Nine intent-free -> intent windows open a walk from a
  register held at ~1 (a brake tail carried across the transition, not a
  reset - PR-519's "v_raw_x carried across untouched"). Seven are
  ZARIA's A_WALK parameters (PR-520 showed the [rec+0x3c] vector mis-
  names them A_DEAD; the parameters, not the name, decide). In each the
  entry does the same thing: both registers FROZEN and the accumulator
  at 0 for 3-6 samples (0.06-0.12 s, the gate_95 arm), THEN exactly ONE
  register step: v -> v + idiv(F*s,20) + G_x - idiv(v*T_x,100), with
  idiv(v*20,100)=0 for the tiny v, i.e. a full force add. The step
  flips gate_95 1->0; the accumulator at that instant is 0 or 1 (only
  the new v//100 fed AFTER the step), never >= the authored threshold 6,
  so this step is NOT a row-accumulator admit. It is the entry seed, and
  it is what OI-013's [obj+0x95] one-shot gates: armed = physics held,
  then one step, then the per-admit loop. The port's row-admit path has
  NO seed, so it deadlocks exactly where PR-519 found it. (2) THE
  CLOSED FORM THAT BINDS IT TO OI-011. The walk only starts if the
  seeded register reaches 100 or more, because the accumulator is fed by
  v//100 and a register below 100 feeds 0 forever. The seed is
  idiv(F*s,20)+G_x (F=100, G_x=30), so the walk starts iff
  5*s + 30 >= 100, i.e. s >= 14. At the port's LL_PLAY_INTENT_FULL =
  10 the seed is idiv(1000,20)+30 = 80, register 81 from the carried v=1
  -> v//100 = 0 -> it NEVER admits -> the walk is dead at position 0
  (simulated 25 iterations, position 0). At s=20 the seed is 130,
  register 131, which feeds 1 per iteration, crosses threshold 6 on the
  6th, and the walk ramps 131,235,318,385,438,481,515,542,564,582,
  596,607 - value for value PR-520's live A_WALK ramp. So the cold-
  start feed and the intent constant are the SAME open question: the
  flip must seed the register at entry AND carry the keyboard's 20, or a
  ZARIA walk never begins. (3) WHAT THE FLIP MUST DO, and NOT do. It
  must NOT treat entry as a full admit (PR-519's reverted patch, 94 vs
  90): the entry advances no row cursor and leaves the accumulator at 0;
  it runs only the register step + the position write at the new
  register//100 (the capture's first step moved +1 = 131//100). The
  seed's own physics uses the same closed form PR-521 already implements
  - nothing new in the force arithmetic, only the trigger (entry, not
  accumulator) and the constant (20). The entry HOLD (gate_95 armed for
  3-6 samples) is measured but not modelled here - that is OI-013's
  remaining half (no writer of the [obj+0x95] reset has been read), and
  the port should seed on the entry iteration rather than reproduce the
  hold.
ADDRESSES: 0xba (intent_x), 0xc2 (the x register), 0xa1 (accum_a1),
  0x95 (gate_95, the physics-hold one-shot), 0xca (row_dx, the v//100
  feed), 0x54250 (the register step), 0x521f0 (the admit test, which
  the entry does NOT run).
NAMES: A_WALK, A_DEAD, A_WSP, A_DOSTAL, LL_PLAY_INTENT_FULL,
  LEO_PLAY_ROW_PHYSICS, pr516i.jsonl, OI-011, OI-013, OI-015.

HOOKS: none.
OPENS: OI-013 (gate_95's set/reset writer still unread - the entry
  hold is measured but its mechanism is not), OI-011 (now bound to the
  cold-start: s=10 cannot cold-start a walk at all)
CLOSES: OI-015's cold-start-feed half (the entry-seed mechanism and its
  s>=14 condition are measured, not assumed)
CORRECTS: none. PR-519's "the cold-start feed ... stays open" and
  "the live walk entries all carry a non-zero x register, so this
  capture cannot say" is answered by this capture: it CAN say, and the
  carried value is ~1, not a walk-ready register.
MEASURED: (a) 9 intent-onset windows, 7 with A_WALK's parameters; in

  drag 0) from a carried v in [-1,2], gate_95 1->0 at that step,

  s=10 seed 81 -> 25 iterations -> position 0 (deadlock); s=20 seed 131

  (a)); s>=14 is the start condition.
```

- WHY. The whole ZARIA playability chain runs through "pressing right

MEASURED: (a) THE TRIO AND ITS GUARDS, read this session: 0x54f40

  0x54f7b` - if value 1 is SET the trio is SKIPPED - and the trio
  is `[vt+0x48]` (lion: 0x23aa0, esi = the element record),
  `[vt+0x50]` (0x53e40, ebx = the flip sign), `edi = [element+0x33]`,

  state record -> its current-row word at +0x2e -> the frame list

  grammar PR-49 pinned and ll_mov_frame_ref implements. 0x53e40

- WHY. "ZARIA.01 playable" was the session objective and PR-524 had
  just narrowed the whole traversal to one law: the climb entry
  worked, the seat did not. This is that law - and the shape of it
  is the lesson: a directive word's apply is not one bit, it is a
  guarded CALL CHAIN into the element the actor is standing on, and
  the engine's own "art" numbers (LIFT.SEQ's +40) are the physics
  constant the route was waiting for. With it the authored ladder
  route runs end to end in two pinned legs, up onto the canopy and
  off the big tree, and what ZARIA.01 still lacks is now one
  subsystem, not a chain of guesses: the level end (0x5d1f5 stage
  re-entry, no end_level text exists to pin it).

- WHY. The session objective is "ZARIA.01 playable", and PR-525 had
  left exactly one subsystem named: the end. ZARIA has no
  `end_level` row, so every earlier attempt to reach an exit looked
  for a row that does not exist. The engine does not need one: a
  level's end is a property of the class ITS OWN .DES names, and the
  word the loop reads FIRST is that object's. That turns "make the
  level endable" into "honour the name the data already carries" - and
  it explains the authored wet animation: the dive is not an
  animation with an exit clause, it is the level's end, which is why
  its block ends in `unlock` and its transition leads to a state the
  player never sees again. It also moves the remaining gap into one
  honest shape: the entry data (one DRECT pool box) and the exit rule
  are both now measured, and what is missing between them is the
  938 px of ground in between.

## PR-527 - THE ROW-WALK DIRECTION LAW: `rev` NEGATES [obj+0x99], THE

```

NAMES: rev, revcmd, rowdir, broke_prev, LL_SIG_AC_BREAK_PREV,
  [obj+0x99], [obj+0x71], [rec+0x12], AC_BREAK_PREV, AC_BREAK_NEXT,

CODE: yes: ll_mov_fr.revcmd - the one-word `rev` tail parsed beside
  `lock`/`ldir`; ll_player.rowdir (signed char; 0 stands for the
  engine's +1) written +1 by ll_player_start (0x5388f), by every
  state change (0x52377) and by the landing-recovery state start;
  the flip applied at the row CLOSE of the row that carries the word
  (before the cursor step, as the advance's own verb order demands);
  the cursor step is now two-way - the forward branch is unchanged
  (bit 2 + cursor 0 at the top end), the reverse branch walks fi--
  and at 0 writes fi = nfr-1 and raises p->broke_prev, with no
  row-entry pull on either wrap, exactly as before; ll_mov_tr_mask
  turns broke_prev into 1 << LL_SIG_AC_BREAK_PREV and the iteration
  head zeroes both break pulses (0x5358e's one-iteration law).
HOOKS: none new.
MEASURED: (a) THE STEP, byte-exact, in the one row-advance method
  (a byte search of the image finds its underflow copy exactly
  once): the gate 0x52184 `cmpl $0xffffffff,0x99(%eax)` XORed at
  0x52193 with the two SEQ_REV terms; when the parity is non-zero
  0x5219a `mov 0x4(%esi),%edx`, `test`, non-zero cursor -> 0x521ae
  `lea -0x1(%edx),%ebx` writes cursor-1, and at cursor 0 the list
  UNDERflows: 0x521a1 `orb $0x8,0x0(%ebp)` - mask bit 3, the name
  0x91a2e is AC_BREAK_PREV - and 0x521a5-0x521a9 write count-1.
  The forward branch 0x521b6-0x521d7 is the twin the port already
  modelled. (b) WHY THE WORD FLIPS ITS OWN ROW'S CLOSE: 0x520da-
  0x520e1 load the CURRENT row `edi = [rec+0x2e][cursor]` and call
  its class's +0x4 verb (PR-218's clone call) BEFORE the step;
  0x52124-0x5213d then call that class's +0x10 verb with edx = 6,
  ebx = &[rec+4] and ecx = &answer, and 0x52140 skips the whole
  step when the answer is 6 (PR-323's GOTO protocol). The class the
  `rev` parse arm writes at [node+4] (0x45ea1) is 0xa0f28: its
  +0x4 verb IS 0x459b0 - bind through the shared 0x457e0, then
  `mov ebx,[eax+0x99]`, `neg ebx`, write back - and its +0x10
  verb 0x458e0 only walks the row's next chain. So the row that
  carries `rev` negates the direction and the step a few
  instructions later walks THAT close backward. Whether the node is
  the row-table entry itself or chained behind it is not settled -
  both readings apply the +0x4 verb at the same close, and no
  shipped row pairs `rev` with another tail word. (c) THE WORD'S
  WRITERS, exhaustive over the image (`0x99(%e` sites): +1 at the
  object build block 0x5388f beside [obj+0x6d]/[obj+0x71] = 1 and
  [obj+0xa1] = 0; +1 again at every state start 0x52377, in the
  block that zeroes the row accumulator 0x5236b and writes the row
  index 0x523cb (PR-95's method) - a `rev` therefore belongs to
  the state that authored it; `neg` 0x459b0; and one object-to-
  object copy 0x5338d-0x53393, plus one read in a compare 0x45b66,
  both unread here. (d) THE SEQ_REV HALF IS DATA, NOT HYPOTHESIS:
  ZARIA's lion spells SEQ_REV_X in A_TURN and SEQ_REV_Y in
  A_TURN_BACK/A_WSP/A_WSP_LIN (LEW.MOV lines 215/323/357/378),
  8 of the 777 extracted .MOV texts are lion scripts spelling it,
  and all three lion class records answer +0x70 with 0x239f0 - but
  neither flag term has a reader in this port (PR-99/100/101 read
  the flags only), A_LOOKUP and the RV-S fixtures spell NEITHER
  flag, and every leg here runs on the word alone: that half
  stays at OI-113. (e) CENSUS: 21 `rev` rows in 15 scripts of the
  777; the lion ones are ALL in A_LOOKUP (ZARIA.01 LEW.ZAR line
  629 + LEWPL 626, ZARIA.02 x2, TUNGA.11, TUNGA2.12) and TUNGA's
  A_BLOW_END/A_BLOW_DOWN_END (TUNGA.11 line 138 `8,500,REV`); the
  rest are object scripts (WODA1, GORYL, BUTLA, MALPA, KADMAR 0).
  A_LOOKUP's shipped row tail is `8,200,WAIT !K_UP` / `7,200,
  GOTO_REL 2` / `5,200,GOTO 4` / `6,200,REV`, and its only
  non-key exit line is `A_DRAP(1)=AC_BREAK_PREV` (line 615) -
  forward walking can only ever arm bit 2, which is why every
  probe through PR-526 ended seated in A_LOOKUP: probe3 held FWD
  from 295 to tick 900 and never left the state, max x 218.
  (f) RV-S (--play-selftest, RED first): fixture A rows
  `1..5,100` with `rev` on row 2 - the cursor walks 1,2, then
  BACK 1,0, then the underflow writes 4 with bit 3 armed and bit 2
  NOT (afi 1,2,1,0,4; rowdir 1,1,-1,-1,-1; broke_prev only on the
  underflow iteration), then the authored `A_RV_B(1)=AC_BREAK_PREV`

  has `rev` on rows 0 and 2 - reverse at once (cfi 4,3,2), the
  second `rev` restores the forward walk (3,4) and the TOP wrap
  arms bit 2 only. Parser pins hold the word on its own row only,
  and `ll_mov_tr_mask` resolves `AC_BREAK_PREV` to bit 3.
  MUTATION: with the row-close flip deleted, exactly the 15 leg
  A/C checks fail (afi/ard, the underflow pulse, the hand-off,

  `rev` row reverses the walk right there - frames 5,4,3,2,1

  own `A_WALK(1)=K_FWD` starts at 303 ON THE CANOPY at 205,485,

```

- WHY. The session objective is "ZARIA.01 playable", and since
  PR-524 the level had been dying in one state. The reason was not
  physics and not geometry: A_LOOKUP's authored exit names a signal
  the shipped row walk could NEVER raise. That made the missing law
  a playability law - if bit 3 has no producer, the state is a
  trap and the level cannot be finished from its own top. The
  engine's producer is a direction WORD, [obj+0x99], not a flag in
  the row: the same advance method that PR-99/107/323 read walks
  backward while it is -1, and its underflow is exactly the signal
  the authored exit names. And the row that carries `rev` flips the
  direction BEFORE its own step, because the verb order does that:
  the close calls the row's own verbs first, the cursor step comes
  last. That is also why every earlier attempt to make A_LOOKUP end
  - waiting for a timer, a wrap, a key release - could not work:
  the state ends by WALKING ITS ROW LIST BACKWARD off the top.

- WHY. The session objective is "ZARIA.01 playable end to
  end", and since PR-527 the level died at one known place:
  the 408..624 chasm, with exactly two authored candidates
  named and NEITHER bound. One of them - the rope the census
  had already pointed at - was a bounded read: its factory
  arm, its verb, and the placement grammar were all already
  modelled for the ladder, and the two verbs turned out to
  share the grammar line for line except at three places,
  which are exactly the numbers a rope needs (a narrower
  catch column, a catch signal instead of a rung signal).
  Binding it also settles a question the level itself asked:
  the band of the pit-side rope overlaps the canopy walk, so
  the authored A_SCIAG descent, the hang, and the UP lift
  are not dead text - they are the level's recovery device
  for its own edge. And measuring the hang's position
  against the east lip turns "maybe the rope is the bridge"
  into a NUMBER: 75 px short. That is what makes the next
  step the air-carry law instead of another class.

## PR-529 - THE x INTENT WORD IS THE KEY'S, NOT THE STATE'S: [obj+0xba]

  every state (auto_walk keeps the BY_X scope); `zero_restart`
  keys on the persisted FEED WORD [obj+0xca], scoped to BY_X, not
  on a zero register; three Makefile legs re-pinned, two added
  (ly_pool, ly_cjump_fwd), two hermetic legs added (A_JUMPX,
  A_AIRX); ll_level.c comment corrected.
HOOKS: none
MEASURED: (a) THE WINDOW IS BYTE-EXACT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. pr516i's
  named A_JUMP window - [A_JUMP] is BY_TIME, `F=180,0 T=20,1
  G=0,55`, no BY_X bit anywhere - holds intent 20 through an
  airborne state and the register answers idiv(F*s,20) = 180 at the
  value it carries: 26->201, 201->341, 341->453, 363->471,
  377->482, 386->489, 392->494, 396->497, 398->499, nine pairs
  nine exact; the instant the key lets go the SAME register decays
  on the drag alone - 400, 320, 256, 205, 164, 132, 106, 85, 68,

  341->453 the capture pulls every OTHER step - its own arithmetic

  zero feed word, not a zero register. Causality, selftest: HEAD

  (d) THE SCOPE PROVEN AS A SCOPE. A BY_TIME fixture with

  (f) THE KEY WORD IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN TWO JOURNEYS

  rows set the lion down GROUNDED on the canopy at (547,506) at

  ladder. (g) THE RE-PINNED LEGS, and what did NOT move: ly_trv

OPENS: OI-015 (which gate runs the pull: the capture's alternating
  cadence or the port's every-admit pass - it now decides whether

CLOSES: none as a row. "The chasm cannot be crossed under keys"
  is spent as a statement about the port: ly_pool runs spawn ->

CORRECTS: PR-523, twice: (i) the seed arm's trigger "a zero
  register met by a held intent" - it is the zero FEED WORD
  [obj+0xca], and the effective scope is unchanged since the old
  arm was only reachable through a BY_X s; (ii) the ly_cjump
  note's "A_PRE_JUMP's OWN `F=180,0` header - the state's
  authored x force, idiv(180*20,20) = 180 a pass, the raw
  register 300, 540, 732" - that ladder is the state's `G=300,55`
  word, which rides every admitted pass with no key held at all;

  separates the two.
```

- WHY. The session objective is ZARIA.01 playable end to end,
  and PR-527/528 had narrowed the level to exactly one gap - the
  408..624 chasm - with two authored candidates, of which the
  rope had been measured OUT as a carrier. What was left standing
  was a question about the port's own law, not about a class:
  PR-517's capture carries the intent word [obj+0xba] in an
  AIRBORNE, non-BY_X state, while the port had kept PR-135's
  BY_X-only scope because the walk was the only window closed at
  the time. That is a bounded read - one named window, nine pull
  pairs and a release ladder - and shipping it either closes the
  level's last gap under keys or measures exactly how far the
  remaining cadence question is from closing it. It did both: the
  level now runs end to end, and the same numbers say the
  original's lion, pulling every other step, would land in the
  pit. The restart arm had to move with the word, because a word
  that is held THROUGH a turn state no longer has a rising edge
  at the walk's entry - and the honest trigger turned out to be
  the one PR-522 measured, the feed word, not the register.

- WHY. The objective since PR-524 has been "ZARIA.01 playable end
  to end", and PR-529 delivered the traversal; what a PLAYER meets on
  the way is the pit, and the port's answer to the pit was written in
  PR-68 and never re-read. Measuring it first (nine falls, no life
  spent, no end) showed the port has a death path with no death in
  it. The read settles the parts that are settled from bytes - the
  starting count, the counter's full census, the verb that spends a
  life, the zero exit and its consumer - and separates them from the
  part that is not: the camera-row death line, which needs the
  camera's row arrays read before any of it can be ported honestly.

  vtable head 0x56d40 - which loads the object (0x49aa0 over the

  and desc+0x0 through the loaded object's verb +0x1c with arg

  HEIGHT. Threefold: (i) 0x57460 - the exact law PR-57/66 shipped
  and capture-verified - uses sx16([desc_i+0x2]) - 0xc8 and
  sx16([desc_R+0x2]) - 0xc8 as the y terms where the port uses

  [P+0x44] array by layer and call the descriptor's verb +0x8
  with the 0x50-tile strip math of the .PCM format; (iii) the

- WHY. The goal asks for collecting balloons to restore health.

  470/618/123. The box test is `by0 <= p.y < by0 + h` with
  by0 = pos_y + the element's f2 margin. For the walk art the
  box BOTTOM is the contact line (PR-97): with the lion standing
  on line L the box spans y = L-32 .. L. So a balloon whose
  point falls on a walkable LINE is spanned by a lion standing
  there, if his box overlaps in x too:

      `3 953,654;994,644;1007,646;1051,633` covers it - at

      the fruit/kokos table at 1542 is not a seat). OUT.
    (1270,460) and (78,460) -> points 470: no .plt line at

## PR-537 - THE PALMS, MEASURED: ZARIA.01 BLOCKS THE SEAT WITH A
WALL AND A WINDOW, NOT WITH A HEIGHT (owner goal 2026-11-26:
"…jumping on palms…" - first evidence)

  reached through the port's own jump physics - the goal's palm
  clause - and the walk boundary of ZARIA.01.

  (`p->vy >= 0 && ground_y >= hit.y - 1.0`, ll_play.c); the WALK
  contact 32 is PR-97's; the 100 px apex is PR-253's; the seat
  table parse and its x-bracket are PR-335/PR-338's (0x45200 /

- THE WALL, measured. ly_pal_walk (`1:FWD 2000:LEFT`, 2600 ticks,

  grounded is 406 - the west lip of the 408..624 chasm - and the

  Zero `state A_JUMP`, zero BAL lines, zero pickups. So no walk
  in this level reaches any seat line, and the walk route of
  OI-133 is not "hard", it does not exist: the chasm is a wall
  for anything that never leaves the ground.

- THE WINDOW, measured. ly_pal_top (`1:FWD 478:FWD,JUMP
  529:FWD 533:JUMP 600:FWD 630:FWD,JUMP`, seats ON): the second
  jump crosses the 475 height INSIDE the 380-seat's x-neighbourhood
  - 855,470 at 615 and 879,472 at 618 - and is not caught, because
  the landing test requires the descent; the very next line reads
  `927,477 grounded 1`, the authored static terrace `1 922,
  509;968,508`. That terrace is therefore reachable and pinned:
  the port can stand the lion at 477 on the east half of the
  level, which no leg had done from the air before. From there the
  630 jump peaks above the 380 seat line at exactly ONE x, 1000
  (44 rows, all at 1000), and the seat's own bracket is 885..947:
  zero rows at pos 348 (380-32) or 443. The seat is missed by 53
  px of x, not by any amount of height. A JUMP pressed while in
  A_DRAP is not that jump either: the port answers A_JUMP_S, a
  smaller pull (the same x 1000, peak pos 375), so only a press
  out of A_WALK/A_RUN has the reach - the port's own A_JUMP law,
  re-confirmed here in the vertical direction.

- WHY THIS IS THE BLOCKER FOR THREE GOAL CLAUSES. The corrected
  census says two balloons are reachable from authored ground:
  (1270,460)'s point (1280,470) from the 506-507 line at x
  1050..1080, and (1880,310)'s from the 347 terrace. Neither is
  walkable into: the 506 line is on the far side of the wall
  above, and the only route to it is this leg's jump chain, which
  pops all six balloons on its first press. The one x-window where
  a balloon point AND a perch meet (1050..1080 at the 380 seat
  line) is on the PALMA table itself - so the palm seat is not an
  alternative to the balloon clause, it IS its perch, and the
  missing step is a landing that carries the lion onto the seat
  line at the seat's own x (OI-128), or a seat whose table the
  lion is standing on while it moves (OI-125's element half).

- THE CARRY, NAMED (not ported here). OI-128's unread carrier is
  now a machine fact. The seat-table reader 0x45250 writes the
  step the table took during the query: 0x4526e-0x45291 copies
  the found record pair into the query's own slot [q+0x89]/
  [q+0x8d] and stores (record.x - old q.x) into [obj+0xca] and
  (record.y - old q.y) into [obj+0xce]. The collector 0x4b430 -
  called only from the ground-contact verb 0x54560 at 0x546f0
  and 0x54732 - builds its answer from provider 0x534e0 (class
  verb +0x68, four words at [esp]) and ADDS [obj+0xca] to words
  0 and 2 and [obj+0xce] to words 1 and 3 (0x4b479-0x4b48c)
  before testing the second registry [ebp+0x70]/count [ebp+0x7c]
  through 0x45620. So the engine's ground answer is already
  shifted by the seat's own motion: that is the carry, and the
  port has the table shift (obj_seat_shift, PR-342) but never
  stores the two deltas and never adds them to an answer. The
  full write/read census of the pair, and which other arms
  (0x45584, 0x45690, 0x27bb8, 0x54365) belong to this family,
  is recorded in OI-128 - and the port is PR-538's subject: a
  RED-first leg that lands the lion at pos 348 INSIDE the seat's
  bracket 885..947 from the terrace this leg pins, with
  LEO_PLAY_SEAT=0 as the control.

- NO CHANGE, AND WHY. No code changed: both legs measure what is
  there. What they change is the QUESTION. The palm clause is not
  a reach problem (the height is available from the terrace by a
  wide margin) and not a seat-ground problem (PR-535's ground is
  in that run); it is the 53 px of x between the port's jump
  trajectory and the seat's bracket, and the same wall/window pair
  is what keeps the balloon pickup and the fruit unreachable.

## PR-538 - THE SEAT'S OWN STEP, AND WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT DO:
0x52b10 IS AN APPEND, AND THE CLOCK ARM SHIFTS THE TABLE AND THE
ELEMENT TOGETHER
KIND: read
SUBSYSTEM: the ani_plat= seat runner pair - the +0xa4 (clock) and
  +0xac (jump) class verbs of KATAPULT/PALMA - read to settle what
  the authored seat motion does, after PR-537 showed the palm seat
  is missed in x and not in height.
ADDRESSES: 0x1e5c0, 0x1e5dd, 0x1e5f8, 0x1e5fd, 0x1e603, 0x1e60c,
  0x1e624, 0x1e630, 0x1e651, 0x1e690, 0x1e886, 0x1e934, 0x1e93e,
  0x1e944, 0x1e952, 0x1e957, 0x45200, 0x45250, 0x4526e, 0x45280,
  0x45286, 0x45291, 0x452c4, 0x52b10, 0x52b13, 0x52b22, 0x52b30,
  0x535db, 0x54012, 0x54155.
NAMES: obj_seat_shift, seat_x, seat_y, ani_plat, ANIPL2.DES,
  KATAPULT, PALMA, A_RUN, K_GEN1, BY_TIME, AC_*, LEO_PLAY_SEAT.
CODE: no: none. The record's finding lives in the OI-125 row,
  which this read edits.
HOOKS: none.
OPENS: none.
CLOSES: none.
CORRECTS: PR-336, PR-342 - the reading recorded there that the
  KATAPULT trailing pair is a LAUNCH applied through 0x52b10. In
  the
  cursor-7 arm 0x1e934-0x1e957, [obj+0xb1] and [obj+0xb5] are
  pushed as a QUEUED ACTION (0x52b10 appends a 16-byte node to
  the chain at [base+0x10]: node+0=0, node+4=EDX, node+8=EBX,
  node+12=ECX) and the returned handle is stored at [obj+0xc1];
  nothing is moved there. The real seat step is the clock arm
  0x1e5c0: 0x1e5f8 shifts the [obj+0xa5] table by y = +1/-1 from
  the row cursor (0x1e5dd), and 0x1e5fd-0x1e624 - the "element
  half" PR-341 counted open - dereferences [obj+0xb1] and calls
  its method at +0x8 with the words (0,1,0): the table and its
  element take the SAME one-row step.
GATE: light: verify-index verify-docs rc=0 (ok);

- WHAT THE CLOCK ARM IS. 0x535db calls the +0xa4 class verb from
  the state applier; for KATAPULT/PALMA that is 0x1e5c0, which
  reads the state record's row cursor ([obj+0x5c] through the
  state array [obj+0x50], PR-341's read) and hands 0x45200
  x = 0, y = +1 while the cursor is below 7 and -1 from 7 on
  (0x1e5dd-0x1e5f8). So a palm table climbs for the first half of
  its own row cycle and descends for the second: a BOB of
  +/-7 px, net zero, exactly what the port's obj_seat_shift
  already implements. The element half then does the same step to
  the .SEQ element behind [obj+0xb1] (0x1e603 tests it, 0x1e60c
  loads it, 0x1e61c-0x1e624 build the (0,1,0) argument block and
  the call is `call DWORD PTR [handle+0x8]`).

- WHAT THE JUMP ARM'S SEVENTH ROW DOES - AND DOES NOT DO. The
  +0xac verb 0x1e690 is a jump table over cursor-3 = 0..4; rows
  0..3 shift the table by the pairs PR-342 lists, and row 4
  (cursor 7) shifts it by (-42,-31), then - only if the handle
  [obj+0xc1] is non-null - calls three global methods and at
  0x1e934-0x1e952 appends (edx=2, ebx=[obj+0xb5], ecx=[obj+0xb1])
  through 0x52b10, storing the returned node at [obj+0xc1]. The
  five arms sum to (0,0) (PR-342), and the append is a QUEUED
  ACTION, not a movement: the walk at 0x52b13-0x52b20 finds the
  end of the chain at [base+0x10] and 0x52b30-0x52b3c writes
  node+0=0 / node+4=EDX / node+8=EBX / node+12=ECX. Whoever walks
  that chain is NOT in the object-runner range (0x52000-0x55000
  reads no [reg+0x10] as a link), and 66 call sites use the same
  helper: the queue's consumer stays open, and it is the next read
  if the catapult's launch is to be ported.

- WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE GOAL. PR-537 proved the palm seat is
  missed by 53 px of x, not by height, and that the port can
  stand the lion on the terrace below it. This read says the
  authored seat motion is a bob, not a lift: neither the clock
  arm nor the jump arm can carry a lion 129 px up to the 380
  line, and the only unaccounted authored effect is the queued
  action of the cursor-7 arm. So the palm clause needs either
  that consumer (the launch) or the CARRY of OI-128 - whose two
  delta fields [obj+0xca]/[obj+0xce] ARE written by the seat
  table reader 0x45250 (0x4526e-0x45291: (record.x - old q.x),
  (record.y - old q.y)) and ARE added to the ground answer by
  0x4b430 at 0x4b479-0x4b48c. The carry is the smaller, pinnable
  half and stays the next port; it does not by itself solve the
  380-line reach, and this record says so rather than hoping.
